docs.title: Global Macroeconomic Analysis Projections and Scenarios — Documentation
docs.text:
The Global Macroeconomic Analysis Projections and Scenarios is an interactive forecasting tool that runs entirely in your browser. It shows quarterly forecasts for 52 economies — growth, inflation, interest rates, public finances, and more — and lets you bend them: click on a chart where you think inflation will be, and every other chart updates so the whole forecast stays consistent with the estimated economics. Thirty-five of the economies (the United States included) are linked through trade and financial channels, so pushing the United States moves the euro area, Japan, and China too. The other 17 are the euro-area member states.

Three rules govern everything on the screen:

  1. Data are data. Solid history is observed, and nothing is filled in before estimation. Where a country's latest quarter has not been published yet (or a quarter inside the history is missing), the model estimates it from everything already observed — and those model estimates are always drawn in amber, never disguised as data.
  2. The model is estimated once a year, then frozen. Within the year, new data releases shift the starting point of the forecast but never silently change the model itself. The data currently run through 2026 Q2, so the forecast starts in 2026 Q3. Re-estimation happens once a year, after the previous year is fully published, on all data published so far (the October 2026 re-estimation runs to 2026 Q2). Each update is archived as a vintage, and the Monitor page shows what each data release did to the forecasts.
  3. Judgment is visible. If you move a forecast away from what the model says — a scenario, a long-run target, a policy counterfactual — the chart says so.

Under the hood it is a Bayesian Vector Autoregression (BVAR) per economy, coupled into a Global VAR (GVAR) with a fully endogenous United States, plus Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium (DSGE) impulse responses for policy counterfactuals. The deployed tool is served at the /bvar-scenario path of the academic website, hosted on GitHub Pages (the matyasfarkas/starter-hugo-academic Hugo Academic site), and at gmapsmodel.com (Netlify, from the gmapsmodel/GMAPS mirror). The build/deploy chain is documented in Build & CI.

The data and the model are separate from the app (since 4.0.0). Everything the app shows — histories, forecasts, the estimated models, the uncertainty draws, the trade weights — lives in a data pack: the folder app/public/data plus one manifest.json that lists every file with its SHA-256 fingerprint and size. The app checks each file before using it, and the dates come from the data themselves. So new data or a re-estimated model ship without a new app version; the desktop app takes them as an update pack in its data folder. The live pack is 2026Q2-reest-20261008b (data through 2026 Q2). See the Update Manual.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• User Manual (PDF) — methodology and usage in one document: each section states a method with its exact implemented conventions — BVAR estimation, COVID-as-missing data augmentation, conditioning, the GVAR coupling and closed-form solve, the fiscal and external accounting, long-run anchors, counterfactuals, vintages, evaluation, and reproducibility — and then shows how to operate it from the interface, with worked Examples naming the exact buttons. If you have five minutes, read §2 (Getting started).
  • The US Bloc Model (PDF) — the estimated United States model written down the way the VAR literature does it: the 40-variable VAR(3) with its domestic/foreign partition, the exact construction of the trade-weighted foreign variables, the GLP prior, the estimated foreign-block loadings, and the solve-time linkage through the \(x = Mx + d\) fixed point.
  • User Guide — a short web quick-start: your first scenario in five minutes, and where to go next. Defers to the manual for everything else.

Empirical results are in

An out-of-sample horse-race — 56 origins, 2010 Q1 – 2024 Q4, across 9 models, Continuous Ranked Probability Score (CRPS)-primary scoring + 90% Model Confidence Set — and the endogenous-US Tier-A spillover analysis have run. The headline: AR(p)/Dynamic Factor Model (DFM) lead the point race, but the EM-Bayesian GVAR is inside the Model Confidence Set on the nominal block (inflation at every horizon, the short rate at h ≤ 4), decisively beats the textbook OLS classical GVAR, and the endogenous-US variant weakly dominates the frozen anchor. Read the numbers and the honest caveats (over-confident draw densities; provisional spillover magnitudes) in Empirical Evaluation.

docs.title: Methodology and data
docs.text:
• Fiscal Block Methodology — how the estimated fiscal drivers relate to the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) and IMF fiscal-policy frameworks, the exact debt-dynamics recursion (snowball + SFA closure + primary balance), and the known limitations.
  • Data & sources — the source families, the yearly re-estimation versus the within-year data shift, and the full country × variable coverage matrix are in the User Manual (PDF) (§11 and Appendix B, generated from app/public/data/coverage_manifest.json). Every economy is rebuilt from its published sources, recorded series by series in pipeline/sources/registry/. Where a series lags its country's release calendar, the gap to the common 2026 Q2 origin is estimated by the cross-country model and flagged as a nowcast in the manifest (imputedThrough) — the same cells the app draws in amber.
  • Empirical Evaluation — the out-of-sample forecast horse-race (9-model density race, CRPS + Model Confidence Set), the endogenous-US Tier-A spillover analysis, and the honest caveats. Implemented in a separate evaluation repository.
  • Paper (PDF) — the accompanying paper. This link previously pointed at paper_outline.pdf, which is not in the documentation tree; it now points at the same file the navigation serves.

docs.title: For developers and maintainers
docs.text:
• Architecture (for AI / developers) — dense codebase map of the compute engine, GVAR topology, fiscal block, data conventions, and tests. Also documents the drag-perf / UX architecture (§5a/§8b): the heavy ~4.5 s GVAR solve runs off the live drag path — zero solves during a drag, exactly one cheap "direct" solve on pointer-up, and the full cross-country fixed point with uncertainty bands only on the Solve full GVAR button; the optimistic conditioned dot (conditionedDotY.ts) snaps to the click instantly; and per-chart React.memo repaints one panel, not all ~35.
  • Pipeline — the offline build → estimate → check → port → couple → test → deploy pipeline that produces the shipped data.
  • Modules & API — module-level reference for the compute and data layers.
  • Data Schemas — the JSON contracts the browser app reads.
  • Build & CI — the green gate, the test taxonomy, and the deploy chain.
  • Update Manual — how the data and the model are kept current without a new app version (since 4.0.0): data packs, the desktop data folder and update packs, the monthly check, the quarterly data shift, the yearly model update, and releasing a new app version.
  • Maintainer's Guide — operations, adding a country, and re-estimating models. Quarterly data shifts run through npm run data:shift -- --asof <quarter> (in app/; the script is scripts/auto_update.mjs), which archives the old vintage, nowcasts ragged edges cross-block, rebuilds provenance and the vintage comparison behind the /monitor page, and re-stamps the data pack.

docs.title: Runbook: adding a country / updating a country's data and model
docs.text:
This is a human, step-by-step guide for the data-and-estimation side of the tool. It covers three jobs:

  • A. Update an existing country (refresh its data, re-estimate, redeploy). Worked example: the US.
  • B. Add a brand-new country from scratch (standalone single-country model, optional GVAR link).
  • C. Add / refresh a 4-variable fiscal block (41 economies carry one today).

October 2026 — read first. Two things changed how this runbook applies: - The data and model are a data pack, separate from the app (4.0.0). Any change under app/public/data must end with node app/scripts/pack-build.mjs --pack-id <new id> and npm run data:verify (in app/). There is no date constant: each history records its firstQuarter. Adding a brand-new country still needs a new app version: the list of countries is compiled into the app (countries.ts, the CountryCode union), so a data pack can update existing countries but not add one (UPDATE_MANUAL.md §10, Known limits). - Panels come from source registries. A country's data are now declared in pipeline/sources/registry/<CC>.json and built by python3 pipeline/sources/build_panel.py --bloc <CC> (no fills of any kind). The FRED/builder templates below (§A1, §B1–B2, §B7) are the older path. The current estimation and post-run chain is the ★ section of REESTIMATING_MODELS.md.

The frontend is generic: it reads n (the number of variables) and every index from the model JSON, so once a country's JSON files are in app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/ and the country is registered in the single registry app/src/lib/data/countries.ts, the charts, conditioning, uncertainty, and the long-run anchor (LRP / entropic tilt) all work automatically — no extra data files are needed for any of them. The only hard part is the data and the estimation. (For the code-side architecture, see ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI.md.) The deployed tool is live at the /bvar-scenario path of the academic website, hosted on GitHub Pages (the matyasfarkas/starter-hugo-academic Hugo Academic site), and at gmapsmodel.com (Netlify).

Long-run anchor. Once a model ships, the user can set a long-run target for a variable; the app shifts that variable's forecast by a deterministic overlay built from the bloc's estimated companion (driftSetter.ts; it replaced the earlier entropic tilt). This is entirely frontend — adding a country needs no anchor-specific files (default targets, if any, live in app/public/data/default_anchors.json).

Current topology (pack 2026Q2-reest-20261008b). The coupled GVAR has 35 blocs: the US, the euro-area aggregate EA, and 33 Rest-of-World blocs (JP UK CA CN CH KR MX AU TR SE PL NO DK IN BR ID SA ZA TH MY CL CO CR CZ HU IS NZ TW HK SG RO PE PH); Russia, Argentina and Israel were dropped. The US has n=40 (29 domestic + 4 global + 4 fiscal + 3 stars). Augmented coupling dimension 2180, ρ(M) = 0.971875 < 1. With the 17 euro members, 52 country directories ship. The 17 members are estimated one at a time (export_bvar_euro_redesign.m, fixed companion, growth rates, seasonal dummies): domestic and fiscal blocks, rest-of-euro-area GDP and HICP, and the euro-area rates as external variables — no global commons and no weights row.

History — the callout as it read for the earlier 33-bloc deploy: The coupled GVAR had 33 blocs, and the US is now a FULLY ENDOGENOUS coupled bloc, not the frozen anchor. Its spec.json carries the three ROW*_US stars (ROWDEM_US/ROWINF_US/ROWFIN_US, block:'row') built from a US trade-weights row, so it both drives Rest-of-World and receives RoW→US feedback (n=41: 30 domestic + 4 global + 4 fiscal + 3 stars). The set is: the US + euro area as one aggregate bloc (EA) + 31 Rest-of-World blocs (JP UK CA CN CH KR MX AU TR SE PL NO DK IN BR RU ID SA AR ZA TH MY CL CO CR CZ HU IL IS NZ TW). With the US endogenous the coupling is the augmented (stars + US-global) closed-form operator of dimension 2060, with spectral radius rho(M) = 0.947 < 1 (stable; verified off the shipped coupling_default.json.gz header — rhoSpectral = 0.945494, eigendecomposition-exact since 2026-07-17; the earlier field read 0.935044 from an under-converged power iteration; prior builds read 0.945166 and 0.922404). The engine detects endogeneity from the data: US_ENDOGENOUS = !!usIdx.row && !!WEIGHTS24.weights.US in gvarSolve.ts, so COUPLED_COUNTRIES = ['US', ...rows]. The 17 euro members (DE FR IT ES NL AT BE FI GR IE LU PT SI SK EE LT LV) are standalone single-country models (domestic + 4 global commons + trade-weighted foreign stars, estimated in separation via MAXIT=1) — they are not in the coupled GVAR and have no weights row. Reason: the fully-disaggregated euro GVAR was non-convergent (rho>1); aggregating the euro area restores stationarity, which is why EA is one bloc and the members are standalone. (50 country directories ship in all: 33 coupled GVAR blocs + 17 standalone euro members.)

Seasonal-v2 expansion (history — now shipped; the live set is the 35 blocs above). This branch grew the coupled set from 33 to 38 blocs by adding five FSAP-coverage economies — HK, SG, RO, PE, PH — bringing the roster to ~55 economies (38 coupled GVAR blocs + 17 standalone euro members). AE (United Arab Emirates) was assessed and rejected: it publishes only ANNUAL real GDP, and the no-interpolation rule forbids inventing quarters, so it fails the viability bar. On this branch the static weights come from pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/weights/weights_full_38.json (the app's weights_24bloc.json is swapped to that 38-bloc content at deploy), and the augmented coupling dimension grows 33·60+80 = 2060 → 38·60+80 = 2360. The LIVE production tool is still the 33-bloc set (bvarscenario/main) — the callout above describes prod; the numbers below default to prod and the §B7 recipe builds the 38-bloc set. The concrete "add a new bloc" sequence is §B7.

Registry / selector. The country dropdown is driven by app/src/lib/data/countries.ts (one entry per economy, { code, name, group }). Adding a country = add an entry there + drop its data files; no dropdown edit is needed. The selector groups entries into "GVAR" / "Other countries" optgroups (driven by isGvarCountry from gvarLoader in controls/TopBar.tsx; plain names, no "- GVAR" suffix). group is only a coarse tag (core/oecd/em); GVAR membership is data-driven — a bloc is GVAR-linked iff its spec.json carries block:'row' vars AND it has a row in app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_24bloc.json (the filename is historical — the file now holds the 35-bloc weights, including the US row). The legacy app/public/data/meta/countries.json is display metadata only.

docs.title: What a country needs (the contract)
docs.text:
The app loads these files from app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/ (<CC> = 2-letter code, e.g. US, EA):

File Required What it is spec.json yes { n, variables:[{id,name,transformation,isFinancial,prior,block}] } — block ∈ domestic/row/global/fiscal; row+global are the GVAR foreign/commons blocs, fiscal tags the 4 fiscal-accounting vars; a standalone non-fiscal bloc is all domestic companion_mean.json yes estimated VAR coefficients { betahat, sigmahat, n, lags } baseline.json yes unconditional forecast in growth/display space (mean + q16/q84/q05/q95) baseline_levels.json yes unconditional forecast in level space historical.json / historical_levels.json yes last ~40 quarters (growth / level) transformations.json yes ['log'\|'lin', ...] per variable companion_draws.json optional posterior draws → enables Full uncertainty bands fiscal_meta.json fiscal economies fiscal-block indices {gdp,deflator,revenue,primaryExp,effRate,sfa} + d0 (dated d0_quarter) + sfaDefault. Present for 41 economies (6 core, 17 euro members, 18 others) external_meta.json economies with the external block external-block column positions idx and the variable ids they came from (idxIds), plus nfa0, fxShare and source notes (47 economies) estimation_mask.json every bloc since Oct 2026 the cells the sampler drew (no published value) — shown as model estimates in amber

transformation: 'log' = the series is stored as 100·log(level) and shown as 4·Δ (q/q annualized growth) — use it for real GDP, prices, indices. 'lin' = passed through as-is — use it for rates, ratios, unemployment. isFinancial just groups the variable under the "financial" header.

Fiscal block — 4 variables (41 economies today; originally the 6 core: US/EA/JP/UK/CA/CN). They carry four estimated fiscal vars (block:'fiscal', all lin):

  1. FREV_GDP — revenue / GDP × 100 (% of GDP, 4-quarter trailing ratio)
  2. FPEXP_GDP — primary expenditure (= total exp − interest) / GDP × 100 (% of GDP, 4-quarter trailing ratio)
  3. EFFI — effective interest rate = net interest / lagged gross debt × 100 × 4 (% per annum). This reverts the earlier debt-service swap (DSVC) back to the rate — older builds estimated DSVC; the current builds estimate EFFI.
  4. SFA — stock-flow adjustment, a new estimated lin BVAR variable = the EXACT one-step residual that closes the app's debt recursion (see below).

fiscal_meta.json idx is {gdp, deflator, revenue, primaryExp, effRate, sfa} — there is no debtService key any more. In fiscalAccounting.ts computeFiscalBlock reads idx.effRate as the rate driver, and — because idx.sfa is set — reads the per-quarter SFA forecast off the level path (levelPaths[t][idx.sfa]), so the debt/GDP projection now carries the deficit–debt discrepancy forward with its own dynamics and bands instead of being defaulted to 0. (fiscalAccounting.ts still contains a dormant idx.debtService branch for backward compat; the shipped metas leave it unset.)

The debt recursion (per quarter, computeFiscalBlock): 

pb_t  = FREV_GDP_t − FPEXP_GDP_t                                  (% of GDP, annual)
gNomQ = 100·Δlog(realGDP) + 100·Δlog(deflator)                   (% per quarter, off the level path)
d_t   = d_{t-1}·(1 + EFFI_t/400)/(1 + gNomQ_t/100) − pb_t/4 + SFA_t/4     (debt/GDP, %)
Debt-to-GDP is DERIVED (never an estimated variable); d0/sfaDefault seed and fall-back it.

SFA = the EXACT app residual (data-build only — see §C). For every non-COVID quarter the build rearranges that same recursion onto the observed gross-debt/GDP path: 

snowball_t = ((1 + EFFI_t/400)/(1 + gNomQ_t/100) − 1)·d_{t-1}
SFA_t      = 4·(d_obs_t − d_{t-1} − snowball_t + pb_t/4)          (% of GDP, annual)
so rolling the recursion forward with this SFA reproduces the observed debt path to machine precision (closure checked < 1e-6pp). The COVID quarters are set to NaN (NOT interpolated — an interpolated value cannot equal the residual) so the COVID-as-missing Gibbs imputes them with the rest of the block. SFA captures the deficit–debt-discrepancy / gross-debt-perimeter seam (intragovernmental holdings, federal-flows-vs-gross-debt). Deployed sfaDefault (≈ non-COVID SFA mean, % GDP): US 1.7518, EA 0.325, JP 2.233, UK 3.1487, CA 3.191, CN 4.017 (verified in each bloc's shipped fiscal_meta.json). The SFA estimation-sample length (number of non-COVID quarters with an SFA observation) is US 41, EA 21, JP 21, UK 23, CA 23, CN 18 — these are SFA-column sample lengths, not the bloc's spec variable count n (which is US 41, EA 24, JP 23, UK 25, CA 25, CN 20; the US 41 = 41 is a coincidence — the two counts differ for every other bloc). Do not conflate the two.

A checkable walkthrough lives in docs/fiscal_accounting_walkthrough_US_UK.xlsx (built by pipeline/build_fiscal_walkthrough_xlsx.py) alongside the source docs/Fiscal_Accounting_US_UK_NSA.xlsx.

The estimation tooling lives in pipeline/:

  • build_country_data.py — pulls FRED-based countries (EA/UK/JP/CA …) → raw CSV/.mat.
  • build_oecd_eurostat.py / build_oecd_batch.py — pull the OECD (EU/EFTA + others) economies.
  • build_us_auto.py — hands-off US builder (pulls everything from FRED + builds the fiscal drivers).
  • build_fiscal_<cc>_4var.py (cc ∈ us/ea/jp/uk/ca/cn) — the 4-var fiscal-block builder: writes {FREV_GDP, FPEXP_GDP, EFFI, SFA} into the bloc's country_rawdata/DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json (the exact-residual SFA + COVID-NaN recipe) and rewrites fiscal_meta/<CC>.json (see §C). Data build only — no estimation, no deploy.
  • export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m — the GVAR-EM iterative estimator (despite the 24 in the name it produces the 35-bloc coupled set with the US ENDOGENOUS and the euro area as one EA aggregate). Set env US_ENDOGENOUS=1 (requires a US weights row). It runs a parfor Jacobi sweep over the blocs (MAXIT iterations, TOL=0.03; production since Oct 2026 adds BVAR_DIFF_GP=1 GVAR_NOFILL=1 GVAR_FIXHYPER=1 and converges — see REESTIMATING_MODELS.md ★), each bloc estimated by COVID-as-missing Gibbs (cgl_bvarV5). MAXIT=1 = single-country (separated) mode for standalone blocs / euro members.
  • export_bvar_us_covid.m / export_bvar_oecd_covid.m / export_bvar_country.m — single-country exporters (US-only, OECD, generic).
  • country_specs.ts (variable lists for spec.json) / app/src/lib/data/countries.ts (the country registry / dropdown).

API key: the FRED pullers read FRED_API_KEY from the environment. Always pass your own: FRED_API_KEY=<your_key> python3 pipeline/.... Do not commit a key (app/.env.local is the place for local secrets and is git-ignored). Get a free key at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/api_key.html.

Network: the FRED/IMF pulls need outbound HTTPS. If you run inside a sandbox that blocks the network, disable it for the pull step.

docs.title: A. Update an existing country (worked example: the US)
docs.text: The US is fully automated end-to-end — this is also the test case for this runbook. Because the US is now an endogenous GVAR bloc, a US data refresh is a GVAR re-estimation (§B6 path), not a single-country export. The single-country export_bvar_us_covid.m still exists for an isolated US-only model, but the deployed US is produced by the GVAR-EM loop.

docs.title: A1. Rebuild the US dataset (macro + fiscal)
docs.text:
cd "<repo root>"
FRED_API_KEY=<your_key> python3 pipeline/build_us_auto.py    # macro + fiscal drivers, COVID handled
python3 pipeline/build_fiscal_us_4var.py                     # SFA → exact app residual, COVID-NaN

build_us_auto.py pulls every US series on the auto-detected quarterly grid and assembles the raw matrix. (Since October 2026 the US panel is built from pipeline/sources/registry/US.json instead: python3 pipeline/sources/build_panel.py --bloc US.) build_fiscal_us_4var.py then overwrites only the SFA column in pipeline/country_rawdata/DataRaw_US_glob.json with the exact one-step residual of the app recursion (reading FREV_GDP/FPEXP_GDP/EFFI + the real-GDP & deflator level columns the app reads, plus the observed debt/GDP from pipeline/fiscal_raw/us_grid.json), NaN-ing the COVID window (2020Q2–2021Q4), runs the < 1e-6pp closure check, and rewrites pipeline/fiscal_meta/US.json (idx{gdp,deflator,revenue,primaryExp,effRate,sfa}, d0, sfaDefault = non-COVID SFA mean).

docs.title: A2. Re-estimate the coupled GVAR (the US is endogenous)
docs.text:
# In MATLAB, with the repo's BVAR/ on path (the .m adds it). Production flags since Oct 2026 —
# exact script: docs/reest-2026/runs/run_gvar35b.sh
BVAR_DIFF_GP=1 US_ENDOGENOUS=1 GVAR_NOFILL=1 GVAR_FIXHYPER=1 NDRAWS=1000 MAXIT=30 BVAR_SEED=1 \
  GVAR_WEIGHTS_FILE="$PWD/app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_full_38.json" \
  GVAR_DUMMY_BLOCS="CL CN CO CR EA ID IL IN IS JP KR MX NO TR UK ZA HK PE" \
  matlab -batch "run('pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m')"

This estimates all 35 blocs (adding/refreshing the US changes everyone's trade-weighted RoW, so the whole set is re-estimated), with the US folded into the convergence loop with its ROW*_US stars. It saves the workspace to /tmp/gvar24_workspace.mat and writes the full JSON contract per bloc to /tmp/gvar24_export/<CC>/. Confirm the printed per-iteration max star change falls below TOL (convergence) and the printed GDP1q central forecasts are sane.

For an isolated US-only refresh (no GVAR), export_bvar_us_covid.m (cgl_bvarV5, sur=0, empirical-Bayes lambda/mu, 1000 draws / 500 burn-in) still writes a standalone US export to /tmp/us_export/. But the deployed US is the endogenous GVAR bloc, so prefer the loop above.

docs.title: A3. Sanity-check, then port over the live data
docs.text:
Inspect /tmp/gvar24_export/ first (never overwrite live data blind). Then port every bloc (6-sigfig compaction is the deployed convention) and refresh the fiscal meta:

cd "<repo root>"
python3 pipeline/port_gvar_exports.py                 # all blocs → app/public/data/bvar/<CC> (6 sig-figs)
cp pipeline/fiscal_meta/US.json app/public/data/bvar/US/fiscal_meta.json

docs.title: A4. Regenerate the coupling artifact
docs.text:
Any change to a deployed bloc invalidates the precomputed coupling (it is keyed by modelSig):

cd app
npx vite-node scripts/precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs    # → public/data/bvar/gvar/coupling_default.json.gz

docs.title: A5. Run the green gate
docs.text:
cd app
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run                         # all must pass; watch the GVAR + scaling canaries
BASE_PATH=/bvar-scenario npm run build

If n changed, the canary test scenario-scale-convention.test.ts may carry a fixture pinned to the old layout — regenerate it (the pipeline has _verify/gt.m, which resolves columns by variable id, so it is layout-robust) and re-run. Everything else is index-agnostic.

docs.title: A6. Deploy
docs.text:
cd "<repo root>"
git add app/public/data/bvar
git commit -m "Update US + coupled GVAR (data through <quarter>)"
git push bvarscenario main              # host auto-builds on push

The push to bvarscenario (matyasfarkas/BVARScenarioTool) triggers a GitHub Actions run that builds the static app (BASE_PATH=/bvar-scenario) and copies app/out/* into the matyasfarkas/starter-hugo-academic website repo's static/bvar-scenario/. That repo is a Hugo Academic site published to GitHub Pages, which rebuilds and serves it at the /bvar-scenario path. (The Action itself has no Hugo step.) Hugo is pinned to 0.122.0 in the website repo (0.123+ removed getCSV and broke the wowchemy/academic theme — do not bump it).

Done = the gate is green and the push succeeded. Open the live site (the /bvar-scenario path of the academic site on GitHub Pages) and confirm the US baseline, a quick conditioning scenario, and a "Solve full GVAR" run look sane.

docs.title: B. Add a brand-new country
docs.text: Use an existing FRED country (EA/UK/JP/CA) as the template.

docs.title: B1. Choose the variables and find FRED IDs
docs.text: Decide the variable block (a typical small open economy uses ~12–16: real GDP, consumption, investment, government spending, exports, imports, industrial production, unemployment, CPI/HICP, a short rate, a 10Y yield, the nominal effective exchange rate). For each, find the FRED series ID and tag it log (levels/indices) or lin (rates/ratios). Prefer quarterly, seasonally adjusted, long-history series. If a country's data is not cleanly on FRED (e.g. China), source it from IMF IFS/WEO or OECD and assemble the same raw matrix by hand — but use real observed data, never synthetic placeholders.

docs.title: B2. Add the country to the data builder
docs.text:
Add a block to COUNTRIES in pipeline/build_country_data.py (mirror the EA entry):

"XX": {
  "name": "Country Name",
  "start": "YYYY-01-01",
  "domestic": [
    ("FRED_ID", "GDP_XX", "XX Real GDP", "log", False),
    ... one tuple per variable: (fred_id, internal_name, display_name, 'log'|'lin', is_financial)
  ],
},

Then run FRED_API_KEY=<key> python3 pipeline/build_country_data.py to pull the raw data.

docs.title: B3. Reflect the spec + register the country
docs.text:
Add the matching variable list to pipeline/country_specs.ts (used to emit spec.json) and add a one-line entry to the registry app/src/lib/data/countries.ts:

{ code: 'XX', name: 'Country Name', group: 'oecd' },   // group: 'core' | 'oecd' | 'em'

That single entry is what puts the country in the dropdown (in the "Other countries" optgroup until it becomes a GVAR bloc) — the engine reads the real n from companion_mean.json, so no size metadata is needed here. (The legacy app/public/data/meta/countries.json is display-only and not required.)

docs.title: B4. Estimate + export
docs.text:
Estimate with the COVID-as-missing Gibbs sampler (cgl_bvarV5) and emit the full JSON contract (§"What a country needs"). For a standalone single-country bloc the cleanest template is pipeline/export_bvar_oecd_covid.m / export_bvar_country.m; for a GVAR bloc use export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m (§B6). The exporter produces companion_mean, baseline (growth) and baseline_levels, historical and historical_levels, transformations, and companion_draws. Standard config: the 2020 COVID quarters are NaN'd (window self-calibrated to the 2020Q2 GDP trough, searched within 2019Q4–2021Q1) and DK (Durbin–Koopman)-imputed; lambda/mu are empirical-Bayes (MH (Metropolis–Hastings) on the completed-data marginal likelihood); 'sur',0,'noc',1,'Ndraws',1000,'Ndrawsdiscard',500. The macro COVID window here is self-calibrated and may differ from the fixed 2020Q2–2021Q4 window the fiscal SFA builder NaNs (§A1); they serve different purposes.

If the estimator returns a singular/NaN SIGMA, the data is the cause: a NaN in a discontinued series, or near-collinear national-accounts identities. Drop the offending leading-NaN rows and/or fix a multicollinear variable. With COVID imputed, the empirical-Bayes lambda optimum is well-behaved (estimated ~0.24–0.56), so a fixed lamfix is no longer needed; if you do pin one, keep noc=1 or sur=1 free or lambda degenerates to NaN.

docs.title: B5. Place files, regenerate coupling (if GVAR), gate, deploy
docs.text:
cp /tmp/<XX>_export/*.json app/public/data/bvar/XX/      # or: python3 pipeline/port_gvar_exports.py
cd app
# (if XX is a GVAR bloc, regenerate the artifact — see B6.4)
# npx vite-node scripts/precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs
npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run && BASE_PATH=/bvar-scenario npm run build
cd .. && git add app/public/data/bvar/XX app/src/lib/data/countries.ts pipeline/*.py pipeline/country_specs.ts
git commit -m "Add XX country model" && git push bvarscenario main

docs.title: B6. (Optional) GVAR integration
docs.text:
To link the new country into the 35-bloc coupled GVAR (a Rest-of-World bloc rather than a standalone single-country model). Caveat: keep the euro area aggregated — adding the euro members as their own coupled blocs makes the system non-stationary, which is why the 17 euro members ship as standalone models (no weights row) and EA is one bloc. Verify the spectral radius stays < 1 after re-estimation (it is 0.971875 for the current 35-bloc / dim-2180 endogenous-US set).

  1. Add the bloc to the trade-weights file. Add XX (with its ISO-3 code) to the bloc list in app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_24bloc.json (regenerated by pipeline/build_trade_weights_full.py / pipeline/build_trade_weights.py from IMF IMTS (International Merchandise Trade Statistics); the US own-reporter row is built by pipeline/build_us_weights_row.py). Every bloc's row is renormalized over the active set, so adding a country changes everyone's trade weights.
  2. Give the bloc its foreign + global variables. Its spec.json must carry the 3 Rest-of-World stars (ROWDEM_XX/ROWINF_XX/ROWFIN_XX, block:'row') and the 4 shared global commons (GLB_OIL/GLB_USLR/GLB_USBAA/GLB_USEQ, block:'global'). The estimator export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m builds the stars from partners' completed series and iterates the foreign components to a cross-country fixed point — re-estimating every bloc (adding a country changes everyone's trade-weighted RoW). The raw inputs are the pipeline/country_rawdata/DataRaw_<XX>_glob.json files (domestic + the 4 globals; the stars are appended at export time, not stored in the glob). Run with US_ENDOGENOUS=1 so the US stays a coupled bloc.
  3. No frontend code edits are needed for topology. The GVAR engine self-configures from the deployed spec.json files + weights_24bloc.json (configureGVARTopology/deriveBlocIdx/US_ENDOGENOUS in gvarSolve.ts): a bloc becomes active automatically once it ships block:'row' vars and has a weights row. Do not hand-edit IDX/W/COUPLED_COUNTRIES.
  4. Regenerate the precomputed coupling. After re-estimating + porting, rebuild the coupling artifact: 
    cd app && npx vite-node scripts/precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs
    It builds the augmented-state coupling M in JS (DK-smoother probes), inverts (I − M) via a MATLAB BLAS (Basic Linear Algebra Subprograms) batch (app/scripts/invert_coupling.m), and writes the gzipped artifact app/public/data/bvar/gvar/coupling_default.json.gz directly ({modelSig, pinStructure:'', dim, rhoSpectral, M, invImM}, 6-sig-fig). The plain .json is removed/skipped because at this bloc count it would exceed GitHub's 100 MB per-file limit (gzip brings the current dim-2060 artifact to ~30 MB); the loader decompresses it in-browser via the native DecompressionStream (falling back to a plain .json only if the .gz is absent). The browser solves x = (I − M)⁻¹d from this artifact; without it the in-browser inverse (~19 min at 24 blocs; far worse at the augmented endogenous dim) is infeasible. The artifact is keyed to the data by modelSig, so it must be regenerated whenever any deployed bloc changes.
  5. Add tests. Extend the GVAR canaries in app/src/__tests__/compute/ (e.g. gvar-closed-form-routing.test.ts, gvar-coupling-artifact.test.ts, gvar-derived-topology.test.ts, and the endogenous-US / closed-form stress tests) to cover the new bloc.

Two-tier solve UX, drag off the heavy path (FYI, no per-country work). On the live ~50-country US-endogenous panel every mean solve is multi-second (~4.5 s warm / ~13 s cold), so no GVAR solve fires during a drag: the drag path is a cheap conditioning preview (the conditioned dot snaps to the cursor instantly via conditionedDotY.ts), exactly one cheap DIRECT first-order solve (solveGVARDirect, affine per-probe kernels, numerically exact) fires on pointer-up, and the complete fixed point + uncertainty bands run only on the "Solve full GVAR" button / top-bar Compute. A "computing…" badge and a direct/full mode pill are shown; the ≈95 MB (decompressed) coupling artifact is stripped from direct-mode worker posts; and per-chart React.memo means one conditioning edit repaints one panel, not all ~35. New blocs inherit this automatically.

docs.title: B7. New-bloc build recipe (the FSAP-expansion path — current)
docs.text:
§B1–B6 add a bloc "by hand" from FRED templates. The current path used for the FSAP expansion (HK/SG/RO/PE/PH) is a set of dedicated staging scripts under pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/. Follow it verbatim to add another coupled bloc <CC>. The GVAR topology mechanics (stars, globals, the self-configuring engine, coupling regen) are exactly §B6 — this section is the concrete, copy-pasteable data build that feeds them, ending in the same port/verify gate.

Viability bar — check FIRST. A bloc is viable iff quarterly REAL GDP exists on a public source. AE (UAE) failed: it publishes only ANNUAL real GDP, and the no-interpolation rule forbids inventing quarters. Everything else (short rate, 10Y yield, house prices, credit, equity) may be ragged or entirely absent; quarterly real GDP is the one hard requirement.

1. Source the core series into the staging tree (genuine data only). Write one {"id","source","dates","values"} JSON per series into pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/newblocs/<CC>/. Each series is a single live-API pull; monthly inputs are quarterly-averaged over complete quarters only (3 observed months); ragged tails are kept; no fabrication / backfill / interpolation. The three blocs with a committed builder script:

cd "<repo root>"
python3 pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/newblocs/PE/build_PE.py   # BCRP (real NA, IPC, 10Y yield, credit, equity) + BIS (policy rate, real RPPI)
python3 pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/newblocs/PH/build_PH.py   # PSA OpenSTAT (SA real NA, CPI) + BIS (policy rate, real RPPI)
python3 pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/newblocs/RO/build_RO.py   # Eurostat (real NA, HICP, 10Y, debt) + BIS (policy rate, RPPI)
# HK / SG have NO builder script — their core series were pulled from HK C&SD / SG SingStat and staged directly.

The shared satellites write into the same tree: - NEER — pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/neer/build_neer.py (BIS WS_EER, key M.N.B.<CC>, nominal broad basket; monthly → quarterly mean, complete quarters only) → neer/NEER_<CC>.json. - Real trade X/M — pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/trade/build_trade.py (Eurostat namq_10_gdp P6/P7, CLV, SCA for EU blocs; national statistical offices / OECD-QNA-on-FRED otherwise) → trade/EXP_<CC>.json / IMP_<CC>.json. - NFA / external (only if the bloc joins the external-balance satellite) — pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/nfa/build_nfa_external.py (IMF BOP current account + IMF IIP net-IIP nfa0 anchor + World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD nominal-GDP denominator).

2. Assemble the raw panel. pipeline/build_newbloc_panel.py reads the staged series (resolving each role across newblocs/, neer/, trade/) and writes pipeline/country_rawdata/DataRaw_<CC>_2025q4.json:

python3 pipeline/build_newbloc_panel.py PE PH RO HK SG    # no args = all five

It uses a per-bloc MANIFEST (the variable order, GDP anchor first — only genuinely-sourced roles are listed, so partial blocs are fine) and a ROLE dict that fixes transformation + isFinancial per role (GDP/CONS/INV/GOV/EXP/IMP/CPI = log macro; HP/NEER/EQ/CREDIT/CREDIT_GDP = log financial; RATE/YIELD10 = lin financial). The grid runs from max(GDP's first obs, 2000Q1) — a 2000Q1 EM-peer floor matching the deployed PL/HU/CZ blocs — to the 2025-Q4 vintage. A series absent at a date is stored as JSON null (the estimator back-fills the leading NaN; the DK smoother imputes interior holes), and ragged financial tails are kept as-is. Later 2026Q1/Q2 observations are deliberately excluded here — they feed the separate 2026Q1 rebase (step 8).

3. Inject the global commons. pipeline/build_globals_new_blocs.py takes a CLI subset (it defaults to the euro-member list, so always pass your blocs) and, per bloc, drops the legacy _US foreign block, appends the 4 US-determined globals (GLB_OIL/GLB_USLR/GLB_USBAA/GLB_USEQ, block:'global', forced isFinancial:1 so COVID masking keeps them observed), date-aligned by slicing the longest existing _glob file, and writes DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json:

python3 pipeline/build_globals_new_blocs.py PE PH RO HK SG

This DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json (domestic + 4 globals; the 3 ROW*_<CC> stars are appended at export time, not stored here) is exactly the estimator input §B6.2 describes.

4. Add the bloc to the static weights. A new bloc needs its own row and must appear as a partner in every other bloc's row (renormalized over the enlarged set). The worked example is pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/weights/weights_full_38.json — the 2021–2023 average of the time-varying panel over the 38-bloc set (pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/weights/build_weights_timevarying.py pulls the underlying annual bilateral X+M from IMF IMTS and writes weights_timevarying.json; the full-38 file is the window average: zero diagonal, <0.05% links dropped, row-normalized). At deploy time the app's app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_24bloc.json is swapped to this content (the filename is historical — step 7). (The live file holds 35 blocs: the 38-bloc set minus Russia, Argentina and Israel.)

5. Register the bloc. Add one line to app/src/lib/data/countries.ts ({ code: '<CC>', name: '…', group: 'em' } — the five FSAP entries are the HK/SG/RO/PE/PH lines). GVAR membership stays data-driven (a weights row + block:'row' vars), so nothing else in the frontend changes — §B6.3.

No-policy-rate bloc (SG). A bloc with no own short rate is fine. SG ships with no RATE (nor YIELD10) variable — its MP is exchange-rate-based, so its manifest omits the roles; the estimator then prints has no own short rate -> excluded from partners' ROWFIN and drops it from the financial star exactly like CH / NO. SG still contributes to ROWDEM/ROWINF.

Seasonal-dummy decision (NSA blocs). If the bloc's headline series are calendar-seasonal (the panel scan's calendar-R²≥0.40 and display-amplitude ≥2 — e.g. a raw NSA national-accounts block), add it to GVAR_DUMMY_BLOCS. On this branch the default set grows from 16 to 18 by adding HK and PE (PE's BCRP real-expenditure block is raw NSA — build_PE.py flags it; HK clears the same scan). The dummies stay in estimation + imputation, but the shipped forward forecast is seasonally adjusted (it uses the annual-mean deterministic term); set GVAR_NSA_FORECAST=1 only if you want the quarter-specific (NSA) forecast. See REESTIMATING_MODELS.md §1.3 for the full seasonal-v2 knob table — do not re-tune it here.

6. Re-estimate the whole coupled set (adding a bloc changes everyone's trade-weighted RoW, so all blocs are re-estimated — §B6.2). The current command (October 2026 settings; see REESTIMATING_MODELS.md ★ and docs/reest-2026/runs/run_gvar35b.sh):

BVAR_DIFF_GP=1 US_ENDOGENOUS=1 GVAR_NOFILL=1 GVAR_FIXHYPER=1 NDRAWS=1000 MAXIT=30 BVAR_SEED=1 \
GVAR_WEIGHTS_FILE=<repo>/app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_full_38.json \
GVAR_DUMMY_BLOCS="CL CN CO CR EA ID IL IN IS JP KR MX NO TR UK ZA HK PE <CC if seasonal>" \
matlab -batch "run('pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m')"

7. Port + regenerate the coupling. Then follow the §A3–A5 gate, with two extra steps for a bloc-set change (swap the shipped weights; rebuild the coverage manifest). (Since October 2026 the GVAR exports are copied raw rather than ported at 6 significant figures — docs/reest-2026/runs/port_to_app.sh.)

python3 pipeline/port_gvar_exports.py                     # all blocs -> app/public/data/bvar/<CC> (6 sig-figs)
cp pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/weights/weights_full_38.json app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_24bloc.json
cd app
npx vite-node scripts/precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs        # dim = #blocs*60+80; MATLAB BLAS inverts (I - M)
node scripts/build_coverage_manifest.mjs                  # rebuild the provenance/coverage manifest

(If any bloc's variable order shifted, also run node pipeline/fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs and node pipeline/fix_external_meta_indices.mjs — §C4.)

8. Date, nowcast the ragged edge, re-stamp, gate, deploy. Since 4.0 there is no date to set: run node scripts/stamp_calendar.mjs (each history gets its firstQuarter), nowcast the ragged edge (scripts/nowcast_complete.mjs), regenerate baselines and bands, and re-stamp the data pack under a new pack id — the ★ chain in REESTIMATING_MODELS.md. (If the export ends before the latest published quarter, npm run data:model-update -- --then-shift dates it and shifts it forward instead.) Remember that a brand-new country also needs a new app version (the country list is compiled in). Finish with the green gate (§A5) and deploy only on user confirm — prod is bvarscenario/main, and the coupling + weights swap overwrites every live bloc.

docs.title: C. Add / refresh a 4-variable fiscal block
docs.text: The fiscal economies (41 today) carry {FREV_GDP, FPEXP_GDP, EFFI, SFA} (block:'fiscal', all lin). Since October 2026 the block is built inside the panel build from the source registry's fiscal section (pipeline/sources/registry/README.md). The older dedicated builders, for the 6 core economies, are pipeline/build_fiscal_<cc>_4var.py. They are data-build only (no estimation, no deploy, idempotent).

docs.title: C1. What the builder does
docs.text:
Each build_fiscal_<cc>_4var.py:

  1. Computes the four columns from the country's raw fiscal source (e.g. pipeline/fiscal_raw/<cc>_grid.json
  2. the macro glob), with the same scaling as the legacy build_fiscal_drivers.py columns: FREV_GDP = 100·rev4/ngdp4, FPEXP_GDP = 100·(exp−interest)4/ngdp4, EFFI = 100·4·interest_t/gross_debt_{t-1} (% p.a.).
  3. Computes SFA = the exact one-step residual that closes the app recursion on the OBSERVED debt/GDP path (reading EFFI, pb = FREV − FPEXP, and gNomQ = 100·Δlog(realGDP) + 100·Δlog(deflator) off the SAME glob columns the app reads), then NaN-s the COVID window so the COVID-as-missing Gibbs imputes those quarters (do NOT interpolate). It runs a closure check (< 1e-6pp) and aborts if the residual does not reproduce the observed debt path.
  4. Edits in place pipeline/country_rawdata/DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json — replacing the prior fiscal columns at their positions and appending the 4th (SFA) column with block:'fiscal' tags — and rewrites pipeline/fiscal_meta/<CC>.json so idx = {gdp, deflator, revenue, primaryExp, effRate, sfa} (NOT debtService), with d0 (last observed debt/GDP) and sfaDefault (non-COVID SFA mean).

docs.title: C2. Run it
docs.text:
cd "<repo root>"
python3 pipeline/build_fiscal_<cc>_4var.py     # cc ∈ us ea jp uk ca cn ; edits glob + fiscal_meta in place

(The US builder, build_fiscal_us_4var.py, overwrites only the SFA column and leaves FREV_GDP/FPEXP_GDP/EFFI byte-identical; the others — ca/cn/ea/jp/uk — additionally revert DSVC → EFFI and append SFA.)

docs.title: C3. Re-estimate, port, deploy
docs.text: The fiscal columns are part of the bloc's domestic/fiscal block, so they are estimated by the same GVAR-EM loop (or single-country exporter). Continue with §A2–A6 (re-estimate via export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m, port with port_gvar_exports.py, copy the refreshed pipeline/fiscal_meta/<CC>.json to app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/fiscal_meta.json, regenerate the coupling artifact, gate, deploy). The shipped fiscal_meta.json is what the frontend reads — porting the bloc JSON alone is not enough; the meta must be copied too.

docs.title: C4. MANDATORY RULE — regenerate fiscal_meta indices after ANY variable-order change
docs.text:
RULE (must run after any re-estimation or port that can change a fiscal bloc's variable order or count): run node pipeline/fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs.

fiscal_meta.json stores the fiscal-driver columns by POSITION (idx = {gdp, deflator, revenue, primaryExp, effRate, sfa}), and the debt recursion in fiscalAccounting.ts reads the level path at exactly those positional indices. Any change to a bloc's variable order or count silently re-points those indices at the WRONG columns. This is not hypothetical: the 33-bloc GVAR-EM refit inserted variables ahead of the fiscal block in every spec except US, which re-pointed (e.g.) EA's effRate onto the equity index (~col 537) and made the EA/UK debt-to-GDP path explode. port_gvar_exports.py now re-resolves the meta for the blocs it ports; raw-copied GVAR exports need the script.

pipeline/fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs re-resolves the fiscal indices by variable id (the canonical, order-independent source) from the deployed spec.json and rewrites fiscal_meta.json for every fiscal bloc (41 today), preserving the model parameters d0/sfaDefault (verified — it only rewrites meta.idx). It is idempotent.

cd "<repo root>"
node pipeline/fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs
# prints per bloc:  US: ok {…}   |   EA: FIXED {old} -> {new}   …   N fiscal_meta.json files corrected.

Run it after every port that touches a fiscal bloc (it is cheap and idempotent — when nothing moved it prints ok for every bloc and changes nothing). The same applies to external_meta.json: run node pipeline/fix_external_meta_indices.mjs (it re-resolves idx from the stored idxIds; added in October 2026 after inserting DEFL_<CC> re-pointed 35 exchange-rate indices). The test app/src/__tests__/data/meta-column-indices.test.ts guards both files. The fiscal conditioning/back-cast canaries (fiscalAccounting.test.ts, fiscal-backcast.test.ts, fiscal-conditioning-integration.test.ts) are the backstop, but the explicit re-index is the fix — a green build with stale indices is still wrong.

docs.title: Quick reference — files touched when adding/updating a country
docs.text: Concern File(s) Data pull pipeline/build_country_data.py (FRED) / build_oecd_eurostat.py (OECD) / build_us_auto.py (US) Spec definition pipeline/country_specs.ts Fiscal block (US/EA/JP/UK/CA/CN) pipeline/build_fiscal_<cc>_4var.py → pipeline/country_rawdata/DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json + pipeline/fiscal_meta/<CC>.json (idx{gdp,deflator,revenue,primaryExp,effRate,sfa}); ship as app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/fiscal_meta.json Fiscal meta re-index (RULE) pipeline/fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs — re-resolve fiscal indices BY ID from the deployed spec; run after ANY variable-order change (§C4) Data (Oct 2026) pipeline/sources/registry/<CC>.json → pipeline/sources/build_panel.py --bloc <CC> Estimate + export JSON pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m (GVAR-EM, US_ENDOGENOUS=1, 35 blocs) / export_bvar_us_covid.m / export_bvar_oecd_covid.m / export_bvar_country.m Port exports → live data pipeline/port_gvar_exports.py (6-sig-fig) → app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/*.json Country registry (dropdown) app/src/lib/data/countries.ts (selector groups via isGvarCountry in app/src/components/controls/TopBar.tsx) GVAR weights / RoW (optional) app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_24bloc.json (35-bloc weights incl. US row; name is historical), pipeline/build_trade_weights_full.py, pipeline/build_us_weights_row.py, pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m GVAR coupling regen (optional) app/scripts/precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs → app/public/data/bvar/gvar/coupling_default.json.gz (gzipped, dim-2180 augmented endogenous-US, ρ = 0.971875) Data pack (since 4.0) app/scripts/pack-build.mjs --pack-id <new id> → app/public/data/manifest.json; npm run data:verify Topology (auto, no edit) app/src/lib/compute/gvarSolve.ts self-configures from spec + weights (US_ENDOGENOUS, configureGVARTopology) Manual tables regen (RULE) python3 docs/generate_manual_tables.py regenerates the manual's per-economy Appendix B from the shipped specs; rebuild docs/GMAPS_User_Manual.pdf and cp to app/public/GMAPS_User_Manual.pdf after any spec/roster change Fiscal recursion (read-only) app/src/lib/compute/fiscalAccounting.ts (computeFiscalBlock, SFA via idx.sfa) Tests app/src/__tests__/compute/ (canaries + GVAR closed-form / coupling / topology / endogenous-US stress)

docs.title: Codebase Guide (for AI agents and new developers)
docs.text:
This document is a dense, accurate map of the Global Macroeconomic Analysis Projections and Scenarios (a global projection and scenario tool, built on an EM (Expectation–Maximization) Bayesian Global VAR engine) for an automated agent or a developer who needs to make a correct change quickly. It explains where things are, why they are shaped the way they are, and the conventions you must not break. Read it before editing compute or pipeline code.

Companion docs: README.md (overview), USER_GUIDE.md (UI), fiscal-block-methodology.md (fiscal math), ADDING_A_COUNTRY.md (human runbook for data/model updates).

docs.title: 1. What the app is
docs.text:
A static, client-side web app: a Next.js (App Router) frontend that does all econometrics in the browser in TypeScript. There is no required backend for the core features — the pre-estimated models are static JSON under app/public/data/ and every Kalman filter / smoother / matrix op runs on the user's machine. A FastAPI backend exists only for computing DSGE IRFs from custom policy rules and is not needed for normal use. The same build also ships as a Tauri desktop app (Windows/macOS) that runs fully offline.

Since 4.0.0 the data and the estimated model are separate from the tool. Everything under app/public/data/ is a data pack: the files plus one manifest.json that lists each file's SHA-256 and size and dates every economy. The tool reads every data file through that manifest (lib/data/dataManifest.ts), checks it before use, and takes all dates from it — nothing about the data is compiled in except the list of economies the UI knows. A new pack (a quarterly data shift or a re-estimated model) therefore needs no new app version: the web build serves whatever pack it was built with, and the desktop app reads an update pack dropped into its data folder. See §2a. The live pack is 2026Q2-reest-20261008b (Oct 2026 genuine-data re-estimation, data to 2026Q2).

The economic content is a three-layer methodology:

  1. Conditioning — impose user paths on any BVAR variable; solve the conditional forecast with a Durbin–Koopman (DK) simulation smoother on the BVAR companion form.
  2. Counterfactual — overlay a DSGE-model policy counterfactual (MMB — Macroeconomic Model Data Base — IRFs + a policy rule, or the Barnichon–Mesters optimal-policy QP).
  3. Uncertainty — posterior-draw fan charts.

On top of these sit three extensions: a fiscal block in 41 economies (derived debt/GDP), a 35-bloc GVAR layer with a fully endogenous US (cross-country spillovers across an endogenous US bloc + an EA aggregate + 33 Rest-of-World blocs), and a long-run anchor (a deterministic companion-drift counterfactual that glides a bloc's forecast to a user-set long-run target along its own estimated convergence profile — the reactive, no-re-estimation analogue of a Villani steady-state prior; driftSetter.ts, default transition shape).

A fourth layer, Drivers, is experimental and sits strictly downstream of the other three: it reads the scenario path the app is already displaying and asks a chosen DSGE model from the MMB which sequence of that model's own structural shocks would reproduce it over the first twelve forecast quarters. It writes nothing back into the forecast. The claim is model-conditional — "through model M's lens, this is the mix of M's shocks that reproduces the path" — and it is validated by same-model recovery, never by any model-free statement about what caused the path. See §8c.

🔴 TOPOLOGY CHANGE — the US is now an ENDOGENOUS coupled bloc, NOT the frozen anchor. The deployed US/spec.json carries n=40: its domestic + fiscal vars plus 3 ROW*_US trade-weighted stars (0-based cols 37–39, block:'row') plus the 4 global commons it determines. With a US row in weights_24bloc.json, configureGVARTopology sets US_ENDOGENOUS = true: the US now drives RoW AND receives RoW→US feedback through its own stars. The frozen-anchor code paths still exist (gated on !US_ENDOGENOUS) and stay byte-identical for legacy/US-less-stars data, but the live deployment runs the endogenous path. The closed form is solved on an augmented state (stars ++ US-global deltas, dim=2180, ρ(M)=0.971875 in the live artifact). See §5/§5a.

The app ships 52 economies in one compiled registry (app/src/lib/data/countries.ts; Argentina, Israel and Russia were dropped in 2026). 35 of them are GVAR-coupled — the endogenous US bloc + an EA aggregate bloc + 33 RoW blocs listed in weights_24bloc.json (the filename is stale; it holds 35 blocs, US first, with a US weights row that activates the endogenous coupling). The other 17 are the euro-area members (DE FR IT ES NL AT BE FI GR IE LU PT SI SK EE LT LV): each has its own model (domestic + fiscal block + euro-area-wide external columns + two rest-of-euro-area aggregates, estimated one by one, outside the coupled GVAR), not in the coupled GVAR and with no weights row. The reason: the fully-disaggregated euro GVAR was non-convergent (ρ(M)=1.089>1); aggregating the euro area into one EA bloc restores stationarity (ρ(M)=0.726 at the time) — this is why EA is a single bloc and the members are separate.

docs.title: 2a. The data pack — how the tool reads data (4.0.0)
docs.text:
• One indirection. dataManifest.loadManifest() reads manifest.json (no-store), checks compatibility (schemaVersion major = 2, minToolVersion ≤ app version) and, for an update pack, that every reused file matches the app's built-in copy. Then fetchVerified(logical) / fetchJSON / fetchGzJSON look a file up in the manifest, read it, and check byte length and SHA-256 (for .gz, of the compressed bytes) before use. loader.ts and gvarLoader.ts read every data file this way. A failure is an error with the file's name, and the file is never used. Since Oct 2026 fetchVerified also reports every failure of a LISTED file to an on-screen channel (reportDataLoadError → components/DataErrorBanner.tsx); a file the pack does not list throws NotInPackError and is never reported (optional files: fetchJSONIfInPack → null). Callers stop instead of degrading: loadGVARModels refuses a partial bloc set (only NotInPackError blocs are skipped), loadGvarWeights no longer falls back to the build-time weights for a listed file, and page.tsx covers the grid with an error panel for a country that failed (the grid stays mounted with the previous country).
  • Where the bytes come from (getDataSource). Web: <base path>/data/. Desktop (Tauri): the pack built into the app, unless <appDataDir>/gmaps-data/manifest.json exists — then that folder (read with the Tauri fs plugin), with the same checks. An update pack in that folder may mark files inherit: true (= take the built-in copy). Rollback = delete that manifest.json and reload.
  • Dates come from the data. loadManifest calls dates.setPanelDates(manifest) before any bloc data is used. lastHistOf(country) throws if read earlier — there is no compiled fallback date. The pack's dating itself comes from each historical_levels.json firstQuarter + rows − 1 (stamp_calendar.mjs, checked by pack-verify).
  • DataPackGate (inside LoginGate) renders the app only after the manifest has loaded, so every component that reads dates during render sees them initialised; an incompatible pack is shown as one full-screen message. DataPackSection (Settings) shows the pack id, "data through", and its source (bundled / update / external), plus the desktop "Open data folder" and "Reload" buttons.
  • What is still compiled in: the economy list (countries.ts, the CountryCode union) and a build-time copy of the weights + 6 specs in gvarSolve.ts (module-load default topology, test default, fetch-failure fallback, and the candidate-bloc list GVAR_BLOC_CANDIDATES). So a pack can update existing economies but cannot add one.
  • Tools: pack-build.mjs --pack-id <id> stamps the manifest (packs are immutable by rule: never re-use an id for different content — the script does not enforce it); pack-verify.mjs --full checks every hash, the weights↔coupling link, the dating against the estimation panels, and that the pack does not need a newer app; pack-delta.mjs cuts an update pack against a recorded release (pipeline/released_packs/<version>.manifest.json). User and maintainer guide: docs/UPDATE_MANUAL.md; field reference: DATA_SCHEMA.md §1.1.

docs.title: 3. The render/compute flow (one pass)
docs.text:
ChartGrid is the hub. Per render it computes:

  • condForecast = useConditionalForecast(...) — single-country conditional forecast (mean + level deviation + scenario levels) via the DK smoother.
  • gvarFc = useGvarForecast(...) — for any active GVAR bloc (the endogenous US + EA + the 33 RoW blocs), the cross-country propagated forecast (solved in a Web Worker). null for a non-GVAR country (a euro member). Under the endogenous-US topology it returns a two-tier result: a fast mode:'direct' first-order preview on every pin edit, and the complete mode:'full' fixed point on the explicit "Solve full GVAR" button (solveFullToken) — see §5a/§8.
  • effective = (isGvar && gvarFc && !hasFiscalTarget) ? {...condForecast, ...gvarFc fields} : condForecast — the path actually drawn. This is the single source of truth for "the displayed scenario line".
  • fiscalBlock (the 41 economies with a fiscal block) — derived PB / debt-service / debt-to-GDP from effective.scenarioLevels by the accounting identity.
  • setDriversInput({ displayed, isolated, coupled, displayedIsCoupled, external, baselineDisplay, histDisplay }) — a publish into the store of the level-deviation paths the Drivers drawer reads (§8c). ChartGrid writes it in an effect and never subscribes to it, so the publish cannot re-render the grid; the same pattern as setChartExportData.

Refs gvarBandRef and fiscalMeanRef snapshot effective and fiscalBlock so the band-computation effect (which fires only on Compute, deps [uncertaintyComputing]) reads fresh values without re-subscribing.

docs.title: 3a. Per-chart render memoization (so one edit repaints ≈1 of ~35 panels)
docs.text:
A single conditioning edit changes scenarios, re-running the monolithic charts useMemo → every chart object gets a fresh identity. Absent memoization, Plotly would repaint all ~35 panels for one dragged point. Two levers (in ChartGrid.tsx) collapse that to ≈1 panel:

  • reconcileCharts(next, prev, onRebuilt?) (ChartGrid.tsx:205) reuses the PRIOR render's chart object reference for any panel whose freshly-built content is deep-equal (chartDeepEqual, :173), keyed by chartVar.bvarIdx. It returns the prior array outright when every element kept its reference (stable outer identity → no [charts] effect churn). The data is byte-identical — this only preserves reference identity where the content did not move.
  • MemoDraggableChart = memo(DraggableChart) (:2523) skips the re-render entirely when a panel's chart reference and the grid's useCallback'd handler props are all ===.

So a conditioning edit (or a GVAR spillover) repaints only the conditioned panel + any partner panels that actually moved. Pinned by chartgrid-render-memo.test.ts via the exported chartRebuildCounter / draggableChartRenderCounter instrumentation (test-only, ~zero production cost). This is the render optimization; the compute optimization (keeping the heavy GVAR solve off the drag path) is §5a/§8b.

docs.title: 4. The compute engine (app/src/lib/compute/)
docs.text: File Role matrix.ts Flat Float64Array row-major matrices + Cholesky/solve/Toeplitz. All linear algebra. kalman.ts DK Kalman filter + simulation smoother. conditionalForecast (conditional MEAN, no shock), bvarForecastDraw (per-draw unconditional, no shock), dkSimulationDraw (adds innovation). affineBlocKernels = the GVAR perf kernel: conditionalForecast is affine in the pinned VALUES for a fixed pin MASK, so it computes the time-invariant filter/smoother factors ONCE (one filter+smoother pass on the probe baseline) and makes each per-period unit-pin probe a cheap delta forward/backward matvec recursion — replaces (#cols·H) full smoother passes with O(#cols·H) matvec backward passes, byte-equal arithmetic. This is the engine behind the endogenous-US kernel cache (see §5a). useConditionalForecast.ts React hook: builds companion form, runs conditionalForecast, returns { forecasts, levelDeviation, scenarioLevels, counterfactualLevels, ... }. Handles counterfactual modes + fiscal constraints. taylor-rule.ts The 9 preset rules + custom Taylor rule. barnichon-mesters.ts B&M (2023) optimal-policy QP. fiscalAccounting.ts computeFiscalBlock — the debt/GDP accounting recursion, 6 countries (US/EA/JP/UK/CA/CN; see §7). driftSetter.ts Long-run anchor (§8a): a deterministic per-horizon display translation (level-space Sₕ·δc) that moves the display mean and every quantile toward a user long-run target — terminal hit exactly, band widths invariant; perVariable/joint solve modes + rigid/transition shapes (default transition), applied in ChartGrid. Supersedes the removed entropic-tilt PLR mechanism. driversDecomp.ts The Drivers decomposition engine (EXPERIMENTAL, §8c): decompose (column-normalised ridge min-norm deconvolution of a scenario deviation into a DSGE model's structural shocks over H=12), the measured observable↔BVAR-column unit maps, the class-view licence predicate classViewLicensed, the greedy non-collinear selection useAllShockSelection, and the FRB/US cluster composites (clusterCompositeIRF / buildClusterIRFs). Pure — its only import is ./matrix; no React, no store, no fetch. gvarDragState.ts Module-level signal bus (drag begin/end + compute-in-flight flags) off the zustand store, so a drag does not re-render the grid. useSyncExternalStore lets only the badge subscribe; useGvarForecast defers the heavy solve to drag-END (see §5a/§8b). ../conditionedDotY.ts The optimistic conditioned-dot display↔stored inverse pair (conditionedDotDisplayY / conditioningDeviationFromDisplayY) so a pinned marker snaps to the click instantly (see §8b). Note: lives at app/src/lib/conditionedDotY.ts (not under compute/).

docs.title: 5. The GVAR engine (app/src/lib/compute/ + lib/data/gvarLoader.ts)
docs.text:
35-bloc GVAR. The US is a fully endogenous coupled bloc (n=40; PZTEXP was dropped in the 2026-07 dedup as an exact duplicate of GLB_OIL): it carries its domestic + fiscal vars, the 4 global commons as its OWN endogenous variables (the US determines oil / US10Y / USBAA / USeq), AND 3 ROW*_US trade-weighted stars (0-based cols 37–39, block:'row') from a US trade-weights row — so the US drives RoW through the globals/its linked series AND receives RoW→US feedback through its own stars, iterating in the cross-country fixed point exactly like a RoW bloc. The other 34 blocs are an EA aggregate plus 33 Rest-of-World blocs (JP, UK, CA, CN, CH, KR, MX, AU, TR, SE, PL, NO, DK, IN, BR, ID, SA, ZA, TH, MY, CL, CO, CR, CZ, HU, IS, NZ, TW, HK, SG, RO, PE, PH — the blocs list of weights_24bloc.json; RU, AR and IL were dropped in 2026). EA and all 33 RoW blocs each carry two kinds of foreign variable:

  • 3 trade-weighted stars (block:'row'): ROWDEM/ROWINF/ROWFIN = trade-weighted partner real-GDP growth / inflation / short rate, renormalized over partners present each quarter.
  • 4 global commons (block:'global', the SAME 4 ids in every bloc, US-determined): GLB_OIL (WTI), GLB_USLR (US 10Y), GLB_USBAA (US BAA → credit spread), GLB_USEQ (US equity). All 4 globals are isFinancial:true in every bloc (verified across US/EA/JP/CN/…), so the COVID-as-missing window keeps them OBSERVED (not macro-masked / imputed) — a coherence fix that applies in particular to GLB_OIL and GLB_USEQ, which were previously mis-tagged: oil and US equity are market data and must condition the COVID imputation, not be holes in it.

How the globals propagate (applyGlobalPins in gvarSolve.ts). Each RoW bloc PINS its 4 global columns to its own baseline + the US scenario DEVIATION of the matching global (matched by id, 1:1): pin = cBaseLvl[col] + (usScenLvl[usCol] − usBaseLvl[usCol]). So a shock to US oil / US financial conditions moves the SAME common delta into every RoW bloc, and each bloc's domestic vars respond via its own estimated coefficients. deriveBlocIdx exposes the global columns as IDX[c].glob (id → column); a bloc with no globals gets glob = {} and applyGlobalPins is a no-op (the legacy globals-free path stays byte-identical).

Frozen-anchor vs endogenous-US treatment of the US global delta. In the frozen-anchor path (!US_ENDOGENOUS) the US is solved FIRST and frozen, so the US scenario deviation is a constant: the global pin is a US→RoW exogenous forcing that enters the per-bloc forcing/baseline d, NOT the RoW↔RoW coupling M (the globals are held fixed across the per-period M probes). Under the endogenous-US path (the live deployment), the US scenario deviation of each global is itself part of the fixed point (the US responds to RoW feedback), so the US-global delta becomes an augmented state variable and its coupling enters M via the buildLinearSystemEndo channels (2)+(3) — see §5a. Indirect effects (globals move a bloc's macro → its stars → other blocs) always flow through the existing star coupling M and are not duplicated.

🔴 DESIGN DECISION — pin the US DELTA, not the US LEVEL (load-bearing). Each RoW bloc estimated its OWN baseline path for the globals (weakly-exogenous regressors), and those baseline LEVELS differ from the US's by tens of 100·log units on oil. Pinning the US level would inject that entire baseline gap as a spurious delta even at ZERO scenario (every country would jump the moment it was selected). Pinning the US delta on each bloc's own baseline gives exactly zero spillover at zero scenario AND an identical common shock under conditioning — mirroring how the star pins use baseRoW + partnerDelta, not the partner level. The first (wrong) implementation pinned the level; it was caught by the CN-deflation and zero-scenario tests. Verified on the real GVAR data: a US GLB_OIL pin yields an identical oil delta across all RoW blocs to ≤1e-9, and a zero scenario yields zero RoW spillover.

The scenario deviation is a linear fixed point x = M·x + d (baseline is data-driven, computed once). The engine solves it in closed form as x = (I − M)⁻¹·d. Under the live endogenous-US topology the state is augmented (RoW+US stars ++ the US-global deltas), so dim = 2180 and ρ(M) = 0.971875 < 1 in the deployed artifact (pack 2026Q2-reest-20261008b; see §5a for the channel construction; the value moves with each refit — 0.957724 for the Sep 2026 model — and what is load-bearing is < 1; a pre-2026-07-17 artifact field read 0.935044 from a power-iteration estimator that missed the complex dominant pair — corrected by eigendecomposition). M and its inverse come from the precomputed coupling artifact (bvar/gvar/coupling_default.json.gz, read from the data pack via fetchGzJSON: hash-checked, then decompressed in-browser with DecompressionStream; no plain .json fallback) — building/inverting M at this scale is many minutes in-browser, so the artifact is mandatory for interactivity, not optional. The shipped artifact carries modelSig (35-bloc, US:40), pinStructure: '' (the empty/baseline structure), dim, rhoSpectral, M, AND the BLAS-computed invImM. The manifest records the weights the coupling was built from (gvar.coupling.inputs.weightsSha256); gvarLoader drops the artifact (and the solver recomputes) if that differs from the served weights' hash. Gauss–Seidel (solveGVAR, which now iterates the US too when endogenous) is kept as a cross-check; closed-form ≡ iterative to ~1e-6 over the full conditioning battery. (Historical note: the pre-endogenous frozen-anchor coupling had dim≈1920, ρ(M)≈0.726 — those figures no longer describe the deployed artifact.)

Topology is self-configured, not hardcoded. configureGVARTopology(specs, weights) (in gvarSolve.ts) reads each deployed spec.json + the trade weights fetched from the data pack (weights_24bloc.json; the filename is stale — it lists all 35 blocs; the build-time copy is only the default/fallback) and, for every candidate bloc, derives its gdp/price/rate columns (deriveBlocIdx, mirroring the estimator's findcol prefix order), its RoW-star indices, and its global columns (IDX[c].glob). A RoW bloc is active iff its spec carries block:'row' vars AND it has a weights row. The US is endogenous iff its OWN spec carries the 3 ROW*_US stars AND weights_24bloc.json has a US row — this sets the module flag US_ENDOGENOUS. Two derived sets are mutated in place: - ROW_COUNTRIES = every bloc except the US (the weight-row + global-pin recipients; the US is the global SOURCE, never a global RECEIVER). - COUPLED_COUNTRIES = the blocs that iterate in the fixed point: ROW_COUNTRIES when the US is frozen, or ['US', ...ROW_COUNTRIES] (US first) when US_ENDOGENOUS.

IDX, W, ROW_COUNTRIES, and COUPLED_COUNTRIES are mutated in place at load (importers hold live references); W is keyed for every COUPLED bloc (the US too, when endogenous), renormalised over the active panel. gvarLoader re-configures from whatever blocs are actually deployed. Never hardcode bloc indices or a bloc subset — read IDX/ROW_COUNTRIES/COUPLED_COUNTRIES at runtime.

File Role gvarSolve.ts The engine. configureGVARTopology/deriveBlocIdx (self-config from spec+weights; sets US_ENDOGENOUS), IDX/W/ROW_COUNTRIES/COUPLED_COUNTRIES (live, mutated in place), solveGVARClosedForm (the production entry — routes to the endogenous augmented closed form when US_ENDOGENOUS, else the frozen-anchor (I−M)⁻¹d, both with the amortized coupling cache), solveGVARClosedFormEndo/buildLinearSystemEndo/blocKernels (the augmented-state endogenous path, §5a), solveGVARDirect (fast first-order preview from prewarmed kernels), prewarmGVARKernels/prewarmGVARKernelsChunk (off-critical-path kernel-cache warm), solveGVAR (Gauss–Seidel cross-check; iterates the US when endogenous), buildGVARCouplingMEndo (export-time M build), seedGVARCouplingCache/hydrateGVARCoupling (consume the precomputed artifact), solveViewedScenLvl (viewed-bloc-only; US short-circuits the sweep ONLY when frozen). buildScenarioPins.ts Converts own-pins into the conditional-path matrices the solve consumes. runGvarSolve.ts Pure mean solve wrapper (worker + tests); routes through the closed-form solve. runGvarBandSolve.ts Pure per-draw band solve (experimental). Re-solves the GVAR per posterior draw → conditional cloud. mapGvarSolved.ts Maps a solved level path into display space (same forecasts/levelDeviation/scenarioLevels shape as useConditionalForecast). gvarWorker.ts / gvarMessages.ts Web-Worker glue + message types. useGvarForecast.ts React hook: debounced, stale-guarded worker solve; main-thread fallback. gvarLoader.ts Loads every deployed GVAR bloc's raw JSON (GVAR_BLOC_CANDIDATES, 404-tolerant), the trade weights and the coupling artifact — all through the data pack (dataManifest.ts); re-runs configureGVARTopology with the fetched weights; refuses a coupling built from other weights.

Special-case handling baked into the topology config: CN's GDP is real (since the 2026-06 surgical CN-only re-estimate — NOMINAL_GDP_BLOCS is now empty) → its DEM contribution reads gdp directly, not the deflated gdp − price; rate-less blocs (on the shipped roster only SG: no RATE_/POLRATE/YIELD10_ column) are dropped from partners' FIN; hyperinflation blocs (AR, while it was in the roster) are dropped from partners' INF and FIN (kept in DEM). These mirror the estimator (export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m) exactly. W is renormalized over the active bloc set at config time; the weights provenance is app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_24bloc.json.

Variable-coherence audit (verified at the time, 2026-07). All 1048 variables across the then 50 blocs were audited for coherent transformation / prior / isFinancial tagging, and the per-economy variable table (each bloc's variables with their transformation · prior · financial flag) was added to the LaTeX manual (docs/GMAPS_User_Manual.tex, Appendix B — generated from the shipped specs by docs/generate_manual_tables.py). Two coherence fixes shipped with the WN-prior refit: the 4 globals are now isFinancial:true everywhere (above), and IP_CA (Canada industrial production) was rebuilt as a log LEVEL rather than a growth/diff series, so it lives in the same 100·log level space as the other log variables (verified: IP_CA transformation:'log' in CA/spec.json; since the Oct 2026 rebuild its source is the OECD production index, pipeline/sources/registry/CA.json).

docs.title: 5·EM. How the coupled blocs are estimated — the GVAR-EM loop (offline)
docs.text:
The coupling above operates on blocs that are already estimated. They come out of the offline GVAR-EM iterative estimator pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m (the M-step/E-step loop; the runbook to run it is §12a). The fixed point is in the completed star variables, not in the scenario deltas — distinct from the solve-time x=Mx+d of §5. Algorithm (verified against the script):

GVAR-EM (export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m), env knobs MAXIT (default 12), TOL (default 0.03):

  load every bloc's raw panel  DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json   (≤ vintage; 100·log / lin via transformData)
  mask COVID:  NaN the macro columns over 2020Q2..Q4 (financials + ROWFIN stay OBSERVED)   # COVID-as-missing
  initialise each bloc's completed panel D.<CC>.comp (seed interpolation; under GVAR_NOFILL=1 the seed
    only starts the chain — every gap stays missing data that the sampler draws)
  repeat up to MAXIT times:
    # --- E-step: rebuild the trade-weighted stars from the current completed partner panels ---
    for each COUPLED bloc c:
      ROWDEM/ROWINF/ROWFIN_c  =  Σ_j  w_{c,j} · partner_j's (deflated) gdp-growth / inflation / rate
                                  read from D.<j>.comp, renormalised over partners present each quarter
                                  (rate-less blocs — today SG — dropped from FIN; AR, while in the roster,
                                   dropped from INF/FIN; time-varying annual weights per quarter, §5·EM.w)
    # --- M-step: re-estimate every bloc in PARALLEL on its [domestic | 3 stars] panel ---
    parfor each bloc c:                                                  # parpool('local')
      pos = find(prior=='WN')                                           # §6a — WN cols (fiscal ratios + the differenced GDP/price under DIFF_GP)
      [Xcond, BETA, SU, Dforecast] = cgl_bvarV5([dom | stars], lags=3, pos, nDraws, nBurn, MCMCconst, H,
                                                'mcmc',1,'MNpsi',0,'sur',0,'noc',1, 'Ndraws',1000,'Ndrawsdiscard',500)
      #  cgl_bvarV5 = GLP/Minnesota csminwel mode (bvarGLPmf) + Durbin–Koopman simulation smoother:
      #  the DK smoother fills the masked COVID + missing-star cells given the OBSERVED columns (per-cell, not per-row)
      D.<c>.comp <- Xcond                                              # the DK-completed panel
    until  max | Δ(stars) | < TOL   or   MAXIT reached                  # MC noise floor ~0.13 ⇒ a few iters suffice

  # MAXIT=1  ⇒  no star re-convergence = single-country / "separated" estimation (the (iv-b)/single-BVAR ablation)
  export per bloc:  spec.json, companion_mean.json, companion_draws.json, baseline(_levels).json, historical(_levels).json

Settings of the deployed run (Oct 2026, pack 2026Q2-reest-20261008b; script docs/reest-2026/runs/run_gvar35b.sh): BVAR_DIFF_GP=1 US_ENDOGENOUS=1 NDRAWS=1000 MAXIT=30 BVAR_SEED=1 GVAR_FIXHYPER=1 GVAR_NOFILL=1, 35-bloc weights, time-varying weights on. - BVAR_DIFF_GP=1: real GDP and the price series (incl. DEFL_<CC>) enter as growth rates with a WN own-lag prior; everything else in levels. The mixed VAR(3) is exported as the equivalent level VAR(4). - GVAR_NOFILL=1: no fills anywhere — leading, interior and trailing gaps are missing data drawn by the DK smoother, like the COVID quarters; the panel runs to the latest published quarter per series (ragged end). The cells the sampler drew are exported per bloc in estimation_mask.json. - GVAR_FIXHYPER=1 + a fixed seed (common random numbers): the EM sweeps use the smooth sampler (hyperparameters at the posterior mode, re-seeded stream), so the sweep-to-sweep star change measures the fixed point and can meet TOL; then ONE final full-MH pass at the frozen converged stars produces the shipped posterior. The deployed run converged at sweep 6 (change 0.0109 < 0.03). Before this (and the explicit rng(0,'twister') fix in cgl_bvarV5) the random stream depended on the parallel worker and the Sep 2026 run stopped at 12 sweeps unconverged.

The "E-step" is the Durbin–Koopman completion of the foreign/star (and COVID-masked) cells; the "M-step" is the Bayesian re-estimation of each bloc; iterating to a fixed point in the completed stars is the EM analogy. Set US_ENDOGENOUS=1 to fold the US into the parfor set (it then builds its own ROW*_US stars from its partners and feeds the global commons — §5/§5a). This is the estimator the empirical horse-race (§14) drives at every out-of-sample origin.

E-step companion mode (fixed vs exact data-augmentation). The outer EM/Jacobi loop runs the DK imputation with a FIXED-companion E-step (cgl_bvarV5 'fixedcomp'=1, CGL_FIXED_COMPANION) so consecutive iterations share random numbers (common random numbers) and the star fixed point CONTRACTS to TOL (e.g. run 3: 14.7→1.07→0.20→0.11→plateau ~0.1). A separate exact data-augmentation mode ('fixedcomp'=0, GVAR_POLISH_EXACT) rebuilds the companion from the current draw every Gibbs sweep (the open-issue-#4 fix) and is available as a final polish sweep, but it is NOT used to ship the coupled GVAR — it (i) breaks the outer-loop convergence and (ii) marginally raises companion persistence. The shipped coupled models use the fixed-companion posterior; the 17 euro members in the deployed pack were also run with CGL_FIXED_COMPANION=1 (docs/reest-2026/runs/run_members.sh). See the 'fixedcomp' header in BVAR/MFBVAR/cgl_bvarV5.m.

docs.title: 5·EM.s. Seasonal dummies for NSA-seasonal blocs (offline estimation contract)
docs.text:
Some blocs carry not-seasonally-adjusted (NSA) series (NSA HICP/CPI, unemployment LR, house prices, India GOV, UK/KR SFA) whose within-year cycle, left unmodelled, is otherwise absorbed by a near-Nyquist companion root (an alternating-sign root ≈ −1) that produces a spurious sawtooth in forecast.
