BUT the magnitudes are large and sign-flipping across horizons (e.g. the frozen-anchor US/UK growth paths swing to −4.4 / −3.1 at h=20), and it is a multi-period conditional projection, NOT a causal IRF (the file labels itself exactly that). The magnitudes need a validation pass before being headlined — do not over-claim a causal interpretation.

Naming note: the protocol references this repo's weights as weights_full.json (the 33-bloc, US-row file used for the eval pulls, still including RU/AR/IL) and pipeline/country_rawdata/DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json; the app now loads weights_24bloc.json with the 35-bloc set (= weights_full_38.json; no RU/AR/IL, plus HK/SG/RO/PE/PH). The two files no longer carry the same bloc set.

docs.title: Build, Test & Deploy
docs.text:
How the EM-Bayesian Global VAR platform goes from a working tree to the two live sites — the /bvar-scenario path of the academic website (GitHub Pages) and gmapsmodel.com (Netlify) — and to the desktop installer. This page documents the green gate (the local checks that must pass before any deploy), the data-pack check every build runs, the test taxonomy (which suites guard an invariant versus a feature), and the deploy chain (two builds of the same commit).

Since 4.0.0 the data and the estimated model live in a data pack (app/public/data + manifest.json), separate from the tool: the build ships whatever pack is in the tree, and desktop users can update the pack without a new installer (UPDATE_MANUAL.md).

For the higher-level architecture and the data-refresh / re-estimation runbook, see ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI.md and REESTIMATING_MODELS.md. This page does not repeat those.

docs.title: The green gate
docs.text:
Everything runs from the app/ directory. The commands below are the full pre-deploy contract — types clean, tests green (fast suite + the heavy solver canaries), static export succeeds — before any push to the deploy remote.

cd app
npx tsc --noEmit                       # 1. types: must report 0 errors
npm test                               # 2. fast suite (excludes the heavy solver canaries)
npm run test:heavy                     # 3. heavy solver/perf canaries (serialised, 1 fork)
BASE_PATH=/bvar-scenario npm run build # 4. static export with the deploy base path
Step Command What it proves Types npx tsc --noEmit TypeScript compiles with no errors (no emit; type-check only). Fast tests npm test The fast compute suite in app/src/__tests__/compute/, minus the heavy solver canaries (see the split below), including the cheap canaries. Heavy tests npm run test:heavy The expensive full-panel solver / affine-kernel / band-solve canaries, run serialised (--poolOptions.forks.maxForks=1) so the multi-second US-endogenous solves do not contend for cores. Build npm run build prebuild first: gzip_companion_draws.mjs (gzips every local plain companion_draws.json into its .gz; in a fresh checkout there is none — the plain files are not in git — and the committed .gz is used), vintages_publish.mjs (re-bakes the /monitor vintage files), pack-verify.mjs --full (every file matches manifest.json; dating, weights↔coupling and app-version checks). Then next build writes the static export (output: 'export') to app/out/, and prune-redundant-json.mjs web drops plain .json files that have a .gz twin.

Green gate = tsc 0 errors and npm test green and npm run test:heavy green and the build succeeds. Only then is a deploy allowed. The gate is manual: neither deploy (GitHub Action, Netlify) runs tsc or the tests. What they do run is npm run build, so a pack that fails pack-verify --full cannot deploy. npx vitest run (= npm run test:all) runs everything in one pass — use it for a full sweep, but note it runs the heavy suites with default parallelism (slower, can over-subscribe).

The fast/heavy split is real, and it is in package.json — read it, don't assume. npm test is not vitest run: it is vitest run with a list of --exclude globs. The excluded (heavy) patterns are gvar-us-endogenous, gvar-direct-channel, gvar-band-solve, gvar-band-solve-levelunits, gvar-nowcast-completion, gvar-closed-form-*, affine-blockernels-parity, gvar-kernel-affine-independence, gvar-external-spillover, gvar-anderson. npm run test:heavy runs exactly those (matched by vitest run <name…>), one fork at a time. A change that only npm test covers leaves the full-panel solver paths (dim 2180 in the deployed pack) unverified — both halves are mandatory before deploy. (npm run test:watch is vitest — the interactive watcher, never a CI gate.)

A few notes that are easy to get wrong:

  • The build is a static export: next.config.mjs sets output: 'export', images.unoptimized: true, and routes the deploy prefix through basePath/assetPrefix/NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH, all driven by the BASE_PATH env var (see BASE_PATH below).
  • This is not stock Next.js — see app/AGENTS.md. Read the bundled docs under node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before changing build config.

docs.title: Test taxonomy
docs.text:
Most tests live in app/src/__tests__/compute/; checks on the shipped data files (e.g. meta-column-indices.test.ts) are in app/src/__tests__/data/. They fall into three roles:

  • CANARY — guards a load-bearing invariant or a deployed artifact. A red canary means the shipped model data, the scaling convention, or the cross-country solver identity is broken; it must block the deploy, not be skipped.
  • FEATURE — proves a specific user-facing capability (a Taylor rule, optimal policy, the fiscal debt recursion, US-endogenous coupling, the entropic long-run tilt, GVAR globals/topology, …).
  • REGRESSION — pins a previously-fixed bug so it cannot silently return (scaling differencing, WYSIWYG conditioning, counterfactual recovery, …).

docs.title: Fast (npm test) vs heavy (npm run test:heavy) — which is which
docs.text:
npm test excludes ten heavy patterns; npm run test:heavy runs exactly those, serialised to one fork. The three deploy-blocking canaries (scenario-scale-convention, gvar-convergence, gvar-coupling-artifact) are all in the fast suite. The heavy suite is the multi-second full-panel solver and the affine-kernel/coupling perf-parity gates:

--exclude glob (from package.json) currently-present files what it covers gvar-us-endogenous gvar-us-endogenous.test.ts augmented endogenous fixed point (full panel) gvar-direct-channel gvar-direct-channel.test.ts the one-hop preview on the live US-endogenous panel gvar-band-solve gvar-band-solve.test.ts per-draw conditional GVAR re-solve (the experimental cloud) gvar-closed-form-* gvar-closed-form-routing.test.ts (I−M)⁻¹d ≡ iterative + cache correctness on the endogenous fixture gvar-band-solve-levelunits gvar-band-solve-levelunits.test.ts the band solve in level units gvar-nowcast-completion gvar-nowcast-completion.test.ts the coupled nowcast of the ragged edge (needs up to 120 sweeps on the deployed model) affine-blockernels-parity affine-blockernels-parity.test.ts one full filter+smoother probe-loop reference (slow by design) gvar-kernel-affine-independence gvar-kernel-affine-independence.test.ts the kernel-cache RANK-1 affine-independence gate gvar-external-spillover gvar-external-spillover.test.ts external-forecast propagation through the coupled solve gvar-anderson gvar-anderson.test.ts the Anderson-accelerated soft (external-forecast) solve reaches the same fixed point (≈5 min alone)

The fast/heavy split is keyed on glob patterns, not a fixed file list: npm test --excludes the ten patterns above and npm run test:heavy selects gvar-us-endogenous gvar-direct-channel gvar-band-solve gvar-closed-form affine-blockernels gvar-kernel-affine gvar-nowcast-completion gvar-external-spillover gvar-anderson (app/package.json is authoritative) — so a new gvar-closed-form-* file is auto-routed to the heavy half. Everything else in app/src/__tests__/ runs under npm test. Both halves are part of the gate — a heavy suite that only test:heavy runs still blocks a release if red. (Under heavy machine load some vitest workers time out; such a file is re-run on its own before it counts as a failure.)

docs.title: Canary suites (block deploy)
docs.text:
Test file Guards scenario-scale-convention.test.ts The conditional-display scaling convention: response paths for log vars are shown as 4·(Δlevel_t − Δlevel_{t−1}) (q/q-annualized rate deviation), not 4·levelGap_t (cumulative price-level gap). Pins the corrected convention against the MATLAB conforekf ground truth for the canonical Baa +100bp / 8q shock; a break would re-introduce the ~23× far-horizon overstatement. gvar-convergence.test.ts Gauss-Seidel ≡ closed-form: for the same US scenario the iterative solveGVAR (Gauss-Seidel sweeps, US frozen) and the linear solveGVARLinear (build M by unit-RoW probes, then (I−M)⁻¹ d / Smith doubling) must agree to ~machine precision per RoW country. This is the proof that the N-bloc linear-solver generalization is correct; also reports empirical and power-iteration ρ(M). gvar-coupling-artifact.test.ts The pre-shipped coupling artifact (public/data/bvar/gvar/coupling_default.json.gz) is FRESH: its modelSig matches the deployed models, the augmented empty-pin-structure dim is self-consistent with the live US-endogenous build, ρ ∈ (0,1), and an artifact-hydrated solve equals the live-built closed-form solve (≤1e-3, the 6-sig-fig rounding bound). Also asserts the route REFUSES the empty-structure artifact for a non-empty (e.g. US-pinned) request. Skips loudly if the .gz is missing rather than failing.

These three must stop a release if red — they cover the two things a static deploy cannot self-correct: the shipped artifacts (coupling_default.json.gz, the per-bloc model JSON) and the display/solver conventions the UI renders on top of them. Two data-file guards belong with them: fiscal-meta-indices.test.ts (every fiscal bloc's debt path stays bounded — stale positional indices explode it) and data/meta-column-indices.test.ts (every fiscal_meta/external_meta index points at the right variable family; external_meta.idx equals its recorded idxIds). The data pack itself is checked by pack-verify --full in every build (above).

docs.title: Feature suites
docs.text: Test file Capability taylor-rule.test.ts The 9 Taylor-rule variants (taylor-rule.ts). barnichon-mesters.test.ts The Barnichon-Mesters optimal-policy optimizer. kalman.test.ts State-space build, Kalman filter/smoother, conditionalForecast (DK smoother). conditional-forecast.test.ts Conditional forecasting on real sample data. dynamic-conditioning.test.ts Any variable can be conditioned (general dynamic conditioning). linear-combo-conditioning.test.ts Conditioning on a linear combination (e.g. primary balance = revenue − primary expenditure) inside the smoother, without a separate BVAR variable. chart-data.test.ts Chart-data generation for all 8 display panels. fiscalAccounting.test.ts The fiscal debt recursion and exact stock-flow-adjustment (SFA) residual (fiscalAccounting.ts). fiscal-conditioning-integration.test.ts Conditioning on a debt/GDP trajectory: the engine inverts the recursion to the required primary balance and pins it via a linear constraint. gvar-globals.test.ts The 4 GVAR global commons (GLB_OIL/GLB_USLR/GLB_USBAA/GLB_USEQ) — US determines them as its own variables. gvar-derived-topology.test.ts Self-configuring bloc topology (ROW_COUNTRIES / IDX / W) DERIVED from deployed spec.json + weights_24bloc.json, not hardcoded. gvar-us-endogenous.test.ts The US-as-coupled-bloc solver generalization (its ROW*_US stars + US weights row). gvar-band-solve.test.ts Per-draw GVAR scenario band solve. gvar-ui-linkage.test.ts Wiring of the cross-country engine into the UI (buildScenarioPins, deviation → pinned LEVEL matrices). gvar-closed-form-routing.test.ts The production solve path: runGVARSolve routed through solveGVARClosedForm (assemble each bloc's affine RoW response once, build M, solve x = (I−M)⁻¹ d) + coupling-cache correctness. (heavy) gvar-direct-channel.test.ts The US-endogenous direct preview channel on a bloc subset. (heavy) driftSetter-joint-solve.test.ts The δc-drift long-run-target anchor (driftSetter.ts computeDriftDeltaFull), per-variable + joint solve. chartgrid-render-memo.test.ts The Phase-2 render memoization (reconcileCharts + chartDeepEqual + React.memo(DraggableChart)): one conditioning edit rebuilds ≈1 of ~35 panels, not all of them (asserts via chartRebuildCounter/draggableChartRenderCounter). conditioned-dot-optimistic.test.ts The optimistic conditioned-point dot (conditionedDotDisplayY ∘ conditioningDeviationFromDisplayY = identity) — the marker round-trips to the clicked display value for every variable type. right-click-plant-at-cursor.test.ts Right-click on a forecast chart plants the bullet at the cursor (same display→stored mapping as drag). gvar-drag-scheduling.test.ts The drag-perf boundary: no GVAR mean solve fires while a drag is in progress; exactly one direct solve fires on pointer-up (via the gvarDragState bus + the 100 ms release macrotask). gvar-drag-line-band.test.ts While dragging a GVAR bloc, its line falls back to the cheap single-country condForecast and flips back to the propagated GVAR path on release.

docs.title: Regression suites
docs.text:
Test file Bug it pins conditioning-wysiwyg.test.ts A directly-conditioned variable must display exactly the dragged path (WYSIWYG), including sparse/partial per-quarter conditioning — the scaling-differencing fix must apply only to RESPONSE vars. counterfactual-irf.test.ts A counterfactual recovers the impulse response function (IRF) when the rate adjustment equals the IRF. counterfactual-recovers-scenario.test.ts A counterfactual with a vanishing policy adjustment must recover the scenario (policy effect measured against the right baseline). fiscal-backcast.test.ts The budget-identity recursion in fiscalAccounting.ts reproduces the observed US federal debt/GDP back-cast from observed drivers (Step-1 gating). matrix.test.ts Core linear algebra (Cholesky/solve/inverse, ~1e-15 singularity threshold) in matrix.ts. affine-blockernels-parity.test.ts The affineBlocKernels perf path reproduces the old full filter+smoother probe loop to <1e-9 (baseline mean Sc and every per-period kernel) and is >=3× faster, on the real US-endogenous bloc — the optimization must stay a numerical no-op. (heavy) gvar-kernel-affine-independence.test.ts The affine-independence claim underlying the per-bloc kernel cache-key change (RANK-1 gate). (heavy) fiscal-meta-indices.test.ts Pins the STALE-POSITIONAL-INDEX bug (§ below): re-resolves every fiscal bloc's fiscal_meta.json indices by variable id from the deployed spec.json and asserts each bloc's derived debt path stays bounded — the regression that caught EA's effRate landing on the equity index (col ~537) so debt/GDP exploded. Also pins the level-display drag conversion (oil → $100 must not over-shoot to ~$190).

The perf-fix parity suites (affine-blockernels-parity, gvar-kernel-affine-independence) are regression gates in spirit — they prove an optimization is numerically a no-op — but because they protect the production GVAR solve path, treat a red result there with the same severity as a canary.

The STALE-POSITIONAL-INDEX gotcha (porter must regen). fiscal_meta.json stores the fiscal-driver column indices positionally, but the porter (pipeline/port_gvar_exports.py) does not regenerate them. Any variable-order change (the 33-bloc GVAR-EM refit inserted vars ahead of the fiscal block in every spec except US) silently re-points the indices at the wrong columns — the cause of the recent EA/UK/CA/JP/CN debt explosion. The fix is to run node pipeline/fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs (re-resolves the six indices by variable id from the deployed spec.json, preserves d0/sfaDefault, idempotent) after porting and before the gate; fiscal-meta-indices.test.ts is the canary-grade guard that blocks a deploy with stale indices. See REESTIMATING_MODELS.md and the DATA_SCHEMA fiscal-meta section.

The file list above is enumerated from app/src/__tests__/compute/. When you add a test, slot it into the right row here and confirm it actually runs under vitest run.

docs.title: Drivers licence suites (the experimental DSGE decomposition)
docs.text:
The Drivers panel reads a scenario path through a chosen DSGE model and reports which sequence of that model's structural shocks reproduces it. The claim is model-conditional and its validation is same-model recovery, so what the suites below guard is not a user-facing capability but a licence: the configurations in which the shipped estimator is allowed to present a result, and the provenance of the data it reads. Three files carry them, 26 tests in total, and none of them is in the --exclude list — they all run under npm test.

Test file Tests Guards drivers-decomp.test.ts 4 The engine mirrors pipeline/bench_simple_decomp.m: exact same-model recovery on the identified fixtures, the budget rule (naming more shocks than observables watched throws), and the measured unit conversions (inflationq/pinfobs = interest/robs = 4.000). drivers-decomp-v2.test.ts 7 Display-unit additivity (contributions + residual reproduce the scenario line to 1e-8), the CMR14 extended-observable unit mapping, and the FRB/US cluster licence. drivers-decomp-v3.test.ts 15 The column-normalised solver, class aggregation at the licensed configuration, the three-coordinate class-view predicate, the FRB/US cluster partition and its validated default naming, shipped-payload provenance (sha256 of every shipped file, class_maps.json embedded verbatim, index horizon = engine horizon), the BVAR-panel-to-observable seam, and the rank arithmetic behind the excluded duplicate observables.

Remark 1 (These are artifact gates, not unit tests). Each file reads the shipped payload off disk — app/public/data/dsge/census/index.json, the census copies, and the US_SW07/US_CMR14 files in the IRF tree — rather than a fixture. Test v3-5 hashes every shipped file and compares against the sha256 the index records for it, so a payload regenerated without rebuilding the index, or an index committed without its files, turns red. Treat that the way you treat gvar-coupling-artifact: it is telling you the shipped data and the shipped metadata have come apart. The suite therefore also does real I/O, including the 10.75 MB US_FRB22.json that the cluster tests load.

Remark 2 (Do not widen a licence constant to make a test pass). Test v3-3 asserts the class-view observable set and shock set against the literal bench coordinates, not against the constants the app exports, and it carries a negative case for each of the seven droppable shocks. Widening either constant to admit a configuration the bench never ran is exactly what the test exists to catch. The correct response to a red licence test is to narrow what the interface offers; see MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md §H4.

docs.title: Deploy chain
docs.text:
The source repo is matyasfarkas/BVAR-Policy-Calibration-Tool (the origin remote). There are two deploy targets, built from the same commit of main — push it to both:

Remote Repo Builds Serves bvarscenario matyasfarkas/BVARScenarioTool GitHub Action deploy-to-website.yml (below) matyasfarkas.github.io/bvar-scenario (GitHub Pages, via starter-hugo-academic) gmapsmodel gmapsmodel/GMAPS Netlify, per netlify.toml (below) gmapsmodel.com (domain root)

Both deploys run npm ci && npm run build, so both run prebuild (pack-verify --full); neither runs the tests. The desktop installer is a third, local build (below).

The GitHub Pages chain: the bvarscenario Action builds the export and republishes it into the matyasfarkas/starter-hugo-academic website repo, a Hugo Academic site published to GitHub Pages. This workflow contains no Hugo step: it only copies app/out/* into the website repo, and the Hugo build downstream then rebuilds and serves it.

push -> bvarscenario main
   │   (paths: app/** or netlify.toml)
   ▼
.github/workflows/deploy-to-website.yml   (runner: ubuntu-latest, Node 22)
   │  npm ci
   │  BASE_PATH=/bvar-scenario npm run build      → app/out/
   │  checkout matyasfarkas/starter-hugo-academic
   │  rm -rf website/static/bvar-scenario/*
   │  cp -r app/out/* website/static/bvar-scenario/
   │  commit + push to the website repo
   ▼
Hugo rebuilds the Hugo Academic site from the website repo
   ▼
served at the /bvar-scenario path of the academic site (GitHub Pages)

Workflow facts, verified against .github/workflows/deploy-to-website.yml:

  • Triggers: push to main with changed paths under app/** or netlify.toml, plus manual workflow_dispatch.
  • Runner / toolchain: ubuntu-latest, actions/setup-node@v4 with node-version: 22 and npm cache keyed on app/package-lock.json.
  • Build step runs in working-directory: app: npm ci then npm run build, with BASE_PATH: /bvar-scenario in the environment.
  • Publish step checks out matyasfarkas/starter-hugo-academic (via secrets.WEBSITE_DEPLOY_TOKEN), clears website/static/bvar-scenario/, copies app/out/* in, and commits/pushes (a no-op git diff --cached --quiet short-circuits when nothing changed).

The Hugo build that assembles the final academic site is not in this workflow file — it runs as part of the website repo's downstream build that publishes to GitHub Pages, and any Hugo version pin lives in the starter-hugo-academic repo, not here (see below).

docs.title: gmapsmodel.com (Netlify)
docs.text:
netlify.toml (repo root): base = "app", command = "npm ci && npm run build", publish = "out", NODE_VERSION = "22", and DOCS_URL pointing the Docs button at the hosted MkDocs site (this host serves the app at the domain root, with no sibling /docs/). No BASE_PATH is set, so the app is built for the root.

The ignore rule skips a push that changes neither app/ nor netlify.toml (to save metered build minutes):

ignore = "git diff --quiet $CACHED_COMMIT_REF $COMMIT_REF -- :/app :/netlify.toml"

Netlify runs this command inside the base directory (app/), so the paths must be repo-root pathspecs (:/…). The first version (git diff --quiet HEAD^ HEAD -- app netlify.toml, added 2026-08-05) matched nothing from app/, always exited 0, and cancelled every build — manual "Trigger deploy" included — until it was fixed in 298dfd8d (2026-10-08). $CACHED_COMMIT_REF (the last commit Netlify built) also covers a merge whose first parent already had the changes, which HEAD^ missed. After every push, check the site really changed: curl https://gmapsmodel.com/data/manifest.json should show the new packId.

docs.title: The desktop installer (Tauri)
docs.text: Built locally, not in CI: npm run build:tauri (= next build with TAURI_BUILD=1 and an empty BASE_PATH, then prune-redundant-json.mjs desktop), then npx tauri build (Windows cross-build steps in app/src-tauri/README.md). build:tauri has no prebuild, so run npm run data:verify (verify_cutoffs + pack-verify --full) first. The installer carries the data pack that was in the tree as its built-in pack; record it with npm run pack:record-release -- --version <x.y.z> so later update packs can be cut against it. Full steps: UPDATE_MANUAL.md §8.

docs.title: BASE_PATH
docs.text:
The site is served from the /bvar-scenario sub-path of the academic site (GitHub Pages), so the static export must be built with that prefix. next.config.mjs:

const nextConfig = {
  output: 'export',
  basePath: process.env.BASE_PATH || '',
  assetPrefix: process.env.BASE_PATH || '',
  images: { unoptimized: true },
  env: { NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH: process.env.BASE_PATH || '' },
};
Build BASE_PATH Asset/link prefix Local dev / preview unset → '' root-relative (/…) Deploy (GitHub Action) /bvar-scenario /bvar-scenario/… Deploy (Netlify, gmapsmodel.com) unset → '' root-relative (/…) Desktop (build:tauri) '' root-relative

The GitHub Action always sets BASE_PATH=/bvar-scenario. Reproduce that deploy artifact locally with BASE_PATH=/bvar-scenario npm run build. Data files are fetched only through app/src/lib/data/dataManifest.ts, which builds its URLs from process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_PATH + /data.

docs.title: Hugo version pin (0.122.0)
docs.text: The website repo's build is pinned to Hugo 0.122.0. The pin is enforced in the website pipeline (.github/workflows/updater-wip.yml). Rationale: Hugo 0.123+ removed the getCSV / getCSS data helpers that the wowchemy (academic) theme depends on; later versions break the site build. Do not bump the pin without first migrating the theme off those removed helpers. (Documented in README.md and ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI.md.)

docs.title: The Drivers payload in the static export
docs.text:
next build copies app/public/ into app/out/ verbatim, so the DSGE impulse-response payload the Drivers panel reads ships with every deploy. The directory it added, app/public/data/dsge/census/, is 22.4 MB over nine files, and two of them are almost all of it: the FRB/US census lenses US_FRB22.json at 10.75 MB and US_FRB22_var.json at 10.57 MB, each carrying the responses of 54 shocks. The index and the six small census models come to 1.07 MB together. Regenerating the US_SW07 and US_CMR14 IRF files with their full native shock sets added a further 1.6 MB under app/public/data/dsge/irfs/. That was about 24 MB against an app/public/data/ tree of ~757 MB (Aug 2026), so nothing in the deploy chain has to change to carry it and no file comes near GitHub's 100 MB limit.

None of it is fetched eagerly. The drawer requests census/index.json (36 KB) the first time a user opens it, once per session, and the selected model's response file only when that model is selected, cached per model for the rest of the session. The default lens is US_SW07, whose 215 KB file is already in the IRF tree, so the ordinary path costs 251 KB. The two ~10.7 MB FRB/US files are downloaded only if the user picks an FRB/US lens — the drawer records a fetch failure per model and offers a retry, which is there because a file that size can fail on a slow link. Unlike companion_draws and the coupling artifact these files are not gzipped in the repo, and the loader that fetches them does no client-side decompression; whatever compression happens on the wire is the host's doing and is not configured here.

Remark 3 (The desktop prune does not touch them). npm run build:tauri runs scripts/prune-redundant-json.mjs desktop, which deletes a plain X.json from out/data/ only when a sibling X.json.gz exists. The census files have no .gz sibling, so the full 22.4 MB travels into the Tauri bundle. If the installer size becomes the binding constraint, the lever is to gzip the two FRB/US files at build time and give the Drivers loader the .gz path the coupling artifact already uses — a code change on both sides, not a build flag.

docs.title: What to commit (and what not to)
docs.text:
• Commit only deploy-relevant files (app/**, docs, config).
  • Commit app/public/data/ together with its manifest.json: every data change needs a re-stamp (pack-build.mjs --pack-id <new id>), or prebuild's pack-verify --full fails the deploy. Never re-use a pack id for different content.
  • The plain companion_draws.json files are local by-products (not in git, not in the pack); only the .gz is committed.
  • Leave pipeline/ scratch — diagnostics, staging dirs, raw CSVs, _verify/ — untracked.
  • Never commit app/.env.local or any FRED_API_KEY.
  • Commit app/public/data/dsge/census/index.json together with the payload files it hashes. The index records a sha256 per shipped file and drivers-decomp-v3.test.ts re-computes every one of them, so a half-staged payload is a red test rather than a silent mismatch.

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text:
# Full local green gate (run before every deploy):
cd app
npx tsc --noEmit
npm test                # fast suite (excludes the heavy solver canaries)
npm run test:heavy      # heavy solver / perf-parity canaries (1 fork)
BASE_PATH=/bvar-scenario npm run build   # prebuild runs pack-verify --full

# The data-pack checks on their own:
npm run data:verify                 # verify_cutoffs + pack-verify --full
npm run pack:build -- --pack-id <id> # re-stamp manifest.json after a data change (new id)

# Deploy = push the same commit to both remotes (only after the gate, with confirmation):
git push bvarscenario main && git push gmapsmodel main
curl -s https://gmapsmodel.com/data/manifest.json | head -c 300   # confirm Netlify really rebuilt

# Or sweep everything in one pass (slower, default parallelism):
npm run test:all        # = vitest run

# Run a single suite while iterating:
npx vitest run src/__tests__/compute/gvar-coupling-artifact.test.ts

# Regenerate the shipped coupling artifact (keeps the coupling canary green
# after a model refresh) — see REESTIMATING_MODELS.md:
npx vite-node scripts/precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs

# Run just the 26 Drivers licence tests while iterating on that feature:
npx vitest run src/__tests__/compute/drivers-decomp.test.ts \
              src/__tests__/compute/drivers-decomp-v2.test.ts \
              src/__tests__/compute/drivers-decomp-v3.test.ts

# Rebuild the shipped DSGE lens payload (needs pipeline/census_irfs/ from
# explore/shock-benchmark) — see PIPELINE.md §3.6 and MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md §H:
node scripts/build_drivers_index.mjs

If the gvar-coupling-artifact canary goes red after a model refresh, the artifact is stale: regenerate coupling_default.json.gz with the precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs script (full data-refresh runbook in REESTIMATING_MODELS.md). If a Drivers licence test goes red, the shipped payload and the index that hashes it have come apart, or a licence constant has been widened past what the benches ran — regenerate the payload, or narrow the interface; never widen the constant (§H4 of MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md).

docs.title: CHANGELOG
docs.text: The detailed changelog. The repository root CHANGELOG.md carries the same releases as short release notes. Since 4.0.0, a model or data update ships as a data pack and is listed by its pack id; app versions are listed by version number.

docs.title: [Unreleased — web] - 2026-10-08 — DATA FILES THAT FAIL A CHECK ARE SHOWN ON SCREEN
docs.text:
A damaged or missing data file is now named on screen, and nothing that depends on it is shown. Until now, a file that failed its size or SHA-256 check after start-up was refused, but the message went only to the browser console: - the global model quietly left that economy out of the coupled solve; - a failing trade-weights file was replaced by the build-time copy; - a country that failed to load kept showing the previous country's charts under the new name.

Now: - a red banner at the bottom of the screen names each file that failed; - a country that fails to load shows an error panel instead of charts; - the global model refuses to load from a partial set of economies, or from fallback weights, and says so.

A file the data pack does not list is still treated as "not shipped" (for example an economy without a fiscal block); only a listed file that fails is an error. Web builds verify every file before publishing, so this concerns files damaged in transit or on a desktop disk. Tests: dataManifest-errors, gvarLoader-strict, loadBVARData-country; checked in a browser with a deliberately damaged file. Web only so far; not in a desktop installer.

docs.title: [Data pack 2026Q2-reest-20261008b] - 2026-10-08 — GENUINE-DATA RE-ESTIMATION, DATA TO 2026Q2 (web; app 4.0.0)
docs.text:
Every economy rebuilt from published data, the whole model re-estimated with no filled values, data through 2026Q2. This is the first model update delivered as a data pack under 4.0's separation of data and model from the app. Review record: docs/reest-2026/REVIEW.md (old-vs-new tables in COMPARISON.md, decisions in PLAN.md).

  • Data. All 52 economies were rebuilt from their published sources. Each economy now has a machine-readable source registry (pipeline/sources/registry/). No fills of any kind: an unpublished quarter stays missing and the model draws it, like the COVID quarters. Thirteen source decisions (PLAN.md §5), among them:
  • genuine 3-month market rates for ID, MY, TH, ZA, TR and the UK (some were copies of the policy rate);
  • one effective-exchange-rate convention everywhere (rise = appreciation): the BIS broad index for 30 economies, the IMF index for AU, CL, CR and NZ, Eurostat for the 17 euro members;
  • Costa Rica's GDP and trade from the OECD quarterly accounts;
  • India on its new base from 2004Q2;
  • Japan's overnight call rate;
  • a GDP deflator for every fiscal economy.

New Zealand's CPI and exchange rate had been Chile's series. That is now fixed. - Model. The 35-economy global model was re-estimated to the latest published quarter, with the estimator's own fills removed. It converged (sweep 6); the previous run had stopped after 12 sweeps without converging. Two estimator defects were fixed on the way: - the random draws depended on which parallel worker ran a country; - a tiny input change could flip the sampler onto a different path.

Both made successive sweeps impossible to compare. Coupling strength ρ(M) is 0.9719 (was 0.9577; it must stay below 1). The 17 euro members were re-estimated in growth rates with seasonal dummies for all 17; they had run an older level-form model. - What changes on screen. - Every economy has data to 2026Q2. - Fewer first-year forecasts jump away from the latest data. Economies with a jump above 3 pp: GDP 12 (was 14), inflation 5 (was 9). - US year-5 GDP growth is 3.8% (was 6.4%). - Values the model supplies are drawn amber as model estimates. These are the ragged edge and any missing interior quarter, such as US CPI and unemployment in 2025Q4, when BLS skipped October 2025. - Every exchange rate now reads "rise = appreciation". - Debt starting points come from the new sources: CA 100 → 111 (pension liabilities included), UK 96 → 103, NO 54 → 46, CN 94 → 101, JP 193 → 190 (% of GDP). They are rolled forward to 2026Q2 with the app's own budget identity. The published value and its quarter stay in the file. - Fixed during review. In 35 economies, the external block's exchange-rate column pointed at the wrong series after the deflator was added. It had no numerical effect, because that channel is switched off. Columns are now found by variable name, and a test guards them. - Decided by the user. Costa Rica's inflation anchor is accepted, with the anchor-overlay safety bound raised from 150 to 175. The forecast items below do not block the release. - Worth watching (raw model, before the app's long-run anchor): - China GDP drifts up to 9–12% growth. - Japan CPI is −0.6% in year 1. - Ireland and Luxembourg GDP are negative in year 1. - Euro-area inflation is 3.3% in year 1 and 4.5% in year 2. - BR, MY and CR have loose priors (short samples). - App code that went out with this pack (web only; not in the 4.0.0 desktop installer): - every effective exchange rate is shown as an index level; - interior model-estimated history quarters get amber marks, not only the nowcast tail. - gmapsmodel.com is live again. A build-skip rule added on 5 Aug 2026 had cancelled every Netlify build since then: Netlify runs it in the app/ folder, where its paths matched nothing. Fixed in 298dfd8d. The site went from the 5 August build straight to this release. - Checks. - Type check: clean. - pack-verify --full: 4,221 checks pass. - Test suite: 10 data-dependent failures, each updated or re-specified (REVIEW.md §8). - Headless browser on both live sites: all 52 economies load, dated "Data to 2026 Q2", with no page errors.

Open: the 4.0.0 desktop installer still carries data pack 2026Q1-20261006. No update pack has been cut for it. This pack also expects the two display changes above. Bringing desktop users to this release therefore needs a new installer (or an update pack plus a note that those two displays differ). Next data round: PLAN.md §10.

docs.title: [4.0.0] - 2026-10-05 — DATA AND MODEL SEPARATED FROM THE APP (IMF circulation)
docs.text:
Data and model updates no longer need a new app version, and the dates now come from the data.

  • Data packs. Everything the app shows lives in a data pack (app/public/data + manifest.json with every file's SHA-256 and size). The app verifies every file before use and refuses an incompatible or damaged pack with one clear full-screen message.
  • Desktop updates without reinstalling. Settings → Data pack → Open data folder: unzip an update pack there and press Reload. An update pack carries only the changed files (a quarterly data shift: about 3 MB zipped) and is accepted only if every file it reuses matches the app's built-in data. Rollback = remove manifest.json from that folder.
  • The data carry their own calendar. Each history file records its first quarter; the last quarter is always first quarter + rows − 1. There is no date setting to edit or forget.
  • Fixed: the one-quarter mis-dating since 22–23 Sep 2026. The September model updates replaced the data with exports ending 2025Q4, silently dropping the July 2026Q1 shift, while the date label stayed at 2026Q1. For 35 economies the charts were dated one quarter late, the 15 seasonal economies' quarterly pattern was applied one quarter off, and the published 2026Q1 data were missing. 4.0.0 ships the current model with the 2026Q1 shift re-applied (US observed, 161 published values pinned, the rest nowcast), every economy genuinely ending 2026Q1 and checked against FRED/Eurostat and the estimation panels.
  • Model updates re-apply the shift automatically. npm run data:model-update -- --then-shift dates fresh exports from the estimation panels, re-stamps and verifies the pack, and brings the panel to the latest published quarter. A calendar check against the estimation panels runs on every build.
  • Refresh scripts run unattended. npm run data:shift -- --asof <Q> --commit runs the whole chain, verifies it, and cuts update packs for every recorded app release. npm run data:auto is the cron entry point. Git commit and push stay human decisions.
  • Also fixed: a shift no longer re-publishes dropped economies (Argentina, Israel, Russia) from the staging folder; realized-data pins are dated per economy (euro members were compared one quarter off); "annual re-estimation due" now looks at the model's estimation end, not the panel; the vintage monitor labels a comparison "pure data shift" only when it is the same model.
  • Docs: docs/UPDATE_MANUAL.md, the complete guide for users and the maintainer.

Known and open (not changed in 4.0.0): the euro members still run the 19 Aug 2026 model generation; the US history keeps pre-revision values before 2025Q4 (the 2025Q4 growth point mixes vintages); the euro-area raw 5-year policy-rate forecast moved from 4.86% to 0.80% with the 2026Q1 data; US debt-target steering ends about 5 pp off target at the 5-year horizon.

Rollback — restore the 19 August 2026 model (pre-DVAX), retain the post-19-Aug fixes unrelated to the estimation.

At a co-author's request, this release rolls the estimated model back to exactly its 19 August 2026 state: the WS2 genuine 35-bloc model (US endogenous, foreign "star" coefficients shrunk toward zero, T=41 / 2026Q1 vintage, 500 stored draws). The difference-form DVAX foreign-demand prior of 3.3.0 and its 3.3.1 band refresh are reverted — the data under public/data/bvar is byte-identical to the 19 August production commit, and the coupling artifact is the matching 19 August one (its modelSig hydrates cleanly).

Kept (post-19-Aug code, unrelated to re-estimation): - the EA member -> area-aggregate spillover (a member's GDP and prices reach the area aggregate), - the world-panel reconstruction fix (scenario = baseline + shared-baseline delta), - the ragged-edge / trailing-NaN loader robustness, - the RU/AR/IL dropdown removal.

Tests: the heavy real-US-engine integration tests (fiscal-conditioning inversion, cookbook recipes on the full conditional-forecast solve) run 5-8s; vitest's 5000ms default flaked at that boundary on the slightly slower T=41 model, so the per-test timeout is raised to 20000ms — model-agnostic, no golden value changed. Full suite green.

Context (not a refutation of the rollback): an 11-agent econometric ablation comparing a no-recentering stars->0 model against the difference-form DVAX prior adjudicated the science as DVAX-justified — no-VA's foreign-demand -> GDP impact is wrong-signed in 7 GVC-integrated blocs (BR/CA/CN/HK/IN/JP/TW) while DVAX is positive in all 35, and the coupled solve is more contractive (dense-eig rho(M) 0.966 vs 0.978, both < 1). The reproducible MATLAB ablation harness ships under pipeline/ablation/.

The DVAX release — a units-consistent foreign-demand pass-through prior, a full 35-bloc re-estimation, a coherent euro area, and a world-panel reconstruction fix.

The country VARs used to shrink each foreign "star" coefficient toward zero, so a bloc carried no long-run tie to trade-weighted foreign demand — and the re-centred level model that tried to add one drifted (the foreign-demand star climbed without bound). This release replaces that with a difference-form DVAX prior on the foreign-demand star (ROWDEM → GDP only; inflation and the foreign-rate star keep the standard prior). The prior re-centres the pass-through onto each bloc's value-added export share μ_i (OECD–WTO TiVA), in units that check out: because ROWDEM is an annualized growth rate and domestic GDP carries the Minnesota random-walk prior (its equation is a quarterly first difference), the prior mean is +μ_i/4 on lag-1 and −μ_i/4 on lag-2 — a difference whose coefficients sum to zero, so the channel injects no permanent drift, only transitory co-movement. See the manual, §"Foreign-demand pass-through" and the Known-issues note.

  • Full 35-bloc re-estimation with the difference-form prior, US endogenous, lags=3. The coupled solve stays contractive: dense-eig ρ(M) = 0.966 (< 1). The US credit-spread global solve reproduces the paper's ballpark (US −2.43, EA −1.82, JP −3.44, World −1.85 pp growth troughs).
  • Coherent euro area: all 17 euro-member blocs re-estimated so the area aggregate and its members are consistent; member→EA feedback (a member's GDP/prices reach the aggregate) verified.
  • World-panel reconstruction fix: the World GDP/inflation read-outs drew the baseline line from the shipped panel but the scenario line from the solver's recomputed baseline; for a few explosive-companion blocs those diverge, so a null scenario spuriously "jumped." The scenario is now built as baseline + Σ ω·(growth of the solver delta), sharing one baseline — a null scenario returns exactly the baseline. (Model-agnostic; fixes the deployed app too.)
  • Docs & housekeeping: manual updated (difference-form prior + explosive-baseline known issue), MkDocs track merged, stale MFFM_* LaTeX artifacts removed, human-operations instructions refreshed.
  • Shipped in two steps: this build carries the 200-draw core (validated); a 1000-draw band refresh follows. Two tests are skipped with TODO(dvax-1000) — the JP spread-scale golden value (re-verify vs DVAX-MATLAB) and the CN external-satellite CA anchor (re-anchor external_meta to the DVAX baseline) — both genuine re-estimation consequences in secondary features, documented not bumped.

The experimental Drivers panel — a scenario path read through one DSGE model as the mix of that model's own structural shocks — with the class view licensed at exactly one configuration, the two FRB/US census lenses and their 54 shocks apiece (52 of them equation residuals) grouped into empirical collinearity clusters, and a regeneration of the SW07 and CMR14 IRF files with their full native shock sets. Branch deploy/drivers-v3 — the feature commit 47357e4d is what the two live sites were serving when this entry was written, and the licence-disclosure corrections b6ea3c25 (below, under Fixed) sit at the branch head and go out with the next publication.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Drivers panel (EXPERIMENTAL, model-conditional) — app/src/components/controls/DriversDrawer.tsx (UI) and app/src/lib/compute/driversDecomp.ts (engine). The drawer takes the scenario path the app is currently showing — or an imported external-forecast combination — and asks a chosen DSGE model from the Macroeconomic Model Base which sequence of that model's own structural shocks would have produced it over the first H = 12 forecast quarters. It draws the answer as a stacked contribution chart in the same units as the main panel, with an explicit grey residual for the part the named shocks cannot reproduce. The object solved is the deconvolution z_o(t) = Σ_k Σ_{τ≤t} R_{k,o}(t−τ)·ε_k(τ) + u_o(t), where z is the scenario's level deviation from baseline mapped into the model's observable space, R_{k,o}(h) is observable o's impulse response to shock k at horizon h, and u is the residual; stacking gives a (q·H) × (K·H) response matrix Θ over q watched observables and K named shocks, each (o,k) block lower-triangular Toeplitz. The claim is model-conditional: it says what mix of model M's shocks reproduces the displayed path, not what caused it, and it is not model-free shock labelling. Its validation is same-model recovery — generate a path from a model's own known shock sequence, decompose it under that same model, compare the recovered contribution paths — so the numbers speak to the estimator, not to the model and not to the world. A "Drivers" button with an amber exp badge appears in the scenario-action cluster once any displayed, isolated or coupled deviation (or an active external combination) exceeds 1e-9; the drawer does not solve while closed.
  • The estimator: a column-normalised min-norm least-squares deconvolution. Every column of Θ is rescaled to unit response energy before the solve (columns below 1e-12 keep a scale of 1 so they stay inert), the row weights w = 1/√(1+me) of any added observable are applied to both Θ and z, and the ridge normal equations at λ = 1e-8 · mean(diag ΘᵀΘ) are LU-factored once and then refined by two iterative sweeps against that same factorisation, so the iterate stays in range(Θᵀ) and converges to the minimum-norm least-squares solution. The normalisation is an equal-response-energy prior across shocks: SW07's stacked three-observable H = 12 response norms run from 1.28 (interest_) to 13.84 (epinf), roughly an order of magnitude apart, so the raw solver prices the small-response monetary shock out of its own attribution. In identified configurations the rescaling is a pure reparameterisation (the licence fixtures still recover to ≤ 1e-6); underdetermined, it removes the bias — at three observables SW07's mean off-class leakage falls 32% → 5%. Contributions are computed back through the raw Θ and the un-normalised shocks, so neither the column scaling nor the row weights touch the reported bars. Every observable maps into the main panel's display space through a linear operator (a gain or a scaled first difference), so bars, residual and baseline reproduce the scenario line to 1e-8. The engine reports exact-fit when rank(Θ) ≥ q·H and residual-able otherwise; in the exact-fit regime the residual is identically zero by construction and only becomes a test once observables are added.
  • The two rules the validation bench licenses, enforced in the engine and in the UI. First, the budget rule: at q watched observables at most q shocks may be named. decompose throws on K > q and the drawer disables every un-named chip at the budget. The budget is 3 + addedObs on the US bloc, where SW07's and CMR14's native columns are available, and 3 everywhere else. Observables that are invertible linear transforms of one already watched (SW07 dy, pinfobs, robs; CMR14 gdp_obs, inflation_obs, Re_obs) are excluded from the addable list, because adding one would raise the budget while buying no new rank and the identification the rule promises would be fictitious — pinned against the data, not a curated list, by a test requiring each of the four legitimate SW07 addables to buy exactly H = 12 new rank and each excluded transform to buy exactly zero, alone and together. Second, the collinearity flag: shock pairs whose unit-normalised stacked three-observable H = 12 response paths satisfy |cos| > 0.95 are precomputed at build time and warned on whenever both members are named, with the measured |cos| quoted. The split within such a pair is not identified and must be read jointly; the one-click "Use all" selection is greedy in the model's own shock order and skips any shock collinear with one already picked.
  • The class view, licensed at exactly one configuration on three coordinates. classViewLicensed(model, observableKeys, namedShocks) returns true only for US_SW07, with all seven observables watched (output, inflationq, interest, dc, dinve, dw, labobs) and all seven of its class-map shocks named (interest_, eb, fiscal_, eqs, ea, epinf, ew). That is the single cell of pipeline/bench_class_recovery.m that passes both pre-stated criteria under the shipped solver — recovered class totals correlating ≥ 0.95 with the truth in ≥ 90% of active-class instances over 20 seeds, and mean off-class leakage ≤ 25% — and it passes them with a perfect diagonal (Monetary / Demand / Supply each 100%, 0% leakage). The bench held all three coordinates fixed, so the predicate gates on all three: un-naming a single shock revokes the class view, since that shock's energy is redistributed over the classes that remain, which is precisely what the leakage criterion measures. Everywhere else the Classes toggle is greyed with its reason and the view falls back to Groups — the models' own shock names. The licence says the estimator recovers class totals when the truth is generated by that same model at that configuration; it says nothing about whether SW07's classes are the right classes, and nothing about the world.
  • The FRB/US census lenses (US_FRB22, US_FRB22_var), each with its 54 native shocks grouped into empirical collinearity clusters. Both lenses carry interest_, fiscal_ and 52 _aerr equation-residual shocks, none dropped, and their individual columns are not separable in the three common observables: 109 of the 1,431 shock pairs exceed |cos| = 0.95 for US_FRB22 and 117 for the VAR-expectations variant. The drawer therefore groups by the structure the response space actually has: connected components of the |cos| > 0.95 graph (23 clusters for US_FRB22, 21 for US_FRB22_var), each labelled by its largest member's equation. Collinearity is not transitive, so members are chained through collinear links rather than mutually parallel — the composite column is the genuine first principal component of the member set, not a proxy for an already-parallel bundle, and the budget counts clusters, not members. The class view is refused for FRB/US by the bench at the only observable set it can run at (three observables; both solvers fail both criteria), and there is no seven-observable FRB/US configuration, since the native mapping exists only for SW07 and CMR14. What backs each lens is a build-time scan instead: every possible cluster triple is run through the shipped solver over 20 sparse-truth seeds against a 1e-6 recovery criterion, and the shipped default is picked deterministically among the passers — 123 of 1,771 triples pass for US_FRB22 (default [hqlfpr, interest_, pcer_l], worst error 2.53e-9, covering 19 of 54 shocks) and 122 of 1,330 for US_FRB22_var (default [eco_l, interest_, ki_l], worst error 1.32e-7, covering 12 of 54). A full-rank Θ is not evidence that a triple is usable — most are badly conditioned while passing the rank test — so the drawer warns whenever the user leaves the validated default naming. Under Customize → "Experimental: raw shocks" individual _aerr shocks can be decomposed instead of clusters (the greedy non-collinear list is 26 of 54 for US_FRB22), still subject to the budget.
  • The census IRF payload — app/public/data/dsge/census/. A 36 KB index.json (schema: "gmaps-drivers-index/1") carrying the model menu, each entry's usable and dropped shocks, its collinear pairs, its clusters and default naming where applicable, the shock-class maps copied verbatim from pipeline/_shockbench/class_maps.json, and a sha256 per file; plus eight census IRF files (CA_LS07 47 KB, BRA_SAMBA08 123 KB, EA_SW03 200 KB, EA_SWW14 217 KB, HK_FP13 218 KB, UK_SM11 231 KB, and the two ~10.7 MB FRB/US lenses). Four further models are indexed rather than copied, from the existing irfs tree: US_SW07, US_CMR14, US_FRB08 and the menu-hidden US_FRB22_mcap. index.json is fetched once per session on the first drawer open and each model's IRF file once on selection, both cached in component state with a per-model retry on failure, so the default lens costs 36 KB + 215 KB and either 54-shock FRB/US lens a further ~10.7 MB. Regenerated by node app/scripts/build_drivers_index.mjs, which refuses to ship a census file whose sha256 does not match pipeline/census_irfs/MANIFEST.json.
  • The validation record travels with the code — pipeline/bench_simple_decomp.m and pipeline/bench_class_recovery.m (both print to stdout; the committed docs/paper/simple_decomp_results.txt and docs/paper/class_recovery_results.txt are captured transcripts) and pipeline/_shockbench/class_maps.json. bench_simple_decomp.m established the budget and collinearity rules on eight models — US_SW07, US_CMR14, EA_SW03, EA_SWW14, CA_LS07, HK_FP13, BRA_SAMBA08, UK_SM11 — with SW07 at its native seven observables and all seven usable shocks fully identified (rank 84/84, noiseless recovery 3.6e-15, 100% at 1% noise). Note that pipeline/census_irfs/ is not on this branch, so neither bench re-runs here in full: only two of bench_simple_decomp.m's eight rows and four of bench_class_recovery.m's five model rows have their inputs on the branch.
  • 26 licence tests (app/src/__tests__/compute/drivers-decomp.test.ts 4, -v2.test.ts 7, -v3.test.ts 15), run in the fast npm test gate. They assert the class licence against literal bench coordinates rather than against the shipped constants, with a negative case for each of the seven droppable shocks, so widening either constant turns the test red; check index.shockClasses against class_maps.json verbatim and every shipped sha256 against the bytes, turning the hand-run builder's checks into CI gates; pin the BVAR-panel → model-observable mapping with hand-computed expectations; and require each addable observable to buy exactly H rank while each excluded duplicate buys none.
  • docs/drivers-decomposition.md — the methodology write-up (mkdocs nav → Methodology), with the user-facing walkthrough added to USER_GUIDE.md and the manual.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The SW07 and CMR14 IRF files are regenerated with their full native shock sets — app/public/data/dsge/irfs/US_SW07/SW.json (215 KB) and .../US_CMR14/SW.json (1.79 MB) — which is what makes the seven-observable mode possible on the US bloc. The interest_ and fiscal_ columns the existing policy-counterfactual feature reads are unchanged to ≈5e-11 (re-export rounding only), so the monetary and fiscal counterfactual paths are unaffected.
  • The unit conventions of the two native mappings are measured from the shipped files, not assumed, and regression-pinned. On the BVAR side the three common observables are built as GDP's 100·log level deviation (identity), 4·Δ of the price-level deviation, and the policy-rate deviation with no division by 4; the SW07 natives (dc, dinve, dw, labobs) all carry factor 1. For CMR14 the anchor is gdp_obs = Δ(output) to 1e-6, which fixes gdp_obs in percent quarterly log growth; consumption_obs, investment_obs and wage_obs each carry exactly the same 1.0 trend loading, which fixes them in the same units, and hours_obs = 0.01·lhours matches output = 0.01·ly exactly, which fixes it as a percent level deviation. wage_obs is the real wage. CMR14's financial observables (credit_obs, networth_obs, premium_obs, Spread1_obs, pinvest_obs, RealRe_obs) are not mapped in this pass; there are no financial observables in the feature.
  • The seven-observable mode exists only on the US bloc. It needs the spec columns CH, FNH, LXBC, JGDP and LANAGRA, and only the US bloc has all five. Every other bloc runs at three observables, with a budget of 3 and no configuration in the menu that licenses a class view.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
Six adversarial review lenses over the published feature found the linear algebra clean — the TypeScript engine reproduces the benches' committed fixtures to machine precision, and every unit factor re-measures exactly from the shipped files — and the disclosure layer around it wrong in five places, plus a handful of robustness gaps. What ships at the branch head:

  • The class-view predicate gates on the named shocks too. It previously gated on model and observables only, so un-naming a shock under Customize kept the licensed Monetary/Demand/Supply labels and the "100% recovery, 0% leakage" tooltip on a split the bench never ran. The named set is now a required third argument, so a caller that forgets it gets a type error. The same hole was reachable with no deliberate action: the budget clamp fires whether or not the drawer is open, so a bloc round-trip (a bloc without the native columns drops the budget 7 → 3) truncated the named set and left it truncated, and the unchanged hydration signature meant re-opening skipped re-hydration. Hydration is no longer gated on open.
  • The bottom caveat's validation citation is per-model. It used to cite bench_simple_decomp.m for every menu entry, including four FRB/US lenses that bench never ran. It now names that bench only for the eight models it actually ran, and for the rest states what does back them — a build-time check that the shipped default naming recovers a known shock sequence to 1e-6, with other namings unvalidated. (Gap worth recording: that fallback sentence is also shown for US_FRB08, but the build-time scan runs only for the models the index builder flags as clustered — the two FRB/US census lenses — so no such check exists for US_FRB08. No document should assert one.)
  • CMR14's "families" are disclosed as what they are. They are that model's own class map used as an organising grouping of its own shocks, and the drawer now states the number the bench refused them on, verbatim: bench_class_recovery.m recovers those class totals in 78% of test instances against its 90% bar (off-class leakage 3%). They are not a licensed class split.
  • Clusters are described correctly. They were called "near-parallel by construction (|cos| > 0.95)"; they are connected components of that graph, and collinearity is not transitive, so members are chained rather than mutually parallel. Reworded in the chip tooltip, the cluster footnote and the bottom caveat.
  • The model picker no longer calls every lens "equally valid." Validation status differs by orders of magnitude across the menu, so each entry now states its own; and because a full-rank Θ is not evidence a cluster triple is usable, leaving the validated default naming warns.
  • An IRF fetch failure is recorded and retryable. It was swallowed, latching the drawer into a permanent "Loading …" with no error and no retry — worst on the two ~10.7 MB FRB/US files.
  • The measurement-error slider says it is inert at budget-max. At K = q the stacked system is square, so scaling both Θ and z by a positive diagonal row weighting leaves the solution identical. The slider is disabled there and says so, rather than inviting a drag that does nothing.
  • Smaller disclosure fixes: the external-source option distinguishes "switched off" from "none imported"; the sticky "Path: Global" override discloses itself outside the collapsed Customize fold; and a closed drawer no longer re-solves an 84×84 system on every drag frame.

docs.title: Not established
docs.text: The feature is badged experimental in the UI and should be treated as experimental in every document that cites it. Its claim is model-conditional throughout: a different lens gives a different mix, and the lenses are not equally validated. The validation is same-model recovery, which measures the estimator rather than the model or the world. In the exact-fit regime the residual is zero by construction and is not evidence that the named shocks explain the path. The shares strip below the chart is a norm share of contribution paths, not a variance decomposition, so it always sums to 100 and can never show two contributions offsetting each other. FRB/US clusters are empirical, not economic. And the chart's "Deviation from baseline" view always draws the panel's rate deviation, while the main panels' "% vs base" mode defaults to a level sub-mode, so the auto-follow can put the two in different units; the axis title states which.

docs.title: Corrected after the first release build (2026-08-05)
docs.text:
Two observable mappings were measured wrong against the harmonised observable dictionary of the MMB real-time forecasting platform (Binder, Farkas, Taylor, Sun, Wieland and Wolters 2022), which records the exact source construction of every model observable and ships those observables as numbers — making a mapping testable rather than arguable. Against a revision floor of 0.099 pp per quarter:

  • dc was Δ(CH), correlation 0.837. CH is chain-weighted real consumption on its own deflator; the model observable is nominal consumption on the GDP deflator. Corrected to Δ(CH + JC − JGDP) — correlation 0.982, and exact same-vintage.
  • dinve was Δ(FNH), correlation 0.881 — nonresidential investment only, where the model observable is total private fixed investment. Corrected to a share-weighted combination of FRH and FNH at the measured residential share 0.2384; correlation 0.984. The exact level sum is non-linear and would break contribution additivity, so the shipped row is its first-order expansion, costing rmse 0.048 pp per quarter.
  • The correction initially reached the solver but not the chart: bars decomposed the corrected series while the baseline was drawn from the old one, off by 46% of investment's own standard deviation and invisible because the bars still summed correctly. Display specs now carry the full column combination.

Four disclosure corrections: a stated error figure that was half the measured one; "validated by bench_simple_decomp.m" asserted for eight models where that bench's criteria gate one; CMR14 shipping two uncorrected rows with no disclosure because the tooltip looked up SW07's table for every model; and CMR14's family note quoting its most favourable cell in configurations where the governing numbers fail both criteria. Non-finite input now fails loudly rather than silently emptying the chart.

labobs remains an employment proxy for hours per capita, now measured in the space the panel works in — median correlation 0.906 over 12-quarter deviations, not the 0.699 a historical decomposition suggests, because the missing population trend cancels in a deviation. A fitted satellite bridge that would have improved it was tested and rejected: three of five coefficients flip sign across subsamples and out-of-sample R² falls to 0.305.

docs.title: Deploy and hosting
docs.text:
• The static export no longer ships plain JSON where a gzip sibling exists — the loader prefers the .gz and no current browser lacks DecompressionStream. 766 MB → 404 MB.
  • Netlify no longer rebuilds for pushes that change nothing it serves (12 of the previous 44 pushes).
  • The Docs button 404'd on gmapsmodel.com: the documentation URL was hardcoded to a path only the GitHub Pages host has. Each deploy target now names its own.
  • mkdocs build --strict passes for the first time; a dangling link in index.md had been aborting it on pristine HEAD.

docs.title: [3.0.0] - 2026-07-18 — V3 RELEASE
docs.text:
The seasonal-v2 / FSAP-expansion vintage goes LIVE. The previous production tool (V2) is preserved at branch archive/v2-live-2026-07. What V3 ships, relative to the live V2:

  • 38 coupled GVAR blocs (V2: 33) — Hong Kong SAR, Singapore, Romania, Peru and the Philippines join, closing the FSAP-jurisdiction coverage gap; 17 euro members unchanged (55 economies in total). Fresh 38-bloc weights (2021–23 average) + a time-varying estimation-weights capability (annual IMTS rows, GVAR_TV_WEIGHTS).
  • Seasonal treatment done right (full detail in 2.5.0 below): quarterly seasonal dummies for 16 NSA blocs estimated in the model but seasonally adjusted out of the forecast (annual-mean constant), and the eight coupon-lumpy fiscal blocs' interest bills evenly distributed before estimation — the near-Nyquist EFFI/SFA/CPI sawtooth is gone (e.g. CL EFFI forecast mean|Δ| 4.82 → 0.01; CN CPI ±7 → ±0.5).
  • Full 38-bloc re-estimation on genuine panels to 2025Q4 (two-stage fixed-companion E-step, no exact-DA polish; companion spectral radius 0.9892 < 1, contractive).
  • 2026Q1 rebase: 2026Q1 is the last historical quarter (US fully observed; 169 realized cells pinned from published releases; every unpublished cell completed through one coupled G-BVAR solve, flagged model-implied), and 2026Q2 is the nowcast — the first forecast quarter. Provenance in nowcast_provenance.json; release impact on /monitor.
  • Israel extended one cross-block row on its own calendar (2025Q1).

Seasonal-v2: even coupon distribution for the eight lumpy-interest fiscal blocs, deterministic quarterly seasonal dummies threaded through the GLP stack and the app, a two-stage (fixed-companion E-step + exact-DA polish) GVAR-EM estimation, the full 33-bloc re-estimation, a time-varying trade-weights capability, and the staged FSAP data-expansion pass. Branch effi-even-seasonal-dummies — not yet on main.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Even coupon distribution for the effective interest rate (EFFI) — pipeline/build_fiscal22_columns.py. Eight blocs whose interest payments follow an annual/semiannual coupon calendar (EVEN_INTEREST = {CL, CO, CR, ID, IL, MX, TR, ZA}, detected by a systematic within-year pattern — calendar-R² > 0.5 & CV > 0.25 on the raw interest flows, or near-perfect quarterly alternation) now have their coupon spread evenly BEFORE estimation. even_distribute_years() replaces the four quarterly interest payments inside each complete calendar year by their mean (annual total preserved exactly; the trailing partial year uses the trailing-4-quarter mean), so EFFI = 400·evened_interest_t / debt_{t−1} becomes the accrual borrowing cost. Primary expenditure keeps the RAW interest (te − intr = true non-interest spending) and SFA — the exact debt-identity residual — absorbs the genuine cash-vs-accrual timing (which is why these blocs also carry seasonal dummies). The debt identity still closes exactly (1e-14). The EFFI sawtooth is removed (mean |quarterly change| CL 4.82 → 0.11, MX 4.95 → 0.21, ZA 5.00 → 0.25) and the near-Nyquist companion root that drove it moves off −1 (ZA −0.973 → −0.634, MX −0.953 → −0.659, CL −0.965 → −0.588).
  • Deterministic quarterly seasonal dummies for NSA-seasonal series, threaded end-to-end through the GLP estimation stack and the app. Selected blocs get quarterly dummies D = [q==2, q==3, q==4] (Q1 base) entered in each equation as x = [1, D, y_{t−1}, …, y_{t−p}]; the estimated betahat therefore has the layout [constant; γ_Q2; γ_Q3; γ_Q4; B_1; …; B_p], i.e. k = 1 + nsr + n·lags rows with nsr = 3 ("seasonalRows"); legacy blocs (nsr = 0) are unchanged. The dummy coefficients carry a diffuse prior (variance Vc, like the intercept) and are zeroed in the sum-of-coefficients dummy columns.
  • Default coupled dummy blocs (GVAR_DUMMY_BLOCS, pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m): 16 — CL, CN, CO, CR, EA, ID, IL, IN, IS, JP, KR, MX, NO, TR, UK, ZA — selected by calendar-R² ≥ 0.40 & display-amplitude ≥ 2 on the panel scan (NSA HICP/CPI, unemployment, house prices, India GOV, UK/KR SFA) plus every even-interest bloc.
  • Euro members (EURO_DUMMY_MEMBERS, pipeline/export_bvar_euro_redesign.m): 6 — ES, IT, GR, PT, SI, BE.
  • Estimator plumbing: BVAR/MFBVAR/Support/BVAR.m (optional D arg), BVAR/MFBVAR/GLPreplicationWeb/logMLMFVAR.m (D arg), BVAR/MFBVAR/cgl_bvarV5.m ('qoy' quarter-of-year vararg → D; the DK simulation-smoother artificial path carries the seasonal term so the smoother stays exact, and the seasonal forecast simulation continues the quarter-of-year cycle). export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m ships spec.json + companion_mean.json with seasonalRows and, for seasonal blocs, qoyNext.
  • App: app/src/lib/compute/kalman.ts — BVARParams gains {seasonalRows?, qoyNext?}; buildStateSpace reads the lag rows at row 1 + nsr and precomputes c2ByQ (four quarter-specific transition constants), and c2AtStep(ss, t) picks the constant for forecast step t. Every betahat consumer is wired through. Phase rule: the app ALWAYS computes qoyNext from its own date grid (dates.qoyNextOf), never the shipped estimation-grid qoyNext (one quarter behind after the production shift).
  • Result: NSA series now honestly show their seasonal cycle in-forecast as a bounded deterministic cycle instead of a spurious near-Nyquist explosive root; the residual SFA cycle is bounded (year-1 ≈ year-5 amplitude). All nsr = 0 paths are byte-identical to before.
  • Time-varying trade-weights capability (pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m, buildstars(c, D, W, blocs, TVW)). When app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_timevarying.json exists and GVAR_TV_WEIGHTS ≠ 0, star construction applies annual weight rows per quarter, each quarter using its calendar-year row (clamped to the file's span); a partner absent from a year's row gets weight 0 (absorbed by the existing per-component availability renormalization). Solve-time coupling still uses the static/current-year file — promoting the latest year is a separate step. Legacy (no artifact / GVAR_TV_WEIGHTS = 0) is the static row everywhere, byte-identical. The staged artifact is annual IMTS bilateral 1995–2024 over 39 blocs; the honest empirical reading is a reversal, not a monotone trend — the US→China trade share rises to a 2017 peak (0.176) then FALLS after the 2018 trade war (0.119 by 2024), while the US→euro-area share does not decline (rises to 0.178).
  • FSAP data-expansion pass (staged, not yet integrated) — pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/. The tool targets FSAP coverage (32 five-year + 15 ten-year jurisdictions); 41 economies are currently covered. Staged this session: (1) weights_timevarying.json (above); (2) NEER for all gaps and candidates (BIS WS_EER); (3) exports/imports — 49 of 50 coupled blocs already carry real EXP/IMP (only RU lacks IMP), with X/M staged for the five viable candidates; (4) NFA — the shipped external recursion (app/src/lib/compute/externalAccounting.ts) rolls b_t = b_{t−1}/(1+g_nom) + ca_t/4 + val_t from a sourced nfa0 seed (net IIP / nominal GDP) with iNFA (default 3) and fxShare (default 0.4) modeling defaults; IMF-IIP now delivers net-IIP nfa0 anchors for JP/UK/CA (and 48 others), staged for 54 blocs, with current-account data for 53 — the design recommendation is Option B (add an estimated CA_GDP_<CC> panel column like FREV_GDP, keep NFA/GDP a derived display recursion, retire iNFA); (5) five new blocs are FULL-viable — HK (C&SD real GDP, 145q), SG (SingStat, 205q), RO (Eurostat, like PL/HU/CZ), PE (BCRP; NSA real block → seasonal-dummy candidate), PH (PSA SA real GDP; needs a 10Y-yield + credit tail) — while AE is not viable (only annual real GDP exists; the quarterly series is current-price only, and interpolation is barred by the no-synthetic-data rule) and TW is absent from IMF for the external treatment.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Two-stage GVAR-EM estimation E-step (pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m). The outer EM/Jacobi loop runs the DK imputation with a fixed-companion E-step (cgl_bvarV5 'fixedcomp' = 1) so consecutive iterations share random numbers (common random numbers) and the star fixed point contracts to tolerance — the inside-the-loop exact data augmentation is deliberately not used for the outer iterations because the MH accept flips re-randomize the completions each sweep, breaking CRN and leaving a star-churn floor that never meets TOL. The shipped coupled models use the fixed-companion posterior from the converged loop. An optional exact-DA polish sweep (GVAR_POLISH_EXACT = 1; companion rebuilt from the current draw every Gibbs sweep, 'fixedcomp' = 0) can re-estimate every bloc at the frozen converged stars, but it is off by default for the coupled system: exact augmentation marginally raises companion persistence and lifts the coupled operator's spectral radius ρ(M) above 1 (1.0067 with the polish vs <1 without), which would leave pinned-scenario spillovers non-contractive. cgl_bvarV5.m documents the 'fixedcomp' switch; single-bloc estimators (euro members) use exact DA directly and are unaffected. (CGL_FIXED_COMPANION = 1 together with 'qoy' is not a supported combination — the legacy fixed companion carries no seasonal term.)
  • Full 33-bloc re-estimation on branch effi-even-seasonal-dummies, incorporating the evened EFFI, the seasonal dummies, and the two-stage E-step. The coupling is regenerated as part of the re-estimation; ρ(M) remains < 1 (contractive), with the artifact value recorded on promotion. Not yet merged to main.

Rename to Global Macroeconomic Analysis Projections and Scenarios, the code-exact US-bloc model note, the ρ(M) correction (artifact + estimator + repo-wide docs), exact data augmentation in the estimator, and the mid-drag unmount fix.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• docs/GMAPS_US_bloc_model.pdf (15pp, + .tex) — the estimated United States model written down the way the VAR literature does it: the 40-variable VAR(3) with its domestic/foreign partition and the three explicit foreign feed-in channels, the exact star construction, the GLP prior as implemented, the estimated foreign-block loadings (posterior means recomputed from the shipped companion_mean.json), the solve-time linkage through x = Mx + d, and a mapping table to the classical Pesaran GVAR. Adversarially verified against code and artifacts; linked from the mkdocs nav (Methodology) and the docs landing page.
  • docs/GMAPS_management_presentation/gbvar_vs_pesaran/ — a 6-slide native PPTX comparing the EM-Bayesian G-BVAR global solve to the classical Pesaran GVAR (TikZ diagrams, side-by-side table, shipped numbers), in the management-deck style.

docs.title: Changed / corrected
docs.text:
• Renamed the tool: Monetary-Financial-Fiscal Model → Monetary-Financial-Fiscal Macromodel (acronym GMAPS unchanged) across the app (tab title, header, Excel export notes), mkdocs site name and docs, the user manual (recompiled + republished into the app), and the management deck (rebuilt).
  • ρ(M) corrected to 0.945494 (was 0.935044). The artifact's rhoSpectral was an under-converged power-iteration reading: spectralRadius power-iterated M², which assumes a real dominant eigenvalue — valid for the legacy 2-bloc topology but not for the 33-bloc M, whose dominant eigenvalues are the complex pair 0.9459±0.0368i (eigendecomposition of the shipped M). Fixed the estimator (telescoped geometric-mean growth rate, exact for any dominant structure, and cheaper — no M·M multiply), patched the shipped artifact field, and updated every doc that asserted the stale value (manual, paper outline, ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI, MODULES, DATA_SCHEMA, ADDING_A_COUNTRY, MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS, EMPIRICAL_EVALUATION, the comparison deck). Nothing analytic changes: ρ(M) < 1 throughout.
  • Exact data augmentation in cgl_bvarV5.m: the DK simulation smoother's companion matrices are now rebuilt at the top of every Gibbs sweep from the current (β, Σ) draw — textbook Tanner–Wong DA — instead of being fixed at the csminwel posterior-mode fit for all sweeps. CGL_FIXED_COMPANION=1 restores the legacy behaviour for reproduction. Smoke-tested on the US panel; shipped artifacts are unchanged (estimated pre-change; takes effect at the next re-estimation).
  • Removed the stale CN nominal-GDP deflation branch in export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m (panelfrom): China's panel now ships a chain-linked real volume index, so the legacy X_g − X_p deflation would wrongly deflate a real series on the next run.
  • bvarGLP.m lamfix guard: with a pinned tightness (MIN.lambda == MAX.lambda) the csminwel start point inverted a degenerate logistic (NaN at lamfix == 0.2, complex otherwise); the start coordinate is now a finite constant, which the degenerate transform ignores.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Mid-drag unmount leak (ChartGrid): unmounting a chart during a drag gesture (country switch, scenario delete) leaked the window mousemove/mouseup listeners and left the module-level drag flag stuck, permanently deferring every subsequent structure-change GVAR solve. The gesture teardown is now also run from an unmount cleanup.

Manual rewritten in working-paper style (79pp, code-exact math, generated appendix tables), the soft-conditioning/external-forecast layer, the shared clickable legend + uncertainty shading, and a repo-wide documentation accuracy pass against the June-28 coupling artifact.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• docs/GMAPS_User_Manual.tex — full rewrite in the style of Ferroni & Canova (2021): one continuous document, every equation checked against the implementation, tool usage interleaved as worked Examples, notation/roster/glossary appendices. 256pp → 79pp. The old manual is retrievable at git 5f7c5b6.
  • docs/generate_manual_tables.py — regenerates the manual's Appendix B (roster + 50 per-economy variable tables, 1,111 variables) directly from the shipped spec.json / coverage_manifest.json, so the tables cannot drift from the deployed models. Added as a RULE to the re-estimation and add-a-country runbooks.

docs.title: Changed / corrected
docs.text:
• ρ(M) = 0.935116 at dim 2060 (June-28 coupling_default.json.gz) recorded across README, ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI, MODULES, DATA_SCHEMA, PIPELINE, ADDING_A_COUNTRY, REESTIMATING_MODELS, MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS, EMPIRICAL_EVALUATION — superseding the stale 0.924041 (June-12 build).
  • DATA_SCHEMA: the frozen-anchor dim/ρ pairing corrected (24-bloc → dim 1380; the ≈1920 dim belongs to the 33-bloc pre-endogenous frozen configuration).
  • external-block-methodology: the NFA recursion stated as coded — NFAₜ = NFA₋₁/(1+gₜ) + CAₜ/4 + valₜ (the growth-dilution division was missing from the doc, not from the code) and the income leg's /100 restored in the schematics.
  • MODULES: the 8-registry-codes vs 9-scored-models count reconciled (the rw code emits the climatology sibling as a separate label).
  • Manual-facing corrections vs the old text: default scenario bands are re-centred predictive draws (not the DK simulation smoother), the debt roll uses the structural sfaDefault constant, the model-signature fingerprints are the first-equation intercept + a last-lag-row entry, 23 fiscal blocs (6 majors + 17 euro members), uniform 2026Q1 panel origin with Israel on its own calendar.

Drag-off-the-heavy-path GVAR UX (optimistic pin + right-click-to-plant + Compute-gated full solve), a consistent re-estimation lifting the coupling spectral radius to ρ(M) = 0.924, the fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs re-index guard for the EA/UK debt explosion, the produced out-of-sample horse-race results, and a documented known-issues list.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• pipeline/fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs — fiscal-meta re-index (and a MANDATORY runbook RULE). fiscal_meta.json stores the fiscal-driver columns by position (idx = {gdp, deflator, revenue, primaryExp, effRate, sfa}); the 33-bloc GVAR-EM refit inserted variables ahead of the fiscal block in every spec except US, which silently re-pointed those positional indices at the wrong columns — EA's effRate landed on the equity index (~col 537) and the EA/UK debt-to-GDP path exploded.
