The new script re-resolves the indices by variable id from the deployed spec.json (order-independent) and rewrites all six fiscal metas, preserving d0/sfaDefault (it only touches meta.idx); it is idempotent. RULE (now documented in the maintainer runbooks): run node pipeline/fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs after ANY re-estimation/port that can change a fiscal bloc's variable order or count. The porter does not regenerate the meta, so this re-index is the fix — a green tsc/build with stale indices still ships a wrong debt path.
  • Optimistic conditioned-point pin (app/src/lib/conditionedDotY.ts). When you click, drag, or right-click to set a conditioned point, the marker (dot) now snaps to the clicked value instantly — it is reconstructed from the conditioning path (conditionedDotDisplayY), the exact inverse of the display→stored mapping (conditioningDeviationFromDisplayY), so it never waits for the (multi-second, on GVAR) forecast solve. The smoothed line + uncertainty bands reconcile around the pinned point once the solve lands. A single source of truth for the display↔stored round-trip prevents the two from drifting.
  • Right-click to plant a pin at the cursor. Right-clicking a forecast chart conditions that variable (if needed) and plants the conditioned point exactly at the cursor (the same forward mapping handleDrag uses, via onContextMenu in ChartGrid.tsx); left-clicking the "condition" button still toggles conditioning without moving a point.
  • Produced OOS empirical-evaluation results (separate repo em-bayesian-gvar-eval, results/tables.{txt,json} + results/tierA/us_rate_100bp.json). The recursive expanding-window horse-race — 56 origins (2010Q1–2024Q4, 2020 dropped) × 9 models, rolling as-of-t0 trade weights, CRPS-primary density score + 90% Model Confidence Set — now has numbers: AR(p)/DFM have the lowest point CRPS, but the EM-GVAR is in the inflation MCS at all horizons (h=1,2,4,8) and the short-rate MCS at h=1,2,4, statistically indistinguishable from the best on the nominal block, and decisively beats the textbook OLS classical GVAR (cgvar_a dropped from most MCS sets); emgvar_endo ⪰ emgvar_frozen in the MCS (best INFL h=1 relRMSE = emgvar_endo, 0.799). Honest caveats documented: the draw-based densities are over-confident (PIT cov90 ≈ 0.73–0.85 vs 0.90), the parametric log-score column is numerically broken on the under-covered clouds (CRPS + MCS are the robust primaries), and the Tier-A US-+100bp spillover is a multi-period conditional projection (large, sign-flipping magnitudes), not a causal IRF.
  • Known-issues / limitations sections in README.md and docs/MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md — five honestly-flagged, not-yet-fixed defects: (1) the CN fiscal debt inflation double-count (the snowball reads GDP_CN = nominal GDP plus a CPI deflator → inflation counted twice); (2) longRunTilt.ts does not filter non-finite long-run moments before the entropic-weight solve (a NaN draw can silently empty the anchor band); (3) the closed-form GVAR solve has no ρ(M)<1 divergence guard; (4) the conditional band uses the filtered (not DK-smoothed) covariance, overstating the band before a future pin; (5) the porter does not regenerate fiscal_meta (the stale-index cause of the EA/UK debt explosion — now guarded by the re-index RULE).

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Drag perf — the heavy GVAR solve is OFF the live drag path. On the live ~50-bloc US-endogenous panel every mean solve is multi-second (~4.5 s warm / ~13 s cold — the US-pinned structure misses the empty-pinStructure shipped coupling artifact), so the engine now withholds every solve during a drag (value-only or structure-change). The drag path is a cheap conditioning preview (the optimistic dot snaps to the cursor); exactly one cheap direct first-order solve fires on pointer-up; and the full cross-country fixed point + uncertainty bands run only on the "Solve full GVAR" button / top-bar Compute. A direct/full mode pill and a "computing…" badge make the mode explicit; the ≈95 MB coupling artifact is stripped from the worker post in direct mode. Drag state is a module-level signal bus (app/src/lib/compute/gvarDragState.ts) so begin/end/in-flight flags do not re-render the whole grid. Per-chart React.memo + reconciled chart references mean a single conditioning edit repaints one panel of ~35, not all of them.
  • Coupling spectral radius is now ρ(M) = 0.924 (was 0.896 / 0.896156 in an earlier refit). A later consistent re-estimation produced a new shipped coupling_default.json.gz (dim 2060, gzipped ≈ 31 MB) with a different modelSig and rhoSpectral = 0.924041 (still < 1, stationary; verified off the artifact header). Docs corrected to read the live value off the header rather than a copied number.
  • Docs accuracy pass. Corrected ρ(M) (0.896 → 0.924) across README.md, docs/ADDING_A_COUNTRY.md, docs/REESTIMATING_MODELS.md, docs/MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md (incl. the verify-command expect-line); fixed the fiscal bloc variable counts in README.md (EA 24, JP 23, UK 25, CA 25, CN 20 — previously conflated with the SFA estimation-sample lengths) and the stale GVAR-bloc count in USER_GUIDE.md (24 → 33, US now endogenous); replaced the stale ~0.45 s / ~3.4 s drag timings with the verified drag-off-the-heavy-path behaviour; documented the npm test (fast gate) vs npm run test:heavy split; and rewrote the generic app/README.md into a project-specific front-end guide.
Fiscal stationary prior + mean-reversion, GVAR coherence fixes, a full consistent 33-bloc refit, a per-economy variable table in the manual, and the out-of-sample empirical-evaluation harness.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Stationary white-noise (WN) prior for the fiscal GDP-ratios. FREV_GDP (revenue/GDP), FPEXP_GDP (primary expenditure/GDP) and SFA (stock-flow adjustment) are now estimated with a stationary white-noise prior — the own-first-lag prior mean is set to 0 (vs the default random-walk own-lag of 1) — so these mean-reverting shares revert to their in-sample means at the long end instead of drifting. Mechanism: the GLP prior in BVAR/MFBVAR/GLPreplicationWeb/bvarGLPmf.m zeroes the selected own-lag prior means (diagb(pos)=0; b(2:n+1,:)=diag(diagb)), threaded as the pos/stationary 3rd positional argument of cgl_bvarV5.m (function [...] = cgl_bvarV5(x,p,stationary,...), pos=stationary). The estimators pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m (and the euro builder) read the per-variable prior from the spec (priorsfrom → statCols = find(Spec.Prior=="WN")) and pass it down. The effective debt rate EFFI stays RW (prior:RW, isFinancial:true). Result, e.g.: US revenue/GDP now mean-reverts to ~17.4% instead of being stuck near ~19% under the RW prior. The change is a no-op (byte-identical) for the 44 non-fiscal blocs (their statCols is empty). Verified in the deployed specs: US/EA/CA/UK/JP/CN FREV_GDP/FPEXP_GDP/SFA carry prior:WN, EFFI carries prior:RW. Committed in 6f0161a / 22250be / e38673a.
  • Out-of-sample empirical-evaluation harness (new Empirical Evaluation page; full design in the separate repo /home/farkas/github/em-bayesian-gvar-eval). A recursive expanding-window OOS forecast horse-race (proposed endogenous-US emgvar_endo + frozen-anchor emgvar_frozen vs six benchmarks: random walk + climatology, AR(p), single-country BVAR, textbook OLS GVAR, single-pass Bayesian GVAR, and a Bayesian DFM) plus a Tier-A endogenous-vs-frozen spillover contrast. The harness references the main tool via BVAR_TOOL_ROOT (it addpaths the estimator and imports gvarSolve.ts via vitest; it never copies estimator code). Origins 2010Q1–2024Q4, rolling as-of-t0 trade weights (the shipped 2021–2023 weights_full.json is forbidden in the sweep), four enforced look-ahead invariants, scoring by CRPS (primary) + parametric log-score + PIT/coverage, with Giacomini–White / Clark–West / Diebold–Mariano + Romano–Wolf + Model Confidence Set inference (matlab/oos_driver.m, eval/score.py, eval/tests.py, eval/tables.py). The empirical results are forthcoming/preliminary; the design is final.
  • Per-economy variable table in the methodology manual (docs/user_manual.tex, §Economy Coverage): every variable of every economy tabulated by transformation (log / lin) · prior (RW / WN) · financial tag, alongside new manual sections (the stationary-prior derivation, the EM-convergence and spectral-radius diagnostics, the empirical-results scaffold) and additional TikZ figures (architecture, Kalman, GVAR coupling, EM-trace schematic). Committed in fa104cd / 34d3e15.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• GLB global commons coherence — GLB_USEQ and GLB_OIL are now isFinancial:true everywhere. Both the US equity common (GLB_USEQ) and the oil common (GLB_OIL) are tagged financial across all blocs, so they are kept OBSERVED through the COVID-as-missing window (financials are not imputed) rather than NaN-masked with the macro block. Verified in the deployed EA spec (GLB_OIL/GLB_USEQ isFinancial:true, joining GLB_USLR/GLB_USBAA).
  • Canada industrial production (IP_CA) rebuilt as a log-LEVEL. The discontinued FRED level index is chained forward with the growth series to 2025Q4 and carried as a transformation:"log" log-level (pipeline/build_ca_ip_level.py), removing the level/growth incoherence in the CA bloc. Committed in 9839a46.
  • Full consistent GVAR-EM refit (33 blocs + coupling). All blocs were re-estimated together so the fiscal WN prior, the GLB financial tags, and the CA IP log-level are applied coherently across the whole system, with the coupling artifact regenerated. All 1048 per-economy variables were audited coherent (transformation · prior · financial). Committed in e38673a / 22250be.

Major release: the 24-bloc Global VAR with US-determined global commons (oil + US financial conditions), ~50-economy coverage, and a self-configuring cross-country solver. Breaking vs 1.x: the US anchor grew to n=37, every GVAR bloc carries 4 block:'global' commons, the whole panel is on a single 2025Q4 vintage (first forecast = 2026Q1), and the pre-shipped coupling artifact (coupling_default.json) is now mandatory for interactivity at 24 blocs.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Coverage expanded to ~50 economies. One registry (app/src/lib/data/countries.ts) now drives the dropdown: 6 core majors + 34 OECD members + 10 non-OECD emerging markets. Each is a single-country BVAR except the 24 that are GVAR-linked. Sources: FRED (cross-checked against national sources) for the core, Eurostat for EU/EFTA OECD, OECD-QNA / national-bank / IMF for the rest.
  • 24-bloc Global VAR (~90% of global demand). The GVAR was extended from 6 to 24 blocs: the US closed anchor + 23 Rest-of-World blocs (EA, JP, UK, CA, CN, CH, KR, MX, AU, TR, SE, PL, NO, DK, IN, BR, RU, ID, SA, AR, ZA, TH, MY). The bloc list + row-normalized trade weights live in app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_24bloc.json. The 23 RoW blocs are re-estimated to a cross-country fixed point by the GVAR-EM loop pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m (each bloc's 3 stars built from partners' DK-completed series, iterated to convergence).
  • Global commons (shared US-determined variables). Each RoW bloc now also carries 4 block:'global' variables identical across blocs: GLB_OIL (WTI), GLB_USLR (US 10Y), GLB_USBAA (US BAA → credit spread), GLB_USEQ (S&P 500) — a standard GVAR global-variable treatment that transmits oil and US financial-conditions shocks to every bloc.
  • Self-configuring GVAR topology. configureGVARTopology/deriveBlocIdx (gvarSolve.ts) derive the active bloc set, per-bloc variable indices, and renormalized weights at load from the deployed spec.json files + weights_24bloc.json — no hardcoded IDX/W. A bloc is GVAR-active iff its spec carries block:'row' vars and it has a weights row.
  • Closed-form cross-country solve + precomputed coupling. The scenario fixed point is solved as x = (I − M)⁻¹d. At 24 blocs the in-browser inverse is infeasible (~19 min), so a precomputed coupling (M, (I − M)⁻¹, ρ) is shipped as app/public/data/bvar/gvar/coupling_default.json (regenerated by app/scripts/precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs) and hydrated into the solver cache, giving a sub-second matrix–vector solve — the key interactivity enabler for the full system.
  • User-defined long-run anchor (PLR). Pin a variable's long-run (≈10-year) forecast to a target; the posterior draws are entropically tilted toward it (per-draw weights, no re-estimation), pulling both the baseline and scenario fans (app/src/lib/compute/longRunTilt.ts). Single-country (non-GVAR) models only.
  • Global-common transmission in the solver (applyGlobalPins, gvarSolve.ts). The 4 block:'global' commons are now propagated end-to-end: deriveBlocIdx exposes them as IDX[c].glob (id → column), and each RoW bloc's global columns are pinned to its own baseline + the US scenario DEVIATION of the matching global (matched by id). A shock to US oil / US financial conditions therefore moves the identical common delta into every RoW bloc (verified on the real 24-bloc data: a US GLB_OIL pin gives an identical oil delta across all 23 RoW blocs to ≤1e-9), while each bloc's domestic variables respond through its own estimated coefficients. The forcing enters the per-bloc d, not the RoW↔RoW coupling M, so the shipped coupling artifact is unchanged. Gauss–Seidel ≡ closed-form to ≤1e-9 with globals present.

🔴 ASSUMPTION (load-bearing): the globals pin the US deviation on each bloc's own baseline, not the US level. Each RoW bloc estimated its own (differing) baseline path for the globals, so a level pin would inject a 17–70-unit spurious delta at zero scenario. The delta pin gives zero spillover at zero scenario and an identical common shock under conditioning. See docs/ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI.md §5.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• US anchor re-estimated at n=37 (was n=36). The 4 global commons (GLB_OIL/GLB_USLR/GLB_USBAA/GLB_USEQ) are tagged block:'global' so the RoW blocs match them by id, and the DDEBT_GDP fiscal driver was replaced by EFFI ("Effective rate on debt, % p.a.", block:'fiscal') — the fiscal recursion now reads an estimated effective debt rate (fiscal_meta.idx.effRate) instead of the Δdebt-column shim.
  • All 50 blocs share a single 2025Q4 data vintage, so the first forecast ("nowcast") quarter is uniformly 2026Q1. app/src/lib/dates.ts now dates every bloc from the common 2025-10-01 panel end via lastHistOf() (the old per-bloc LAST_HIST_DATE map covered only 6 blocs at stale 2025Q2/Q3 vintages, leaving the other 44 with undated axes).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• GVAR baseline ↔ engine consistency (mean AND bands regenerated). The 24 GVAR blocs' stored baseline was fully regenerated from the shipped companion so it reproduces what the app computes in-browser:
  • Means (app/scripts/regen_gvar_baselines.mjs): the deterministic all-NaN smoother on companion_mean.json, stored at full double precision. Previously they drifted 0.07–1.77 (100·log) vs the engine — a zero-scenario showed a small spurious deviation and the baseline-reproduction canary fired; now they reproduce to 0.
  • Bands q05/q16/q84/q95 (app/scripts/regen_gvar_bands.mjs): the predictive density the chart itself draws — bvarForecastDraw(paramsDraw, hist, H, addInnovation=true) over all 500 posterior draws (parameter draw + per-step innovation), with a seeded PRNG for byte-reproducibility, reduced to fractiles in both 100·log LEVEL space (baseline_levels.json) and DISPLAY space (baseline.json). Band widths match the prior export to ~MC noise; q05≤q16≤q84≤q95 and the mean sits inside the 90% band for every cell.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• COVID-as-missing re-estimation of all six models. The 2020 pandemic quarters are now treated as MISSING (NaN) and imputed with the Durbin–Koopman simulation smoother inside a data-augmentation Gibbs sampler (BVAR/MFBVAR/cgl_bvarV5.m): each sweep draws the missing data, updates the Minnesota hyperparameters (lambda, mu) by Metropolis–Hastings on the completed-data marginal likelihood, then draws the VAR coefficients. This is deliberately not Lenza–Primiceri (2022) COVID volatility scaling. The COVID window self-calibrates to the 2020Q2 GDP trough. New canonical estimators: pipeline/export_bvar_gvar_covid.m (EA/JP/UK/CA/CN), pipeline/export_bvar_us_covid.m (US, n=36, sur=0 so the 2-hyperparameter Gibbs is well-defined). The old export_bvar_gvar.m / export_bvar_us_fiscal.m (bvarGLP) are superseded.
  • lambda is now unconstrained / empirical Bayes for every model — the per-country lamfix (EA/JP/UK/CA 0.10, CN 0.04) is gone; with COVID imputed, the marginal-likelihood optimum is well-behaved (estimated lambda 0.24–0.56).
  • Uncertainty bands are now PREDICTIVE (parameter + innovation + missing-data forecast-error variance), from the Gibbs predictive density (Dforecast) in the export and bvarForecastDraw(..., addInnovation=true) in the browser. The old parameter-only bands (spread of posterior mean paths) collapsed under a tight prior and badly understated uncertainty. GDP 68% bands (q/q ann., pp): US 4.2, EA 5.0, JP 7.9, UK 9.5, CA 4.9, CN 13.5. The plotted mean stays the deterministic posterior-mean-coefficient forecast (so the unconditional smoother still reproduces it — gvar-convergence canary).

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • "Reset all" button (Scenario panel) — clears every scenario and all cross-country GVAR conditioning back to one empty default, behind an inline confirmation. Distinct from the per-scenario Reset (active scenario, current country only).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• EA (and all GVAR blocs) density bands were too tight — the parameter-only methodology under EA's tight prior gave a ~1.9pp GDP band; fixed by the predictive bands + COVID-as-missing re-estimation above (~5pp).
  • No uncertainty band in the "% vs base" (deviation) view for GVAR blocs — the GVAR override was replacing the computed levelDeviationStd with the GVAR engine's null; now falls back to the single-country conditional std so the deviation band renders for EA et al.
  • Regenerated the US conforekf ground truth (pipeline/_verify/gt.m) for the scenario-scale-convention canary after the US re-estimation; companion draws compressed to 6 significant figures (US 52→26 MB).

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Full six-country GVAR. Every non-US model is now a GVAR bloc with its own three trade-weighted Rest-of-World stars (ROWDEM/ROWINF/ROWFIN): United States (closed anchor, n=36) + Euro Area (n=13), Japan (n=13), United Kingdom (n=15), Canada (n=15), and China (n=10). Conditioning any bloc propagates to all others through the shared RoW stars, solved as the linear cross-country fixed point Δ = M·Δ + d. The Gauss-Seidel and direct solvers agree to ~5e-11 across all six blocs (per-country and multi-country-mix, gvar-convergence.test.ts); the full system has spectral radius rho(M) ~ 0.59 and converges in ~10 sweeps. Trade weights row-normalized over the six blocs (pipeline/gvar_rawdata/weights_6bloc.json); the five non-US models are estimated by pipeline/export_bvar_gvar.m.
  • China as a full GVAR bloc. China is re-estimated as a 10-variable RoW bloc (7 domestic + 3 stars) at a tighter Minnesota prior lambda=0.04 — the wider 0.10 prior let the posterior mode extrapolate China's high-growth-2000s sample (~11% nominal GDP) far above the draw distribution, leaving export/import densities off-centre; the tighter prior re-centres the bands on the unconditional forecast. (Supersedes the earlier standalone single-country CN model; export_bvar_cn.m is deprecated.)
  • Reporting-units policy (displayUnits.ts). Index / FX / equity / commodity series (FXTWM, SP500, HP, PZTEXP, GSNE, NEER_EA, NEER_UK, NEER_CA, REER_CN, EQ_CN) are now displayed as the index level (e.g. 2010 = 100) instead of q/q-annualized growth — a trade-weighted FX or equity index q/q-ann. is not an informative number, the level is. Stored as 100·log(index) and conditioned in that space; only the display is exponentiated. baseline_levels.json now carries level-space quantiles (q16/q84/q05/q95/q50) for the level uncertainty fan, generated reproducibly inside the export scripts.
  • Level-space uncertainty fans for the level-displayed series, computed from the same posterior draws as the growth bands so the two are mutually consistent.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• All six countries refreshed to 2025Q4 from official national sources (Eurostat, ONS, StatCan, e-Stat, NBS) cross-checked against FRED, then re-estimated.
  • Unemployment-rate display bands floored at 0. LR, LR_JP, LR_UK, LR_CA can no longer render an impossible negative lower band. (A persistently-low central unemployment forecast remains a model question for re-estimation, not a display fix.)
  • GVAR cross-country slice now engages for all six blocs in the chart layer, not just US/EA/JP.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Experimental per-draw GVAR band dropped UK/CA/CN own-pins. A leftover 3-bloc ['US','EA','JP'] loop in ChartGrid.tsx (from the pilot) meant the experimental per-draw band for UK/CA/CN was computed without their own conditioning pins, so the band sat on the baseline while the line followed the propagated path. Now iterates the canonical six-bloc list.
  • Stale 3-bloc gvar/weights.json replaced with the six-bloc matrix (provenance only — the solver weights are compiled into gvarSolve.ts).
  • Pipeline header/dimension comments corrected to per-bloc sizes; export_bvar_cn.m marked DEPRECATED (running it would overwrite the live GVAR China model).

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Global VAR (GVAR) cross-country linkage. The Euro Area and Japan models now carry a Rest-of-World block of three trade-weighted "star" variables (foreign demand ROWDEM, foreign inflation ROWINF, foreign policy/financial conditions ROWFIN). Conditioning the US propagates to EA and JP, with EA<->JP back-feed, solved as a linear cross-country fixed point Δ = M·Δ + d at solve time. Two solvers (Gauss-Seidel and direct/doubling) agree to ~1e-11; the US->EA->JP pilot converges in ~4 sweeps (rho(M)~0.29). The solve runs in a debounced, stale-guarded Web Worker with a convergence read-out (sweeps, rho, ms). Trade weights come from the IMF IMTS database (build_trade_weights.py); the star series are built by build_gvar_data.py; EA/JP are re-estimated by export_bvar_gvar.m. New engine: gvarSolve.ts, runGvarSolve.ts, runGvarBandSolve.ts, gvarWorker.ts, useGvarForecast.ts, gvarLoader.ts.
  • US fiscal block (stock-flow-consistent). The US BVAR estimates government current-receipts and primary-expenditure ratios as drivers; primary/overall balance and the debt-to-GDP path are derived outside the VAR by the budget-identity recursion (CBO / IMF financial-programming style). Debt is parametrized as the change in debt/GDP and accumulated (debt = d0 + cumsum(Δd)). Conditioning a driver flows through to the derived debt path. Methodology: docs/fiscal-block-methodology.md; engine: fiscalAccounting.ts.
  • Per-draw GVAR uncertainty bands. In GVAR mode the uncertainty bands re-solve the cross-country system per posterior draw, so derived (RoW and fiscal) series get a band that is correctly centred on the propagated mean path rather than the baseline. Draw subsampling uses a deterministic stratified stride (reproducible, full tail coverage).
  • Auto-updating US dataset. build_us_auto.py rebuilds the US model hands-off from public FRED series, with the effective federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) as the policy instrument (the 2-year yield moves to the financial block). The model auto-detects its sample span (currently to 2025Q4).
  • China (CN) added as the sixth country — a real estimated BVAR from public FRED data (17 variables, 3 lags: nominal GDP, industrial production, CPI, 3M rate, exports, imports, real effective FX, Shanghai equity + a US block), replacing an earlier synthetic placeholder. Built by pipeline/build_country_data.py + pipeline/export_bvar_cn.m.
  • Opt-in experimental features — a lower-left toggle. The first experimental feature is the per-draw iterative GVAR density (re-solves the cross-country system for each posterior draw); the default band is the faster model-specific density (see Changed).
  • Dated (calendar) x-axis on all charts, with date+value hover and dated Excel export. The left-hand conditioning sliders keep the NC / 1Q / 2Q / 3Q labels.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• US model re-estimated at n=36 with the fiscal drivers and FEDFUNDS policy rate. The Minnesota tightness is auto-selected; redundant real federal-consumption (GFH, a ~0.98-correlated subcomponent of government spending) is dropped, which restores a healthy auto-lambda (~0.28) and well-behaved conditioning.
  • EA/JP RoW models estimated with a fixed Minnesota tightness lambda=0.10: the auto-lambda optimum (~0.5-0.6) was too loose for the small n=15, T~90 systems and produced oscillating unconditional baselines; the fixed moderate-tight prior yields smooth, mean-reverting forecasts.
  • Fiscal reporting charts simplified. Under the change-in-debt/GDP parametrization the effective interest rate is backed out of the identity and degenerates to approximately nominal growth, so the effective-rate, interest (debt-service), and overall-deficit charts were removed; revenue, primary expenditure, primary balance, and debt/GDP are kept.
  • Default scenario uncertainty band reworked. The default band is now the model-specific (unconditional) forecast density parallel-shifted onto the propagated scenario path — it keeps the full forecast width (it no longer collapses when only a point or two is conditioned) and centres on the displayed line. The earlier per-draw iterative cross-country re-solve (which compressed the band and was slow) is preserved behind the experimental toggle.
  • Drag and band performance. Dragging now coalesces to one update per animation frame (rAF); posterior draws load as Float64Array (faster worker transfer + indexing); a US-viewed band skips the frozen-US's irrelevant EA/JP cross-country re-solve; and an unused Cholesky per draw was removed.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text: • Germany (DE) model removed from the platform.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Fiscal policy counterfactuals -- autonomous government spending shocks via DSGE fiscal_ IRFs. 60 models support fiscal shocks (including US_SW07, EA_SW03, EA_QUEST3). Fiscal and monetary adjustments can be combined, with separate Toeplitz convolutions for each instrument and summed DSGE-implied deltas.
  • Barnichon & Mesters optimal policy -- the "Compute optimal rate path" button now runs the B&M (2023) QP optimizer using the selected model's IRFs and lambda weights to generate an optimal rate adjustment path.
  • Policy rule parameters -- selecting a rule updates displayed parameters (read-only); parameters are embedded in the DSGE equilibrium and require Dynare to change.
  • Editable scenario names -- scenarios can be named in the control panel; names appear in chart titles and exported files.
  • Improved exports -- Excel exports with per-variable sheets (Q16/Median/Q84 + deviations), PNG as ZIP, PDF as combined multi-page document.
  • Example scenario -- bundled "Inflation Surge (10%)" example with SW07/SW rule counterfactual, downloadable from the control panel.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Multi-country BVAR conditional forecasting for 5 economies: United States (33 variables), Euro Area (22), United Kingdom (22), Japan (22), and Canada (22). Each country BVAR includes companion-form VAR coefficients, posterior mean baselines, and historical data pre-computed from FRED series.
  • Durbin-Koopman (DK) Kalman smoother for conditional forecasting, ported from MATLAB (conforekf.m / VARcf_DKcks.m / runKF_DK.m). State-space representation with companion-form transition matrices and Cholesky-based simulation draws.
  • 155 DSGE models from the Macroeconomic Model Data Base (MMB) with pre-computed impulse response functions across 9 policy rules (Taylor, GR, LWW, SW, CEE, OW08, OW13, Coenen, CMR). Models span 6 categories: Estimated US (69), Calibrated (50), Estimated Euro Area (20), Adaptive Learning (11), Estimated/Calibrated Multi-Country (10), and Estimated Other-Country (9). A total of 726 model-rule IRF files are included.
  • Three counterfactual modes for policy analysis:
  • Hold targets -- condition on the scenario paths for all user-specified variables while applying a rate adjustment via the DK smoother.
  • Let adjust -- condition only on the policy rate adjustment and allow all macro variables to adjust freely through the BVAR dynamics.
  • IRF-consistent -- use DSGE model IRFs to compute structurally consistent inflation and output gap responses to the policy shock sequence (Toeplitz convolution), then condition the BVAR on these DSGE-implied deltas.
  • Barnichon and Mesters (2023, AER) optimal policy solver. Quadratic programming approach using sufficient statistics (DSGE IRFs) to find the optimal monetary policy shock sequence minimizing a weighted loss function over inflation and output gap deviations.
  • Per-variable, per-quarter conditioning via the control panel. Users can select any BVAR variable for conditioning, set deviation paths with sliders (-3 to +3 percentage points), and toggle individual quarters on or off. Conditioning paths are expressed relative to the DK smoother's unconditional forecast.
  • Interactive draggable chart interface using Plotly.js. Inflation, GDP growth, and policy rate charts support direct drag interaction on forecast points. Other variables can be conditioned via a "condition" button on each chart panel.
  • Uncertainty bands with two modes: Quick (analytical 16th/84th percentile bands from the DK smoother covariance) and Full (Monte Carlo simulation draws from the posterior distribution of companion matrices, loaded lazily from companion_draws.json).
  • Up to 4 simultaneous scenarios with color-coded overlays (blue, red, green, purple). Each scenario maintains independent model selection, policy rule, conditioning paths, counterfactual settings, and rate adjustments.
  • Excel export and import of scenario configurations. Export produces multi-sheet .xlsx files containing settings, conditioning paths, active quarters, rate adjustments, and a variable index map. Import supports both .xlsx and legacy .json formats, with robust variable matching across spec changes.
  • Full session export from the top bar, producing a single Excel workbook with one sheet per scenario including all settings, conditioning paths, and rate adjustments.
  • Levels vs. deviations display mode toggle, and quarter-over-quarter vs. year-over-year growth rate display for applicable variables.
  • Custom matrix algebra library (matrix.ts) using flat Float64Array storage in row-major order for browser-side linear algebra, including Cholesky decomposition, matrix solve, and Toeplitz construction.
  • Docker Compose deployment configuration with a Next.js frontend container (port 3000) and a Python backend container (port 8000) with FRED API key support and IRF caching volumes.

docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text:
• 14 DSGE models have no pre-computed IRFs (shown as having zero available rules in the catalog). These are primarily adaptive learning variants and two other models:
  • CA_ToTEM10 -- Murchison & Rennison (2006)
  • EAUS_NAWMctww -- Cogan et al. (2013)
  • NK_BGG99AL -- Bernanke et al. (1999) AL
  • NK_CDK24 -- Chan, Diz, & Kanngiesser (2024)
  • NK_CGG02AL -- Clarida et al. (2002) AL
  • NK_CGG99AL -- Clarida et al. (1999) AL
  • NK_IR04AL -- Ireland (2004) AL
  • NK_LWW03AL -- Levin et al. (2003) AL
  • NK_RW06AL -- Ravenna & Walsh (2006) AL
  • NK_RW97AL -- Rotemberg & Woodford (1997) AL
  • US_FM95AL -- Fuhrer & Moore (1995) AL
  • US_MI07AL -- Milani (2007)
  • US_SW07AL -- Slobodyan & Wouters (2012)
  • US_YR13AL -- Rychalovska (2016)
  • Docker backend not tested end-to-end. The docker-compose.yml defines frontend and backend services, but the backend (Python/MATLAB bridge for live BVAR estimation and MMB IRF computation) has not been validated in an integrated deployment.
  • China BVAR has limited data. The CN BVAR includes 23 variables with baseline and companion matrices, but lacks companion_draws.json (no full uncertainty bands), baseline_levels.json, and historical_levels.json. The underlying data does not come from FRED and may have coverage gaps.
  • IRF-consistent mode falls back silently to let-adjust when the selected DSGE model lacks IRFs for the chosen policy rule. A small warning is shown in the UI but no explicit user confirmation is required.

docs.title: Technical Notes
docs.text:
• All BVAR computation (Kalman filtering, DK smoothing, conditional forecasting, uncertainty simulation) runs entirely client-side in the browser using TypeScript and Float64Array-backed matrix operations. No server round-trips are required after initial data loading.
  • Pre-computed data totals approximately 152 MB, served as static JSON from /public/data/. This includes BVAR posterior estimates for 6 countries, 726 DSGE model-rule IRF files, and the model/rule catalogs. The US companion_draws.json (posterior simulation draws for full uncertainty) is loaded lazily only when the user clicks Compute.
  • The unconditional DK smoother result is cached and reused across conditioning changes to avoid redundant computation. A 30ms debounce is applied to conditioning path updates.
  • Built with Next.js 14.2, React 18, Zustand 4.5 for state management, Plotly.js for interactive charts, and SheetJS (xlsx) for Excel I/O. Styled with Tailwind CSS. Tested with Vitest.

docs.title: Data packs
docs.text:
This page moved into the complete GMAPS 4.0 Update Manual, which covers:

  • what a data pack, an update pack and the data's own calendar are (§1, §4);
  • installing GMAPS 4.0.0 and updating the data on your computer, including rollback and messages (§2–§3);
  • the monthly check, the quarterly data shift and the yearly model update (§5–§7);
  • releasing a new app version, troubleshooting, and every command and check (§8–§10).

Field-level format of the history files (firstQuarter): DATA_SCHEMA.md §7.

docs.title: Data Contracts & JSON Schemas
docs.text:
This page is the reference for every JSON contract the app reads from app/public/data/bvar/ — and, since the experimental Drivers panel shipped, from app/public/data/dsge/census/ as well (§13). It is the authority for what each file contains, the exact field names, the array shapes, and the conventions (variable ids, block tags, transformations, the 6-significant-figure compaction). It complements — and does not duplicate — the prose in the companion docs:

  • ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI.md — how the compute engine uses these files (§4–§10).
  • README.md / USER_GUIDE.md — overview & UI.
  • fiscal-block-methodology.md — the math behind fiscal_meta.json.
  • drivers-decomposition.md — the math and the licence behind the Drivers payload (§13).
  • ADDING_A_COUNTRY.md / REESTIMATING_MODELS.md — how the files are produced.

If a fact here disagrees with the code, the code wins — these contracts are verified against the live files (app/public/data/bvar/US, …/EA, …/DE, …/CN, …/gvar) but the data is re-ported on every re-estimation. Values quoted below are from data pack 2026Q2-reest-20261008b (Oct 2026 genuine-data re-estimation, panel ending 2026Q2) unless labelled as history.

Since 4.0.0 every file on this page belongs to a data pack (§1.1): the app reads it only through the pack's manifest.json, which lists each file with its SHA-256 and size. The data and the estimated model are therefore separate from the tool — a new pack updates them without a new app version.

docs.title: 1. Where the files live
docs.text:
Each economy is one directory app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/ keyed by ISO-2-ish country code (US, EA, JP, …; EA = euro-area aggregate). The cross-country GVAR coupling lives in app/public/data/bvar/gvar/.

app/public/data/
  manifest.json                      THE PACK: every file's path + sha256 + bytes, dating per economy (§1.1)
  coverage_manifest.json             per-variable sources, coverage, flags, model-implied quarters
  nowcast_provenance.json            which history cells the coupled nowcast supplied (model-implied)
  default_anchors.json, cookbook/, dsge/, vintages/, weo_forecasts.json, …   (also in the pack)
  bvar/
    US/   EA/   JP/  …               one directory per economy (52: 35 coupled GVAR blocs + 17 euro members)
      spec.json                      variable manifest (ids, blocks, transforms)
      companion_mean.json            posterior-mean VAR (betahat, sigmahat)
      companion_draws.json.gz        flat posterior draws, gzipped (lazy-loaded, large); the plain
                                     .json is a local by-product, not in git and not in the pack
      baseline.json                  baseline fan in DISPLAY/GROWTH space
      baseline_levels.json           baseline fan in LEVEL space
      historical.json                last 40q in DISPLAY/GROWTH space
      historical_levels.json         last 40q in LEVEL space + firstQuarter (the calendar, §7)
      transformations.json           per-variable 'log'|'lin' list
      estimation_mask.json           history cells the estimator drew as missing data (§7.1)
      fiscal_meta.json               the 41 economies with a fiscal block (§9)
      external_meta.json             the 47 economies with the external-accounts satellite (§9.1)
    gvar/
      weights_24bloc.json            35-bloc trade-weight matrix + topology source (§10)
      coupling_default.json.gz       gzipped precomputed (I−M)⁻¹ coupling artifact (§11)

Loader (app/src/lib/data/loader.ts). Every read goes through the pack: loadJSON(path) is dataManifest.fetchJSON(path), which looks the file up in manifest.json, fetches it, and checks its byte length and SHA-256 before parsing (a mismatch is an error, the file is never used, and the error is shown on screen by DataErrorBanner). Optional files go through fetchJSONIfInPack: a file the pack does not list is absent (null, a NotInPackError underneath); a listed file that fails is an error and fails the load. loadBVARData(country) fetches spec/companion_mean/baseline/historical eagerly, then optionally baseline_levels/historical_levels/fiscal_meta/external_meta (a missing file → null, normal for economies without a fiscal block or external satellite). companion_draws.json.gz is loaded lazily by loadCompanionDraws(country) only when Compute is clicked (it is the largest file — tens of MB): the compressed bytes are hash-checked, gunzipped with the browser's DecompressionStream, and the flat arrays converted once to Float64Array for fast indexing and zero-copy structured-clone into the band worker.

docs.title: 1.1 manifest.json — the data pack
docs.text:
Written by app/scripts/pack-build.mjs, checked by app/scripts/pack-verify.mjs (every web build runs pack-verify --full in prebuild), read at runtime by app/src/lib/data/dataManifest.ts. The manifest itself is the root of trust: it is fetched without caching and not hash-checked (a detached signature is a planned upgrade; today the format only leaves room for it).

Field Type Meaning schemaVersion string "major.minor" contract version ("2.0"). The tool refuses a different major, or a minor below the one it needs minToolVersion string oldest app version that may read this pack ("4.0.0"); an older app shows a full-screen block packId string the pack's name, e.g. "2026Q2-reest-20261008b". Packs are immutable: a changed pack gets a new id previousPackId string | null the pack it was cut from, if any generatedAt, generatedBy string build time and builder panel.lastHistQuarter "YYYYQn" the common last historical quarter of the coupled panel ("2026Q2") blocs.<CC> object per economy: lastHistQuarter, qoyNext (seasonal phase of the first forecast quarter, null if no dummies), qoyNextEstimation, seasonalRows, shiftQuarters (quarters added after estimation; 0 in this pack), estimationEnd gvar.weights {path, sha256, bytes} the trade-weights file the coupled solve uses gvar.coupling {path, sha256, bytes, inputs:{weightsSha256, companionSig}} the coupling artifact and the weights it was built from (pack-verify requires inputs.weightsSha256 = gvar.weights.sha256; the app ignores a mismatched coupling) files.<logical> {path, sha256, bytes, inherit?} every file of the pack (1,997 in this pack). For .gz files the hash is of the compressed bytes. inherit: true appears only in an update pack: the file is taken from the app's built-in pack, and only if that copy has the same hash and size delta object, optional update packs only: the built-in pack they were cut against (basePackId) and how many files they ship / reuse

Where the bytes come from. On the web, from <base path>/data/. In the desktop app, from the pack built into the app — unless the user's data folder (<appDataDir>/gmaps-data, opened by Settings → Data pack → Open data folder) contains a manifest.json, in which case that folder is used, with the same checks. Rollback = delete that manifest.json. Full user and maintainer guide: UPDATE_MANUAL.md.

Dating. When the manifest loads, dates.setPanelDates(manifest) sets each economy's last historical quarter from blocs.<CC>.lastHistQuarter (§7) and checks each seasonal economy's qoyNext against the tool's own recomputation — a mismatch stops the load. There is no compiled date in the tool.

docs.title: 2.1 The data space (log / lin)
docs.text:
Every variable has a transformation:

transformation stored as chart display "log" 100·log(level) q/q annualised growth = 4·Δ(100·log level) "lin" the level itself (rates, ratios, %-of-GDP, sentiment indices) the level as-is
  • *.json files in display/growth space (baseline.json, historical.json) carry the already-differenced 4·Δ(100·log level) for log vars and the level for lin vars.
  • *_levels.json files carry 100·log(level) for log vars and the level for lin vars (this is the "level space" that feeds the fiscal recursion, the GVAR solver, and the level-display fans).

This is the single most bug-prone convention in the codebase — a stray ×4 or /100 between the two spaces diverges forecasts silently. The canary test scenario-scale-convention.test.ts pins it.

docs.title: 2.2 The 6-significant-figure compaction
docs.text:
Precision depends on how a bloc's files reach the app. In the deployed pack the 35 coupled GVAR blocs are copied raw from the estimator's export, at full double precision (docs/reest-2026/runs/port_to_app.sh step 1; e.g. US betahat[0][0] = 3.6855229634904627). The 17 euro members go through pipeline/port_gvar_exports.py, and those eight per-bloc files are rounded to 6 significant figures and serialised as compact JSON (separators=(",",":"), no whitespace) by pipeline/port_gvar_exports.py (sig6 → float(f"{x:.6g}"), recursing through lists/dicts via compact). The compacted set is exactly the FILES list in that script: spec.json, companion_mean.json, companion_draws.json, historical.json, historical_levels.json, baseline.json, baseline_levels.json, transformations.json. Integers, None, strings, booleans, and ±inf/NaN pass through (0/±inf/NaN map to 0/themselves). So in a member's files expect values like 4.16884, -5.50528 (AT) — never full double precision. Do not assume either precision when validating; read the file.

coupling_default.json.gz is also 6-sigfig: its builder (app/scripts/precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs) rounds M/invImM/rhoSpectral with round6 = x => Number(x.toPrecision(6)) before gzip.

Two more files are NOT 6-sigfig — they are written full precision by their own builders and are not in port_gvar_exports.py's FILES:

  • fiscal_meta.json — built with the panel by pipeline/sources/build_panel.py (derived.fiscal4; pipeline/country_rawdata/fiscal_meta_<CC>.json, members in pipeline/euro_redesign_staging/<CC>/), then d0 is rolled to the panel end by app/scripts/roll_d0_forward.mjs; d0 is full double precision, sfaDefault has 3 decimals.
  • weights_24bloc.json — all 35 receiver rows carry full double precision.

Do not assume 6-sigfig when validating these two files.

docs.title: 2.3 Variable ids, blocks, isFinancial
docs.text:
Variable ids are stable string keys (e.g. GDPH, POLRATE, HICP_EA, GLB_OIL, ROWDEM_US). Suffixes encode role:

  • GLB_* — a global common (the 4 US-determined commons, ids GLB_OIL/GLB_USLR/GLB_USBAA/GLB_USEQ). These ids are shared across the 35 GVAR blocs (US, EA, JP, …). The 17 euro members carry no global columns.
  • ROW{DEM,INF,FIN}_<CC> — a GVAR bloc's 3 trade-weighted stars.
  • ROWEA_{GDP,HICP}_<CC> — a euro member's 2 rest-of-euro-area aggregates (block:'row').
  • _<CC> on a domestic var (GDP_EA, RATE_DE) — the country's own series.

Each variable also carries a block tag that drives the GVAR/fiscal topology (read at runtime by configureGVARTopology / deriveBlocIdx in gvarSolve.ts — never hardcode indices):

block meaning where it appears domestic the bloc's own endogenous macro/financial vars every model fiscal the 4 fiscal drivers {FREV_GDP, FPEXP_GDP, EFFI, SFA} the 41 economies with a fiscal block (24 GVAR blocs + all 17 euro members) row GVAR: the 3 trade-weighted stars ROW{DEM,INF,FIN}_<CC>; euro member: the 2 rest-of-euro-area aggregates ROWEA_{GDP,HICP}_<CC> all 35 GVAR blocs (incl. endogenous US) and all 17 members global the 4 US-determined commons (oil, US 10y, US Baa, US equity) the 35 GVAR blocs (as GLB_*) external euro-area-shared regressors (e.g. for AT: POLRATE_AT, EACORP, RATE_AT, YIELD10_DE) the 17 euro members

History: until the euro-member redesign the members were "FSAP standalones" with global columns under US ids (WTI_US, …) and a us block. No shipped spec uses those any more.

A bloc is GVAR-active iff its spec.json carries the 3 block:'row' stars and it has a row in weights_24bloc.json (euro members have neither). The US is endogenous iff its spec carries the 3 ROW*_US stars and the weights file has a US row — this sets the module flag US_ENDOGENOUS. See ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI.md §5/§5a.

isFinancial (boolean) flags financial variables (rates, spreads, FX, equity, house prices, leverage, oil). It drives display units and the COVID treatment (financials are kept observed through 2020Q2–Q4 while macro vars are masked).

docs.title: 2.4 Exchange rates — one direction everywhere (rise = appreciation)
docs.text: Every exchange-rate variable in the published data — NEER_<CC> in each economy, the US FXTWM, and China's real index REER_CN — is an effective exchange-rate index of the domestic currency: a rise is an appreciation, a fall is a depreciation, in every economy. Sources: BIS broad nominal index (WS_EER), IMF (EER; AU, CL, CR, NZ) and Eurostat (ert_eff_ic_q, 42 partners; the euro-area members) — all quote the index this way; the direction was verified on the data (see pipeline/sources/registry/README.md, Conventions). Until the 2026 re-estimation, NEER_CA and NEER_EA were in fact bilateral rates against the US dollar (domestic currency per dollar: a rise was a depreciation); data packs from the 2026 re-estimation on use the harmonised direction for every economy. In log space a 1-unit move is a 1% appreciation (positive) or depreciation (negative).

docs.title: 3. spec.json — the variable manifest
docs.text:
The authoritative list of variables in fixed column order. The engine reads n and the per-variable metadata; it is index-agnostic otherwise (resolves fiscal/GVAR columns by id, not position).

Field Type Shape Meaning n int scalar number of endogenous variables (= length of variables) variables array [n] one entry per variable, in column order variables[i].id string stable variable key (column identity) variables[i].name string human-readable label (for the UI dropdown) variables[i].transformation "log"|"lin" data-space (§2.1) variables[i].isFinancial bool financial-var flag (§2.3) variables[i].prior "RW"|"WN" prior-mean family on the own first lag (§3.1): "RW" = random walk (own-lag prior mean 1, the default); "WN" = stationary white-noise (own-lag prior mean 0 → mean-reverting). In the deployed growth-rate model "WN" marks real GDP, the headline price and the GDP deflator (estimated as growth rates) and the three fiscal GDP-ratios (FREV_GDP,FPEXP_GDP,SFA); everything else is "RW" variables[i].block string topology tag (§2.3) seasonalRows int scalar optional, top level (not per variable): 0 (legacy/default, absent) or 3 — the number of quarterly seasonal-dummy rows the estimator inserted into betahat for an NSA-seasonal bloc (§3.3). qoyNext int scalar optional, top level: quarter-of-year (1..4) of the first forecast row on the estimation grid. Present only when seasonalRows>0. The app ignores this value and recomputes the phase from its own date grid — see §3.3.

Example (US, n=40, abridged — first/price/fiscal/global/star columns — a non-contiguous selection; the shown entries are NOT columns 0…11):

{
  "n": 40,
  "seasonalRows": 0,
  "variables": [
    {"id":"GDPH","name":"Real Gross Domestic Product","transformation":"log","isFinancial":false,"prior":"WN","block":"domestic"},
    {"id":"JGDP","name":"Gross Domestic Product: Chain Price Index","transformation":"log","isFinancial":false,"prior":"WN","block":"domestic"},
    {"id":"GLB_USLR","name":"US 10Y Treasury yield (%)","transformation":"lin","isFinancial":true,"prior":"RW","block":"global"},
    {"id":"FREV_GDP","name":"Federal Receipts (% of GDP)","transformation":"lin","isFinancial":false,"prior":"WN","block":"fiscal"},
    {"id":"FPEXP_GDP","name":"Federal Primary Expenditure (% of GDP)","transformation":"lin","isFinancial":false,"prior":"WN","block":"fiscal"},
    {"id":"EFFI","name":"Federal Effective Interest Rate (% p.a.)","transformation":"lin","isFinancial":true,"prior":"RW","block":"fiscal"},
    {"id":"SFA","name":"Stock-Flow Adjustment (% of GDP)","transformation":"lin","isFinancial":false,"prior":"WN","block":"fiscal"},
    {"id":"GLB_OIL","name":"WTI crude oil, WTISPLC q-avg ($/bbl)","transformation":"log","isFinancial":true,"prior":"RW","block":"global"},
    {"id":"ROWDEM_US","name":"US RoW Demand","transformation":"lin","isFinancial":true,"prior":"RW","block":"row"},
    {"id":"ROWINF_US","name":"US RoW Inflation","transformation":"lin","isFinancial":true,"prior":"RW","block":"row"},
    {"id":"ROWFIN_US","name":"US RoW Fin","transformation":"lin","isFinancial":true,"prior":"RW","block":"row"}
  ]
}

The US carries the 4 globals as its own endogenous vars (cols where block:'global') plus its 3 ROW*_US stars (cols 37–39, block:'row') — this is what makes the US endogenous. A RoW bloc (EA, n=26) also carries the globals as its own columns; the coupled solve ties every bloc's copy to the single US-determined path. A euro member (DE, n=23) carries no globals and no trade-weighted stars: its foreign side is the external euro-area columns (POLRATE_DE, EACORP, RATE_DE) and the two rest-of-euro-area aggregates (ROWEA_GDP_DE, ROWEA_HICP_DE, block:'row').

docs.title: 3.1 The prior field — "RW" (default) vs "WN" (stationary fiscal ratios)
docs.text:
variables[i].prior selects the prior mean on each variable's own first lag in the GLP/Minnesota prior. It takes exactly two values:

prior own-first-lag prior mean implied behaviour who carries it "RW" 1 (random walk — the historical default) the series can drift at the long end (a unit-root prior centre) every other variable "WN" 0 (white noise — stationary) the series mean-reverts to its in-sample mean FREV_GDP, FPEXP_GDP, SFA (all 41 fiscal economies); and, in the deployed growth-rate model (BVAR_DIFF_GP=1), real GDP, the headline price (CPI/HICP; JGDP for the US) and DEFL_<CC> — these are estimated as quarterly growth rates, so it is their growth that mean-reverts

Growth-rate (DIFF_GP) columns. Under BVAR_DIFF_GP=1 (both deployed estimators, Oct 2026) the estimator first-differences real GDP and the price series to 4·Δ(100·log) and leaves every other column in levels. It exports the equivalent level VAR (one more lag — hence lags = 4 in the shipped files), so transformation stays "log" and the app's level-space engine is unchanged. The "WN" tag on those columns refers to the differenced series.

Why this exists. Under a pure "RW" prior the fiscal GDP-ratios (revenue, primary expenditure, stock-flow adjustment) inherited a unit-root centre and drifted over the 20-quarter projection — e.g. US federal receipts stuck at ~19% of GDP instead of reverting to their ~17.4% in-sample mean. Switching them to "WN" centres the own-lag prior at 0 so the ratios mean-revert to their sample means at the long horizon, which is the economically correct stationary behaviour for a bounded share-of-GDP. EFFI (the effective interest rate) stays "RW" — it is a slow-moving level, not a bounded ratio. This change is committed (6f0161a/22250be/e38673a); at the time it was a no-op (byte-identical export) for the blocs without a fiscal block.

The mechanism (verified end-to-end in the estimator).

  1. Spec → pos. The MATLAB estimators read the per-variable prior string out of spec.json and build the index vector of stationary columns:
  2. pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m (statCols=find(Spec.Prior(keep)=="WN")', on the kept domestic block; stars are appended after and are always "RW").
  3. pipeline/export_bvar_euro_redesign.m (the 17 euro members; statCols = find(Prior=="WN")', plus the differenced GDP/price/deflator columns under BVAR_DIFF_GP). The older export_bvar_euro_fsap.m uses the same rule. Both resolve via a robust priorsfrom(...) helper (handles MATLAB's jsondecode dropping a prior field that is present on only some variables; absent → all-"RW").
  4. pos → cgl_bvarV5. statCols is threaded as the 3rd positional argument (stationary) of BVAR/MFBVAR/cgl_bvarV5.m, where pos=stationary (line 19) and passed on as 'pos',pos to bvarGLPmf.
  5. pos → prior mean = 0. In BVAR/MFBVAR/GLPreplicationWeb/bvarGLPmf.m the own-first-lag prior block is built from diagb: 
    diagb=ones(n,1);
diagb(pos)=0;            % zero the own-first-lag prior mean for the WN columns
b(2:n+1,:)=diag(diagb);  % default columns keep prior mean 1 (random walk)
    So a "WN" column gets own-lag prior mean 0 (stationary); every other column keeps 1 (the random-walk centre). A bloc with no "WN" column has pos=[], so diagb=ones(...) unchanged → identical to the historical default.
  6. Round-trip. On export each estimator re-stamps the per-variable prior back into spec.json from statCols (if any(statCols==i), v.prior='WN'; else v.prior='RW'), so the shipped spec always reflects the prior actually used.

Deployed prior assignment for the fiscal block (verified in the live specs — identical in all 41 fiscal economies):

Variable block prior rationale FREV_GDP (revenue % GDP) fiscal "WN" bounded ratio → mean-revert FPEXP_GDP (primary expenditure % GDP) fiscal "WN" bounded ratio → mean-revert SFA (stock-flow adjustment % GDP) fiscal "WN" bounded ratio → mean-revert EFFI (effective interest rate % p.a.) fiscal "RW" slow-moving level, not a bounded share everything else (macro, financial, stars, globals) any "RW" random-walk default

docs.title: 3.2 The isFinancial flag — coherence audit
docs.text:
isFinancial (§2.3) gates two things: the chart display units and the COVID treatment — financial variables are kept observed through the 2020Q2–Q4 data-augmentation window, while macro variables (and the two macro stars ROWDEM/ROWINF) are masked and DK-completed (Durbin–Koopman simulation smoother). A miscoded flag therefore changes both the picture and the estimate.

Two coherence fixes are baked into the deployed specs (verified across all blocs):

  • GLB_USEQ (US equity) and GLB_OIL (oil) are isFinancial:true everywhere. Both are market-priced and continued trading through 2020 — keeping them observed (not imputed) through the COVID window is the correct treatment. (The earlier GLB_OIL:isFinancial=false was incoherent and has been corrected.)
  • Canada's IP_CA is a log-LEVEL. It is now transformation:"log", isFinancial:false, block:"domestic" — a proper 100·log(level) series (its q/q annualised growth is the 4·Δ display form), not a level-vs-growth mismatch. Since the Oct 2026 rebuild it is the OECD monthly production index (DF_INDSERV, quarterly average), per pipeline/sources/registry/CA.json; earlier it was the discontinued FRED level index chained forward with growth.

All 1048 variables across the deployed blocs were audited for transformation · prior · isFinancial coherence; a per-economy variable table now lives in the user manual.

docs.title: 3.3 The seasonalRows / qoyNext fields — quarterly seasonal dummies (NSA blocs)
docs.text:
Blocs with not-seasonally-adjusted (NSA) series (NSA HICP/CPI, unemployment LR, house prices, India GOV, UK/KR SFA, and every even-interest bloc) are estimated with deterministic quarterly seasonal dummies so the within-year cycle is a bounded deterministic term rather than a spurious near-Nyquist companion root. Two top-level fields record this on the shipped bloc files:

File · field Values Meaning spec.json.seasonalRows 0 (absent/legacy) or 3 number of quarterly-dummy rows the estimator added spec.json.qoyNext 1..4 (present only when seasonalRows>0) quarter-of-year of the first forecast row on the estimation grid (mod(qlast,4)+1) companion_mean.json.seasonalRows 0 (absent/legacy) or 3 the SAME count, so betahat can be sliced (§4)

Which blocs carry seasonalRows=3 (set by pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m GVAR_DUMMY_BLOCS + pipeline/export_bvar_euro_redesign.m EURO_DUMMY_MEMBERS; the Oct 2026 runs are in docs/reest-2026/runs/): in pack 2026Q2-reest-20261008b, 34 economies — the 17 coupled blocs {CL, CN, CO, CR, EA, HK, ID, IN, IS, JP, KR, MX, NO, PE, TR, UK, ZA} and all 17 euro members. The manifest lists them (blocs.<CC>.seasonalRows). Every other bloc ships seasonalRows=0 (or omits it) and uses the layout without dummy rows.

Effect on the betahat row layout (§4). A seasonal bloc's betahat has k = 1 + seasonalRows + n·lags rows: row 0 = constant, rows 1..3 = the γ_Q2/γ_Q3/γ_Q4 quarterly-dummy coefficients (Q1 base), rows 4..k−1 = the lags blocks of n lag coefficients. The dummy rows are inserted between the constant and the lags — a consumer that assumes lag coefficients start at row 1 would read the wrong columns, which is why seasonalRows is shipped alongside betahat. For a legacy bloc (seasonalRows=0) the layout is the historical k = 1 + n·lags with lags at row 1.

The app RECOMPUTES qoyNext; it does NOT trust the one in spec.json. A within-year data shift moves the app's display origin past the estimation grid (by shiftQuarters in the manifest), so after a shift spec.json.qoyNext is behind what the forecast needs. The runtime always derives the phase from its own date grid via dates.qoyNextOf(country) (quarter after lastHistOf, wrapped 1..4; lastHistOf comes from the pack manifest) and feeds it to BVARParams.qoyNext. When the manifest loads, setPanelDates also compares that value with the manifest's declared blocs.<CC>.qoyNext and stops the load on a mismatch. In pack 2026Q2-reest-20261008b no quarter was shifted (shiftQuarters = 0), so all three agree. See ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI.md §5·EM.s and MODULES.md (kalman.ts).

docs.title: 4. companion_mean.json — posterior-mean VAR
docs.text:
The posterior-mean reduced-form VAR(lags) coefficients and residual covariance. The constant (intercept) row is first — this matches kalman.ts's companion construction. Do not transpose.

Field Type Shape Meaning betahat number[][] [k][n], k = 1 + seasonalRows + n·lags coefficient matrix; row 0 = intercept, then seasonalRows quarterly-dummy rows (0 or 3), then lags blocks of n own/cross lags; column j = equation for variable j sigmahat number[][] [n][n] residual covariance (symmetric, PD) n int scalar number of variables (matches spec.n) lags int scalar VAR lag order seasonalRows int scalar optional: 0 (absent/legacy) or 3 quarterly seasonal-dummy rows inserted between the intercept and the lags (§3.3). Absent ⇒ treat as 0.

k = 1 + seasonalRows + n·lags. For a seasonalRows=0 bloc this is the historical n·lags + 1 (US, non-seasonal, in the deployed pack: 40·4 + 1 = 161); a seasonalRows=3 bloc adds the three dummy rows (e.g. EA, which is in the seasonal set: 1 + 3 + 26·4 = 108). Always compute k from the file's own seasonalRows (absent ⇒ 0), never assume n·lags + 1.

Example (US shapes & first values, pack 2026Q2-reest-20261008b):

{
  "betahat": [
    [3.6855229634904627, 0.20334889999965236, -7.2726999385650455, "… 40 cols"],  // row 0 = intercept
    ["… lag-1 coefficients …"],                                                   // row 1 = lag-1 of var 0, etc.
    "… 161 rows total (1 + 40·4) …"
  ],
  "sigmahat": [ ["… 40×40 …"] ],
  "n": 40,
  "lags": 4
}

docs.title: 5. companion_draws.json.gz — flat posterior draws
docs.text:
The full posterior sample, stored as flat row-major arrays (boxed number[] in JSON; converted to Float64Array on load), shipped gzipped — the pack lists only the .gz, and its hash is of the compressed bytes. Lazy-loaded; the US .gz is about 29 MB.

Field Type Shape Meaning n_draws int scalar number of posterior draws (currently 500) n int scalar variables lags int scalar lag order beta_shape int[3] [k, n, n_draws] shape of the flattened beta (k = 1 + seasonalRows + n·lags; the draws file carries no explicit seasonalRows field — the app infers it as beta_shape[0] − (1 + n·lags), so a seasonal bloc's beta_shape[0] is 3 larger, §3.3) beta number[] k·n·n_draws flattened coefficient draws sigma_shape int[3] [n, n, n_draws] shape of the flattened sigma sigma number[] n·n·n_draws flattened covariance draws

Flat indexing (column-major within the 3-D shape, matching ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI.md §6):

beta[ draw*k*n  + j*k + i ]     // draw, equation column j, coef row i
sigma[ draw*n*n + j*n + i ]     // draw, (i,j) of the n×n covariance

Example (US, decompressed):

{
  "n_draws": 500,
  "n": 40,
  "lags": 4,
  "beta_shape": [161, 40, 500],
  "beta": [2.1346969787685293, 0.6328602990834148, 0.1826483603167455, "… 3 220 000 doubles …"],
  "sigma_shape": [40, 40, 500],
  "sigma": ["… 800 000 doubles …"]
}

docs.title: 6. baseline.json / baseline_levels.json — the baseline fan
docs.text:
The unconditional baseline forecast and its predictive bands, over the projection horizon H (currently 20 quarters). Two files, identical shape, different space:

  • baseline.json — display/growth space (§2.1).
  • baseline_levels.json — level space (feeds the fiscal block, the GVAR solver, and the level-display fans).
Field Type Shape Meaning mean number[][] [H][n] central path q05,q16,q84,q95 number[][] [H][n] predictive-band quantiles (5/16/84/95%) q50 number[][] [H][n] optional median; present in baseline_levels.json only, and only for the 17 euro members (AT, BE, DE, EE, ES, FI, FR, GR, IE, IT, LT, LU, LV, NL, PT, SI, SK). No baseline.json (display-space) carries q50, and the GVAR blocs (US/EA/JP/…) carry it in neither file — read defensively horizon int scalar H (= number of forecast quarters, e.g. 20)

Example (US, H=20, n=40):

{
  "mean": [ [1.70336, 2.96332, -21.5881, "… 40 cols"], "… 20 rows" ],
  "q16":  [ ["…"], "…" ],
  "q84":  [ ["…"], "…" ],
  "q05":  [ ["…"], "…" ],
  "q95":  [ ["…"], "…" ],
  "horizon": 20
}

baseline_levels.json has the same keys but in level space — e.g. mean[0] = [1010.69, 973.587, 673.278, …] (100·log levels for log vars; values rounded here).

docs.title: 7. historical.json / historical_levels.json — recent actuals
docs.text:
The last 40 quarters of data (in pack 2026Q2-reest-20261008b: 2016Q3–2026Q2 for every economy), used to anchor the charts. Two files, same shape, different space (display/growth vs level).

Field Type Shape Meaning firstQuarter string "YYYYQn" scalar historical_levels.json only — the calendar quarter of row 0. The last row's quarter is always derived: firstQuarter + rows − 1. It is the ONLY dating source (4.0): there is no separate "last quarter" label to keep in sync. data number[][] [n_periods][n] realised values, oldest → newest n_periods int scalar number of historical quarters (40 after a model export, +1 per within-year shift)

firstQuarter is written once, when the history is created: by app/scripts/stamp_calendar.mjs after a model export (npm run data:model-update — it derives the quarter from the estimation panel and refuses a bloc it cannot place). Every pipeline writer (refresh-quarter, nowcast_complete, member_extend) keeps it, so an appended row is dated automatically. pack-verify cross-checks the dating against the estimation panels (the calendar canary). Why: in Sep 2026 two re-exports reset the 35 GVAR histories to 40 rows ending 2025Q4 while the separate date label stayed at 2026Q1 — every chart was one quarter late and nothing failed. See docs/UPDATE_MANUAL.md.

Example (US, historical.json; the firstQuarter key is in historical_levels.json):

{
  "data": [
    [2.82754, 2.77285, 3.67354, "… 40 cols"],    // oldest quarter (2016Q3)
    "… 40 rows …",
    [2.19592, 3.69877, -0.416967, "… 40 cols"]   // newest quarter (2026Q2)
  ],
  "n_periods": 40
}

historical.json growth is already the 4·Δ(100·log level) form for log vars (no further differencing in the chart). historical_levels.json is the matching level path. A cell with no value in the file (unpublished, or a COVID-withheld macro quarter) is null, never 0. The last rows of a series that ends early are filled by the coupled nowcast and flagged in nowcast_provenance.json / coverage_manifest.json (imputedThrough, imputedQuarters), which is what draws them amber in the charts.

docs.title: 7.1 estimation_mask.json — cells the estimator drew as missing data
docs.text:
Written by the estimators under GVAR_NOFILL=1 (export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m estmask, export_bvar_euro_redesign.m) and shipped for every economy since the Oct 2026 re-estimation. It lists, per domestic variable, the panel cells the sampler did not see as data — so they are model estimates wherever they appear. The browser does not read it today (the amber marks come from coverage_manifest.json); it is provenance, and app/scripts/apply_member_completion.mjs reads the members' completedLast8.

Field Meaning bloc, firstQuarter, lastQuarter the estimation panel's span ("YYYY-Qn"; longer than the 40-row history) missing.<id>.{leading,interior,trailing} unpublished cells, by position in the series covidWithheld.<id> published macro cells withheld from estimation (2020Q2–Q4) completedLast8.<id> euro members only: [quarter, value] pairs — the model's completion of the missing cells in the last 8 quarters, in level space note members only: a one-line description

Example (US): "missing": {"UI": {"leading": [], "interior": ["2025-Q4"], "trailing": []}, …} — the BLS skipped October 2025, so 2025Q4 unemployment is a genuine gap the model drew.

docs.title: 8. transformations.json — per-variable space
docs.text:
A redundant, fast lookup of each variable's data space, aligned to spec.variables column order. (The same information is in spec.variables[i].transformation.)

Field Type Shape Meaning transformations string[] [n] "log" or "lin" per variable column

Example (US, abridged):

{"transformations":["log","log","log","log","log","log","log","log","log","log","log","log","log","log","lin","log","lin","log","log","lin","lin","lin","lin","lin","lin","lin","log","log","log","log","lin","log","log","lin","lin","lin","lin","log","lin","lin","lin"]}

docs.title: 9. fiscal_meta.json — fiscal-block parameters (41 economies)
docs.text:
Shipped by the 41 economies with a fiscal block (24 GVAR blocs + all 17 euro members; the list is blocs with a fiscal_meta.json entry in the pack manifest); for any other economy the file is absent and the loader yields null. It supplies the debt recursion's initial stock, default SFA, and the column indices the recursion reads from the level path (computeFiscalBlock in fiscalAccounting.ts). See fiscal-block-methodology.md and ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI.md §7 for the math.

Field Type Meaning d0 number initial debt-to-GDP ratio (%) at the projection seam (the last history quarter) d0_quarter "YYYY-Qn" the quarter d0 refers to ("2026-Q2" in the deployed pack) d0_observed, d0_observed_quarter number, "YYYY-Qn" 38 economies: the last published debt ratio and its quarter, kept when d0 was rolled forward d0_note string how d0 was rolled forward (same 38 economies) sfaDefault number default stock-flow adjustment (% of GDP) used by the app's debt projection — the historical mean of the SFA, excluding the COVID quarters idx object column indices into the level path (spec/*_levels column order) idx.gdp int real-GDP column idx.deflator int price column for nominal growth: the genuine GDP deflator DEFL_<CC> wherever the economy has one (38 of 41; decision D4, Oct 2026); otherwise JGDP (US), CPI_CN, CPI_NZ idx.revenue int FREV_GDP (revenue % GDP) column idx.primaryExp int FPEXP_GDP (primary-expenditure % GDP) column idx.effRate int EFFI (effective interest rate, % p.a.) column idx.sfa int SFA (stock-flow adjustment, % GDP) column

Where d0 comes from. The panel build (pipeline/sources/build_panel.py, derived.fiscal4) records the debt ratio at the last quarter with published debt. app/scripts/roll_d0_forward.mjs then rolls it to the panel's last quarter with the app's own budget identity on the completed history, keeping the published value in d0_observed*. Where a flow it uses is model-implied (nowcast), the rolled d0 is a model estimate. Example (AT): d0_observed = 82.66 at 2026-Q1, d0 = 83.18 at 2026-Q2.

The legacy idx.debtService key was removed; idx.sfa (the estimated SFA column) replaced it. With idx.sfa set and idx.debtService unset, computeFiscalBlock takes the effective-rate interest form and reads the per-quarter SFA from idx.sfa. Do not re-introduce debtService.

Values for the six largest fiscal economies (pack 2026Q2-reest-20261008b; read from the live files; NEVER hardcode indices — they are positional and DRIFT, see the gotcha below. d0 is rounded here — the file stores it full precision):

Bloc n d0 sfaDefault idx {gdp,deflator,revenue,primaryExp,effRate,sfa} deflator id US 40 124.18 1.753 {0, 7, 32, 33, 34, 35} JGDP EA 26 88.96 0.187 {0, 7, 18, 19, 20, 21} DEFL_EA JP 27 190.26 −0.94 {0, 8, 17, 18, 19, 20} DEFL_JP UK 28 102.58 0.234 {0, 9, 19, 20, 21, 22} DEFL_UK CA 28 111.00 3.106 {0, 9, 19, 20, 21, 22} DEFL_CA CN 22 101.39 3.247 {0, 1, 13, 14, 15, 16} CPI_CN

🔴 STALE-POSITIONAL-INDEX gotcha. These idx values are positional offsets into the level path, so any change to a bloc's variable ORDER or COUNT silently re-points them at the wrong columns. History: the 33-bloc refit once sent EA's effRate onto the equity index (~537) and d·(1+effRate/400) exploded the EA debt path. Two safeguards now: (1) pipeline/port_gvar_exports.py regenerates fiscal_meta.json (and external_meta.json, §9.1) by variable id after every port; (2) blocs copied raw (the 35 GVAR blocs in the Oct 2026 chain) need node pipeline/fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs, which re-resolves all six indices by id (FREV_GDP/FPEXP_GDP/EFFI/SFA, gdp=0, deflator=DEFL_<CC> else the first HICP|CPI|JGDP|PGDP) and keeps every other field; idempotent. The tests fiscal-meta-indices.test.ts (debt paths bounded) and data/meta-column-indices.test.ts (every index points at the right variable family) block stale indices.

Example (US):

{"d0":124.18119030476353,"d0_quarter":"2026-Q2","sfaDefault":1.753,"idx":{"gdp":0,"deflator":7,"revenue":32,"primaryExp":33,"effRate":34,"sfa":35}}

CN's idx.gdp (GDP_CN) is real GDP (since the 2026-06 CN-only re-estimate), so the fiscal recursion gQ = Δ(idx.gdp) + Δ(idx.deflator) is real growth plus price growth, as for the other economies. CN's price column is CPI (no quarterly GDP deflator is used for CN). The column counts above (n) reflect the live specs; treat them as data, not constants.

docs.title: 9.1 external_meta.json — external-accounts satellite (47 economies)
docs.text:
Read by externalAccounting.ts (net foreign assets, current account). Like fiscal_meta.json it stores positional column indices, so since the Oct 2026 re-estimation it also stores the variable ids they must point at:

Field Meaning idx {exports, imports, gdp, deflator, fx} column indices (+ non-index keys such as gdpIsNominal) idxIds the variable id each index must resolve to, e.g. US {exports:"XH", imports:"MH", gdp:"GDPH", deflator:"JGDP", fx:"FXTWM"} nfa0, iNFA, fxShare, caAnchor, … satellite parameters and provenance (fxShare = 0 everywhere today: the FX valuation channel is off)

port_gvar_exports.py re-resolves idx from idxIds on every port (and stops if an id is missing); pipeline/fix_external_meta_indices.mjs does the same for blocs copied raw. Why: the Oct 2026 data inserted DEFL_<CC> ahead of the exchange rate in 35 blocs and their fx index pointed at house prices, unemployment or a bond yield until it was fixed by id (no numerical effect, because fxShare = 0; docs/reest-2026/REVIEW.md §6).

docs.title: 10. weights_24bloc.json — GVAR trade-weight matrix & topology source
docs.text:
The single source of GVAR topology: the bloc list and the row-normalised bilateral trade-weight matrix that builds each bloc's trade-weighted stars and the cross-country coupling. The filename is stale — it holds 35 blocs, not 24 (US first, with a US row that activates the endogenous-US coupling). Its content is identical to weights_full_38.json, the file the Oct 2026 estimation read.

How the tool gets it. At runtime gvarLoader.loadGVARModels fetches it from the data pack (hash-checked; the manifest names it in gvar.weights) and passes it to configureGVARTopology, so a re-weighting of existing blocs takes effect without a new app version. gvarSolve.ts also imports a build-time copy, which is used only (a) to configure a default topology at module load and in tests, (b) as the fallback if the fetch fails, and (c) for the compiled list of candidate blocs (GVAR_BLOC_CANDIDATES) — so a pack can update the blocs the app was built with but cannot add a new one.

Field Type Shape Meaning source string provenance (IMF IMTS bilateral X+M, 2021–2023 average, from weights_timevarying.json) window string averaging window ("2021-2023 average") blocs string[] [35] the candidate bloc list, US first (= GVAR_BLOC_CANDIDATES) weights object 35 keys the matrix: weights[receiver][partner] = w, zero diagonal, each receiver row sums to 1 over its partners

(Earlier versions of the file also carried indicators, euro_area_code, bloc_codes and note; the deployed one has only the four fields above.)

The weights matrix is keyed by receiver bloc (35 rows, including a US row); each row maps partner code → weight and is row-normalised (zero diagonal, sums to 1). At config time configureGVARTopology renormalises each row over the blocs that are actually deployed/active.

Example (abridged):

{
  "source": "IMF IMTS bilateral X+M, 2021-2023 average, 38-bloc set (…). Row-normalized, zero diagonal, <0.05% dropped. From weights_timevarying.json.",
  "window": "2021-2023 average",
  "blocs": ["US","EA","JP","UK","CA","CN", "… 35 total"],
  "weights": {
    "US": {"EA":0.172788, "MX":0.165043, "CA":0.164823, "CN":0.142355, "JP":0.048899, "…": "…"},
    "EA": {"US":0.157679, "CN":0.144444, "UK":0.096806, "PL":0.085059, "CH":0.066849, "…": "…"}
  }
}

Other weight files in gvar/ (weights_full.json, weights_49.json, weights.json, weights_full_38.json, weights_timevarying.json, .bak*) are estimation inputs or alternate-panel artifacts; the live topology source is weights_24bloc.json (the one named in the manifest's gvar.weights).

docs.title: 11. coupling_default.json.gz — precomputed GVAR coupling
docs.text:
The gzipped precomputed cross-country coupling: the linear-system matrix M and its BLAS-computed inverse (I − M)⁻¹ for the empty/baseline pin structure. Building/inverting M at this scale is many minutes in-browser (the in-JS O(dim³) inverse at dim≈2060 is ~46 min), so shipping this artifact is mandatory for interactivity, not optional. Read from the pack through fetchGzJSON (hash of the compressed bytes checked, then decompressed with the browser's DecompressionStream; there is no plain .json fallback). The manifest records which weights it was built from (gvar.coupling.inputs.weightsSha256); if that differs from the served weights' hash, gvarLoader drops the artifact and the solver recomputes rather than use a stale inverse.

Field Type Shape Meaning modelSig string model signature keying the artifact to the deployed data (see below) pinStructure string the pin-structure signature this artifact was built for — "" (empty/baseline) for the shipped one dim int scalar augmented-state dimension (currently 2180: 35 coupled blocs, endogenous US) rhoSpectral number scalar spectral radius ρ(M) (the live coupling_default.json.gz reads 0.971875 < 1; it moves with each refit — what matters is < 1) M number[][] [dim][dim] the coupling matrix (6-sigfig) invImM number[][] [dim][dim] (I − M)⁻¹, the BLAS-computed inverse (6-sigfig)

modelSig is built by gvarSignature(raw) (gvarLoader.ts): for each qualified bloc c, "{c}:{n}_{lags}_{horizon}_{b0}_{bM}_{s0}" where b0 = betahat[0][0], bM = betahat[n·lags][n-1], s0 = sigmahat[0][0] (each in toExponential(6) form), joined with "|". So a change to any bloc's data changes modelSig and invalidates the artifact — it must be regenerated. At solve time (runGvarSolve.ts) the hydrated inverse is used only if art.modelSig === gvarSignature(raw) and the request's pin-structure signature matches art.pinStructure; otherwise the solver rebuilds.

Header example (values are real; matrices abridged):

{
  "modelSig": "US:40_4_20_3.685523e+0_0.000000e+0_7.607104e-2|EA:26_4_20_1.703399e+0_0.000000e+0_1.271297e-1|…",
  "pinStructure": "",
  "dim": 2180,
  "rhoSpectral": 0.971875,
  "M": [ ["… 2180 cols …"], "… 2180 rows …" ],
  "invImM": [ ["… 2180 cols …"], "… 2180 rows …" ]
}

Regenerate (mandatory after any data change) from app/:

npx vite-node scripts/precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs

This builds M for the empty pin structure, inverts it via MATLAB BLAS (invert_coupling.m), and writes the gzip. gvar-coupling-artifact.test.ts asserts the shipped .gz hydrates and matches a fresh build (a canary that blocks deploy on drift).

Spectral radius by panel size (context, not a contract): 6-bloc pilot ρ≈0.59; 24-bloc frozen-anchor ρ≈0.72–0.73 (dim 1380 = 23·3·20); 33-bloc endogenous-US ρ≈0.92–0.95 (dim 2060; artifacts of Jun–Sep 2026); the Sep 2026 35-bloc model ρ=0.957724; the deployed Oct 2026 genuine-data re-estimation ρ=0.971875 (dim 2180). The value moves with each refit; what is load-bearing is that it stays < 1 (precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs prints it; the maintainer checks it before shipping — the script does not stop on its own). Only the last figure describes the live artifact.

docs.title: 12. Validating a freshly ported bloc
docs.text:
A quick sanity pass when adding or re-porting a bloc (paths absolute under app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/):

  1. spec.n === companion_mean.n === companion_draws.n, and length(spec.variables) === n.
  2. companion_mean.betahat is [1 + seasonalRows + n·lags][n]; sigmahat is [n][n] (seasonalRows = companion_mean.seasonalRows else spec.seasonalRows else 0; §3.3).
  3. companion_draws.beta_shape === [1 + seasonalRows + n·lags, n, n_draws] (same seasonalRows, inferred from beta_shape[0] on the draws side); sigma_shape === [n, n, n_draws]; length(beta) === product(beta_shape); length(sigma) === product(sigma_shape).
  4. baseline.mean and baseline_levels.mean are [horizon][n] with all of q05/q16/q84/q95 present (q50 optional).
  5. historical.data and historical_levels.data are [n_periods][n].
  6. transformations.transformations has length n and matches spec.variables[i].transformation.
  7. A fiscal bloc additionally ships fiscal_meta.json with all six idx keys in range [0, n) AND each idx resolving to the correct variable id (idx.revenue → FREV_GDP, etc.); likewise external_meta.json (idx = idxIds).
