docs.text: Constant Value Site Purpose Ridge λ 1e-8 · mean(diag G) decompose conditions the normal equations; removed to O(1e-15) by the two refinement sweeps Column-norm floor 1e-12 decompose a near-zero response column keeps scale 1, so it stays inert rather than being amplified Rank pivot tolerance 1e-12 · max(diag) thetaRank full-rank vs rank-deficient models are ~20 orders of magnitude apart in conditioning Collinearity threshold 0.95 index build (index.collinearThreshold) \|cos\| between unit-normalised stacked 3-obs H = 12 paths Usable-shock floor 1e-9 index build a shock whose stacked 3-obs path has smaller norm is dropped and named (SW07 em, CMR14 e_term) Licence criterion 1e-6 benches + build-time scan worst contribution-path recovery error a configuration may show

docs.title: Example 1 (Decompose a US scenario at the licensed configuration)
docs.text:
We decompose the displayed US scenario through the SW07 lens at the one configuration the class view is licensed in: the three locked observables plus the four addable natives, and all seven usable shocks named. We proceed in steps. First we measure the observable rows off the level-deviation panel, then we call the solver. The seven-observable set makes the system square at q·H = 84, so the regime comes back exact-fit and the residual is identically zero.

import {
  DRIVERS_H, decompose, commonObservablePaths, nativeObservablePath,
  NATIVE_OBS_BY_MODEL, meToWeight, type DecomposeObservable,
} from '@/lib/compute/driversDecomp'

// levelDev: [t][j] scenario-minus-baseline in smoother level space (100·log for log vars)
// specIds:  the bloc's spec variable ids, in column order
const idx = { outputIdx: cGDPH, inflationIdx: cJGDP, rateIdx: cPOLRATE }
const common = commonObservablePaths(levelDev, idx, DRIVERS_H)

const rows: DecomposeObservable[] = [
  { key: 'output',     irfField: 'output',     path: common.output },
  { key: 'inflationq', irfField: 'inflationq', path: common.inflationq },
  { key: 'interest',   irfField: 'interest',   path: common.interest },
]
const map = NATIVE_OBS_BY_MODEL['US_SW07'].map
for (const k of ['dc', 'dinve', 'dw', 'labobs']) {
  const p = nativeObservablePath(k, levelDev, specIds, DRIVERS_H, map)   // null off the US bloc
  if (p) rows.push({ key: k, irfField: k, path: p, weight: meToWeight(1) })
}

const d = decompose(irf, ['interest_', 'eb', 'fiscal_', 'eqs', 'ea', 'epinf', 'ew'], rows, DRIVERS_H)
// d.rows === 84, d.rank === 84  ⇒  d.regime === 'exact-fit', d.residual ≡ 0
// d.contributions[k][o][t] : unit k's contribution to observable o at quarter t
// d.eps[k * DRIVERS_H + τ]  : the recovered shock sequence

Naming an eighth unit here would throw: the budget is seven (Remark 1).

docs.title: Example 2 (Aggregate into classes and check the display identity)
docs.text:
We take the decomposition of Example 1, aggregate its seven shocks into the Monetary, Demand and Supply classes of the shipped class map, and transform the class paths into the units the Output panel draws. The check at the end is the additivity invariant the drawer's chart depends on.

import {
  classViewLicensed, aggregateContributions, obsDisplaySpec, toDisplayDev,
} from '@/lib/compute/driversDecomp'

classViewLicensed('US_SW07', d.observableKeys, d.shocks)      // true; false if any of the seven is dropped

const classMap = index.shockClasses!.models['US_SW07']         // class_maps.json, copied verbatim
const groups = ['Monetary', 'Demand', 'Supply'].map((c) => ({ id: c, label: c, members: classMap[c] }))
const { groups: kept, contributions } = aggregateContributions(d, groups)

const spec = obsDisplaySpec('output', idx, specIds, 'US_SW07')!   // { op: 'diff', scale: 4, … }
const bars = contributions.map((c) => toDisplayDev(spec, c[0]))   // observable 0 = output
const resid = toDisplayDev(spec, d.residual[0])
// Σ_g bars[g][t] + resid[t] === toDisplayDev(spec, d.z[0])[t]   to 1e-8  (test v3-2)

docs.title: Example 3 (Decompose an FRB/US path through collinearity clusters)
docs.text:
The two 54-shock FRB/US lenses are not separable shock by shock in the three common observables, so the drawer decomposes their empirical collinearity clusters instead. We build the composite columns, name the build-time validated default triple, and solve at three observables, where the budget is three. Naming a cluster names one column, so the budget counts clusters and not members.

import { buildClusterIRFs, decompose, DRIVERS_H } from '@/lib/compute/driversDecomp'

const meta = index.models['US_FRB22']                       // 54 shocks, 109 collinear pairs, 23 clusters
const clusterIrf = buildClusterIRFs(irf, meta.clusters!, DRIVERS_H)
const d = decompose(clusterIrf, meta.defaultNamed!, rows3, DRIVERS_H)
// meta.defaultNamed === ['hqlfpr', 'interest_', 'pcer_l'] — 19 of the 54 shocks covered
// rows3 = the three locked observables only ⇒ rows 36, rank 36, regime 'exact-fit'

The hqlfpr cluster contains fiscal_, so on this lens the fiscal shock is not separately nameable in cluster mode. Test v3-4 pins the default triple, cross-checks the shipped cluster partition against the shipped pair list as a set of sets, and confirms rank 36/36 on the three composite columns.

docs.title: What the tests pin
docs.text: The 26 licence tests live in app/src/__tests__/compute/drivers-decomp.test.ts (4), drivers-decomp-v2.test.ts (7) and drivers-decomp-v3.test.ts (15), all in the fast npm test suite. The engine-side invariants they carry: exact same-model recovery at ≤ 1e-6 for UK_SM11 at three observables and for US_SW07 at seven, through both the plain and the colnorm solver (tests 1, 2, v3-1a, v3-1b); the budget-rule throw (test 3); the measured 4.000 unit factors (test 4) and the CMR14 conventions (v2-3); display-unit additivity at 1e-8 for shocks (v2-1a) and classes (v3-2); the colnorm equal-split signature (v3-1c); the residual-able regime and an out-of-span residual share (v2-4, v2-5); the class licence on all three coordinates with a negative case per droppable shock (v3-3); the cluster partition and the validated default naming (v3-4); the index's shockClasses being class_maps.json verbatim, every shipped census file matching its recorded sha256, and index.horizonQuarters === DRIVERS_H (v3-5); the panel-side unit arithmetic (v3-6); and the rank arithmetic behind the addable / excluded observable split (v3-7).

docs.title: data/dataManifest.ts — the data pack (4.0.0)
docs.text:
Responsibility. The one place the tool touches data files. It reads the pack's manifest.json, checks it can use it, and serves every other file by its logical name, verified against the manifest. This is what keeps the data and the estimated model separate from the tool: nothing in the bundle assumes a particular pack.

Export Purpose loadManifest() / getManifest() load once (no-store), then: compatibility gate (schemaVersion major 2, minor ≥ the supported one; app version ≥ minToolVersion) → for an update pack, check every inherit file against the app's built-in manifest → setPanelDates(manifest). Failures throw (IncompatibleDataError for the gate). fetchVerified(logical) bytes of one file, checked for byte length and SHA-256 (of the compressed bytes for .gz); content-hash cache-busting on the web fetchJSON<T>(logical) / fetchGzJSON<T>(logical) verified + parsed (gzip via DecompressionStream; a browser without it gets a clear error) hasFile(logical) is the file in the pack (for optional files) getDataSource() / isTauriRuntime() / EXTERNAL_PACK_DIRNAME 'web' (<base path>/data, also the desktop's built-in pack) or 'external' (<appDataDir>/gmaps-data, used only when it holds a manifest.json)

The manifest's own fields are in DATA_SCHEMA.md §1.1. The pack is built and checked offline by app/scripts/pack-build.mjs and pack-verify.mjs (§ Build & test); the user/maintainer guide is UPDATE_MANUAL.md.

docs.title: dates.ts — panel dating from the pack
docs.text: setPanelDates(manifest) sets the panel's last historical quarter (panel.lastHistQuarter) and each economy's own quarter where it differs, then checks every seasonal economy's declared qoyNext against qoyNextOf (mismatch ⇒ throw). lastHistOf(country) throws if called before initialisation — there is deliberately no compiled fallback date (a stale compiled date mis-dated the charts in Sep 2026). qoyNextOf, offsetLabel, offsetYQ keep their signatures. Tests initialise the dates in a setup file; Node scripts initialise them from the pack manifest.

docs.title: data/loader.ts
docs.text:
Responsibility. Per-country single-bloc JSON fetch, plus the DSGE catalog/IRF loaders. Every data file goes through dataManifest.ts (loadJSON = fetchJSON), so it is hash-checked and read from the active source.

Function Returns loadJSON<T>(path) dataManifest.fetchJSON(path): look up, fetch, verify, parse; throws on a missing or mismatched file loadBVARData(country) { spec, companion, baseline, historical, companionDraws: null, baselineLevels, historicalLevels, fiscalMeta, externalMeta }. baseline_levels / historical_levels / fiscal_meta / external_meta are optional (missing → null). companion_draws is not fetched here (loaded lazily). loadCompanionDraws(country, expect?) the heavy draws file, companion_draws.json.gz (verified + gunzipped; no plain-JSON fallback). Converts beta/sigma from boxed number[] to Float64Array once (faster indexing + memcpy into the worker). A failure → null; a shape that does not match the mean companion is warned and left to the caller's band guard. loadDSGECatalog() / loadModelIRFs(modelName, ruleName) DSGE catalog + per-rule IRFs loadDriversIndex() Promise<DriversIndex> — the Drivers model menu, dsge/census/index.json loadDriversModelIRFs(file) Promise<any> — one menu model's IRF file, file being the index entry's site-absolute file field (the leading /data/ is stripped before the fetch)

The draws cache is a bounded LRU (_DRAWS_CACHE_MAX = 4): each companion_draws is ~7–26 MB, so browsing all 52 economies would otherwise retain hundreds of MB; eviction is transparent (a miss re-fetches).

docs.title: The Drivers index (DriversIndex / DriversModelMeta)
docs.text:
loadDriversIndex fetches the menu the Drivers drawer is built from — one file, 36 KB, produced by app/scripts/build_drivers_index.mjs (below). The top level carries schema ("gmaps-drivers-index/1"), horizonQuarters (12, asserted equal to DRIVERS_H by test v3-5), commonObservables (the three locked keys), collinearThreshold (0.95), the verbatim copy of pipeline/_shockbench/class_maps.json under shockClasses, and models. Two fields the generator writes are not declared on the TS interface and are simply ignored: generated (the build date) and note (a prose provenance line).

Each models[name] entry is a DriversModelMeta:

  • file — the site-absolute path the drawer fetches, e.g. /data/dsge/census/UK_SM11.json.
  • source — the repository path the file came from.
  • title (optional) — the menu display name; used by the FRB/US entries.
  • sourceNote (optional) — "MMB rule file" or "MMB census run".
  • sha256 / sha256Source — the content hash and where it came from: pipeline/census_irfs/MANIFEST.json for the eight census entries, the hash of the shipped SW.json for the four indexed out of the irfs tree. Test v3-5 re-hashes every shipped file.
  • shocks — the usable shocks: all three common observables present and stacked H = 12 norm ≥ 1e-9.
  • dropped — { shock, reason } for anything excluded; the reasons in use are zero-response and missing-observable. The drawer names them in the lens row rather than hiding them.
  • hasOutput — whether the model exposes an output observable; a false value disables the menu entry. Every shipped entry is true.
  • collinearPairs — { a, b, cos }, cos rounded to six decimals.
  • menuHidden (optional) — true for US_FRB22_mcap only, which stays in the index because the v2 licence fixtures use it.
  • classMapKey (optional) — the shockClasses.models record to use when it differs from the index key; the three FRB22 entries point at US_FRB22_mcap.
  • clusters (optional) — { id, label, members }, present only for US_FRB22 and US_FRB22_var.
  • defaultNamed (optional) — the build-time validated default cluster naming, clustered models only.

What is fetched when. The index once per session, on the first drawer open; the chosen model's IRF file on model selection, cached per model for the session. Both go through loadJSON, a plain fetch with no client-side decompression — unlike companion_draws, these files are not shipped gzipped. The default lens therefore costs 36 KB plus a 215 KB IRF file; selecting either 54-shock FRB/US lens costs a further ~10.7 MB, which is why the drawer records a per-model fetch failure and offers an explicit Retry rather than looping.

docs.title: data/gvarLoader.ts
docs.text:
Responsibility. Multi-bloc GVAR bundle fetch + self-configuring topology, all through the data pack. Fetches the trade weights from the pack first, tries every candidate bloc in GVAR_BLOC_CANDIDATES (the build-time weights_24bloc.json list, US first; 35 in the deployed pack), tolerates missing blocs, and keeps a bloc iff its spec carries block:'row' stars (US always kept). The qualifying set re-configures the solver topology via configureGVARTopology with the fetched weights.

Export Purpose GVAR_COUNTRIES active GVAR codes, US first; mutated in place by qualifyGVARRaw isGvarCountry(country) the single GVAR-membership predicate loadGVARModels() fetches the weights, the 4 engine files per bloc (companion_mean, historical_levels, baseline_levels, spec) — not the heavy companion_draws — plus the coupling artifact (missing → null) → GVARModelsRaw. Drops the coupling if the manifest says it was built from weights other than those served (gvar.coupling.inputs.weightsSha256 ≠ gvar.weights.sha256) qualifyGVARRaw(raw) configures topology + drops non-qualifying blocs; idempotent gvarSignature(raw) cheap stable signature (codes, n, lags, horizon, a few betahat/sigmahat entries) keying the model + coupling caches buildGVARCountryModels(raw) builds (and caches by signature) the CountryModels; each runs the unconditional smoother once

loadCouplingArtifact() reads the gzipped coupling_default.json.gz through fetchGzJSON (hash-checked, decompressed via the native DecompressionStream — the plain JSON exceeds GitHub's 100 MB limit at the full panel); there is no plain-JSON fallback any more. GVARModelsRaw is plain JSON so it round-trips through zustand and the Web Worker.

docs.title: data/countries.ts
docs.text: Responsibility. The static country registry backing the dropdown (TopBar). COUNTRIES is a CountryEntry[] ({ code, name, group }); group ('core' | 'oecd' | 'em') is only a coarse geographic tag for sorting — GVAR membership is data-driven via isGvarCountry / GVAR_BLOC_CANDIDATES, not this field. 52 entries (AR, IL, RU removed in 2026). This list — with the CountryCode union in gvarSolve.ts — is the part of the data that is still compiled into the tool: a data pack can update these economies but cannot add one, so adding a country = add an entry here (a new app version) and ship its app/public/data/bvar/<code>/ files in a pack. Convenience filters: CORE_COUNTRIES, OECD_COUNTRIES, EM_COUNTRIES.

docs.title: conditionedDotY.ts — optimistic conditioned-point dot
docs.text:
Path. app/src/lib/conditionedDotY.ts (it lives directly under lib/, not under lib/compute/).

Responsibility. Convert between the clicked display value and the stored conditioning-path deviation, as an exact inverse pair, so a pinned marker (the "dot") snaps to the just-clicked value instantly — without waiting for the ~700 ms forecast recompute. The dot is sourced from the conditioning path the click writes (instant); the forecast line + uncertainty bands still come from the solve and reconcile a moment later. Two functions, exact inverses (conditionedDotDisplayY ∘ conditioningDeviationFromDisplayY = id):

Function Mapping conditioningDeviationFromDisplayY(displayY, baseMeanVal, baseLevelVal, specVarId) (conditionedDotY.ts:62) display → stored. Level-display vars (oil/FX/equity/house): dev = indexLevelToLog(displayY) − baseLevelVal. Other vars (growth-displayed log / lin): dev = displayY − baseMeanVal. conditionedDotDisplayY(dev, baseMeanVal, baseLevelVal, specVarId) (conditionedDotY.ts:34) stored → display (the inverse). Level vars: logToIndexLevel(baseLevelVal + dev). Other vars: baseMeanVal + dev.

isLevelDisplay(specVarId) (from displayUnits.ts) decides the branch. The forward map is the single source of truth for both handleDrag (drag a pin) and the right-click "plant a bullet at the cursor" activation — keeping them beside each other guarantees a conditioned point always round-trips to the cursor for every variable type (no transform double-applied). Used in ChartGrid.tsx: conditioningDeviationFromDisplayY at the drag/right-click write (lines ~1230, ~1300) and conditionedDotDisplayY at the dot render (line ~1656, where active+conditioned quarters override the scenario forecast y with the reconstructed click value). Pinned by conditioned-dot-optimistic.test.ts and right-click-plant-at-cursor.test.ts.

docs.title: compute/gvarDragState.ts — drag/compute signal bus
docs.text:
Responsibility. A tiny module-level signal bus shared between the chart drag handler (ChartGrid.tsx) and the GVAR solve hook (useGvarForecast.ts). It exists off the zustand store on purpose: the drag begin/end and in-flight flags are pure UI signals that must NOT enter the scenario/pins state — putting them in the store would re-render the whole grid on every pointer-down/up. useSyncExternalStore lets only the badge subscribe to the in-flight flag, while useGvarForecast reads the drag flag imperatively + subscribes to drag-END.

Export Purpose beginGvarDrag() / endGvarDrag() mark pointer-down / pointer-up; endGvarDrag notifies the drag-END subscribers so a held structure-change solve fires exactly once for the committed pin isGvarDragging() / getGvarDragging() imperative read of the drag flag onGvarDragEnd(fn) subscribe to pointer-up (returns an unsubscribe); the channel useGvarForecast uses to dispatch the deferred solve subscribeGvarDragging(fn) useSyncExternalStore subscribe to the drag FLAG (begin + end) — lets ChartGrid's effective memo reactively swap the viewed bloc's line between the frozen GVAR path (idle) and the cheap live condForecast (dragging) setGvarComputing(on) / subscribeGvarComputing(fn) / getGvarComputing() the "computing…" badge state (only the badge re-renders)

Why two listener sets. _dragFlagListeners fires on begin AND end (drives the line fallback); _dragEndListeners fires only on pointer-up (dispatches the held solve). Sharing one would either re-render on every begin or fail to dispatch on end. Tested by gvar-drag-scheduling.test.ts and gvar-drag-line-band.test.ts.

docs.title: useGvarForecast.ts — drag-aware two-tier GVAR solve hook
docs.text:
Responsibility. The React hook that turns the active bloc's own-pins into a propagated GVAR forecast, keeping the heavy solve off the live drag path. It owns a module Worker (main-thread fallback), a stale-response reqId guard, and two timers (a live debounce + a separate drag-release macrotask). The load-bearing perf fact (verified in the code, useGvarForecast.ts:279): on the then-live US-endogenous panel (measured before the Oct 2026 re-estimation) every mean solve — direct OR full — is ~4571 ms warm / ~13327 ms cold (the US-pinned structure misses the shipped empty-pinStructure coupling artifact and falls to the Neumann fixed point (dim 2180 in the deployed pack) + one Kalman smoother per coupled bloc).

The drag boundary (useGvarForecast.ts:287):

  • While a drag is in progress (isGvarDragging()): ZERO solves fire — neither value-only nor structure-change. The hook marks pendingReleaseSolveRef = true and bails. The dragged bloc's own line still follows the cursor live because ChartGrid's effective falls back to the single-country condForecast (a ~1–5 ms DK smoother) while gvarFc is frozen at the last solve.
  • On pointer-up (onGvarDragEnd): exactly one direct solve is dispatched, deferred to a ~100 ms macrotask (coalesces back-to-back gestures + lands after the final store write flushes into dataRef). direct is used so the ~95 MB coupling artifact is stripped (withoutCoupling) from the worker post — solveGVARDirect rebuilds/caches M from the per-bloc kernel cache and never consumes the inverse.
  • Non-drag edits (numeric/programmatic pin entry, Reset, scenario switch) dispatch live: full solves immediately (explicit user action — solveFullToken bumped via Compute / "Solve full GVAR"), direct previews after a 120 ms debounce.

So the full cross-country fixed point (mode:'full', hydrated (I−M)⁻¹) fires only on the explicit Compute / "Solve full GVAR" token bump; everything else is the direct one-hop preview. Pinned by gvar-drag-scheduling.test.ts.

docs.title: controls/DriversDrawer.tsx — the Drivers drawer (EXPERIMENTAL)
docs.text:
Responsibility. The user-facing surface of driversDecomp.ts: a fixed right-side overlay, 480 px wide, role="dialog", closed by its × or by Escape, that chooses the lens, decides which path to decompose, enforces the naming budget in the interface, draws the stacked contribution chart, and states the licence in plain words underneath it.

function DriversDrawer({ open, onClose }: { open: boolean; onClose: () => void })

open and onClose are the only props. The drawer is mounted by ScenarioBar.tsx and stays mounted while closed, so open also gates the solve: decompResult returns early when the drawer is closed, which matters because driversInput is republished on every drag tick and a closed drawer would otherwise re-solve an 84×84 system per frame for a panel rendering nothing. The button that opens it lives elsewhere — in ChartGrid's scenario-action cluster — so the open state lives in the store rather than in either component, which avoids a ChartGrid → DriversDrawer → ChartGrid import cycle (the drawer imports resolveChartVars from ChartGrid).

docs.title: What publishes into it: the DriversPathInput store slice
docs.text:
interface DriversPathInput {
  displayed: number[][] | null       // the deviation of the path the app CURRENTLY DISPLAYS
  isolated: number[][] | null        // the isolated single-country (frozen-partner) conditional deviation
  coupled: number[][] | null         // the coupled cross-country GVAR deviation for the viewed bloc
  displayedIsCoupled: boolean        // true when `displayed` IS the coupled path (reference identity)
  external: number[][] | null        // the external-forecast combination deviation, or null
  baselineDisplay: number[][] | null // baseline DISPLAY rows [t][j], exactly as the panels draw them
  histDisplay: number[][] | null     // the panels' trailing 3-quarter history tail, same convention
}

The first five are [t][j] in smoother level space — 100·log for log variables, native units for lin ones — which is the space the Drivers unit mappings were measured in; the last two are in main-panel display space (drift-adjusted, annualised q/q growth for log variables) and are the anchor the contribution bars stack from. ChartGrid publishes the whole object through useStore.getState().setDriversInput(...) in an effect keyed on the effective, conditional and GVAR level deviations (ChartGrid.tsx:2343), using the same imperative publish pattern as setChartExportData, so ChartGrid never subscribes to driversInput and the publish cannot re-render the grid. displayedIsCoupled is a reference-identity test against gvarFc.levelDeviation, exactly the branch the effective memo takes when a GVAR result drives the display. Deviations are drift-invariant because the long-run δc translation shifts baseline and scenario rigidly, so the undrifted effective is the correct input.

The store also holds driversOpen / setDriversOpen. ChartGrid renders the Drivers button — amber exp badge, alongside the GVAR badges — only when driversAvailable (ChartGrid.tsx:2362): some entry of the displayed, isolated or coupled deviation, or of the external combination, exceeds 1e-9 in absolute value. That gate mirrors the drawer's own hasDeviation test over the same inputs, so the button never opens a drawer with nothing to decompose.

docs.title: The default configuration
docs.text:
On the US bloc, opening the drawer with no further clicks gives the licensed class-view configuration: model US_SW07, all seven observables watched (the three locked plus Consumption, Investment, Real wage and Hours), all seven usable shocks named, grouping Classes (Monetary, Demand, Supply plus a grey residual), chart view Forecast (contribution bars anchored on the baseline in main-panel units, the classic central-bank history decomposition), observable Output, source the displayed scenario. Rank is 84/84, so the regime is exact-fit and no residual, collinearity or rank warning fires.

On every other bloc the model is still US_SW07 but the native columns are absent, so the budget is 3 and the named set is the greedy non-collinear three (interest_, fiscal_, ea); Classes is greyed with its licence tooltip and the view falls back to Groups, three per-shock series. A per-bloc model choice is remembered in localStorage under gmaps-drivers-model:<bloc>; Reset restores the default and overwrites that saved choice.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Always visible: the lens row (model title, the dropped-shock note where applicable, and a "Change model" link opening the grouped picker — Own country, then Reference, then Other), the [Classes | Groups] segmented toggle (Classes disabled unless licensed), the chart-view dropdown (Forecast, or Deviation from baseline), Reset, and Customize. Under Customize:

  • Use all — watch every mappable observable for the model, then name every unit the budget allows, skipping collinear duplicates. For a clustered model it names the build-time validated default triple.
  • Input source — "Scenario (displayed)" or "External forecast combination". The latter is disabled and annotated "— switched off" when imports exist for the bloc but the external master switch is off, and "— none imported" when there is nothing to use.
  • Domestic | Global path — shown only for the scenario source and only when both an isolated and a coupled path exist. The choice is sticky, so the drawer warns outside the collapsed fold when it is decomposing a path other than the one on screen.
  • Observables — three locked chips with a padlock, plus the four addable native chips on the US bloc, each annotated as raising the budget by one.
  • Measurement error — the strict↔permissive slider, shown only once a native observable is added, displaying the current row weight w = 1/√(1+me) (default me = 1). See Remark 6.
  • Named units — one chip per shock, or per cluster on the FRB/US lenses; every un-named chip is disabled once named.length >= budget.
  • Experimental: raw shocks — a fold, clustered models only, switching the decomposition from cluster composites to individual shocks. The chip list is the greedy non-collinear selection (26 of 54 for US_FRB22), and the budget still applies, so at three observables only three may be named.

Below the controls sit the "Contributions to" observable dropdown, the headline chart, the shares strip, a "Cluster membership" expander on the FRB/US lenses, and the caveat paragraph. The caveat cites bench_simple_decomp.m only for the eight models that bench actually ran; for anything else it says the lens is not covered by that bench and that what backs it is a build-time check on the shipped default naming, with other namings unvalidated (see Known issues #6). It adds the cluster-chaining sentence on the FRB/US lenses, the CMR14 family disclosure where those families are shown, and the reason Classes are greyed whenever they are.

docs.title: The two chart builders
docs.text:
function buildMainStyleHeadline(args: {
  H, spec: ObsDisplaySpec, bars: HeadlineBar[], zDisp: number[],
  baselineRows: number[][], histRows: number[][] | null, lastHist: string, lineName: string,
}): { traces: any[]; layout: any } | null

function buildDeltaHeadline(args: {
  H, bars: HeadlineBar[], zDisp: number[], lastHist: string, lineName: string, unit: string,
}): { traces: any[]; layout: any }

Both are exported as pure functions of their arguments so the chart construction is testable without mounting the drawer. A HeadlineBar is { name, color, values: number[] }, one stacked series in display units — a shock, a class or family total, or a cluster composite. zDisp is the input deviation in the same display units; baselineRows and histRows are the panel's own baseline and history rows (driversInput.baselineDisplay / histDisplay), and lastHist is the bloc's last historical quarter label, from which the quarter axis is generated. buildMainStyleHeadline stacks positive contributions upward and negative ones downward from the baseline, per quarter and independently, and returns null when the baseline display series is shorter than H. buildDeltaHeadline stacks the same bars from zero.

Remark 6 (The measurement-error slider does nothing at budget-max). At K = q the stacked system is square, and scaling both Θ and z by a positive diagonal row weighting leaves the solution identical: WΘx = Wz ⟺ Θx = z. The slider is therefore inert in the default US configuration; the drawer disables it there and says so, rather than inviting the user to drag a control with no effect. It becomes real as soon as a shock is un-named, which is what gives the added observables a role.

Remark 7 (The delta view's units need not match the panel that opened the drawer). The chart view auto-follows the main display — when growthDisplay is vsbaseline the drawer opens in "Deviation from baseline", otherwise in "Forecast" — and a manual choice then sticks. But the delta chart's bars are always the panel's rate deviation, while the main panels' "% vs base" mode has a level sub-mode and defaults to level. Auto-follow can therefore put the drawer's chart in different units from the panel that triggered it. The axis title states the unit; do not describe the delta view as matching the panel without that qualification.

Remark 8 (The shares strip is a norm share, not a variance decomposition). For the selected observable, each series' share is ‖its contribution path‖₂ divided by the sum of those norms plus the residual's (normShares). Shares always sum to 100 and are never negative, so two contributions that offset each other both show as positive shares. It is a readability aid, not a fevd.

docs.title: Behaviours worth knowing
docs.text: The chart shows one observable at a time while the solve uses all watched observables jointly, and the horizon is always twelve quarters regardless of the app's display horizon. Warnings fire for the residual-able regime (quoting rank and rows), for nearly collinear named shocks (quoting the measured |cos| inside the raw fold), for decomposing a path other than the displayed one, for the experimental raw-shock mode, for rank-deficient named columns (rank < K·H), and for leaving the validated default naming on an FRB/US lens. An index fetch failure is reported as an error; a per-model IRF failure is recorded per model and offers a Retry, and the recorded failure blocks the loader effect until the user asks again.

docs.title: app/scripts/build_drivers_index.mjs — the Drivers data layer
docs.text: Responsibility. Builds everything the Drivers feature fetches at runtime: it copies the census menu models' IRF files into app/public/data/dsge/census/ and writes the index.json described under data/loader.ts.

docs.title: Example 4 (Regenerate the Drivers index after a new census export)
docs.text:
We rebuild the menu from the census export tree. The script runs from anywhere, refuses to ship a census file whose sha256 does not match the manifest, and rewrites both the copies and the index in one pass. Afterwards the licence tests re-hash every shipped file against the index, so a stale copy fails the fast suite rather than reaching the site.

node app/scripts/build_drivers_index.mjs
cd app && npm test          # v3-5 re-hashes every shipped census file against the index

It reads pipeline/census_irfs/MANIFEST.json and pipeline/census_irfs/<srcDir>/Taylor.json for the eight census entries, pipeline/_shockbench/class_maps.json for the class maps, and app/public/data/dsge/irfs/<M>/SW.json for the four models indexed out of the irfs tree (US_SW07, US_CMR14, US_FRB08, US_FRB22_mcap), which are indexed in place and not copied. Note that pipeline/census_irfs/ is not present on every branch — the census export tree lives on the research branch — and on a checkout without it the script fails at its first read.

What it computes per model. The usable shock list (a shock is usable when it carries all three common observables and its stacked three-observable H = 12 path has norm ≥ 1e-9; anything else is dropped and named, mirroring bench_simple_decomp.m); the collinear pairs, computed exactly as the bench does, as |cos| > 0.95 between unit-normalised stacked paths; for the models flagged clustered, the connected components of that graph, each labelled by its largest member's equation name (the mnemonic minus the _aerr suffix) and ordered by size descending then id ascending; and, for clustered models, the validated default naming.

The default-naming scan. pickDefaultNamed scans every cluster triple through the shipped colnorm solver over 20 sparse-truth seeds (deterministic mulberry32, seed 20260806) against the 1e-6 licence criterion, then picks deterministically among the passers: maximise total member coverage, then prefer a triple containing the interest_ cluster, then first in shipped cluster order. It falls back to pairs and singletons if no triple passes, which does not occur for the shipped data. For US_FRB22, 123 of 1,771 triples pass and the winner is [hqlfpr, interest_, pcer_l], covering 19 of the 54 shocks with a measured worst recovery error of 2.53e-9. For US_FRB22_var, 122 of 1,330 pass and the winner is [eco_l, interest_, ki_l], covering 12 of 54, at 1.32e-7 — passing, but only an order of magnitude inside the criterion, and not pinned by any test. A full-rank Θ is not evidence that a triple is usable: most triples are badly conditioned while still passing the rank test, which is why the drawer warns as soon as the user leaves the shipped default.

docs.title: The shipped menu
docs.text:
Index key Usable K Dropped Collinear pairs Clusters Rank / regime at the default 3-obs configuration US_SW07 7 em (zero response) 0 — 36/36 exact-fit (3 named); 84/84 at the native 7 US_CMR14 9 e_term (zero response) 3 — 36/36 exact-fit US_FRB08 2 — 0 — 24/36 residual-able (2 named) US_FRB22 54 — 109 23 36/36 exact-fit (3 clusters named) US_FRB22_var 54 — 117 21 as above EA_SW03 6 — 1 — 36/36 exact-fit EA_SWW14 6 — 0 — 36/36 exact-fit CA_LS07 3 — 1 — 24/36 residual-able (only 2 named — the greedy skips the collinear partner) HK_FP13 5 — 2 — 36/36 exact-fit BRA_SAMBA08 4 — 0 — 36/36 exact-fit UK_SM11 3 — 0 — 36/36 exact-fit US_FRB22_mcap 2 — 0 — menu-hidden; kept for the v2 licence fixtures

Only three models carry a class map: US_SW07 (Monetary interest_; Demand eb, fiscal_, eqs; Supply ea, epinf, ew — the seven the licence was established over), US_CMR14 (nine members across Monetary, Demand, Supply and Financial) and US_FRB22_mcap, aliased by both FRB22 census entries, whose 54 members are assigned by a rule on the equation each _aerr residual attaches to rather than by economic judgement about the shock. Everything else falls through to a null class map and shows one series per named shock. CMR14's families are that model's own class map used as an organising grouping, not a licensed class split: bench_class_recovery.m recovers their class totals in 78% of test instances against its 90% bar, and the drawer discloses that number verbatim wherever the families are shown. class_maps.json also carries a censusGeneric dictionary which is typed in loader.ts but read by nothing in app/src; it is inert in the shipped app.

docs.title: The validation benches
docs.text:
matlab -batch "run('pipeline/bench_simple_decomp.m')"
matlab -batch "run('pipeline/bench_class_recovery.m')"

Both print to stdout and write no file: the committed docs/paper/simple_decomp_results.txt and docs/paper/class_recovery_results.txt are captured transcripts, so regenerating them means redirecting the output. bench_simple_decomp.m reads the two shipped irfs-tree files plus pipeline/census_irfs/<M>/Taylor.json for its six census rows; bench_class_recovery.m reads class_maps.json, the same two shipped files, and pipeline/census_irfs/US_FRB22_mcap/Taylor.json. On a checkout without the census tree, two of the eight simple-decomposition rows and four of the five class-recovery rows still run; the rest do not.

docs.title: Render memoization in ChartGrid (reconcileCharts + chartDeepEqual + React.memo)
docs.text:
Responsibility (Phase-2 render optimization, issue #68). A single conditioning edit changes scenarios, re-running the monolithic charts useMemo → every chart object gets a fresh identity → absent memoization, Plotly would repaint all ~35 panels. Two levers (in ChartGrid.tsx) make one edit repaint ≈1 panel:

Mechanism Where What it does chartDeepEqual(a, b) ChartGrid.tsx:173 tight structural equality over the chart objects (plain objects / arrays / primitives — no Maps/Sets/Dates/functions appear in a chart object) reconcileCharts(next, prev, onRebuilt?) ChartGrid.tsx:205 reuses the PRIOR render's object reference for any panel whose freshly-built content is deep-equal (keyed by chartVar.bvarIdx, so a panel maps to its prior self even if list order/length shifts on a country switch); returns the prior array when every element kept its reference (stable outer identity, no [charts] effect churn) MemoDraggableChart = memo(DraggableChart) ChartGrid.tsx:2523 so a stable chart reference + the grid's useCallback'd handler props mean an unchanged panel does not re-render / repaint

The math/builder is untouched: reconcileCharts only swaps a NEW object for an EQUAL old one, so the rendered data is byte-identical; it just preserves reference identity where the content did not move. Two test-only instrumentation counters (chartRebuildCounter, draggableChartRenderCounter, both exported, ~zero production cost) let chartgrid-render-memo.test.ts assert that one conditioning edit rebuilds ≈1 panel and re-renders only the touched panel(s), not all ~35.

docs.title: Empirical evaluation (companion repo — in progress)
docs.text:
A separate repository — em-bayesian-gvar-eval (sibling to this one) — turns the deployed engine + the MATLAB estimator into a publishable evaluation. It does not ship in the app; it is the empirical core of the paper. The full design is final in em-bayesian-gvar-eval/docs/EMPIRICAL_PROTOCOL.md; results are preliminary / forthcoming.

It races two proposed models against six benchmarks (model codes are the registry in eval/tables.py / eval/score.py):

Code Model Role emgvar_endo EM-Bayesian GVAR, US endogenous proposed (headline) emgvar_frozen EM-Bayesian GVAR, frozen US anchor proposed rw driftless Random Walk (+ sample-mean "climatology" anchor) universal reference arp AR(p), p by AIC over {1..4}, iterated and direct strong univariate sbvar single-country Bayesian VAR (stars dropped, same prior) isolates coupling cgvar_a textbook OLS Pesaran–Schuermann–Weiner / Dees GVAR (no COVID-as-missing) literature GVAR cgvar_b single-pass Bayesian GVAR (MAXIT=1, COVID-as-missing) isolates EM completion dfm Bayesian dynamic factor model non-GVAR global benchmark

Nesting map (stated in the paper): sbvar ⊂ cgvar_b ⊂ emgvar_*; RW/AR nested in every VAR. Count reconciliation: the table lists 8 registry codes, but the rw code emits both rw and its sample-mean climatology sibling clim as separately scored labels, so the scored suite is 9 models (2 proposed + 6 benchmarks + the climatology sibling; arp is a single label).

Design (final). Recursive expanding window, origins 2010Q1–2024Q4 (drop the 2020 COVID origins from the headline); rolling as-of-t0 trade weights (leak-free — built from IMTS bilateral trade with endPeriod ≤ year(t0); the shipped 2021–2023 weights_full.json is forbidden in the OOS sweep, as it would inject future trade structure); targets {real GDP growth, inflation, short rate} for US/EA/JP/UK/CA/CN; horizons h ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} (each scored only where a ≤2025Q4 realization exists). COVID-as-missing reapplies in-sample at every origin where 2020Q2–Q4 ≤ t0.

Scoring. CRPS is the primary density score (ensemble estimator, robust at the modest draw counts); a parametric Gaussian/skew-t log-score corroborates; PIT / coverage for calibration. Significance: Giacomini–White is the headline test (valid under nesting and the recursive scheme), Clark–West for nested point/MSE comparisons, Diebold–Mariano (HAC, HLN-corrected) for non-nested pairs only; multiplicity handled with Romano–Wolf + the Model Confidence Set per (variable, horizon).

Part 2 — spillovers. Tier A (ships now, zero new estimator code): the conditional-scenario endogenous-vs-frozen US contrast, driven through the shipped gvarSolve.ts (x = Mx + d) — its driver is em-bayesian-gvar-eval/eval/tier_a_scenario.mjs, specified to be exercised from the main repo via a vitest harness (app/src/__tests__/eval/tierA_spillover.test.ts, planned). Tier B (new gvar_girf module, constructible from the exported betahat/Σ + coupling M): GIRF / generalized FEVD / Diebold–Yilmaz index. The protocol is explicit that gvarSolve.ts computes conditional-mean scenario deltas, not GIRFs/FEVD — the only spillover strings in this repo are UI labels.

Headline result (first full pass — results/tables.{txt,json}, 56 origins, 9 models). AR(p)/DFM have the lowest point CRPS, but the 90% Model Confidence Set is the publishable signal: emgvar_endo is in the inflation MCS at all horizons and the short-rate MCS at h=1,2,4 (indistinguishable from the best on the nominal block), out of the growth MCS at h=1 & h=8; emgvar_endo ⪰ emgvar_frozen across the MCS; and the EM-Bayesian treatment decisively beats the textbook OLS classical GVAR (cgvar_a is removed from most sets). The unconditional point leader for inflation h=1 is the univariate AR(p) (relRMSE 0.641); emgvar_endo (relRMSE 0.799) is the best among the EM/GVAR family, not the overall best. Honest caveats: the draw-based densities are over-confident (PIT cov90 ~0.73–0.83 vs 0.90), and the parametric log-score column is numerically broken (CRPS + MCS are the robust primaries). Tier-A (results/tierA/us_rate_100bp.json) shows non-trivial endogenous-only cross-country feedback the frozen anchor omits, but the magnitudes are large/sign-flipping and it is a multi-period conditional projection, NOT a causal IRF — needs a validation pass before being headlined. The design is final; see em-bayesian-gvar-eval/docs/EMPIRICAL_PROTOCOL.md.

docs.title: Known issues & limitations (flagged-for-fix, NOT yet fixed)
docs.text:
Documented honestly so a reader does not mistake a known bias for a verified result. Each is flagged-but-unfixed at the current deployment; cite this section, do not silently rely on the affected output.

  1. CN fiscal debt — inflation double-count (fiscalAccounting.ts). RESOLVED (2026-06). The CN debt-snowball roll-forward computes nominal growth as gQ = Δ(level[idx.gdp]) + Δ(level[idx.deflator]). CN previously shipped a nominal GDP_CN, so the price term was double-counted and the CN debt-to-GDP path was biased. The surgical CN-only re-estimate replaced GDP_CN with real GDP (spec.json var 0 = "CN Real GDP …"), so the snowball now reads the correct real-GDP + price nominal growth, as for the other economies. At the time the fix re-estimated CN only.

  2. [OBSOLETE — longRunTilt.ts removed; superseded by the driftSetter.ts anchor (see above).] The former entropic tilt did not filter non-finite moments before its Newton dual, so an unstable draw's non-finite long-run moment NaN-poisoned the softmax weights and silently emptied the anchor band. The driftSetter.ts display translation does no per-draw reweighting and is not subject to this failure mode.

  3. Only a console-level ρ(M) < 1 divergence guard on the live closed-form solve (gvarSolve.ts, runGvarSolve.ts). The endogenous Neumann fixed point x ← d + M·x iterates to maxIt = 2000 or a relative tolerance 1e-10·(1+‖x‖). If it does not converge, solveGVARClosedFormEndo now computes ρ(M), and runGvarSolve treats ρ ≥ 1 (or a non-finite residual) as diverged: a console warning and no caching. But nothing tells the user on screen, so a refit with ρ ≥ 1 would still show a wrong path. ρ is computed at export time and shipped in the artifact (0.971875 in the deployed pack); check it when the coupling is rebuilt. Fix: surface the diverged flag in the UI (or refuse a coupling with rhoSpectral ≥ 1 at load).

  4. Conditional band uses the FILTERED, not DK-smoothed, covariance (kalman.ts). conditionalForecast returns the smoothed MEAN but extracts the per-horizon variance from the filtered state covariance: variances.push(submatrix(filteredP[t], 0, 0, n, n)) (kalman.ts:405–:409, the comment says "Extract forecast variances from filtered covariances"). The DK smoother would tighten the covariance for quarters that precede a future pin (a later observation reduces earlier-quarter uncertainty); using the filtered covariance does not apply that reduction, so the conditional band is overstated for the quarters before a future pin. The mean is correct; only the band is conservative.

  5. Positional meta indices — STALE-POSITIONAL-INDEX (mitigated, not removed). fiscal_meta.json's six idx values and external_meta.json's five are positional column offsets. Any variable-order change silently re-points them — EA's effRate once landed on the equity index (~col 537) and debt/GDP exploded; in the Oct 2026 data the inserted DEFL_<CC> sent 35 blocs' external fx index to the wrong series (no numerical effect: the FX channel is off). Mitigation: pipeline/port_gvar_exports.py now regenerates both files by variable id on every port; for blocs copied raw, run node pipeline/fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs and node pipeline/fix_external_meta_indices.mjs (by id, idempotent; the external one uses the recorded idxIds). fiscal-meta-indices.test.ts and data/meta-column-indices.test.ts guard them — but the deploy workflows do not run tests, so run them before pushing. See DATA_SCHEMA §9 and ARCHITECTURE §7.

  6. The Drivers caveat claims a build-time check that US_FRB08 does not have (DriversDrawer.tsx). For any model outside the eight bench_simple_decomp.m ran, the drawer's bottom caveat says the lens is backed by "a build-time check that the shipped default naming recovers a known shock sequence to 1e-6". That scan (pickDefaultNamed in build_drivers_index.mjs) runs only for clustered models, so it exists for US_FRB22 and US_FRB22_var and not for US_FRB08, which is on the visible menu, has no bench row and carries no defaultNamed. The sentence overstates what backs that one lens. Nothing else is affected — the engine, the budget rule and the collinearity flag are model-independent, and US_FRB08's two shocks at three observables put it in the residual-able regime in any case. Fix: branch the fallback sentence on meta.defaultNamed != null, and for the remaining case say plainly that the lens is unvalidated.

docs.title: Build & test
docs.text:
From app/:

npx tsc --noEmit     # type check
npm test             # FAST suite (vitest run minus the heavy solver --exclude globs)
npm run test:heavy   # HEAVY solver/perf canaries (1 fork) — BOTH halves are the maintainer's gate
npm run build        # static export; prebuild = gzip draws + vintages + pack-verify --full
npm run pack:verify -- --full   # the data-pack check on its own

Compute-engine tests live in app/src/__tests__/compute/ (data checks in app/src/__tests__/data/). The suite is split — npm test is vitest run minus ten heavy --exclude patterns; npm run test:heavy runs exactly those serialised to one fork; npm run test:all sweeps everything (see BUILD_AND_CI.md). The key canaries (all in the fast suite) are scenario-scale-convention, gvar-convergence (Gauss-Seidel ≡ closed-form), gvar-coupling-artifact (the shipped .gz matches a live build at the current modelSig), fiscal-meta-indices and data/meta-column-indices (the STALE-POSITIONAL-INDEX guards above). The deploy workflows run the build (and so pack-verify --full) but not the tests: running the tests is a manual step before a push.

The 26 Drivers licence tests — drivers-decomp.test.ts (4), drivers-decomp-v2.test.ts (7) and drivers-decomp-v3.test.ts (15) — are also in the fast suite. They read the shipped IRF files and the shipped index directly, so they fail on a stale app/public/data/dsge/census/ copy as well as on a code regression; see driversDecomp.ts.

docs.title: GMAPS Operations Guide — a step-by-step manual for a human maintainer
docs.text:
Current guide: UPDATE_MANUAL.md. Since 4.0.0 (October 2026) the data and the model live in a data pack, separate from the app; the update manual is the authoritative procedure for data shifts, model updates and app releases. This page is kept for the parts it covers in more depth (adding a series, the test gate, deploy verification) and has been corrected where 4.0 changed a step.

This is the single entry point for keeping the Global Macroeconomic Analysis Projections and Scenarios (GMAPS) tool running: how to update the data each quarter, add a new data series, add a new economy, test everything before a deployment, and deploy to production. It is written to be followed top to bottom by a human who did not build the tool. Each part gives the exact commands; where a task has deep detail, it points to the specialist document rather than duplicating it.

Two golden rules that override everything below. 1. Never ship fabricated data. Every number is either a genuine source observation or a model-implied value produced by the G-BVAR framework and recorded as such. If a series cannot be sourced, you drop it or truncate to the genuine edge — you never invent, back-fill, or extrapolate a value to fill a gap. (See docs/synthetic-data-audit.md.) 2. Never deploy to production without an explicit go-ahead. Production is the bvarscenario repo's main branch. A push there is public and cached by a CDN. Do not push it on your own initiative; confirm first, every time.

docs.title: Prerequisites (one-time setup)
docs.text:
You need Why Check Node 20+ runs the tool, the data pipeline (vite-node scripts), and the tests node --version Octave 8+ or MATLAB R2023b+ re-estimation and the MATLAB ground-truth checks (gt.m) octave --version Python 3.10+ the data-source fetchers in pipeline/ python3 --version pdflatex (TeX Live) compiling the paper/manual, only if you touch docs/ pdflatex --version git + push access to bvarscenario deployment git remote -v FRED API key data fetchers (hardcoded in the pipeline scripts — this is a private repo) grep a fetch_*.py

Where things live. The app is under app/ (Next.js static export; TypeScript compute in app/src/lib/compute/, data in app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/). The data pipeline and MATLAB estimation are under pipeline/. Operator scripts are under app/scripts/. All commands below are run from app/ unless the path says otherwise.

docs.title: Part 0 — The mental model (read once)
docs.text:
The tool estimates the models once and shifts them forward each quarter. There are therefore two different maintenance events:

  • Within-year quarterly shift (the common one — Part 1). New data has arrived; you move the panel forward one quarter and let the coupled G-BVAR nowcast every cell that isn't yet observed. No re-estimation — the estimated coefficients (the "companion") are frozen.
  • Annual re-estimation (rare — Part 6). Once a year, or whenever the variable set changes (Part 2, Case B), you re-estimate the whole coupled system on the final data.

Each bloc's history is stored in historical_levels.json as a T×n matrix. Log variables are held as 100·log(level); linear variables (rates, ratios) as-is. The forecast x-axis is numeric offsets: x = −1 is the last observation, x = 0 is the first forecast (see app/src/lib/dates.ts). There is no date constant any more (4.0.0): each history file records its first quarter (firstQuarter), the last quarter is first quarter + rows − 1, and the app reads the panel dating from the data pack's manifest.json.

Deployment is a two-hop chain, not a single push: bvarscenario/main → a GitHub Actions build → the starter-hugo-academic repo → GitHub Pages, then a CDN. The second site, gmapsmodel.com, is built by Netlify from the gmapsmodel/GMAPS mirror's main. Budget ~25 minutes and verify against a file that actually changed (Part 5) — the first 200 you get back can be a stale cache.

docs.title: Part 1 — Update the dataset each quarter (the within-year shift)
docs.text:
Run this when a new quarter's data is out (advanced economies first; financials are always available). It moves every bloc forward one quarter, pulls genuine observations where they exist, and fills the rest with a cross-block G-BVAR nowcast whose provenance is recorded cell by cell.

Step 1 — Is a shift due? 

npm run data:check           # probes the release calendar
# exit 10 = a quarterly shift is due; exit 11 = an annual re-estimation is due; 0 = nothing due

Step 2 — Dry-run the whole shift (writes nothing). Without --commit the shift runs every source gate but does not write any file. Read its output; make sure the gates pass and the seam looks sane. 

npm run data:shift -- --asof 2026Q3            # the quarter to shift to

Step 3 — Run the shift for real. This archives the current vintage, then runs the full publish chain. 

npm run data:shift -- --asof 2026Q3 --commit
The chain (in order): archive the current vintage → build the counterfactual baseline → pull genuine observed rows for the wired leaders (gate-then-write; revisions are accepted as new knowledge) → apply realized-data pins for the mirror blocs (gated; a pin that fails its sanity gate falls back to the nowcast, never to a made-up number) → cross-block G-BVAR nowcast completion of every remaining cell → publish the staged panel → extend the euro members one row each → re-simulate the predictive bands → rebuild the coverage manifest → rebuild the /monitor vintage comparison → re-stamp the data pack (manifest.json) → run the verification gate → cut one update pack per released app version. There is no date to bump. Step-by-step table: UPDATE_MANUAL.md §6.2.

Step 4 — Verify (Part 4). At minimum: npm run data:verify (verify_cutoffs + pack-verify --full) must pass.

If the chain stops half-way (hiccup recovery). Every step is idempotent — the whole chain is safe to re-run from the top. Never hand-edit a shipped panel to "finish" it: the gate treats a null tail as what it is, an incomplete run. To roll back, git checkout -- app/public/data (and remove the new pipeline/vintages/* folders) — see UPDATE_MANUAL.md §6.4. Full detail, per-step recovery, and exit-code meanings: docs/data-refresh-rollout.md.

docs.title: Part 2 — Add a new data series to an existing bloc
docs.text: First decide which of two kinds it is, because the effort is completely different.

docs.title: Case A — a DERIVED series (no re-estimation)
docs.text:
A derived series is an accounting identity on top of variables the model already estimates — e.g. the fiscal block (primary balance, debt) from revenue/expenditure/rate, or the external block (trade balance, current account, NFA) from exports/imports/GDP/FX. Because nothing new enters the VAR, you do not re-estimate. Steps:

  1. Source the real seed and any parameters. A derived stock (debt, NFA) needs a real, sourced starting value — e.g. nfa0 = net IIP / nominal GDP from a national source. Record the source string in the meta file. Modeling constants that are not sourced (e.g. an imputed return) are shipped with a _flags: "... MODELING DEFAULT ..." note, never presented as estimated.
  2. Write the per-bloc meta file — fiscal_meta.json or external_meta.json in app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/, following an existing one (US is the reference). It holds idx (the column indices of the driver variables, resolved by variable id), the real seed, and the flagged defaults.
  3. The compute is already generic — computeFiscalBlock / computeExternalBlock in app/src/lib/compute/. If the new bloc's units differ (e.g. trade in USD, GDP in local currency), set the units factors in the meta (see the header of externalAccounting.ts) — never a fabricated conversion; a bloc whose units can't be reconciled ships without the block.
  4. Validate the anchor against the published figure (e.g. the trade balance at the nowcast should sit in the published BoP range). Add or extend a fixture test in app/src/__tests__/compute/…Accounting.test.ts.
  5. The chart section (external, fiscal) picks the series up automatically once the meta exists.

docs.title: Case B — an ESTIMATED series (requires re-estimation)
docs.text:
An estimated series enters the VAR — e.g. re-adding a nominal effective exchange rate (NEER), or a new credit series. This changes a bloc's variable count, which changes the coupling dimension, so it requires one combined re-estimation of the coupled system. Steps:

  1. Source it in the bloc's source registry, pipeline/sources/registry/<CC>.json (format: pipeline/sources/registry/README.md): name the provider and key, and how monthly data become quarterly (mean = period average, the usual convention; only complete quarters count). If no provider adapter exists yet, add one (pipeline/sources/providers_<name>.py).
  2. Add it to the bloc's variable list in the same registry entry (the order there is the model's variable order: id, label, transformation log/lin), then rebuild the panel: python3 pipeline/sources/build_panel.py --bloc <CC>.
  3. Rebuild the panel, then re-estimate (Part 6). The GVAR-EM estimator is pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m; it re-fits the coupled system. Follow docs/REESTIMATING_MODELS.md exactly — the scaling conventions there are load-bearing.
  4. Regenerate the coupling artifact (app/public/data/bvar/gvar/coupling_default.json.gz) — the pre-computed (I−M)⁻¹ the browser solves with. This is mandatory: computing it in-browser takes ~20 minutes.
  5. Finish the model update as in UPDATE_MANUAL.md §7 (nowcast of the ragged edge, baselines, bands, data pack re-stamped under a new pack id).
  6. Verify (Part 4), including a re-derivation of any MATLAB golden that depends on the changed bloc (see Part 4, step 6).

The no-synthetic rule applies at every step: if the new series is not genuinely available for a bloc, that bloc gets the series truncated to its real edge or omitted — you do not pad it.

docs.title: Part 3 — Add a new economy (bloc)
docs.text: A new bloc is a bigger version of Part 2, Case B: source its full variable set, build its panel, add it to the GVAR topology and the trade-weights matrix, re-estimate the coupled system, and regenerate the coupling artifact. The full, tested procedure is in docs/ADDING_A_COUNTRY.md — follow it end-to-end; the trade-weights and star-variable steps are easy to get subtly wrong.

docs.title: Part 4 — Test before deployment (the full gate)
docs.text:
Run these in order. The deployment is cleared only when the type-check, both test suites, and the cut-off gate are green. Do not use npm run test:all to make a pass/fail decision — it runs the heavy GVAR tests in parallel workers where they time out; that is a harness artifact, not a real failure.

1. Type-check. 

npx tsc --noEmit          # must exit 0

2. Fast unit suite (everything except the heavy coupled-GVAR tests). 

npm test                  # must be green

3. Heavy GVAR suite — run SEPARATELY and SERIALLY. These validate the coupled solve (closed-form == iterative, RoW↔US feedback, per-draw bands) and are compute-heavy; they only pass with one worker. 

npm run test:heavy        # must be green (takes several minutes; a single band test can take ~80s)

4. Cut-off and pack gate (proves every history's calendar, the coverage manifest and the pack manifest agree, no null tails, nowcast converged; then re-hashes every file of the pack). 

npm run data:verify     # verify_cutoffs ("cutoffs OK: … blocs end <quarter> …") + pack-verify --full

5. Data-consistency audit (run after any data shift). Confirms the shift froze history (rows before the new quarter are byte-identical to the pre-shift vintage) and that every cell of the new quarter is one of exactly three kinds — a genuine observation, a gated realized pin, or a G-BVAR imputation recorded in nowcast_provenance.json — with nothing unexplained. The pattern: compare app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/historical_levels.json against pipeline/vintages/<pre-shift>/…, and check each last-row cell against pipeline/realized_pins_<Q>.json and the provenance imputedMask. (Small value revisions in the recent fiscal/credit tail are expected and accepted; a null→value change or a deep-history rewrite is a red flag.)

6. Paper/manual compile (only if you edited docs/). 

cd docs/paper && pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode gmaps_platform_paper.tex && pdflatex … gmaps_platform_paper.tex
# check the log for "undefined reference" or "Undefined control sequence" — there must be none.

docs.title: One known, benign test gotcha (and how to clear it)
docs.text:
• MATLAB golden re-derivation (scenario-scale-convention): this test pins the tool's conditional forecast against an independent MATLAB conforekf ground truth. Whenever the US bloc is re-estimated, the golden must be re-derived, or the test will fail on a stale reference: 
    cd pipeline/_verify && octave --no-gui --eval "source('gt.m')"     # reads the CURRENT companion
    then copy the infl_corr array from pipeline/_verify/gt_testvals.json into MATLAB_INFL_CORRECT in app/src/__tests__/compute/scenario-scale-convention.test.ts. gt.m resolves columns by variable id, so it is robust to re-estimation. This is a fix (refresh the reference), not a code change — the tool and MATLAB agree to ~1e-6 on the current model.

Green bar = tsc clean and npm test green and npm run test:heavy green and data:verify OK and (after a shift) the consistency audit clean.

docs.title: Part 5 — Deploy to production
docs.text:
Only after the green bar in Part 4 and an explicit go-ahead. Production overwrites the public site.

1. Commit the changes on your working branch, with a clear message.

2. Build the static export. 

npm run build            # → app/out/  (the static site); prebuild runs pack-verify --full

3. Push to production. Production is the bvarscenario remote's main. Push your branch's built state there per the project's deploy convention (a fast-forward of main).

4. Wait for the two-hop build. bvarscenario/main triggers a GitHub Actions build that publishes to the starter-hugo-academic repo, which GitHub Pages serves. Budget ~15 minutes for the build and ~10 minutes more for the CDN's 404-cache to expire.

5. Verify against a file that actually changed. Do not trust the coverage manifest (it can look right while the bundle is stale — this has caused a false "confirmed" before). Poll a vintage-discriminating file, e.g. Hong Kong's spec.json or the euro-area spec.json (seasonalRows: 3): 

curl -s https://matyasfarkas.github.io/bvar-scenario/data/bvar/HK/spec.json | head -c 200
Confirm it shows the new content before you call the deploy done. The cleanest check since 4.0.0 is the pack id: curl -s <site>/data/manifest.json | head -c 300 must show the new packId. Check both sites (https://matyasfarkas.github.io/bvar-scenario and https://gmapsmodel.com).

Rollback. If production is wrong, re-deploy the previous good commit the same way (build → push → verify). The vintage archive in pipeline/vintages/ lets you rebuild any prior data state.

Full deploy-verification notes: docs/data-refresh-rollout.md → "Deploy verification".

docs.title: Part 6 — Annual re-estimation (reference)
docs.text:
Once a year (or after a Part 2 Case B change), re-estimate on the final data: 

npm run data:q1prep      # stages the annual re-estimation prep (see its output for the manual steps)
Then rebuild the panels from the source registries, run the MATLAB estimators, port the exports, regenerate the coupling artifact, and finish the chain (nowcast, baselines, bands, data pack). The exact sequence, the scaling conventions, and the post-run checklist are in docs/REESTIMATING_MODELS.md and docs/UPDATE_MANUAL.md §7; the scripts of the October 2026 run are in docs/reest-2026/runs/. There is no date setting to change.

docs.title: Appendix A — Where everything is
docs.text: Path What app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/ a bloc's data: historical_levels.json, baseline_levels.json, companion_mean.json, spec.json, fiscal_meta.json, external_meta.json app/public/data/bvar/gvar/coupling_default.json.gz the pre-computed coupling (I−M)⁻¹ the browser solves with app/public/data/nowcast_provenance.json per-cell provenance of the nowcast (the imputedMask) app/public/data/manifest.json the data pack: every file's SHA-256 + size, and the per-bloc dating (no date constant in the code) app/src/lib/compute/ the TS compute (conditional forecast, GVAR solve, fiscal/external blocks) app/scripts/ operator scripts (auto_update.mjs, verify_cutoffs.mjs, nowcast_complete.mjs) pipeline/ source registries + panel builder (sources/), older fetchers (fetch_*.py, build_*.py), MATLAB estimation (export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m, export_bvar_euro_redesign.m), _verify/gt.m pipeline/vintages/ archived data vintages (for rollback and the consistency audit) docs/ UPDATE_MANUAL.md (current), this guide, data-refresh-rollout.md, REESTIMATING_MODELS.md, ADDING_A_COUNTRY.md, DATA_SCHEMA.md

docs.title: Appendix B — Guardrails (the hard rules, restated)
docs.text:
1. No synthetic data. Source it, or drop/truncate to the genuine edge. Flag every modeling default; record every source.
  2. No production deploy without an explicit go-ahead.
  3. Never hand-edit a shipped panel to patch a gap — re-run the (idempotent) chain instead.
  4. Quarterly values are period averages ("how": "mean" in a source registry), not end-of-period.
  5. The coupled solve aligns blocs by projection step, not by calendar date — keep the panel on a uniform row grid; never leave one bloc a row short.
  6. Decide derived vs estimated before adding a series (Part 2): derived is data-only; estimated forces a re-estimation.

Keep this guide current: when a script name, a path, or a step changes, update it here first — this is the document a human reaches for.

docs.title: Data & Estimation Pipeline
docs.text:
This page documents the offline pipeline that turns raw public data into the static JSON the web app serves: build → estimate → check → port → couple → complete & stamp the data pack → test → deploy. Everything here runs on the researcher's machine (MATLAB + Python + Node); the deployed browser app only ever reads the resulting data pack (app/public/data + its manifest.json). Since 4.0.0 the pack is separate from the tool: a new pack (a quarterly data shift or a re-estimated model) reaches users without a new app version — see UPDATE_MANUAL.md.

Scope / where to look next. This page is the mechanism reference — the script inventory, the raw-data precedence chain, the GVAR-EM loop internals, the prior/coherence tagging sweeps, and the port/coupling steps. For the decision tree ("what kind of update is this, and what does it re-estimate?") and the operational runbooks (exact copy-paste sequences with the green gate) see MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md, REESTIMATING_MODELS.md and ADDING_A_COUNTRY.md; for the live compute architecture see ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI.md; for the fiscal block see fiscal-block-methodology.md. The per-economy variable table (transformation · prior · financial-tag, all 1048 ported variable rows audited coherent) lives in the user manual (docs/GMAPS_User_Manual.tex, Appendix B — generated from the shipped specs by docs/generate_manual_tables.py). The out-of-sample forecast horse-race + endogenous-US spillover evaluation lives in a separate repo — see §11 and its docs/EMPIRICAL_PROTOCOL.md. This page does not repeat those — it complements them.

The currently-deployed platform (data pack 2026Q2-reest-20261008b, Oct 2026) is 52 economies: 35 coupled GVAR (global vector-autoregression) blocs (the US, endogenous, + 34 partners, with the euro area as one aggregate EA bloc; HK, SG, RO, PE and PH joined in 2026; AR, IL and RU were dropped) + the 17 euro-area members, each with its own model estimated outside the coupled GVAR. Every panel was rebuilt from its publishers with no fills of any kind (pipeline/sources/, §3.0): each series runs to its latest published quarter (2026Q2 where published), and every gap — leading, interior or at the ragged end — is missing data that the sampler draws. Coupling: dim 2180, ρ(M) = 0.971875. AE (United Arab Emirates) was evaluated and dropped earlier: it publishes only annual real GDP, and the viability test for a GVAR bloc is quarterly real GDP existing (§3.1.1).

Older numbers on this page. Several sections were written for the 33-bloc deployment of mid-2026 (coupling dim 2060, ρ ≈ 0.92–0.945, a common 2025Q4 estimation endpoint with WEO-Denton-extended tails). Where they remain they are labelled as history. The authoritative record of the deployed run is docs/reest-2026/ (PLAN.md decisions, REVIEW.md, and the exact scripts in runs/).

docs.title: 1. Flow at a glance
docs.text:
The deployed (Oct 2026) chain — exact scripts in docs/reest-2026/runs/:

                ┌──────────────────────────────┐
  FRED/Eurostat │ pipeline/sources/            │  registry/<CC>.json → build_panel.py --bloc <CC>
  BIS/ECB/OECD  │ build_panel.py (no fills)    │  ──► pipeline/country_rawdata/DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json
  IMF/national  └──────┬───────────────────────┘       (+ .provenance.json, fiscal_meta_<CC>.json)
                       │                              euro members: pipeline/euro_redesign_staging/<CC>/
                       ▼
                ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                │ export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m    │  35 blocs, GVAR-EM (parfor, CRN, GVAR_NOFILL, FIXHYPER)
   (estimate)   │ export_bvar_euro_redesign.m  │  17 members, one run each (fixed companion)
                └──────────┬───────────────────┘  ──►  run dirs (GVAR_OUTDIR / EURO_OUTDIR)
                           ▼  (check: converged sweep, finite exports, estimation_mask.json)
                ┌──────────────────────────────┐
   (port)       │ GVAR blocs: raw copy          │  full precision, incl. estimation_mask.json
                │ members: port_gvar_exports.py │  6-sig-fig; regenerates fiscal/external meta by id
                │ fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs   │  (+ fix_external_meta_indices.mjs for raw copies)
                └─────────┬────────────────────┘  ──►  app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/
                          ▼
   (calendar)    stamp_calendar.mjs (firstQuarter) → build_coverage_manifest.mjs
                          ▼
   (couple)      precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs + invert_coupling.{m,py} → coupling_default.json.gz (check ρ<1)
                          ▼
   (complete)    nowcast_complete.mjs (coupled nowcast of the ragged edge) → apply_member_completion.mjs
                 → roll_d0_forward.mjs → regen_gr_baselines_via_loader.mjs → regen_gvar_bands.mjs
                 → gzip_companion_draws.mjs → build_coverage_manifest.mjs → vintages_publish.mjs
                          ▼
   (pack)        pack-build.mjs --pack-id <new id>  →  verify_cutoffs.mjs  →  pack-verify.mjs --full
                          ▼
   (test)        cd app; npx tsc --noEmit; npm test; npm run test:heavy; BASE_PATH=/bvar-scenario npm run build
                          ▼
   (deploy)      push the same commit to bvarscenario main (GitHub Action → GitHub Pages /bvar-scenario)
                 and gmapsmodel main (Netlify → gmapsmodel.com); desktop: update pack or new installer

Within a year no re-estimation is needed: the quarterly data shift (npm run data:shift) adds the newly published quarter with the model frozen — see UPDATE_MANUAL.md §6.

A second, much shorter offline chain runs beside this one and shares none of it. It stages the DSGE impulse-response files the browser reads for its two model-conditional features — the policy counterfactual and the experimental Drivers panel — and produces them with a single Node script rather than with MATLAB estimation. It is documented in §3.6 and is independent of §4–§7 in both directions.

docs.title: 2. Dependencies
docs.text: Tool Used for Notes MATLAB + Parallel Computing Toolbox All .m estimators The GVAR-EM loop uses parfor; it calls parpool('local') (a no-op if absent — it then runs serially). Bundled MFBVAR / GLP Gibbs sampler + Minnesota prior Vendored in-repo under BVAR/ — the loop adds BVAR/MFBVAR, BVAR/AdditionalFunctions, BVAR/BGLreplication to the path. The COVID-as-missing sampler is BVAR/MFBVAR/cgl_bvarV5.m; the GLP (Giannone–Lenza–Primiceri 2015) marginal-likelihood machinery is BVAR/MFBVAR/bvarGLP.m. No external MATLAB downloads. Python 3 (standard library) Almost all build_*.py data builders Pure stdlib (urllib, json, csv, math) — no numpy/pandas/requests needed. The only exception is build_gvar_2025q4.py, which does import requests for the IMF WEO pull. Node (project's pinned toolchain) Coupling precompute, tests, build Run scripts via npx vite-node / npx tsx; the app builds with next build (output: 'export' → static site). vitest runs the compute test suite. FRED API key FRED data pulls Read from FRED_API_KEY; a hardcoded fallback key is present in the scripts, but always pass your own: FRED_API_KEY=<key> python3 pipeline/.... Never commit a key.

docs.title: 3.0 Source registries — how the deployed panels are built (Oct 2026)
docs.text:
Since the genuine-data re-estimation, every estimation panel is rebuilt from a machine-readable source registry, one file per economy, by one builder:

python3 -B pipeline/sources/build_panel.py --bloc NZ [--end 2026-Q2] [--out DIR] [--refresh] [--dry-run]
python3 -B pipeline/sources/compare.py --bloc NZ      # new panel vs the previous one, column by column
python3 -B pipeline/sources/scaffold.py --bloc NZ     # registry skeleton from an existing panel
  • pipeline/sources/registry/<CC>.json (52 economies) + _globals.json (the four GLB_* columns): for each variable, in the model's variable order, the provider, its exact key, how monthly/daily data become quarters (complete quarters only), any documented unit conversion or sample cut, and labels for proxies. Format and conventions (incl. "every exchange rate: rise = appreciation"): pipeline/sources/registry/README.md.
  • Providers (providers*.py): FRED, BIS, IMF, OECD, Eurostat, ECB, DBnomics, StatCan, Bundesbank, …; staged marks a series already in the repo (e.g. pipeline/sources/staged/) — not a live fetch, and each one is a to-do for a live adapter.
  • Derived columns (derived*.py): the 4-variable fiscal block (fiscal4: revenue and primary expenditure as % of GDP, EFFI direct or trailing-4-quarter, SFA as the exact debt-identity residual) and its fiscal_meta (d0 at the last published debt quarter, sfaDefault).
  • Rule: no fills of any kind. Every cell is a published value (after a declared conversion) or NaN. The output DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json has the estimator's usual schema, plus a .provenance.json (per column: provider, key, fetch vintage, first/last genuine quarter, notes, decision reference).
  • The source decisions behind the registries (D1a–D13: re-sourced rates, BIS effective exchange rates, Costa Rica from OECD accounts, India's new base, a GDP deflator for every fiscal economy, …) are in docs/reest-2026/PLAN.md §5.

The builders in §3.1 are the earlier route (how the panels were assembled up to Sep 2026). They are kept for reference and for the satellite files they produced (e.g. the trade weights and NFA anchors the deployed pack still uses); do not use them to rebuild a deployed panel.

docs.title: 3.1.1 Auto data-pull sourcing scripts (public APIs, no fabrication)
docs.text:
Every builder below pulls from a public API and stores the genuine observation only — ragged edges kept, no interpolation / back-fill / extrapolation. The first block is the standing macro/credit/ fiscal sourcing; the second block (under pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/) is the FSAP-expansion sourcing that assembles the 5 new blocs and the time-varying / external satellites. This table maps each data type → script → public API → what it pulls; the assembler scripts that turn the staged series into a DataRaw_<CC> panel follow.

Data type Script Public API What it pulls Macro (US) build_us_auto.py FRED all US quarterly macro + the 3 fiscal drivers, COVID handled Macro (EU/EFTA + EA) build_oecd_eurostat.py, build_ea_eurostat.py Eurostat SDMX (namq_10_gdp real GDP, prc_hicp HICP) quarterly real national accounts + prices for the EU/EFTA members and the EA aggregate Macro (FRED core) build_country_data.py FRED quarterly macro + financial block for the FRED-based economies Credit build_credit_*.py BIS total-credit / IMF price-of-credit + quantity-of-credit series per bloc Fiscal build_fiscal22_*.py (incl. build_fiscal22_columns.py) national / OECD / IMF fiscal sources the EFFI/SFA/FREV/FPEXP fiscal columns — build_fiscal22_columns.py is the assembler (carries the even-coupon EVEN_INTEREST EFFI, §5.2) Time-varying trade weights fsap_expansion_staging/weights/build_weights_timevarying.py IMF IMTS via api.imf.org SDMX 2.1 — flow IMF.STA:IMTS(1.0.0), indicators XG_FOB_USD+MG_CIF_USD, key COUNTRY.INDICATOR.COUNTERPART_COUNTRY.A, EA = G163 ANNUAL bilateral goods X+M, 1995–2024, 39 reporters (38 blocs + AE candidate);
