Assembling a staged bloc into a panel. Two assemblers turn the staged per-role series above into the DataRaw_<CC> layers of §4:

  • build_newbloc_panel.py [CC …] — assembles DataRaw_<CC>_2025q4.json from the staged newblocs/+neer/+trade/ series via a per-bloc MANIFEST (variable roles GDP/CONS/INV/GOV/EXP/IMP/CPI/HP/NEER/EQ/CREDIT/RATE/YIELD10; a ROLE dict fixes transformation + isFinancial per role, matching the deployed PL/EM template). Grid runs from max(GDP first obs, 2000Q1 EM-peer floor) to the 2025Q4 vintage (later 2026Q1/Q2 obs feed the separate rebase, §6/§10); raw values stored as-is, ragged edges kept, absent cells written null (leading NaN back-filled, the DK smoother imputes interior holes). A rate-less bloc (SG) is fine. Default runs all 5.
  • build_globals_new_blocs.py [CC …] — already in §3.1; injects the 4 GLB_* commons (dropping any legacy _US block, forcing the 4 globals isFinancial:1 per §3.4) → DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json. The same script that converts the euro standalones is reused for the FSAP new blocs via its CLI subset.

A bloc becomes GVAR-coupled purely by data: a row in the static weights file (weights_full_38.json = the 2021–23 average of the TV panel over the 38-bloc set — added as a row and as a partner everywhere, renormalized), block:'row' vars in its spec.json, and a {code,name,group} entry in app/src/lib/data/countries.ts (HK/SG/RO/PE/PH already present). See ADDING_A_COUNTRY.md for the full new-bloc runbook.

docs.title: 3.2 MATLAB estimators (pipeline/*.m)
docs.text:
Estimator Purpose Inputs Outputs export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m Canonical GVAR-EM loop — the coupled set (US endogenous, EA aggregate; 35 blocs in the deployed run — the bloc list comes from the weights file, the script is count-agnostic), missing data (COVID and, under GVAR_NOFILL=1, every gap) drawn per bloc, parfor Jacobi sweeps to convergence country_rawdata/DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json (or BVAR_RAWDATA_DIR), the weights file named by GVAR_WEIGHTS_FILE GVAR_OUTDIR/<CC>/*.json (default /tmp/gvar24_export; contract §5.3 + estimation_mask.json), GVAR_WORKSPACE (default /tmp/gvar24_workspace.mat) export_bvar_euro_redesign.m The 17 euro members as deployed — one member per run (CC=<cc>): domestic + fiscal block + euro-area external columns + two rest-of-euro-area aggregates (block:'row'), COVID-as-missing cgl_bvarV5; Oct 2026 settings BVAR_DIFF_GP=1 GVAR_NOFILL=1 CGL_FIXED_COMPANION=1, dummies for all 17 pipeline/euro_redesign_staging/<CC>/ (DataRaw, spec.json priors, fiscal_meta.json) EURO_OUTDIR/<CC>/ (else the staging folder) export_bvar_euro_fsap.m Earlier euro-member estimator — FSAP-style two-country BVARs (domestic + exogenous US block + 4 globals); not used for the deployed members DataRaw_<CODE>.json (11 domestic + 9-var US block, prepared block tags) /tmp/euro_fsap_export/<CODE>/*.json export_bvar_us_covid.m Isolated US-only single-country export (COVID-as-missing cgl_bvarV5) DataRaw_US*.json /tmp/us_export/*.json export_bvar_oecd_covid.m Single-country OECD exporter (COVID-as-missing) DataRaw_<CC>.json /tmp/<CC>_export/*.json export_bvar_country.m Generic single-country / domestic+US-block exporter DataRaw_<CC>.json per-bloc export dir export_bvar_us_fiscal.m US export with the fiscal drivers appended build_us_auto.py outputs US export dir

docs.title: 3.3 The fiscal stationary ("WN") prior — tag_fiscal_wn.py
docs.text:
§3.3–§3.5 describe one-off tagging sweeps of the earlier route. In the source route (§3.0) each registry entry carries its variable's prior, transformation and isFinancial directly, so the panels come out already tagged; the sweeps below are not part of the deployed chain. (In the deployed growth-rate model the estimator additionally tags the differenced GDP/price/deflator columns WN.)

The GLP/Minnesota prior in BVAR/MFBVAR/GLPreplicationWeb/bvarGLPmf.m builds the prior coefficient matrix b with a unit own-first-lag mean by default (a random walk: diagb=ones(n,1)). Any column listed in the pos vector gets its own-first-lag prior mean zeroed, turning that variable into a mean-reverting white-noise (WN) process under the prior:

% BVAR/MFBVAR/GLPreplicationWeb/bvarGLPmf.m, lines 192–195
b=zeros(k,n);
diagb=ones(n,1);
diagb(pos)=0;          % zero the own-first-lag prior mean for the 'pos' columns -> stationary/WN
b(2:n+1,:)=diag(diagb);

pos is the 3rd positional argument of the COVID-as-missing sampler cgl_bvarV5 (which renames it pos=stationary; and forwards it as 'pos' to bvarGLPmf):

% BVAR/MFBVAR/cgl_bvarV5.m
function [Xcond,storeP,BETA,SU,X_interp0,Dforecast] = cgl_bvarV5(x,p,stationary,nDraws,...)
pos=stationary;
... r = bvarGLPmf(..., 'pos', pos);

Why this matters. Before this change every call passed [] for stationary, so every variable in every bloc was a prior random walk. The fiscal GDP ratios — FREV_GDP (revenue/GDP), FPEXP_GDP (primary expenditure/GDP), and SFA (the stock-flow adjustment) — are economically stationary: they fluctuate around a long-run share, they do not drift. Under the RW prior the projected ratios stayed pinned near their last observation at the long horizon (US revenue stuck near ~19%). The WN prior lets them mean-revert to their in-sample means — US FREV_GDP → ~17.9% (sample mean 17.91, last obs 18.77; commit e38673a) instead of drifting. The effective interest rate EFFI is genuinely persistent and stays RW.

How the tag is consumed. Each estimator reads the per-variable prior field out of the raw JSON via a priorsfrom helper and builds the WN column-index vector, passed as cgl_bvarV5's 3rd arg:

% export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m — on the kept domestic block, indices into x=[dom | stars]
statCols = find(Spec.Prior(keep)=="WN")';   % empty for the 44 non-fiscal blocs
[Xcond,~,B,S,~,Dfc] = cgl_bvarV5(x, lags, Dc.statCols, nDraws, nBurn, ...);

% export_bvar_euro_fsap.m
statCols = find(Prior=="WN")';
[~,storeP,BETA,SU,~,Dforecast] = cgl_bvarV5(x, lags, statCols, nDraws, nBurn, ...);

Because the stars (ROW*) are appended after the domestic columns, the WN indices (which point into the domestic block) are unchanged by the star append — and they remain on the domestic ratios only; stars are always RW. statCols is empty for the 44 non-fiscal blocs, where pos=zeros(1,0) behaves exactly like the old [] — so the WN change is a byte-identical no-op for every bloc that carries no fiscal ratio.

priorsfrom and the cell-array trap. tag_fiscal_wn.py writes prior on every variable object (not just the 3 WN ones) so the field set stays homogeneous: MATLAB's jsondecode returns J.variables as a struct array only when all objects share the same fields; a partial prior tag makes it a cell array and breaks the estimators' arrayfun(@(v)v.id, J.variables) calls. priorsfrom (present in both estimators) is written to be robust to either shape. The Python tagger is format-preserving (a targeted text splice — only the inserted/updated prior bytes change; the data array is untouched) and idempotent (re-running once tags are present is a no-op). It edits the globals-augmented file the GVAR loop actually reads, preferring _glob → _2025q4 → plain.

python3 pipeline/tag_fiscal_wn.py
# DataRaw_US_glob.json: 0 field(s) changed this run; WN = ['FPEXP_GDP', 'FREV_GDP', 'SFA']; RW count = 35
# ... (idempotent: 0 changes once tagged)

The exported spec.json carries the real prior per variable (WN/RW), so the contract and the per-economy coherence table reflect it. Committed in 6f0161a (plumbing) and 22250be/e38673a (the refit). See the fiscal recursion in fiscal-block-methodology.md.

docs.title: 3.4 Global-commons financial coherence — tag_global_financial.py
docs.text:
The COVID-as-missing masking in the estimator NaN's the 2020Q2–Q4 window only for the slow national-accounts macro variables (isFinancial:0), so the Durbin–Koopman smoother imputes them; fast-moving market prices (isFinancial:1) are kept observed through COVID and condition that imputation (§5.1, step 3). An audit found two of the four US-determined global commons mis-tagged: GLB_USEQ (US equity index) was isFinancial:false in every non-US bloc, and GLB_OIL (oil price) was isFinancial:false in every bloc — so they were being NaN-imputed across COVID like a GDP series, which is incoherent for a daily-quoted market price. (GLB_USLR long rate and GLB_USBAA BAA spread were already financial.)

tag_global_financial.py flips both to isFinancial:1 in every DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json so they match WTI_US/PZTEXP and stay observed through COVID. It is a value-only splice (the isFinancial field already exists on every object, so it never inserts a field — avoiding the same cell-array trap as §3.3), format-preserving, and idempotent. The source-of-truth fix is in build_globals_new_blocs.py, which now forces all four globals (GLB_FINANCIAL = {GLB_OIL, GLB_USLR, GLB_USBAA, GLB_USEQ}, line 37) financial when a new bloc is built, so future rebuilds stay coherent; the tagger is the one-time sweep over already-built globs.

python3 pipeline/tag_global_financial.py
# DataRaw_CA_glob.json: 0 field(s) changed this run; {'GLB_USEQ': 1, 'GLB_OIL': 1}

Committed in 22250be/e38673a.

docs.title: 3.5 Canada IP as a log-level — build_ca_ip_level.py
docs.text:
The CA glob's IP_CA column had been stored as a y/y growth rate (transformation:"lin"), incoherent with the US/UK IP blocs (stored as levels, transformation:"log"). build_ca_ip_level.py rebuilds it as a quarterly level index using the same growth-chaining convention as build_gvar_2025q4.py (level_t = level_{t-1}·(1+g_t)):

  1. average the discontinued monthly FRED level index CANPROINDMISMEI (Index 2015=100, ends 2024-02) to complete quarters (last complete quarter ≈ 2023-Q4);
  2. chain forward from there with the q/q growth series PRINTO01CAQ657S (to 2025-Q4): level_t = level_{t-1}·(1 + g_t/100);
  3. align onto the CA glob's exact quarterly grid (1998-Q1 … 2025-Q4), replace the IP_CA column, and flip the spec to transformation:"log", isFinancial:0 (prior RW unchanged).

It reads FRED via the public fredgraph.csv endpoint (no API key), caching CSVs under pipeline/country_raw/. It asserts the reconstructed level is positive/finite/smooth (no q/q spike beyond ~±20%) and ends near the observed ~106–107 range.

python3 pipeline/build_ca_ip_level.py
# WROTE .../DataRaw_CA_glob.json (IP_CA now LEVEL, transformation=log, isFinancial=0)

Committed in 9839a46 (the CA-only targeted re-estimate, §10.2) and folded into the full refit e38673a. After this rebuild, CA's IP propagates correctly through partners' ROW* stars (the earlier CA-IP approximation is removed).

Coherence audit. All 1048 ported variable rows (across the 50 blocs in app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/spec.json) were audited for transformation·prior·isFinancial coherence; the per-economy table is in the user manual (Appendix B, regenerated from the shipped specs).

docs.title: 3.6 The DSGE lens payload — the IRF census and build_drivers_index.mjs
docs.text:
Everything above builds the BVAR side. The app also ships a DSGE impulse-response payload, used by two features that read a scenario through a structural model: the policy counterfactual, which shifts a scenario path by the impulse response to a change in the policy rule, and the experimental Drivers panel, which reads a scenario path back into the structural shocks of one chosen model over the first twelve forecast quarters (the method, its licence and its limits are in drivers-decomposition.md). This payload is produced by one Node script and involves no DataRaw, no estimation, no port and no coupling. A re-estimation ships it unchanged, and a change to it re-estimates nothing.

Where the impulse responses come from. Every lens on the Drivers menu is a model of the Macroeconomic Model Base (MMB), and the responses ship with one of two provenances, recorded per model in the index:

  • Census models (eight). Exported by an MMB census run under the model's Taylor rule and staged as pipeline/census_irfs/<model>/Taylor.json, with pipeline/census_irfs/MANIFEST.json carrying one sha256 per file. These are copied into the served tree. They are EA_SW03, EA_SWW14, CA_LS07, HK_FP13, BRA_SAMBA08, UK_SM11, and the two 54-shock FRB/US linearisations US_FRB22 (source directory US_FRB22_mcap) and US_FRB22_var.
  • Models already in the app's IRF tree (four). US_SW07, US_CMR14, US_FRB08 and US_FRB22_mcap are read in place from app/public/data/dsge/irfs/<model>/SW.json and are indexed, not copied; the two FRB/US entries carry the sourceNote "MMB rule file". US_SW07 and US_CMR14 were regenerated with their full native shock sets when Drivers shipped, which is why they are much larger than before (215 KB and 1.79 MB); the interest_ and fiscal_ columns the policy counterfactual reads moved by ~5e-11, re-export rounding only.

The build step. One script produces the whole payload:

node app/scripts/build_drivers_index.mjs

It takes no arguments and resolves the repository root from its own location, so it runs from anywhere. It reads pipeline/census_irfs/MANIFEST.json, the eight pipeline/census_irfs/<srcDir>/Taylor.json files, pipeline/_shockbench/class_maps.json, and the four app/public/data/dsge/irfs/<model>/SW.json files. It writes app/public/data/dsge/census/index.json (36 KB) and the eight app/public/data/dsge/census/<model>.json copies (1.0 MB for the six small models, 10.75 MB and 10.57 MB for the two FRB/US lenses). A census file whose sha256 does not match the manifest is a hard error: the script refuses to ship it rather than warning.

Every field in the index is derived from the response arrays, not curated by hand. For each model the script records the usable shocks — a shock is usable iff it carries all three common observables output, inflationq and interest and its stacked three-observable, twelve-quarter response path has Euclidean norm at least 1e-9 — and names anything it drops together with the reason (zero-response, missing-observable). It records the collinear pairs, |cos| > 0.95 between unit-normalised stacked response paths, computed exactly as pipeline/bench_simple_decomp.m computes it. For the two 54-shock FRB/US lenses it additionally records the clusters — connected components of that collinearity graph, each labelled by its largest member's equation name, ordered by size — and a validated default naming, the one cluster triple its own build-time recovery scan selects among those that recover a known shock sequence to 1e-6. Finally it embeds pipeline/_shockbench/class_maps.json verbatim as index.shockClasses, so the browser never fetches anything under pipeline/ at runtime.

Remark 1 (Clusters are connected components, not bundles of parallel columns). A cluster is a connected component of the |cos| > 0.95 graph, so its members are chained through collinear links rather than mutually parallel: collinearity is not transitive, and two members of one component can sit well below 0.95 against each other. The single column the app names for a cluster is the first principal component of the member set, not a stand-in for an already-parallel bundle. Do not describe cluster membership as pairwise near-parallel, in the docs or in the interface.

Remark 2 (The census sources are not on the deploy branch). pipeline/census_irfs/ lives on explore/shock-benchmark, together with the rest of the research provenance for this feature. On the deploy branch build_drivers_index.mjs fails at its first read, MANIFEST.json, so regenerating the payload means checking that tree out first. Nothing is lost by not having it day to day: the shipped copies are byte-identical to their census sources by the sha gate, and the tests re-verify that hash on every run.

Example 1 (Re-shipping the payload after a class map changes). We amend a model's shock-class membership and re-ship the payload that carries it. Class membership has exactly one source of truth, pipeline/_shockbench/class_maps.json; the copy inside index.json is a build product, so editing it there would be overwritten on the next build and would fail the provenance test in the meantime. We proceed in steps. First we edit the class map. Then we rebuild the index, which copies the amended map into it verbatim and re-derives every other field. Then we re-run the class-recovery bench, because a changed class map changes what that bench measured and therefore what the class view is licensed at — the criteria, and what to do when a bench stops passing, are in MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md §H. Finally the fast test suite, which re-hashes every shipped file against the index and asserts the embedded map equals the source. The commands are as follows:

# from the repo root, with pipeline/census_irfs/ checked out (Remark 2)
$EDITOR pipeline/_shockbench/class_maps.json                        # the single source of truth
node app/scripts/build_drivers_index.mjs                            # -> census/index.json + the 8 copies
matlab -batch "run('pipeline/bench_class_recovery.m')" | tee docs/paper/class_recovery_results.txt
cd app && npm test                                                  # includes the 26 Drivers licence tests

The payload's weight in the static export, and how much of it a user actually downloads, are in BUILD_AND_CI.md. What the class view is licensed at, and the rule for a bench that stops passing, are in MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md §H.

docs.title: 4. The DataRaw precedence chain
docs.text:
Each bloc has up to three raw-input layers; the GVAR-EM loop picks the first that exists (export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m, the per-bloc load loop):

if BVAR_RAWDATA_DIR set → <dir>/DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json   % STRICT: no fallback (the Oct 2026 run used this)
raw = DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json        % globals-augmented (domestic + 4 GLB_* commons; _US dropped)
if missing → DataRaw_<CC>_2025q4.json   % legacy: common 2025Q4 endpoint (WEO-Denton extended)
if missing → DataRaw_<CC>.json          % legacy: the original FRED/Eurostat pull

In the deployed data every economy has a _glob file built by pipeline/sources/build_panel.py (§3.0); the two fallback layers are legacy.

Layer Built by Contents DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json pipeline/sources/build_panel.py since Oct 2026 (earlier: build_globals_new_blocs.py + fiscal/financial editors) domestic block + 4 global commons; the fiscal columns live here DataRaw_<CC>_2025q4.json build_gvar_2025q4.py domestic series extended to a common 2025Q4 endpoint (balanced panel) DataRaw_<CC>.json build_country_data.py / build_oecd_*.py the original pull (domestic + US block)

The _glob file is the production input: it carries the 4 globals the GVAR estimator expects and the fiscal block (built by derived.fiscal4 in the source route; earlier, edited in place by the 4-variable fiscal builders). The 3 RoW stars are not stored in the glob — the loop computes them at solve time from partners' completed panels and appends them only at export.

Important. This precedence is offline only — it governs which raw input the MATLAB estimator reads. The browser app never sees DataRaw_*; it reads the ported app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/ JSON.

docs.title: 5. The GVAR-EM loop (export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m)
docs.text: The loop is an EM- (expectation–maximisation-) style fixed-point over the cross-country foreign components. It interleaves a Gibbs/DK imputation step (estimate each bloc, fill the COVID + foreign-star holes) with a trade-weighting step (rebuild every bloc's RoW stars from partners' completed panels), and iterates until the foreign components stop moving.

docs.title: 5.1 Per-iteration internals
docs.text:
1. Bootstrap the US (closed anchor). Estimate the US once with no stars (cgl_bvarV5(xUS, …)) over the COVID-masked domestic block, take the posterior-mean DK-completed series XcUS = mean(Xcond,3) and form its [realGDP, price, rate] panel. This seeds iteration-1's stars. With US_ENDOGENOUS=1 the US is then folded into the loop and re-estimated with its own ROW*_US stars (the no-stars fit is discarded — a warm start, not exported).
  2. Build stars (buildstars). For each bloc, ROWDEM/ROWINF/ROWFIN = trade-weighted averages of partners' real-GDP growth / inflation / short rate, renormalised over the partners present each quarter (unbalanced panel). Stars are 4·Δ(100·log) (annualised %), not 400·. Per-component availability: a rate-less partner (today only SG) still feeds DEM/INF; hyperinflation partners (AR, while in the roster) are dropped from INF/FIN but kept in DEM. Without GVAR_NOFILL, leading NaN is back-filled; under GVAR_NOFILL=1 (deployed run) a quarter with no reporting partner stays missing and is drawn by the sampler like any gap; internal COVID NaN is left for the smoother. Weights are the static row by default, or the per-quarter time-varying IMTS rows when GVAR_TV_WEIGHTS is active (§5.2) — so the shifting trade structure enters the star history.
  3. Estimate each bloc (parfor). x = [domestic | ROWDEM ROWINF ROWFIN]; over 2020Q2–Q4 NaN only the macro columns (domestic isFinancial==false + ROWDEM + ROWINF); keep all financial columns + ROWFIN observed. The financial set kept observed now includes all four global commons GLB_OIL/GLB_USLR/GLB_USBAA/GLB_USEQ (after the §3.4 coherence fix), matching the domestic market prices. The WN/stationary columns (fiscal ratios; under BVAR_DIFF_GP=1 also the differenced real GDP, price and deflator) enter as the 3rd positional statCols arg (§3.3). Under GVAR_NOFILL=1 every other gap in the panel is missing data too: a seed fill only starts the chain, and the cells the sampler drew are exported in estimation_mask.json. cgl_bvarV5(..., statCols, ..., 'sur',0,'noc',1,'Ndraws',1000, 'Ndrawsdiscard',500) then imputes the macro holes via the Durbin–Koopman smoother conditioned on the observed financials. The completed panel is the posterior mean mean(Xcond,3).
  4. Converge. Compute max|Δstar| across blocs (excluding the COVID-NaN'd macro-star cells, which are MC noise; ROWFIN stays in the metric). Stop when it>1 && max|Δstar| < TOL.

This is a Jacobi sweep: all stars are built from the frozen start-of-iteration state, then all non-US blocs (or all blocs when US_ENDOGENOUS) are estimated independently in parallel — same fixed point as Gauss–Seidel, ~Ncores faster.

Algorithm (EM-style fixed point over the foreign components).

Input:  per-bloc panels {X_c}, trade weights W, COVID window 2020Q2..Q4, TOL, MAXIT
Output: per-bloc completed panels {X̃_c} + posterior draws (the 8-file contract)

  ── E-step seed ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  Estimate US with NO stars (cgl_bvarV5, COVID-macro-masked) → X̃_US⁰ = mean(Xcond,3)
  Seed each bloc's foreign stars S_c⁰ from the iteration-0 completed panels.

  ── EM loop (Jacobi) ──────────────────────────────────────────
  for it = 1 .. MAXIT:
    M-step / star build:   for every bloc c:               # frozen start-of-iter state
        S_c = buildstars(W, {X̃_p}_{p≠c})                   # ROWDEM/ROWINF/ROWFIN, 4·Δ(100·log),
                                                            #   per-quarter renormalised over present partners
    E-step / re-estimate:  parfor every bloc c:
        x_c = [domestic_c | S_c]                            # WN cols = statCols (3rd arg)
        NaN the 2020Q2..Q4 MACRO cells (isFinancial==false + ROWDEM + ROWINF) only;
            keep all financials + ROWFIN (incl. GLB_*) observed
        [Xcond, β_c, Σ_c, ...] = cgl_bvarV5(x_c, lags=3, statCols, nDraws, nBurn, 1, H, ...)
        X̃_c = mean(Xcond,3)                                 # DK-smoother posterior-mean completion
    convergence:  Δ = max_c |S_c^{it} − S_c^{it−1}|         # exclude COVID-NaN'd macro-star cells
    if it>1 and Δ < TOL: break                              # MC noise floor ≈ 0.13

  save /tmp/gvar24_workspace.mat   then   exportbloc(c) → /tmp/gvar24_export/<c>/ (8 files)

The E-step is the Durbin–Koopman data-augmentation completion of the foreign blocs under COVID-macro-masked / financials-observed missingness; the M-step is the Bayesian (GLP) re-estimation plus the trade-weighted star rebuild. Iterating to a fixed point in the completed stars is what couples the blocs at estimation time (distinct from the solve-time coupling x=Mx+d in §7).

docs.title: 5.2 Defaults & env knobs
docs.text:
In-script defaults (lags=3; H=20; nDraws=1000; nBurn=500; MAXIT=12; TOL=0.03;):

Env var Default Effect BVAR_DIFF_GP unset 1 ⇒ real GDP and the price series (incl. DEFL_<CC>) are estimated as growth rates (4·Δlog, WN own-lag prior), every other column in levels; exported as the equivalent level VAR (one more lag). Deployed. GVAR_NOFILL unset 1 ⇒ no fills: leading, interior and trailing gaps are missing data drawn by the sampler (seed fill only to start the chain); writes estimation_mask.json. Needs BVAR_DIFF_GP=1. Deployed. GVAR_FIXHYPER unset 1 ⇒ the EM sweeps use the smooth sampler (hyperparameters at the GLP mode, re-seeded stream) so sweep-to-sweep changes measure the fixed point; then one final full-MH pass at the converged stars gives the shipped posterior. Deployed (converged at sweep 6). BVAR_SEED unset seeds the run's RNG (rng(seed,'twister')); with the per-bloc stream fix in cgl_bvarV5 this gives common random numbers across sweeps. Deployed run: 1. GVAR_SERIAL unset 1 ⇒ bloc loop runs serially (determinism tests) BVAR_RAWDATA_DIR unset read every DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json from this folder, strict (no fallback layers, §4) GVAR_OUTDIR / GVAR_WORKSPACE /tmp/gvar24_export / /tmp/gvar24_workspace.mat where the exports and the saved workspace go (set both for concurrent runs) US_ENDOGENOUS unset (anchor) 1 ⇒ the US joins the loop with its own ROW*_US stars (requires a weights.US row). Set it for production. BVAR_GVAR_BLOCS all blocs in the weights file space-separated subset, US first (for fast validation) NDRAWS 1000 (burn auto = NDRAWS/2) MCMC draws per bloc MAXIT 12 max convergence sweeps; MAXIT=1 ⇒ single-country / separated (one-shot historical stars, no coupling) TOL 0.03 convergence tolerance on max|Δstar| (Monte-Carlo noise floor ≈ 0.13) GVAR_WEIGHTS_FILE weights_full.json, else weights_24bloc.json which weights/bloc list to use; the file's blocs field is authoritative (US first). Always set it: the default weights_full.json is the old 33-bloc file that still lists AR, IL and RU. The deployed run passed app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_full_38.json (35 blocs, = weights_24bloc.json) GVAR_DUMMY_BLOCS the 16-bloc default (CL CN CO CR EA ID IL IN IS JP KR MX NO TR UK ZA) space-separated override of the quarterly seasonal-dummy blocs (dummies enter estimation + imputation for blocs with a genuinely NSA-seasonal series + the even-EFFI blocs). The deployed run added HK PE (18 codes; IL is no longer estimated, so 17 blocs) GVAR_TV_WEIGHTS on when weights_timevarying.json present 0 ⇒ static row everywhere (byte-identical legacy). Active ⇒ the annual IMTS bilateral rows are applied per quarter in buildstars, so the shifting trade structure reaches the star history the blocs are estimated on (solve-time coupling still uses the static file) GVAR_POLISH_EXACT off 1 ⇒ optional final exact-DA "polish" sweep at the frozen stars. Off for the shipped coupled models — the polish raises companion persistence and lifts ρ(M) above 1 (measured 1.0067), making pinned spillovers non-contractive; the coupled ship uses the fixed-companion posterior from the converged outer loop GVAR_NSA_FORECAST unset ⇒ SA forward path the shipped forward forecast is seasonally adjusted — the dummy row uses the annual-mean deterministic term [¼,¼,¼] (dummies stay in estimation + imputation; the forward path is smooth). Set it to keep the quarter-specific NSA forecast

The seasonal-dummy, time-varying-weights, SA-forecast and two-stage (GVAR_POLISH_EXACT / fixed-companion E-step) mechanics are the seasonal-v2 additions; this table is the knob inventory — see REESTIMATING_MODELS.md §1.3 for the depth (why each default is what it is, the ρ(M) evidence, the two-stage E-step).

# Production, as deployed (Oct 2026; docs/reest-2026/runs/run_gvar35b.sh — ~1 h 40 min on 4 cores)
BVAR_DIFF_GP=1 US_ENDOGENOUS=1 NDRAWS=1000 MAXIT=30 BVAR_SEED=1 GVAR_FIXHYPER=1 GVAR_NOFILL=1 \
  GVAR_DUMMY_BLOCS="CL CN CO CR EA ID IL IN IS JP KR MX NO TR UK ZA HK PE" \
  GVAR_WEIGHTS_FILE="$PWD/app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_full_38.json" \
  BVAR_RAWDATA_DIR="$PWD/pipeline/country_rawdata" \
  GVAR_OUTDIR=<run dir>/gvar35 GVAR_WORKSPACE=<run dir>/gvar35_ws.mat \
  matlab -batch "run('pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m')"
# (time-varying weights are on by default because weights_timevarying.json exists)

# Fast smoke test: 3 blocs, few draws, 1 sweep (separated, no coupling)
BVAR_GVAR_BLOCS="US EA JP" NDRAWS=200 MAXIT=1 US_ENDOGENOUS=1 \
  matlab -batch "run('pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m')"

Outputs. The full estimation state is saved to GVAR_WORKSPACE (default /tmp/gvar24_workspace.mat) before export (so an export-only bug is a cheap re-export, not a multi-hour re-estimation), then each bloc's file contract goes to GVAR_OUTDIR/<CC>/ (default /tmp/gvar24_export/<CC>/).

docs.title: 5.3 The 8-file per-bloc contract
docs.text:
Each export dir contains:

File Contents spec.json { n, seasonalRows?, qoyNext?, variables:[{id, name, transformation('log'\|'lin'), isFinancial, prior, block}] } — block ∈ domestic/external/global/row/fiscal (older specs also us); prior ∈ RW (own-first-lag mean 1, default) / WN (own-first-lag mean 0, stationary — the 3 fiscal ratios FREV_GDP/FPEXP_GDP/SFA, §3.3, and under BVAR_DIFF_GP the differenced GDP/price/deflator) companion_mean.json { betahat, sigmahat, n, lags, seasonalRows? } companion_draws.json { beta, beta_shape, sigma, sigma_shape, n_draws, n, lags } (posterior draws → Full uncertainty bands) baseline.json unconditional forecast in growth/display space (mean, q05, q16, q84, q95, horizon) baseline_levels.json same forecast in level space historical.json / historical_levels.json last 40 quarters (growth / level) — observed data (null where unpublished), not the DK counterfactual transformations.json per-variable 'log'/'lin' estimation_mask.json only under GVAR_NOFILL=1: the cells the sampler drew (leading/interior/trailing gaps, COVID-withheld cells) — provenance

Plus, where applicable: fiscal_meta.json { d0, sfaDefault, idx:{gdp,deflator,revenue,primaryExp,effRate,sfa} } (copied from pipeline/fiscal_meta/<CC>.json) and the GVAR weights_*.json.

docs.title: 6. Port — into app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/
docs.text:
Two routes, as in the deployed Oct 2026 chain (docs/reest-2026/runs/port_to_app.sh):

  • The 35 GVAR blocs are copied raw from the run directory — full double precision — including estimation_mask.json. (The Sep 2026 live model was shipped the same way.) Delete the old companion_draws.json.gz so it is re-gzipped from the new draws, never left stale.
  • The 17 euro members go through port_gvar_exports.py, which writes the 8 contract files at 6 significant figures, compact JSON (f"{x:.6g}"; non-finite → null; separators=(",",":")), copies estimation_mask.json verbatim, and then regenerates fiscal_meta.json and external_meta.json by variable id from the just-ported specs (stops if an external_meta idxIds entry is missing from the spec).
# Members (6 sig-figs; meta regenerated by id)
GVAR_EXPORT_DIR=<run dir>/members GVAR_PORT_BLOCS="AT BE DE EE ES FI FR GR IE IT LT LU LV NL PT SI SK" \
  python3 pipeline/port_gvar_exports.py
python3 pipeline/port_gvar_exports.py --dry-run          # report sizes, write nothing

# fiscal_meta from the panel build (GVAR economies) / the member staging folders
cp pipeline/country_rawdata/fiscal_meta_<CC>.json app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/fiscal_meta.json
cp pipeline/euro_redesign_staging/<CC>/fiscal_meta.json app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/fiscal_meta.json

# For raw-copied blocs: re-resolve the positional indices against the CURRENT specs (by variable id)
node pipeline/fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs
node pipeline/fix_external_meta_indices.mjs              # uses the recorded idxIds; --dry-run to report

Override the source dir with GVAR_EXPORT_DIR. The porter prints per-bloc file count and the MB → MB size reduction.

The app's weights file must match the estimation's. The browser (and the coupling precompute, §7) reads app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_24bloc.json. Its content must be the bloc set the model was estimated on — in the deployed pack it equals weights_full_38.json (35 blocs). Historically validate_and_promote_weights.py promotes weights_full*.json → weights_24bloc.json (rows sum to 1, no US row). The filename is a legacy name; the app keys off the blocs field.

🔴 Positional indices. fiscal_meta.json (six idx) and external_meta.json (five idx) store column positions. A spec change that inserts or reorders variables re-points them — the EA effRate-lands-on-equity (~col 537) debt explosion (33-bloc refit), and in Oct 2026 the inserted DEFL_<CC> sent 35 blocs' external fx index to the wrong series. The porter now regenerates both by id; for raw copies run the two fix_*_indices.mjs scripts above (deflator = DEFL_<CC> where present, else the first HICP|CPI|JGDP|PGDP; idempotent; every other field kept). fiscal-meta-indices.test.ts and data/meta-column-indices.test.ts catch stale indices — run them; the deploy does not.

After the port the deployed chain continues in app/ (all scripts in app/scripts/, see docs/reest-2026/runs/stageA.sh, stageB.sh): stamp_calendar.mjs (writes each history's firstQuarter) → build_coverage_manifest.mjs --panel-quarter <Q> → the coupling (§7) → nowcast_complete.mjs --write --baselines (the coupled nowcast of the ragged edge; check it converged) → apply_member_completion.mjs → roll_d0_forward.mjs → regen_gr_baselines_via_loader.mjs → regen_gvar_bands.mjs → gzip_companion_draws.mjs → build_coverage_manifest.mjs → vintages_publish.mjs → pack-build.mjs --pack-id <new id> → verify_cutoffs.mjs --allow-ragged --dating-only → pack-verify.mjs --full. npm run data:model-update -- --then-shift (UPDATE_MANUAL.md §7) wraps the dating, re-stamping and verification and then shifts the panel to the latest published quarter; the Oct 2026 run called the steps one by one instead (its panels already ended at the latest quarter, with a ragged edge to nowcast).

docs.title: 7. Coupling (precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs) — the pre-shipped inverse
docs.text:
The browser solves the cross-country fixed point x = (I−M)⁻¹ d from a pre-shipped coupling artifact. The in-browser M build (DK-smoother probes) is ~19 min at 24 blocs and worse at the augmented endogenous dimension, so pre-shipping is mandatory, not an optimisation.

app/scripts/precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs (run via npx vite-node):

  1. assembles the deployed bloc bundle exactly like the loader (a non-US bloc qualifies iff its spec.json has block:'row' vars; US is always included), self-configures the topology, and computes modelSig;
  2. builds M in JS (buildGVARCouplingM / buildGVARCouplingMEndo when US_ENDOGENOUS);
  3. inverts (I−M) via MATLAB BLAS (app/scripts/invert_coupling.m; the NumPy invert_coupling.py is the no-MATLAB fallback);
  4. writes the gzipped app/public/data/bvar/gvar/coupling_default.json.gz ({ modelSig, pinStructure:'', dim, rhoSpectral, M, invImM }, 6-sig-fig). The plain .json is removed; the app reads only the .gz (through the data pack, hash-checked, decompressed in-browser via DecompressionStream). In the deployed pack (35 blocs, dim 2180) the artifact is 35,646,004 B gzipped; the raw JSON would exceed GitHub's 100 MB per-file limit, so gzip is mandatory. The coupled dimension is nB·60 + 80 (each bloc's star block + the US-global augmentation), so it grows with the bloc count: 33·60 + 80 = 2060 (mid-2026) → 35·60 + 80 = 2180 (deployed).

After writing the artifact, re-stamp the pack (pack-build.mjs): the manifest records the coupling's hash and the weights it was built from (gvar.coupling.inputs.weightsSha256), and pack-verify checks that they match the shipped weights.

cd app
npx vite-node scripts/precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs

Keyed to the data by modelSig. The artifact MUST be regenerated whenever any deployed bloc changes — a stale modelSig is rejected and the app falls back to the slow path. The script prints ρ(M) but does not stop on ρ ≥ 1: check it yourself.

The augmented operator's spectral radius grows with the bloc count (it must stay < 1 for a stable fixed point):

Topology dim ρ(M) 6-bloc — 0.59 24-bloc (frozen anchor) — 0.726 33-bloc (endogenous US, mid-2026) 2060 ~0.92–0.945 (artifacts of Jun–Sep 2026) 35-bloc (endogenous US, Sep 2026 model) 2180 0.957724 35-bloc (endogenous US, deployed Oct 2026 genuine-data re-estimation) 2180 0.971875 (LIVE coupling_default.json.gz) — must stay < 1 (the fixed-companion E-step keeps it contractive; GVAR_POLISH_EXACT would push it > 1, §5.2)

rhoSpectral moves with each refit; what matters is that it stays < 1. The deployed value is higher than before, so shocks spread a little further and last a little longer (docs/reest-2026/REVIEW.md §2). The artifact's modelSig (per-bloc n_lags_H_<betahat-fingerprint>) keys it to the exact data; the deployed one reads US:40_4_20_… (US n = 40, lags = 4).

docs.title: 8. Test & deploy
docs.text:
cd app
npx tsc --noEmit                       # type-check
npm test                               # FAST compute suite (excludes the heavy solver canaries)
npm run test:heavy                     # HEAVY solver/perf canaries (1 fork) — BOTH halves gate deploy
BASE_PATH=/bvar-scenario npm run build # static export (next build, output:'export')

Tests live in app/src/__tests__/ (compute/, data/, …). The suite is split: npm test is vitest run minus ten heavy --exclude globs (gvar-us-endogenous, gvar-direct-channel, gvar-band-solve, gvar-band-solve-levelunits, gvar-nowcast-completion, gvar-closed-form-*, affine-blockernels-parity, gvar-kernel-affine-independence, gvar-external-spillover, gvar-anderson); npm run test:heavy runs exactly those, serialised to one fork; npm run test:all sweeps everything (see BUILD_AND_CI.md). The deploy workflows do not run tests — running them is the maintainer's gate. Key canaries (all in the fast suite):

  • scenario-scale-convention — the scale conventions (100·log, 4·Δ, q/q annualised).
  • gvar-convergence — Gauss–Seidel ≡ closed-form fixed point.
  • gvar-coupling-artifact — the shipped .gz matches a live rebuild (and its modelSig).
  • fiscal-meta-indices and data/meta-column-indices — the STALE-POSITIONAL-INDEX guards (§6).

What every build does enforce is prebuild: gzip_companion_draws.mjs → vintages_publish.mjs → pack-verify.mjs --full. A pack whose files differ from its manifest, whose dating is inconsistent, or whose coupling was built from other weights fails the build, so it cannot be deployed.

Feature tests cover fiscal*, gvar-us-endogenous, driftSetter-joint-solve, conditioning-*, the drag-perf (gvar-drag-*), the render memoization (chartgrid-render-memo), and the optimistic dot (conditioned-dot-optimistic, right-click-plant-at-cursor).

Deploy is a push of the same commit to two remotes' main:

git push bvarscenario main   # ⚠️ GitHub Pages (matyasfarkas.github.io/bvar-scenario)
git push gmapsmodel main     # ⚠️ Netlify (gmapsmodel.com) — both only after a green gate, with confirmation

gmapsmodel.com (Netlify) builds from gmapsmodel/GMAPS per netlify.toml (base = "app", npm ci && npm run build, publish out, domain root). Its ignore rule skips a push that changes neither app/ nor netlify.toml; because Netlify runs it inside app/, the paths are written as repo-root pathspecs (:/app :/netlify.toml) and compared against $CACHED_COMMIT_REF. (The first version matched nothing and cancelled every build from 2026-08-05 until 298dfd8d, 2026-10-08.) After a push, check that https://gmapsmodel.com/data/manifest.json shows the new packId.

GitHub Pages — the bvarscenario repo (BVARScenarioTool) holds the workflow .github/workflows/deploy-to-website.yml:

The Action triggers on a push to main that touches app/** or netlify.toml (so a data-only change under app/public/data/** still deploys). It runs npm ci && npm run build with BASE_PATH=/bvar-scenario, checks out the matyasfarkas/starter-hugo-academic website repo (token WEBSITE_DEPLOY_TOKEN), then rm -rf website/static/bvar-scenario/* and cp -r app/out/* website/static/bvar-scenario/, and commits/pushes the website repo. The starter-hugo-academic site is a Hugo Academic site published to GitHub Pages, which rebuilds and serves it at the /bvar-scenario path. This workflow has no Hugo step; any Hugo version pin (0.122.0 — 0.123+ removed getCSV and broke the theme) lives in the starter-hugo-academic repo, not in this workflow.

Never push without explicit per-action confirmation (deploy = irreversible public change). See REESTIMATING_MODELS.md §5 for the full deploy gate.

docs.title: 9. End-to-end (copy-paste skeleton)
docs.text:
The yearly model update as run in Oct 2026. The exact, replayable scripts (with absolute paths) are in docs/reest-2026/runs/; this is the same sequence in outline. Each step is a decision point — check its output before the next.

# from the repo root
# 1. rebuild every estimation panel from its source registry (no fills). The 35 coupled economies go to
#    pipeline/country_rawdata/ (the default --out); the 17 euro members to
#    pipeline/euro_redesign_staging/<CC>/ (pass --out). Review with compare.py before estimating.
python3 -B pipeline/sources/build_panel.py --bloc <CC> [--out <dir>]

# 2. estimate the 35 coupled blocs (≈1 h 40 min on 4 cores) — full flags in §5.2
BVAR_DIFF_GP=1 US_ENDOGENOUS=1 NDRAWS=1000 MAXIT=30 BVAR_SEED=1 GVAR_FIXHYPER=1 GVAR_NOFILL=1 \
  GVAR_DUMMY_BLOCS="CL CN CO CR EA ID IL IN IS JP KR MX NO TR UK ZA HK PE" \
  GVAR_WEIGHTS_FILE="$PWD/app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_full_38.json" \
  BVAR_RAWDATA_DIR="$PWD/pipeline/country_rawdata" GVAR_OUTDIR=$RUN/gvar35 GVAR_WORKSPACE=$RUN/gvar35_ws.mat \
  matlab -batch "run('pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m')"

# 3. estimate the 17 euro members (one run each, a few minutes per member)
for CC in AT BE DE EE ES FI FR GR IE IT LT LU LV NL PT SI SK; do
  CC=$CC BVAR_DIFF_GP=1 GVAR_NOFILL=1 CGL_FIXED_COMPANION=1 \
  EURO_DUMMY_MEMBERS="AT BE DE EE ES FI FR GR IE IT LT LU LV NL PT SI SK" EURO_OUTDIR=$RUN/members \
  matlab -batch "run('pipeline/export_bvar_euro_redesign.m')"
done

# 4. port (§6): GVAR raw copy + members via the porter + meta indices by id
#    (docs/reest-2026/runs/port_to_app.sh does exactly this)
node pipeline/fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs && node pipeline/fix_external_meta_indices.mjs

# 5. calendar, coupling, nowcast of the ragged edge, completion, baselines, bands, pack (§6 "After the port")
cd app
node scripts/stamp_calendar.mjs
npx vite-node scripts/build_coverage_manifest.mjs --panel-quarter <Q>
npx vite-node scripts/precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs                # check: rho < 1
npx vite-node scripts/nowcast_complete.mjs --write --baselines --out $RUN/nowcast_stage   # check: converged
#    … publish the staged blocs, then apply_member_completion, roll_d0_forward, regen_gr_baselines_via_loader,
#    regen_gvar_bands, gzip_companion_draws, build_coverage_manifest, vintages_publish (runs/stageB.sh)
node scripts/pack-build.mjs --pack-id <Q>-reest-<yyyymmdd>       # a NEW id — packs are immutable
node scripts/verify_cutoffs.mjs --allow-ragged --dating-only
npx vite-node scripts/pack-verify.mjs --full

# 6. green gate (BOTH halves) + the real build
npx tsc --noEmit && npm test && npm run test:heavy && BASE_PATH=/bvar-scenario npm run build
cd ..

# 7. review (old vs new: docs/reest-2026/compare_old_new.py), commit, and deploy ONLY on an explicit go
git push bvarscenario main && git push gmapsmodel main
#    desktop users: an update pack (npm run pack:delta) or a new installer — UPDATE_MANUAL.md §3, §8

For the fully-annotated runbook with the verification gate, see REESTIMATING_MODELS.md and UPDATE_MANUAL.md §7.

docs.title: 10. Targeted single-bloc re-estimation
docs.text:
Two distinct "re-estimate one bloc" patterns exist; picking the wrong one is the most common maintenance mistake. The rule is set by whether the bloc is in the coupled GVAR. See the decision tree in MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md §0; this is the mechanism behind it.

The bloc is… Pattern Re-estimates Coupling regen? a euro-area member (AT BE DE EE ES FI FR GR IE IT LT LU LV NL PT SI SK) truly single-bloc — it is not in the coupled system (no weights row, no trade-weighted stars) only that bloc no a coupled GVAR bloc (US/EA/any RoW) full GVAR re-estimate — its stars feed every other bloc, so the fixed point moves for everyone all 35 yes

Either way, re-stamp the data pack afterwards under a new id (pack-build.mjs --pack-id …, then pack-verify.mjs --full).

docs.title: 10.1 The euro member — genuinely isolated
docs.text:
A euro member has its own model (domestic + fiscal block + euro-area external columns + two rest-of-euro-area aggregates), estimated by export_bvar_euro_redesign.m, one member per run. It carries no coupling, so re-estimating it touches nothing else:

# update its panel in pipeline/euro_redesign_staging/DE/, then (Oct 2026 settings):
CC=DE BVAR_DIFF_GP=1 GVAR_NOFILL=1 CGL_FIXED_COMPANION=1 \
  EURO_DUMMY_MEMBERS="AT BE DE EE ES FI FR GR IE IT LT LU LV NL PT SI SK" EURO_OUTDIR=$RUN/members \
  matlab -batch "run('pipeline/export_bvar_euro_redesign.m')"
GVAR_EXPORT_DIR=$RUN/members GVAR_PORT_BLOCS="DE" python3 pipeline/port_gvar_exports.py
# NO coupling regen (not in the GVAR); member completion + bands + pack re-stamp; then the green gate (§8)

(The earlier export_bvar_euro_fsap.m route — domestic + exogenous US block + 4 globals — is no longer what the deployed members use.)

docs.title: 10.2 The coupled bloc — there is no "just one bloc" path
docs.text:
Because each coupled bloc's ROW* stars are trade-weighted aggregates of every partner's completed panel, changing one coupled bloc's data perturbs the EM fixed point for all of them. The honest path is the full loop. But you can iterate fast on a subset using BVAR_GVAR_BLOCS (US first), which is the validate-then-commit pattern: confirm a data/coherence fix is correct on a 2–3-bloc smoke run before launching the multi-hour full refit. This is exactly how the §3.5 CA-IP fix and the §3.3/§3.4 tags were landed:

# (a) FAST validation subset (separated, no coupling) — confirm the fix is sane
BVAR_GVAR_BLOCS="US CA" NDRAWS=200 MAXIT=1 US_ENDOGENOUS=1 \
  matlab -batch "run('pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m')"
GVAR_PORT_BLOCS="US CA" python3 pipeline/port_gvar_exports.py   # inspect /tmp/gvar24_export first

# (b) once happy, the FULL coupled refit (the only deploy-grade path for a coupled change)
US_ENDOGENOUS=1 matlab -batch "run('pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m')"
python3 pipeline/port_gvar_exports.py
cd app && npx vite-node scripts/precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs    # MANDATORY: stars changed for everyone

The intermediate commits 6f0161a (WN plumbing) → 9839a46 (CA-only targeted re-estimate, the validate step) → 22250be → e38673a (the self-consistent full 33-bloc refit folding in all three fixes) are this pattern in the git history. A MAXIT=1 subset run is not deploy-grade for a coupled bloc — it freezes the stars at their historical (uncoupled) values; only the full loop, run to convergence (the deployed run: MAXIT=30, converged at sweep 6), reaches the cross-country fixed point. After any coupled change you must regenerate coupling_default.json.gz (§7) — a stale modelSig is rejected and the app silently falls back to the slow path. See MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md §C–§D for the per-bloc checks (n == spec == companion, convergence vs the MC floor, fiscal closure) and §E for the green gate.

docs.title: 11. Empirical evaluation (out-of-sample horse-race + spillover)
docs.text:
A separate repo — em-bayesian-gvar-eval (docs/EMPIRICAL_PROTOCOL.md) — evaluates the platform's forecasts against benchmarks. It consumes the same estimator and conventions documented here; this section is the cross-link, not a duplicate.

Design (final). Two cores:

  1. Out-of-sample forecast horse-race. Recursive expanding-window, origins 2010Q1–2024Q4 (drop the 2020 COVID origins for the headline), targets {real GDP growth, inflation, short rate} for US/EA/JP/UK/CA/CN (full-panel = all 33 blocs in the appendix), horizons h ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8}.
  2. Proposed: the EM-Bayesian GVAR — endogenous-US (emgvar_endo, US_ENDOGENOUS=1) and the legacy frozen-anchor (emgvar_frozen).
  3. Benchmarks: Random Walk (driftless + a sample-mean "climatology" anchor), AR(p) (AIC-selected, iterated + direct), single-country Bayesian VAR (the coupling ablation = strip the ROW* columns, MAXIT=1), textbook OLS Pesaran–Schuermann–Weiner / Dees GVAR (cgvar_a), single-pass Bayesian GVAR (cgvar_b, MAXIT=1 — the EM ablation), and a Bayesian DFM.
  4. Leak-free by construction. Panels truncated ≤ t0 before transformData and before any star is built; rolling as-of-t0 trade weights (IMTS bilateral trade with endPeriod ≤ year(t0)) — the shipped 2021–2023 weights_full.json is forbidden in the sweep (it would inject future trade structure). COVID-as-missing is reapplied in-sample at every origin where 2020Q2–Q4 ≤ t0.

  5. Scoring: CRPS (primary density metric) + parametric log-score + PIT/coverage, scored from the per-draw predictive cloud Dforecast(1:8,:,:). Significance via Giacomini–White (headline — valid under nesting and correct for the expanding scheme), Clark–West (nested point), Diebold–Mariano (non-nested), with Romano–Wolf + the Model Confidence Set for multiplicity.

  6. Endogenous-US spillover analysis. The contribution the endogenous-US GVAR enables and the frozen-anchor cannot: a US shock that propagates abroad and feeds back into the US. Tier A (directly solver-computable conditional scenario propagation via solveGVARClosedFormEndo / solveGVARLinear in app/src/lib/compute/gvarSolve.ts) ships first; Tier B (GIRF/FEVD/connectedness) is a new module built from the exported companion_mean.json (betahat=Γ, sigmahat=Σ) + the coupling M — not a call into the current solver (which computes conditional-mean deltas, not GIRFs).

Headline result (first full pass — results/tables.{txt,json}, 56 origins, 9 models; DESIGN final). AR(p)/DFM have the lowest point CRPS, but the 90% Model Confidence Set carries the value-add: emgvar_endo is in the inflation MCS at all horizons and the short-rate MCS at h=1,2,4 (out of the growth MCS at h=1 & h=8), emgvar_endo ⪰ emgvar_frozen, and it decisively beats the textbook OLS classical GVAR (cgvar_a removed from most sets). Best inflation h=1 = emgvar_endo (relRMSE 0.799). Honest caveats: the draw-based densities are over-confident (PIT cov90 ~0.73–0.83 vs 0.90) and the parametric log-score column is numerically broken (CRPS + MCS are the robust primaries). The Tier-A US +100 bp result shows non-trivial endogenous-only feedback the frozen anchor omits, but the magnitudes are large/sign-flipping and it is a multi-period conditional projection, NOT a causal IRF — validate before headlining. Do not cite the log-score numbers.

See em-bayesian-gvar-eval/docs/EMPIRICAL_PROTOCOL.md for the full leak-free driver design (oos_driver.m), the per-origin forecast JSON schema, the compute plan, and the look-ahead invariants.

docs.title: How to update / re-estimate the models
docs.text:
4.0 (Oct 2026): every re-export must be DATED before anything else. A model export ends each history at the estimation end and carries no dates. Skipping the dating is exactly what happened in Sep 2026: two re-exports silently undid the July 2026Q1 shift and every chart was dated one quarter late. There is no DEFAULT_LAST_HIST_DATE any more — never set a date by hand. - Export that ends at an older quarter than the latest published one (the pre-2026 practice: estimate to a year end, then shift): npm run data:model-update -- --then-shift dates the histories from the estimation panels, re-stamps and verifies the pack, and shifts to the latest published quarter. - Export fitted to the latest published data (the October 2026 practice — ragged edge, no shift needed): node scripts/stamp_calendar.mjs, then the chain in the ★ section below (nowcast of the ragged edge, baselines, bands, data pack under a new pack id).

Operator guide: UPDATE_MANUAL.md §7.

This is the operational runbook for re-estimating the GVAR macro blocs and rebuilding the fiscal block, then porting, verifying, and deploying. The platform today (data pack 2026Q2-reest-20261008b, deployed 2026-10-08): an endogenous-US, 35-bloc GVAR estimated by an iterative GVAR-EM loop (coupling ρ(M) = 0.971875), the 17 euro members estimated one at a time, and a 4-variable fiscal block (with an exact-residual SFA) in 41 economies. Every panel is rebuilt from published sources with no fills, to 2026Q2. The ★ section below is the current procedure; §0–§6 keep the older detail and are marked where they differ.

Bloc count (35). The coupled set is the US, the euro-area aggregate and 33 Rest-of-World blocs, including HK SG RO PE PH (added with the FSAP-coverage expansion; AE was not viable: only annual real GDP exists and we do not interpolate). Russia, Argentina and Israel were dropped. With the 17 euro members that is 52 economies. The bloc list is data-driven from weights_full_38.json (estimation; it holds the same 35 blocs — the name is historical) / weights_24bloc.json (the app's copy, fetched from the data pack); see §0 and §1.2. To add a brand-new bloc from scratch, see the new-bloc recipe in ADDING_A_COUNTRY.md (build_newbloc_panel.py + build_globals_new_blocs.py).

Scope. This covers re-estimation and data refresh of the existing blocs. To add a brand-new country or RoW bloc, see ADDING_A_COUNTRY.md (this runbook reuses the same port / verify / deploy gate). For the live methodology, see ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI.md and fiscal-block-methodology.md.

The deployed tool is live at the /bvar-scenario path of the academic website, hosted on GitHub Pages (the matyasfarkas/starter-hugo-academic Hugo Academic site), and at gmapsmodel.com (Netlify).

Golden rules. Exact MATLAB replication when porting (no shortcuts). Use real observed data, never synthetic placeholders. Never deploy without a green gate. Do not hand-edit the GVAR topology (IDX/W/ROW_COUNTRIES in gvarSolve.ts) — it self-configures from the deployed specs + weights.

docs.title: ★ Current procedure — the 2026 genuine-data re-estimation (supersedes the sections below where they differ)
docs.text:
Everything below §0 documents the pre-2026 path (sig6 port of GVAR blocs, DVAX, the fixed 25-bloc fiscal list, the old panel builders). The October 2026 re-estimation used this chain; details and every decision are in docs/reest-2026/PLAN.md, the data changes in docs/reest-2026/PHASE_D_CHANGES.md, the review in docs/reest-2026/REVIEW.md, and the exact scripts that were run in docs/reest-2026/runs/ (with a README giving the order). Run times on the 4-core workstation: GVAR about 1 h 40 min; members a few minutes each.

  1. Data — one registry per economy (pipeline/sources/registry/<CC>.json, rules in its README: no fills, complete quarters only, exchange rates harmonised rise = appreciation). Build every panel: python3 -B pipeline/sources/build_panel.py --bloc <CC> --end <YYYY-Qn> --out <scratch>; compare with the panels in use (docs/reest-2026/phaseD/ scripts), review, then copy into pipeline/country_rawdata/ (35 coupled) and pipeline/euro_redesign_staging/<CC>/ (17 members) with their .provenance.json and fiscal_meta.
  2. Coupled GVAR (35) — design A (the sampler's own MF start-up; smooth EM sweeps; final full-MH pass): BVAR_DIFF_GP=1 US_ENDOGENOUS=1 NDRAWS=1000 MAXIT=30 BVAR_SEED=1 GVAR_FIXHYPER=1 GVAR_NOFILL=1 GVAR_DUMMY_BLOCS="CL CN CO CR EA ID IL IN IS JP KR MX NO TR UK ZA HK PE" GVAR_WEIGHTS_FILE=app/public/data/bvar/gvar/weights_full_38.json BVAR_RAWDATA_DIR=pipeline/country_rawdata GVAR_OUTDIR=<run>/gvar35 GVAR_WORKSPACE=<run>/gvar35_ws.mat matlab -batch "run('pipeline/export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m')" (converges in ~6 sweeps; gate: sweep 4 below ~1, final max star change < 0.03).
  3. Euro members (17) — CC=<CC> BVAR_DIFF_GP=1 GVAR_NOFILL=1 CGL_FIXED_COMPANION=1 EURO_DUMMY_MEMBERS="<all 17>" EURO_OUTDIR=<run>/members matlab -batch "run('pipeline/export_bvar_euro_redesign.m')".
  4. App chain (docs/reest-2026/runs/port_to_app.sh, stageA.sh, stageB.sh; from app/): port (GVAR raw + members sig6 + estimation_mask.json + fiscal_meta; pipeline/fix_fiscal_meta_indices.mjs must report 0 corrections; then pipeline/fix_external_meta_indices.mjs — added after the 2026 review found 35 stale exchange-rate indices) → scripts/stamp_calendar.mjs → coverage + scripts/pack-build.mjs (calendar) → scripts/precompute_gvar_coupling.mjs (gate ρ(M) < 1) → scripts/nowcast_complete.mjs --write --baselines --out <stage> → publish the 35 coupled dirs + nowcast_provenance.json → scripts/apply_member_completion.mjs → scripts/roll_d0_forward.mjs → scripts/regen_gr_baselines_via_loader.mjs → scripts/regen_gvar_bands.mjs → scripts/gzip_companion_draws.mjs → scripts/build_coverage_manifest.mjs → scripts/vintages_publish.mjs → scripts/pack-build.mjs → scripts/verify_cutoffs.mjs --allow-ragged --dating-only → scripts/pack-verify.mjs --full → tests, build, headless load, python3 docs/reest-2026/compare_old_new.py for the review. Deploy only on the owner's go. Every pack you hand out gets a new pack id (scripts/pack-build.mjs --pack-id <id>): packs are immutable, so after any later fix re-stamp under a new id (2026: …20261008 → …20261008b).
  5. Deploy — push the same commit to bvarscenario main (GitHub Pages) and gmapsmodel main (Netlify, gmapsmodel.com); check /data/manifest.json on both sites shows the new packId. Desktop users need an update pack or a new installer (UPDATE_MANUAL.md §3, §8).

docs.title: 0. The pieces, at a glance
docs.text:
