docs.title: Bottom line — realistic 'as-of' for a refresh TODAY
docs.text:
A clean, no-re-estimation refresh to 2026Q1 is feasible for the advanced economies — US (incl. all fiscal), the euro area + EU/EFTA members (real GDP from Eurostat, HICP from FRED), UK, JP, CA, and the FRED-sourced EMs (BR, MX, ZA). For these, 2026Q1 macro is published and the forecast can simply re-anchor from the new last-observed state.

The binding constraint is the EM laggards (CN, IN) whose real source data still ends ~2025Q2 and which only reach 2025Q4 through WEO-annual disaggregation — no genuine 2026Q1 observation exists for them today.

Recommended as-of quarter: 2026Q1 for the AE + FRED-EM blocs (the bulk of the system), while CN/IN remain at their back-filled 2025Q4 (or are extended again by the same WEO mechanism, flagged as synthetic). If a single common balanced endpoint is required across all blocs, the honest common observed endpoint is still 2025Q4; 2026Q1 is achievable as a deliberately ragged-edge refresh with CN/IN flagged.

docs.title: Part 2 — Refresh MECHANICS & Automation (no re-estimation)
docs.text: Complements Part 1 (data availability). This part answers: given the data, exactly HOW does a no-re-estimation refresh work — what re-projects vs what's a static artifact, which JSONs must be regenerated, whether δc/conditioning/plotting follow, and a one-command automation sketch.

docs.title: (1) How the displayed BASELINE is produced — split brain (precomputed and re-projected)
docs.text:
There are two distinct baseline objects, and the refresh story depends on which:

A. The SCENARIO / DEVIATION engine RE-PROJECTS in-browser (no JSON dependence). makeCountryModel (gvarSolve.ts:344-363) computes baseLvl at load time via conditionalForecast(params, histMat, allNaN) — the DK smoother projecting the fixed companion (companion_mean.betahat/sigmahat) forward from historical_levels.data. It does not read baseline_levels.json. The single-country path is identical: useConditionalForecast.ts:199-203 re-runs the unconditional smoother and explicitly uses "SMOOTHER's unconditional as reference (not stored baseline)" so deviation=0 ⇒ delta=0. ⇒ Every conditioning result, GVAR cross-country solve, δc overlay, and scenario band already re-anchors from historical_levels + companion_mean the instant the history changes — no MATLAB, no JSON regen.

B. The displayed BASELINE LINE + always-on BANDS are PRECOMPUTED MATLAB artifacts. The grey baseline central line and its fan are read directly from static JSON: q/q view from baseline.json .mean/.q16/.q84 (ChartGrid.tsx:1396,1491-1492); level view from baseline_levels.json (ChartGrid.tsx:1399-1402,1539-1540). These come from export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m:218,233-234: meanLvl = VARcf_DKcks([Xc;nan(H,n)],lags,Gam,sm,0) (deterministic DK mean of the fixed posterior-mean companion — byte-identical to the browser's conditionalForecast(allNaN), memory invariant "~1e-11"); bands = quantile(R.Dfc,…) where R.Dfc is the predictive density cgl_bvarV5 produced during estimation from the old last-observed state.

Settled: the engine re-projects (JSON-independent); the displayed baseline line+band is a precomputed artifact. A refresh that re-anchors only the engine but leaves baseline*.json stale shows the scenario on the new vintage while the grey baseline fan stays on the old anchor — visibly inconsistent. So baseline*.json MUST be regenerated.

docs.title: (2) Minimal refresh — exact regen list (per bloc)
docs.text:
File Refresh? How / why historical_levels.json REGEN (append 1 row) observed 100·log levels; engine state anchor historical.json REGEN (append 1 row) q/q-ann display history = gh(levels) (4·Δlog) baseline.json REGEN (mean+bands) mean = re-project fixed companion (deterministic); bands = re-project companion_draws β,Σ from the new state baseline_levels.json REGEN (mean+bands) same, in level space fiscal_meta.json REGEN d0 only (US/EA/JP/UK/CA/CN) d0 = last-observed debt level (US=122.568, 100·log) = debt-recursion seed; sfaDefault/idx unchanged companion_mean.json UNCHANGED estimated model — frozen companion_draws.json(.gz) UNCHANGED posterior β,Σ — frozen (re-used to re-project bands) spec.json, transformations.json UNCHANGED frozen bvar/gvar/coupling_default.json.gz, weights_*.json UNCHANGED (I−M)⁻¹ depends on betahats+trade weights, not data vintage → no 19-min rebuild, no 100MB issue DSGE catalog/IRFs UNCHANGED independent of BVAR vintage

App recomputes for itself (no regen): all conditioning/deviation paths, the GVAR solve, scenario bands (runGvarBandSolve.ts re-runs each companion_draws draw through the solver from the refreshed history), and the δc drift cache.

Bands — the one real "need MATLAB?" question → NO. Today's baseline bands come from cgl_bvarV5's R.Dfc. But companion_draws.json ships the full per-draw (β,Σ), and the browser already re-projects bands from them via conditionalForecast per draw (runGvarBandSolve.ts:64-70, drawCompanion). So the baseline band can be regenerated in pure JS/Python by looping the shipped draws through the same DK projector from the new state. (The app's band is parameter-only by documented design — runGvarBandSolve.ts:11-14 — so reproducing it parameter-only is the intended, consistent choice; R.Dfc additionally carried DK simulation shocks, which the live app does not display anyway.)

docs.title: (3) δc overlay + conditioning on the refreshed baseline — YES, both still work
docs.text:
• δc drift: the drift cache is built from betahat/n/lags (fixed companion) and re-anchors off baseline.mean's terminal (ChartGrid.tsx:1062-1087). Post-baseline by construction — feed it the refreshed baseline.json and it re-anchors automatically. No code change.
  • Conditioning: the engine reference is the recomputed unconditional smoother (§1A), so pins/scenarios re-anchor with zero changes; bands re-run draws from the new history. Fiscal conditioning seeds the debt recursion from fiscal_meta.d0 — hence d0 is in the regen list.

docs.title: (4) Plotting / dates — ONE hardcoded constant blocks the auto-extend
docs.text:
X-axis is numeric offsets (x=−1 last hist, x=0 first forecast) mapped to calendar quarters by lastHistOf(country) (dates.ts). Forecast-start is not derived from historical.json length — it hangs off one constant:

dates.ts:38   export const DEFAULT_LAST_HIST_DATE = '2025-10-01'   // 2025 Q4 — common panel end

Every dated label (offsetLabel/offsetYQ → ChartGrid.tsx:2328,2338,2345, ScenarioBar.tsx, CSV export ChartGrid.tsx:24) flows from this. Left at 2025-10-01, an appended 2026Q1 obs would be mis-dated (new point labelled as a forecast quarter; whole fan slides one quarter into the past). Fix: bump DEFAULT_LAST_HIST_DATE → '2026-01-01'; advance the per-bloc LAST_HIST_DATE overrides only for blocs that actually got a new quarter (CN/IN, if held at 2025Q4, get an override). Horizon stays 20 (H = min(horizon, baseline.mean.length)) — not auto-extended, so the forecast END recedes one quarter (2031Q1), which is the desired re-anchor. No other hardcoded dates/horizons found in app/src (grep 2025Q4/2025-12/2025-10/forecastStart/lastObserved). Stale comments to fix (not load-bearing): ScenarioBar.tsx:10, ChartGrid.tsx:2327, dates.ts:31-37.

docs.title: (5) Automation — one command, NO MATLAB
docs.text:
All four projected artifacts reduce to append + DK-project the shipped companion, a computation the codebase already implements in pure TS (kalman.ts:conditionalForecast, validated to 1e-11 vs MATLAB). A Node refresher reuses the production engine verbatim; MATLAB is needed only to re-estimate β,Σ (out of scope).

refresh-quarter.mjs — for each bloc C in weights_full.json:
 1. PULL 2026Q1 for C from the SAME sources build_*.py use (FRED hardcoded key, Eurostat keys,
    WEO/raw JSON); reuse each build's series map, fetch only the latest obs.
 2. APPEND → rebuild the 100·log level row exactly as the build script does (same transforms,
    COVID-as-missing, window policy); push onto historical_levels.data; historical.json = gh(levels).
 3. RE-PROJECT (pure JS, FIXED companion — import kalman.ts/conditionalForecast):
      params  = companion_mean.json  (UNCHANGED)
      histMat = refreshed historical_levels
      baseline_levels.mean = conditionalForecast(params, histMat, allNaN).mean   # = VARcf_DKcks(…,0)
      baseline.mean        = gh(baseline_levels.mean)
      bands: for each draw (β_d,Σ_d) in companion_draws:
               Lfc_d = conditionalForecast({β_d,Σ_d}, histMat, allNaN).mean
             baseline_levels.q16/84/05/95 = quantile_d(level);  baseline.q16/… = quantile_d(gh(Lfc_d))
 4. FISCAL blocs: fiscal_meta.d0 = refreshed last-observed debt level.
 5. WRITE historical.json, historical_levels.json, baseline.json, baseline_levels.json, (fiscal_meta).
 6. ONE-TIME: dates.ts DEFAULT_LAST_HIST_DATE → '2026-01-01' (+ per-bloc overrides for laggards).
  • Cost: band re-projection = nDraws × conditionalForecast per bloc (US: ~500 × one 20q smoother over 41×41) — exactly what runGvarBandSolve does in the worker; offline it's seconds/bloc. Companion + coupling untouched → no (I−M)⁻¹ rebuild, no GitHub 100MB issue.
  • MATLAB-free: YES for a pure data refresh; required ONLY for re-estimation.
  • Validate before shipping: match each build_*.py source map + the COVID-as-missing / WEO-extension / window rules so the appended row reproduces the harmonised panel byte-for-byte (the panel was built to a common endpoint with held-last/truncate — Part 1; the refresher must apply the same window policy, and treat CN/IN per Part 1's ragged-edge recommendation).

docs.title: Bottom line (mechanics)
docs.text:
• Baseline source: split — engine re-projects from companion_mean+historical_levels (JSON-independent); the displayed line+band is precomputed baseline*.json.
  • Regen exactly: historical.json, historical_levels.json, baseline.json, baseline_levels.json (+ fiscal_meta.d0 for fiscal blocs). UNCHANGED: companion_mean/draws, spec, transformations, coupling, weights.
  • δc + conditioning: unaffected (post-baseline, auto re-anchor).
  • Plotting: one constant dates.ts:DEFAULT_LAST_HIST_DATE 2025-10-01→2026-01-01; rest is offset-based. Horizon stays 20 (forecast end recedes one quarter — desired).
  • Automation: single Node script (append → DK-project the shipped companion for mean AND per-draw bands → write 4 JSONs → bump the date constant) refreshes the whole panel without MATLAB.

docs.title: Part 3 — Synthesis: verdict, risks, and the build plan
docs.text: Consolidates Parts 1–2 into the six deliverables. Parts 1–2 stand as the evidence; this part is the decision-ready answer plus the actual implementation plan for later review on improve-live.

docs.title: (1) FEASIBILITY VERDICT
docs.text:
YES — a no-re-estimation refresh to 2026Q1 is feasible today, for the bulk of the system, and it is exactly the post-estimation "re-anchor the fixed model from a new last-observed state" operation the δc sliders already embody. The companion (companion_mean/companion_draws) never changes; only the observed panel extends by one quarter and the forecast re-projects forward from it.

Realistic as-of quarter: - 2026Q1 for the advanced economies + FRED-sourced EMs — US (incl. all fiscal), EA + EU/EFTA members (real GDP Eurostat, HICP FRED), UK, JP, CA, BR, MX, ZA. 2026Q1 macro is published; monthly rates/CPI already run to 2026-04/05 so the quarterly aggregate is complete. - 2025Q4 (held / WEO-synthetic) for CN and IN — their real source data still ends ~2025Q2 and only reaches 2025Q4 via WEO-annual disaggregation; no genuine 2026Q1 observation exists today. - ⇒ Deliberately ragged-edge refresh: ship 2026Q1 for the AE+FRED-EM blocs, hold CN/IN at back-filled 2025Q4 (flagged synthetic). The honest common balanced endpoint across all blocs remains 2025Q4; 2026Q1 is a ragged edge, which the panel already tolerates (raw JSONs are ragged today: CA/JP at 2026Q1, EA/UK at 2025Q4, CN/IN at 2025Q2).

docs.title: (2) AUTOMATION DESIGN (one command, MATLAB-free) — recap
docs.text: refresh-quarter.mjs: pull → append → re-project the FIXED companion → regen JSONs → bump one date constant. Mean = conditionalForecast(companion_mean, refreshedHist, allNaN) (the production TS DK smoother, validated 1e-11 vs VARcf_DKcks(…,0)); bands = the same projector looped over the shipped per-draw companion_draws (β,Σ) — identical to what runGvarBandSolve already does in the worker. Companion + coupling untouched ⇒ no (I−M)⁻¹ rebuild, no MATLAB, seconds/bloc. Full sketch in Part 2 §5.

docs.title: (3) JSON REGEN LIST + who re-projects
docs.text:
Object Regen by script? App auto-reprojects? historical_levels.json, historical.json YES (append 1 row) — (these ARE the new state) baseline.json, baseline_levels.json (mean + bands) YES engine ignores them, but the displayed grey line+fan reads them → must regen fiscal_meta.d0 (US/EA/JP/UK/CA/CN) YES (debt-recursion seed only) — companion_mean/draws, spec, transformations, coupling_default, weights_*, DSGE NO — frozen — Conditioning / deviation / GVAR solve / scenario bands / δc cache NO YES — re-anchors automatically from historical_levels+companion_mean at load

The split-brain rule (Part 2 §1): the engine re-projects itself JSON-independently the instant history changes; the static baseline line+band does NOT. So regen baseline*.json or the grey fan sits on the stale anchor while scenarios move on the new vintage.

docs.title: (4) PLOTTING CHANGES
docs.text:
• One load-bearing constant: dates.ts:38 DEFAULT_LAST_HIST_DATE = '2025-10-01' → '2026-01-01'. Everything dated flows from it via numeric offsets + lastHistOf(); left stale, the appended 2026Q1 point is mis-labelled and the whole fan slides one quarter into the past.
  • Per-bloc overrides in LAST_HIST_DATE only for blocs that did NOT advance (add a 2025-10-01 override for CN/IN so they stay correctly dated at 2025Q4).
  • Horizon unchanged (H = min(horizon, baseline.mean.length), =20): forecast END recedes one quarter (→2031Q1) — the intended re-anchor.
  • No other hardcoded 2025Q4/2025-12/forecastStart in app/src. Stale comments to tidy (cosmetic): ScenarioBar.tsx:10, ChartGrid.tsx:2327, dates.ts:31-37.

docs.title: (5) RISKS + WHAT TO VERIFY
docs.text: # Risk Mitigation / verification R1 Panel-build mismatch — appended row not built byte-identically to the harmonised panel (transforms, COVID-as-missing, WEO-extension, window/truncate policy) ⇒ a level discontinuity at the seam. Replay each build_*.py source map + transform exactly; diff the re-derived 2025Q4 row against the shipped historical_levels last row → must match to ~1e-9 before trusting the appended 2026Q1 row. R2 Stale-anchor inconsistency — regen the engine but not baseline*.json ⇒ grey fan on old anchor, scenarios on new. Always regen all four JSONs together; visual check that grey baseline central line == unconditional smoother at deviation 0. R3 Date misalignment — forget the DEFAULT_LAST_HIST_DATE bump ⇒ fan slides one quarter. After bump, eyeball the x-axis: last hist tick = 2026Q1, first forecast = 2026Q2 (AE blocs), CN/IN still 2025Q4. R4 Band reproduction drift — JS per-draw projection ≠ original cgl_bvarV5 R.Dfc band. Expected & acceptable: the live app's band is parameter-only by design (runGvarBandSolve.ts:11-14); regen the same parameter-only way → consistent with what users already see. Sanity: new bands ⊇ central path, widen with horizon, no NaN. R5 CN/IN ragged edge — accidentally extending them with fake 2026Q1. Explicitly exclude CN/IN from the 2026Q1 pull; hold at 2025Q4; flag as synthetic in UI/notes. R6 FRED ID traps — discontinued OECD-on-FRED CPI mirrors (GBRCPIALLMINMEI, CPALTT01CAM659N end 2025-03), FREV/FPEXP are internal names not FRED IDs, stale Eurostat HICP endpoint (ends 2025-12). Use only the build scripts' actual series IDs; pull EA/member HICP from FRED, never the Eurostat HICP path. R7 δc / conditioning regression — sliders or pins anchor to the wrong terminal after refresh. Post-refresh smoke test: δc=0 ⇒ overlay == baseline; a single pin re-solves; fiscal pin uses refreshed d0 (debt recursion continuous). R8 Vintage-drift sanity — a refreshed bloc looks crazy (units, sign, 4·log scale). Per-bloc: 2026Q1 q/q-ann within plausible range vs 2025Q4; level continuous; debt %GDP continuous; spot-check 2–3 blocs by hand against the source print.

docs.title: (6) BUILD PLAN (later, on improve-live, for user review)
docs.text:
Read-only today; this is the implementation sequence to propose:

  • Phase 0 — Scaffold & lock sources. Inventory each bloc's exact source map from build_*.py (series IDs, transforms, COVID/WEO/window rules). Define the bloc set: AE+FRED-EM → 2026Q1; CN/IN → hold.
  • Phase 1 — Replay/validate the LAST row (gate). For each bloc, re-derive the existing 2025Q4 row from live sources and diff against shipped historical_levels (~1e-9). Gate: must match before any append — proves the refresher reproduces the panel's transform/window policy.
  • Phase 2 — Append 2026Q1 + re-project (core). Pull 2026Q1, append the 100·log row, run conditionalForecast(companion_mean,…) for the mean and loop companion_draws for bands; write historical*.json, baseline*.json, and fiscal_meta.d0. Reuse kalman.ts/gh verbatim (no re-implementation of the projector).
  • Phase 3 — Plotting. Bump DEFAULT_LAST_HIST_DATE → '2026-01-01'; add CN/IN per-bloc overrides; tidy the stale comments.
  • Phase 4 — Verify (the gate to ship). Run R1–R8 checks: seam continuity, grey-fan vs smoother, axis dates, band sanity, δc=0==baseline, single-pin + fiscal-pin re-solve, 2–3 hand spot-checks. Green-gate + diff review before any commit.
  • Phase 5 — Ship as ragged edge. Commit the regen'd JSONs + the one date change; CN/IN flagged. Document the as-of (2026Q1 ragged; common balanced 2025Q4). Re-runnable each quarter (the script is the quarterly-refresh tool, not a one-off).

One-line cost: nDraws × conditionalForecast per bloc (seconds), companion/coupling frozen — the whole refresh is minutes, MATLAB-free.

docs.title: Data Refresh — Quarterly-Shift / 2026Q1 Rebase Runbook (no re-estimation)
docs.text:
Current guide: UPDATE_MANUAL.md (§6 is the quarterly data shift). This page is the detailed record of the 2026Q1 shift and the engines behind it; where it describes the panel as it was then (2026Q1 origin, 38 coupled blocs, Israel on its own calendar) it is history. Today (pack 2026Q2-reest-20261008b): 52 economies (35 coupled + 17 euro members), all through 2026Q2; Russia, Argentina and Israel are no longer shipped.

4.0 (Oct 2026) — the dating steps below changed. There is no date constant any more: each history file carries its own firstQuarter, and the last quarter is always firstQuarter + rows − 1. Steps 11–15 below are the current chain: coverage manifest (asserted) → vintages → data pack (pack-build) → verification (verify_cutoffs + pack-verify --full with the calendar canary) → update packs. The complete, current procedure — including the model-update step that re-applies the shift after a re-estimation — is UPDATE_MANUAL.md. Other mentions of dates.ts/DEFAULT_LAST_HIST_DATE here are history.

Status: the quarterly-shift procedure is ESTABLISHED and has shipped to production. The 2026 Q1 rebase went live on bvarscenario/main (US observed + cross-bloc nowcast for the rest, per-cell provenance, /monitor release-impact page). This file is the canonical operator runbook for moving the display origin forward one quarter. It complements the design in docs/data-refresh-2026q1-feasibility.md (read that first for the why); this file is the how to run it and the what to check before merge.

Branch note (historical — effi-even-seasonal-dummies, the seasonal-v2 testing ground): when this runbook was first written that branch sat at the FRESH re-estimation vintage 2025 Q4 (dates.ts DEFAULT_LAST_HIST_DATE = '2025-10-01', shown AS-IS with no 2026 Q1 nowcast rebase) to evaluate the seasonal fix (evened EFFI + seasonal dummies). The shipped / current panel origin is now 2026 Q1 (DEFAULT_LAST_HIST_DATE = '2026-01-01'; coverage_manifest.json panelDefaultLastQuarter = 2026Q1). Running the shift chain below is exactly what promotes a 2025 Q4 branch to that 2026 Q1 origin.

docs.title: The method — estimate once, shift quarterly
docs.text:
The companion is estimated once on the 2025 Q4 vintage and then frozen. Within the year the display origin is moved forward one quarter at a time with no re-estimation — the "quarterly data shift". For the 2026 Q1 rebase, 2026 Q1 becomes the LAST OBSERVATION, filled by

  • genuine real-time releases where a bloc is wired (has a live source map — today US, all cells incl. the 4-var fiscal block) or already carries the observed quarter (the new FSAP blocs HK / SG / RO / PE / PH pull current public data, so their 2026 Q1 is mostly observed); plus
  • a cross-bloc G-BVAR NOWCAST for every remaining ragged cell — one coupled GVAR solve conditions each bloc's DK smoother on its own observed cells and carries the wired leaders' 2026 Q1 through the star channel into the laggards' imputed cells. Older ragged blocs get more nowcast fill; the new blocs get little. Imputed cells are treated as data downstream but flagged model-implied per cell in public/data/nowcast_provenance.json — never WEO-extended, never held flat.

2026 Q2 is then the first forecast quarter. Two seasonal-aware engines do the work:

  • app/scripts/refresh-quarter.mjs — per wired bloc, RE-SYNCS the prior shipped quarter's directly-sourced columns to realized values and THEN appends the genuine observed 2026 Q1 row (self-correcting, not append-only — the prior quarter's displayed q/q-growth row is recomputed against the re-synced levels so growth stays consistent; held GVAR-star aggregates and the fiscal-SFA residual are not re-synced), and RE-PROJECTS the FROZEN companion forward (mean via the DK smoother makeCountryModel/conditionalForecast; bands via the shipped per-draw companion_draws). The re-sync happens only under --accept-revisions (the mode the orchestrator runs). Seasonal-aware: it phases the quarter-of-year deterministic term from --asof itself (qoyNext = (asof.q % 4) + 1), NOT from dates.ts.
  • app/scripts/nowcast_complete.mjs — the cross-bloc completion: one coupled GVAR solve (completeRaggedPanel) fills every ragged 2026 Q1 cell across all blocs. Seasonal-aware via a per-bloc quarter-of-year ledger (qoyEndByCode).

No estimation runs. cgl_bvarV5.m is never touched. companion_mean / companion_draws(.gz) / spec / transformations / coupling / weights stay frozen — so modelSig is unchanged and the shipped (I−M)⁻¹ coupling artifact stays valid (no 19-min rebuild). Per bloc the shift rewrites only: historical.json, historical_levels.json, baseline.json, baseline_levels.json, and (fiscal blocs only) fiscal_meta.json d0 — plus the single load-bearing date constant DEFAULT_LAST_HIST_DATE in app/src/lib/dates.ts (bumped to '2026-01-01'; IL keeps its own-calendar override).

docs.title: 0. Who gets genuinely re-pulled vs nowcast-filled
docs.text:
The shift no longer needs a source registry for every bloc. Two paths fill the new quarter:

  • Wired blocs — genuine observed data via refresh-quarter.mjs. The script only re-pulls a bloc that has a SOURCES[<CC>] entry (live source IDs + transform + window, honouring the R6 ID traps). Today only US is mapped (all cells incl. the 4-var fiscal block); extend SOURCES to wire more leaders. Run against an un-mapped bloc it is fail-closed: exit 4 ("NO SOURCE MAP — refusing to touch it"), writes nothing. CN / IN are fail-closed by design (exit 3, structural laggards — R5).
  • Everyone else — cross-bloc nowcast via nowcast_complete.mjs. Once the wired leaders have appended their observed 2026 Q1 rows, the coupled solve pads every other bloc's new quarter with model-implied cells (the star channel carries the leaders' observed values in). The new FSAP blocs HK/SG/RO/PE/PH already carry their own genuine 2026 Q1 (little to impute); the older ragged blocs get more fill. Even CN/IN advance this way — as an honest, flagged model-implied nowcast, never as fabricated observed data.

So the shift is a single orchestrated command (auto_update.mjs --shift, §1). The per-wired-bloc refresh-quarter.mjs command in §1 is only what that orchestrator runs for each wired leader.

docs.title: Panel scope + holds
docs.text:
The shift moves the whole coupled panel forward in one solve. On the seasonal-v2 branch that is 38 coupled GVAR blocs (US anchor + 37 RoW blocs, incl. the new HK/SG/RO/PE/PH) plus 17 euro-member standalones extended by member_extend.mjs — ~55 economies. (History — as of the 2026Q1 shift. The live panel is now 35 coupled blocs + 17 euro members = 52 economies, all ending 2026Q2.)

HELD (never fabricated, R5): CN, IN — excluded from the wired pull (refresh-quarter exits 3); they take their new quarter from the cross-bloc nowcast like any laggard; do not re-pull them as if observed. (History: Israel used to sit on its own calendar with a date override; it is no longer shipped, and since 4.0 there is no date override of any kind — every history carries its own firstQuarter.)

docs.title: 1. The shift chain (copy-paste)
docs.text:
The whole shift is orchestrated by auto_update.mjs --shift. From app/:

# 0) what's due? (probes the release calendar; exits 10 = data shift due, 11 = annual re-estimation due)
npm run data:check

# 1) DRY-RUN the whole shift (refresh gates run, NOTHING is written) — e.g. to 2026Q3
npm run data:shift -- --asof 2026Q3

# 2) COMMIT the shift (archives the current vintage, then runs the full publish chain)
npm run data:shift -- --asof 2026Q3 --commit

FRED_API_KEY is optional: the scripts fall back to the repository's public key. (The 2026Q1 shift ran these as npx vite-node scripts/auto_update.mjs --check|--shift --asof 2026Q1 [--commit].)

--shift --commit runs, in order (each step is a script you can also run by hand — §2):

  1. archive the current shipped vintage → pipeline/vintages/<lastQuarter>_shipped/ (idempotent);
  2. pre-release counterfactual — nowcast_complete.mjs --to 2026Q1 --write --baselines on the old data → pipeline/vintages/pre_2026Q1_counterfactual/ (the baseline /monitor diffs against);
  3. refresh-quarter.mjs for each WIRED bloc (WIRED = ['US'], --accept-revisions) — genuine observed 2026 Q1 rows. A gate failure leaves the bloc untouched (its new quarter is nowcast cross-block instead);
  4. realized_pins.mjs — harvest any published cells for the window as level pins (realized trumps imputation);
  5. nowcast_complete.mjs --to 2026Q1 [--realized …] --write --baselines — one coupled solve completes every ragged cell → staged in pipeline/nowcast_staging/;
  6. publish — copy staging → app/public/data/bvar/ + nowcast_provenance.json (a deliberate second step; the engine never writes public/data directly);
  7. member_extend.mjs --asof 2026Q1 — the 17 euro members follow the shift (one EA-channel-pinned row each);
  8. regen_gvar_bands.mjs — re-simulate predictive bands for all GVAR blocs from the new origin;
  9. build_coverage_manifest.mjs — rebuild public/data/coverage_manifest.json (drives the amber model-implied overlay);
  10. release_impact.mjs — regenerate the /monitor release-impact record (post − pre at the origin);
  11. build_coverage_manifest.mjs --panel-quarter <asof> — the dating comes from the data (every history now ends at the new quarter); the flag only asserts it. (Replaces the old dates.ts bump + manifest re-run.)
  12. vintages_publish.mjs — re-bake the /monitor vintage artifacts against the new live panel. A base counts as a "pure data shift" only if its recorded model fingerprint equals the live model's.
  13. pack-build.mjs — re-stamp the data pack (manifest.json: every file's SHA-256 + the dating the app reads), pack id <asof>-<yyyymmdd>.
  14. verification gate — verify_cutoffs.mjs (data calendars == coverage == pack manifest, every bloc on the new quarter, no null last-row cells, provenance converged) and pack-verify.mjs --full (every file re-hashed + the calendar canary against the estimation panels). The chain EXITS NON-ZERO on any violation.
  15. update packs — one per released app version recorded in pipeline/released_packs/ → packs/<id>_for_<version>.zip.

The script then prints the post-run gate: npm test, npm run build (its prebuild re-verifies the pack), review /monitor + a few charts (amber dashed tails = model-implied nowcasts), and git add app/public/data pipeline/vintages && git commit — push/deploy only on a deliberate decision (prod = bvarscenario/main). Companion untouched ⇒ coupling_default.json.gz stays valid (no regen).

docs.title: Hiccup recovery (why the chain is safe to re-run)
docs.text:
Every step is idempotent or additive: the vintage archive skips if present, refresh-quarter gates before writing, the completion stages to pipeline/nowcast_staging/ and publishing is an explicit copy, the manifest and bands regenerate from what is on disk, and the verification gate only reads. If a step crashes (power, API outage, OOM):

  1. Diagnose from the step's own log line — each step prints its name before running.
  2. Re-run the whole --shift --commit — completed work is skipped or harmlessly redone; or run the failed step's script by hand (each is listed above) and then steps 11–15 manually: npx vite-node scripts/build_coverage_manifest.mjs && npx vite-node scripts/vintages_publish.mjs && node scripts/pack-build.mjs --pack-id <asof>-<yyyymmdd> && npm run data:verify.
  3. Rollback = restore pipeline/vintages/<lastQuarter>_shipped/ over app/public/data/bvar/ (or git checkout the data paths). There is no date to revert: the restored histories carry their own calendar.
  4. Never hand-edit a shipped panel to "fix" a tail: the verify gate treats null tail cells as a failed completion, which is what they are.

docs.title: Deploy verification (two-hop chain — do not trust the first 200)
docs.text: Prod deploys are TWO hops: the tool repo's workflow builds and pushes the static export into the website repo (starter-hugo-academic), whose OWN Pages workflow then publishes — ~8–15 min end to end, plus a CDN quirk: GitHub Pages caches 404s for ~10 min, so a freshly-published file can 404 after the deploy finishes. Verify with a file that only the new vintage has (e.g. a new bloc's spec.json or a changed seasonalRows), NOT with coverage_manifest.json alone — the old vintage may serve a manifest with the same quarter label (the V3 deploy's false-confirm). Poll until the discriminating file serves 200 with the expected content.

docs.title: 1b. The per-wired-bloc command (what step 3 runs)
docs.text:
Gate-then-write for one wired leader, run from app/:

npx vite-node scripts/refresh-quarter.mjs --bloc <CC> --asof <quarter>     # FRED_API_KEY optional

Useful variants (use these while authoring a new registry):

# gate ONLY — proves transform/window/source fidelity, never writes:
… scripts/refresh-quarter.mjs --bloc <CC> --asof 2026Q1 --gate-only
# gate + project + report, still no write (eyeball the seam/bands first):
… scripts/refresh-quarter.mjs --bloc <CC> --asof 2026Q1 --dry-run
# tighten the gate against a full-precision DataRaw_*_glob.json panel:
… --gate-tol 1e-9     # default is 5e-3 vs the 6-sig-fig shipped historical_levels
# accept source revisions (the mode the orchestrator runs): turns the gate into a revision DETECTOR, re-syncs
# the prior quarter, logs the revisions — only a GROSS (wrong-series/unit) error stays fatal:
… --accept-revisions
# tolerance before a revision-prone column (debt / IP / oil) counts as a flagged vintage revision:
… --revision-tol 0.5   # default 0.5 (100·log space ≈ 0.5% level)
# the dimension-aware GROSS ceiling for log columns (absolute, 100·log space):
… --gross-tol 20       # default 20 ≈ 22% q/q; volatile global price series use a fixed 50 (≈65%)

docs.title: Exit codes (what a non-zero means)
docs.text:
code meaning action 0 gate passed, wrote (or, with --gate-only/--dry-run, validated) proceed to verify 1 GATE FAILED — transform/window/source fidelity not proven, or fatal fix the registry; nothing was written 2 bad args (missing --bloc/--asof) fix invocation 3 bloc is a HELD laggard (CN/IN) expected — leave held 4 no source map for this bloc author SOURCES[<CC>] first, then re-run 5 new quarter not fully published yet for this bloc wait for the data; do not partial-write 6 fiscal: debt/GDP series missing at as-of fix the fiscal source id

The gate (R1) is the binding safety check — but it has two modes. Before appending the new quarter it re-derives the existing last shipped row (the prior quarter) from the same live sources the same way and diffs it against the shipped panel. How a diff is treated depends on --accept-revisions:

  • Strict mode (no --accept-revisions) — the bare refresh-quarter.mjs default. STABLE columns must match byte-exact (within --gate-tol); revision-prone columns (debt/IP/cumulative) are allowed a documented --revision-tol. Any breach beyond tolerance writes nothing — there is no override. Use this while authoring a new registry, to prove transform/window/source fidelity.
  • Accept-revisions mode (--accept-revisions) — the mode the orchestrator runs (auto_update.mjs passes it, step 3). The gate stops being a must-match gate and becomes a revision DETECTOR: a diff above tolerance is no longer fatal — it is ACCEPTED and recorded as a source revision (and the prior quarter is re-synced to the realized value). Only a gross diff — the signature of a wrong series / wrong unit, not a plausible vintage revision — remains fatal (exit 1, writes nothing). The gross ceiling is dimension-aware: log columns use an absolute ceiling in 100·log space = --gross-tol (default 20 ≈ 22% q/q); volatile global price series (GLB_OIL / GLB_USEQ / GSNE) get a wider VOLATILE_GROSS = 50 (≈ 65% q/q); lin ratios/rates (fiscal shares, policy & market rates) use a RELATIVE ceiling of 50% of the column's own level (floored). So on the normal orchestrated path a column does NOT have to match the shipped value — only stay within the gross ceiling.

docs.title: 2. Running the chain by hand (step by step)
docs.text:
Prefer the orchestrator (auto_update.mjs --shift --commit, §1) — it passes the right flags and archives the vintage first. These are the exact commands it issues, for when you need to run or debug one step (or re-run after a fix). All from app/:

FK=${FRED_API_KEY:-}     # optional; the scripts fall back to the repository's public FRED key

# 3. genuine observed rows for the wired leaders (US today) — gate-then-write, revisions accepted
FRED_API_KEY=$FK npx vite-node scripts/refresh-quarter.mjs --bloc US --asof 2026Q1 --accept-revisions

# 4. realized-data level pins for the (gap → 2026Q1] window (EU HICP/GDP mirrors, ECB rate, global commons)
FRED_API_KEY=$FK npx vite-node scripts/realized_pins.mjs --asof 2026Q1 --out ../pipeline/realized_pins_2026Q1.json

# 5. cross-block nowcast completion → STAGES to pipeline/nowcast_staging (report-only first, no --write,
#    to eyeball the per-bloc imputed-cell counts, then re-run with --write)
npx vite-node scripts/nowcast_complete.mjs --to 2026Q1 --realized ../pipeline/realized_pins_2026Q1.json --write --baselines

# 6. publish the staged panel into public/data (review the diff first)
cp -r ../pipeline/nowcast_staging/*/ public/data/bvar/                       # per-bloc historical*/baseline*
cp ../pipeline/nowcast_staging/nowcast_provenance.json public/data/

# 7. euro members follow the shift (one EA-channel-pinned row each)
npx vite-node scripts/member_extend.mjs --asof 2026Q1 --realized ../pipeline/realized_pins_2026Q1.json

# 8. re-simulate predictive bands for all GVAR blocs from the new origin
npx vite-node scripts/regen_gvar_bands.mjs

# 9. rebuild the coverage manifest
npx vite-node scripts/build_coverage_manifest.mjs

# 11–15. dating is in the data since 4.0 — nothing to edit. Assert it, re-bake /monitor, re-stamp, verify:
npx vite-node scripts/build_coverage_manifest.mjs --panel-quarter 2026Q1
npx vite-node scripts/vintages_publish.mjs
node scripts/pack-build.mjs --pack-id 2026Q1-<yyyymmdd>   # re-stamp manifest.json under a NEW id
npm run data:verify                         # verify_cutoffs + pack-verify --full

Notes: - nowcast_complete stages, never publishes. It writes pipeline/nowcast_staging/ (or --out <dir>); copying into public/data/bvar is the deliberate review step. It refuses to stage if the coupled solve did not converge — raise --max-sweeps (default 120) or investigate. - --to 2026Q1 extends EVERY bloc's grid to 2026 Q1 (null rows appended, then imputed). After the wired refresh the leaders already carry the observed row, so only their laggard partners are imputed. - Both engines are seasonal-aware: they phase the quarter-of-year deterministic term from the target quarter. (Before 4.0 this mattered because dates.ts was bumped only at the end of the chain; since 4.0 the dating comes from each history's firstQuarter, and setPanelDates cross-checks the declared qoyNext in the manifest.)

docs.title: Wiring a NEW leader (optional — to turn a bloc's imputed cells into observed data)
docs.text:
A bloc only needs a SOURCES[<CC>] registry if you want its 2026 Q1 to be genuine observed rather than cross-bloc nowcast. To add one:

  1. Author SOURCES[<CC>] in refresh-quarter.mjs (live FRED/Eurostat IDs + transform + window). Honour the R6 traps: discontinued OECD-on-FRED CPI mirrors; FREV/FPEXP are internal names, not FRED IDs; stale Eurostat HICP → use CP0000EZ19M086NEST for EA HICP. EA members get the shared-EA exogenous rate/corp handling baked into the spec (do not re-source those endogenously).
  2. Gate with --gate-only until it passes on the STABLE columns. If it can't pass, the registry is wrong — fix the IDs/transform/window, never loosen the tolerance to force it (--accept-revisions only RECORDS known vintage revisions; it does not silence a wrong series).
  3. Dry-run (--dry-run) and eyeball the reported seam + bands (see the Seam continuity check in §3 — a continuous level with a noisy annualized q/q step is fine; a true level discontinuity is not).
  4. Add the bloc to WIRED in auto_update.mjs; it is then re-pulled genuinely on every shift.

docs.title: 3. Verify checklist (before merge)
docs.text:
Run all of these green after a shift (the production 2026 Q1 shift passed every item).

  • [ ] tsc clean: cd app && npx tsc --noEmit → exit 0.
  • [ ] cgl_bvarV5.m 0-diff: git diff --stat BVAR/MFBVAR/cgl_bvarV5.m empty. Production estimator untouched.
  • [ ] Companion + coupling frozen: git status --porcelain app/public/data/bvar/ shows per bloc ONLY historical.json, historical_levels.json, baseline.json, baseline_levels.json, and (fiscal) fiscal_meta.json modified. companion_mean / companion_draws(.gz) / spec / transformations / gvar/coupling_default.json.gz / weights_*.json MUST NOT appear (frozen companion ⇒ modelSig unchanged ⇒ no coupling regen).
  • [ ] fiscal_meta = d0 only (fiscal blocs): git diff …/fiscal_meta.json changes only d0; sfaDefault and idx frozen.
  • [ ] History extends one quarter: every coupled bloc's historical*.json row count +1, last row dated on the new quarter.
  • [ ] R1 gate PASS (wired blocs): on the orchestrated --accept-revisions path, PASS means no column breached the GROSS wrong-series/unit ceiling (accepted revisions are expected, not failures). The re-synced columns + accepted revisions are logged to <bloc>/refresh_revisions.json — an APPENDED log, { log: [ { stampedAt, asof, priorQuarter, note, resynced:[…], gateFlagged:[…] } ] }, never clobbered (resynced = columns actually overwritten, |diff| > gate-tol; gateFlagged = the subset large enough to count as a genuine vintage revision).
  • [ ] Nowcast converged + staged: nowcast_complete reports converged=true; per-bloc imputed-cell counts look sane (new FSAP blocs HK/SG/RO/PE/PH near-zero; laggards more).
  • [ ] Provenance travels: public/data/nowcast_provenance.json regenerated; imputed cells flagged model-implied; the coverage manifest's lastObs/imputedThrough drive the amber chart overlay.
  • [ ] Members followed: all 17 euro members extended one row (member_extend); no member left a quarter short of the EA origin (the common-ECB self-check).
  • [ ] Bands sane: baseline_levels.json mean+bands all finite, q05 ≤ q16 ≤ q84 ≤ q95 everywhere.
  • [ ] Re-anchor (split-brain healed): the engine's re-projected baseline (from the refreshed history) equals baseline_levels.json mean to ~0. The grey fan and the engine sit on the SAME vintage.
  • [ ] δc = 0 == baseline (R7): an all-unconditional solve reproduces the baseline (no spurious shift).
  • [ ] Dates plot: node scripts/stamp_calendar.mjs --check passes and manifest.json panel.lastHistQuarter is the new quarter; in the app, x=−1 is the new last obs and x=0 the first forecast. No off-by-one on the x-axis. (Before 4.0 this item checked DEFAULT_LAST_HIST_DATE.)
  • [ ] Seam continuity: the level across the 2025Q4→2026Q1 join is continuous. A large annualized q/q number on a genuinely volatile quarter (e.g. WTI) is annualization, not a discontinuity — confirm against the underlying level before flagging.
  • [ ] CN/IN honest (R5): CN/IN advanced by cross-bloc nowcast ONLY (flagged model-implied in the provenance), never re-pulled as fabricated observed data.
  • [ ] Old vintage archived: pipeline/vintages/<lastQuarter>_shipped/ exists (the shift is reversible).

docs.title: 4. Guardrails (do not violate)
docs.text:
• No auto-deploy. The chain writes public/data (+ pipeline/vintages, the realized pins), but the commit + push to bvarscenario/main happens only on explicit user confirm (prod = bvarscenario/main; origin is dead).
  • No re-estimation within the year. Reuse kalman.ts / bvarForecastDraw / the shipped companion verbatim; never touch companion_mean/companion_draws. Re-estimation is the annual Q1 step (auto_update.mjs --q1-prep, MATLAB), not a shift.
  • The nowcast STAGES, never publishes. nowcast_complete writes pipeline/nowcast_staging/; the copy into public/data/bvar is a deliberate reviewed step (the orchestrator does it after the solve converges).
  • Never git add -A. Stage git add app/public/data pipeline/vintages pipeline/realized_pins_<q>.json (+ this doc / any wired registry change) — not the whole tree.
  • Fail-closed is a feature. A wired bloc exiting 4/5/6, or refresh-quarter gate-failing, leaves it untouched — its new quarter is then nowcast cross-block. Never force a write.
  • Never loosen the gate to make it pass. A failing gate means the source/transform/window is wrong; --accept-revisions only records known vintage revisions, it does not silence a wrong series.
  • Never fabricate a laggard as observed (R5). CN/IN (and any un-wired bloc) advance only as flagged model-implied nowcasts.

docs.title: 5. Files
docs.text:
Engines + orchestrator (all under app/scripts/): - auto_update.mjs — the shift orchestrator (--check / --shift --asof … [--commit] / --q1-prep). - refresh-quarter.mjs — per-wired-bloc observed refresh (gate + re-project + bands writer). - nowcast_complete.mjs — cross-block nowcast completion (completeRaggedPanel); stages to pipeline/nowcast_staging/. - realized_pins.mjs — harvest published cells as level pins (realized trumps imputation). - member_extend.mjs — extend the 17 euro members one row to the shifted origin. - regen_gvar_bands.mjs — re-simulate predictive bands panel-wide from the new origin. - build_coverage_manifest.mjs — rebuild public/data/coverage_manifest.json. - release_impact.mjs — the legacy single-pair /monitor record (post − pre); the vintage comparison (§7) supersedes it. - vintages_publish.mjs — the /monitor vintage comparison. - pack-build.mjs / pack-verify.mjs — re-stamp and verify the data pack (public/data/manifest.json).

Data + state: - app/public/data/manifest.json — the data pack: every file's SHA-256 and size, and each bloc's dating (no date constant in the code since 4.0). - app/public/data/bvar/<CC>/{historical,historical_levels,baseline,baseline_levels,fiscal_meta}.json — the regenerated per-bloc display/state files. - app/public/data/{nowcast_provenance.json, coverage_manifest.json} — per-cell model-implied flags + panel vintage. - pipeline/vintages/<lastQuarter>_shipped/ — the archived pre-shift vintage (reversible); pipeline/nowcast_staging/ — the review-before-publish stage. - docs/data-refresh-2026q1-feasibility.md — the design and the R1–R8 risk register.

docs.title: 6. Monthly data-check action — the automated reminder
docs.text:
The shift above is run by hand, on purpose (it ships data, so a human reviews it first). But remembering to look every month is easy to forget. A GitHub Action now does the looking for us: .github/workflows/data-check.yml.

What it does — and what it does NOT do. It runs npm run data:check (auto_update.mjs --check) on a schedule, reads the result, and reports it. It is check + alert only: it never writes, shifts, nowcasts, re-estimates, or ships anything. When an update is due it tells a person, who then runs the shift chain in §1 (or the re-estimation runbook) by hand. No data is ever touched by the action.

When it runs. cron: '0 9 5 * *' — 09:00 UTC on the 5th of each month. That is a few days after month-end, so the quarterly QNA / GFS releases that the panel depends on have landed. You can also run it any time from the Actions tab (Run workflow, the workflow_dispatch trigger).

What the three outcomes mean (the probe's exit code, surfaced in the run's job summary):

Exit Meaning What a person does next 0 Up to date — no new full-coverage quarter yet. Nothing. 10 Within-year data shift available — a new quarter is published for every macro sentinel. Companion stays frozen, no re-estimation. Run npm run data:shift -- --asof <YYYYQn>, review, push (all human-gated — §1). 11 Annual re-estimation due — a full final calendar year exists beyond the estimation vintage. Launch the MATLAB re-estimation; prep with npm run data:q1prep -- --year <YYYY>.

How the alert reaches you (zero secrets). When the outcome is 10, 11, or a probe error, the job fails on purpose. GitHub automatically emails a failed scheduled run — no SMTP server, no API key, no stored secret. (GitHub's rule: the notification for a scheduled-workflow failure goes to the user who last edited the cron in the workflow file — i.e. whoever commits this file, here matyasfarkas — following that account's notification settings. So enable the setting below once.) The job summary (Actions → the run → Summary) carries the full detail: the sentinel table, which quarter is available, and the exact command to run. When the outcome is "up to date" the job passes quietly and you hear nothing.

Forwarding the alert to gmapsmodel@gmail.com / matyi.farkas@gmail.com. The built-in email goes to the GitHub account that owns the repo (matyasfarkas), following that account's notification settings — there is no code change to make. To route it onward: - GitHub → Settings → Notifications → Actions: enable "Send notifications for failed workflows only" and point GitHub notifications at the address you want (GitHub → Settings → Emails lets you add gmapsmodel@gmail.com / matyi.farkas@gmail.com as verified addresses and choose which receives notifications), or - add a filter/forwarding rule in the receiving mailbox.

If you later want a direct email to those two addresses (instead of relying on GitHub's own notification), the upgrade path is documented but not built: add a final step using dawidd6/action-send-mail@v3 with a Gmail App Password stored as a repo secret (e.g. MAIL_PASSWORD), sending to both addresses only when steps.probe.outputs.exit_code is 10 or 11. That introduces one secret, which is why the zero-secret built-in notification is the default.

Two things to know about scheduled Actions: - A schedule: workflow fires in every repo the file is pushed to. This repo is mirrored (bvarscenario and gmapsmodel), so the job is pinned with if: github.repository == 'matyasfarkas/BVARScenarioTool' — it runs on the canonical repo only, once. - GitHub auto-disables a scheduled workflow after ~60 days of no repository activity. Any push, or a manual Run workflow, re-arms it.

A caveat the probe inherits (flagged, not a defect of the action). The probe marks a sentinel UNREACHABLE on a network blip and drops it from the coverage test. In the rare case where the only laggards (today KR, CN) go unreachable while the rest are already beyond the panel, the probe can report "shift available" one cycle early. Because the action only alerts — a human verifies full coverage before running the actual shift (§1 gates fail-closed) — this is safe: at worst it prompts a look that finds nothing to do.

docs.title: 6a. 2026 Q2 status (checked 2026-10-01) — superseded
docs.text:
Update 2026-10-08: 2026 Q2 did not arrive through a data shift. The October 2026 genuine-data re-estimation fitted every model to all data published through 2026 Q2 (pack 2026Q2-reest-20261008b), so the next data shift is to 2026 Q3. The text below is the 1 October record.

A 2026 Q2 update needs no re-estimation — it is a within-year data shift (companion frozen). This is the operating model (§"The method"): estimate once on the 2025 Q4 vintage, then shift the display origin forward one quarter at a time with no re-estimation until the next annual Q1 rebase. So when 2026 Q2 is publishable the operator simply runs npm run data:shift -- --asof 2026Q2 and the §1 chain — no MATLAB, no coupling regen.

But 2026 Q2 is not yet runnable. As of 2026-10-01 the probe reports US / EA / JP GDP at 2026 Q2 but KR and CN GDP still at 2026 Q1, so the fail-closed coverage gate correctly says no full-coverage shift available yet (exit 0). We do not force a partial shift and we do not fabricate the missing laggards — we wait for the genuine releases. The monthly action above will flag it automatically (exit 10) once KR and CN publish their 2026 Q2 GDP.

docs.title: 7. Vintage-comparison monitor (/monitor)
docs.text:
The /monitor page compares the live published panel against a prior vintage you choose, and shows the revision on a graph (not just a single scalar). It answers "what did this data update change, versus the time point I pick?"

How it works. app/scripts/vintages_publish.mjs bakes, under app/public/data/vintages/: - index.json — the registry of base vintages (what fills the "Compare against" selector), each tagged pureDataShift: true (model/companion frozen — a true data-release impact) or false (the comparison also spans a re-estimation — "model + data"). - <vintageId>/<bloc>.json — per-economy, the calendar-aligned forward revision (live − base) for every comparable variable, plus each variable's origin-quarter revision. Lazy-loaded one economy at a time.

Alignment is done by the unit-tested app/src/lib/monitor/vintageAlign.ts on two axes — variable id AND calendar quarter — never by raw array index (a 2025Q4 re-estimation has 41 vars vs the live 40, and a different origin; pairing by index would compare the wrong variable in the wrong quarter). Variables whose transformation changed, or that were dropped/added between vintages, are listed and excluded as non-comparable.

Regenerate it: npm run data:vintages. It also runs automatically in two places: late in a --shift --commit (the §1 chain step after the final coverage-manifest rebuild, so it re-bakes against the shifted live panel), and in app/package.json prebuild — i.e. on every next build — as a freshness guard so the baked public/data/vintages/* artifacts can never go stale versus the live panel (the same safeguard class as the companion-draws .gz). The artifacts have no .gz sibling, so the deploy's prune step keeps them (verified in the export).

Bases available today (honest scope). Since the October 2026 re-estimation every archived vintage was made with an earlier model, so all three bases offered now (2025Q4_shipped, 2025Q4_shipped_mb902f2385a, pre_2026Q1_counterfactual_mb902f2385a) are labelled "model + data"; the first pure-data-shift base will be the one written by the next data shift. The paragraph below is the state before the re-estimation: only ONE genuine pure-data-shift base existed — pre_2026Q1_counterfactual_mb902f2385a (same 2026Q1 origin as live, same model; 35 economies, 0 dropped), which the page opens on by default. (An older pre_2026Q1_counterfactual, last built on 26 Aug 2026 with an earlier model and wrongly labelled "model frozen", was removed in Oct 2026.) The picker also offers 2025Q4_shipped, an across-re-estimation base (origin 2025Q4, 47 economies, 5 dropped ids + 28 transform-mismatches excluded) clearly labelled "model + data". The picker grows one pure-data-shift entry each monthly shift (auto_update writes a vintage_meta.json into each new pre_<asof>_counterfactual so the publish script discovers it with no code edit).

Note on the old record. The legacy release_impact.json (the previous single-pair view, kept as a fallback) is a point-in-time snapshot from the 2026Q1 shift and is now stale relative to the current live panel; the vintage monitor recomputes fresh from the shipped files, so its numbers supersede it.

docs.title: Documentation review — flagged for human adjudication
docs.text:
Generated 2026-07-08 by the editorial + mathematical-rigour review swarm (run wf_250f0372-051, 36 agents). These are the items the swarm deliberately did not auto-apply because they touch an equation, a numeric value, a quantitative claim, or need author judgment. 41 safe editorial/render fixes were applied separately. Each item is file — issue → suggested resolution; adjudicate, don't assume the suggestion is correct.

58 items total.

docs.title: Mathematical / quantitative inconsistencies
docs.text:
• [high] REESTIMATING_MODELS.md — Line ~135 SFA-closure formula uses undefined snowball_t; ambiguous whether it is the full interest-growth level term or the increment d_{t-1}·[(1+EFFI/400)/(1+gNomQ/100)−1]. One reading makes line 135 inconsistent with the line-132 recursion. Author must confirm the build script's convention and add an explicit snowball_t definition next to the recursion.
  • [high] paper_outline.tex — eq:debt, line 174: mixed /400 vs /100 scaling on interest vs growth terms plus pb_t/4, sfa_t/4 quarterly-cadence assumptions -- frequency conventions of i^{eff}_t and g^{nom}_t are unstated, so the asymmetry cannot be verified and reads as a possible units mismatch. State frequency conventions explicitly and confirm /400 vs /100 is intended.
  • [medium] scenario-cookbook.md — §3 line ~168: near-term growth boost '~+0.9 pp (real GDP 2.3 % → 2.9 %)' is self-contradictory — 2.3→2.9 is +0.6 pp, not +0.9. The +0.9 figure is reused as the design impulse (lines 176, 192). Reconcile the illustrative pair to +0.9 (e.g. 2.0 % → 2.9 %) or restate the boost as ~+0.6 pp, keeping the +0.9 GDP-impulse pin consistent across the section.
  • [medium] scenario-cookbook.md — §7 line ~345: 'permanent +1 pp inflation RATE applied uniformly ... compounds the price level ~+8 % over 8 q' is inconsistent by ~4x with the doc's kind:'log' = q/q-annualized convention (line 36-37): +1 pp annualized over 8 q ≈ +2 % level. Either restate level as '~+2 % over 8 q' or restate rate as '~+4 q/q-ann (≈ +1 %/qtr)'. Confirm what the old recipe actually pinned first.
  • [medium] fiscal-block-methodology.md — line 92: gNomQ (gⁿ) is defined two inconsistent ways — the symbolic Δ(real-GDP 100·log)+Δ(deflator 100·log) is '% per quarter' but the 'i.e.' code expression divides by 100 (decimal). Code (fiscalAccounting.ts:180,200) uses gQ=(Δgdp+Δdefl)/100 as a decimal directly in (1+gQ). Relabel the /100 expression as gQ = gⁿ/100, not gⁿ, so line 92 matches the recursion (1+gⁿ/100). Do not drop /100 without clarifying gⁿ is in percent.
  • [medium] external-block-methodology.md — The stock is carried as NFA/GDP (a percent-of-GDP ratio — see step 6 Δ(NFA/GDP) and nfa0 = net-IIP/nominal-GDP), yet the roll adds the flow ratios CA/4 and val directly to the stock ratio with no GDP-growth denominator term (a −g·NFA₋₁ term). A ratio recursion b_t = b_{t-1} + ca/4 + val equals the level-space BoP identity NFA_t = NFA_{t-1} + CA + val only if nominal GDP is constant over the horizon. This drops exactly the automatic-denominator/growth term that the parallel fiscal FPP/DSA debt-dynamics identity (line 23) retains, so the asymmetry with the fiscal block is real and the label 'the standard BoP stock-flow identity' is imprecise for a %-of-GDP recursion.
  • [medium] external-block-methodology.md — The schematic formulas in caveats 2 and 3 (and the mapping table) drop the /100 that the precise recursion carries (lines 84 iNFA·NFA₋₁/100, 88 −fxShare·NFA₋₁·dFXₜ/100). With iNFA in % p.a. (~3) and NFA₋₁ in % of GDP (~−66.75), income = iNFA·NFA₋₁ evaluates to ≈ −200, i.e. 100× too large; likewise ΔFX is in 100·log units so the valuation formula needs its /100. Same quantity is written two inconsistent ways.
  • [medium] anchor-review-2026-07.md — The three shipped US kept-set numbers are mutually inconsistent. i−g is (effective rate) − (nominal growth). With EFFI anchored to 5 and the reported kept snowball i−g = −0.03, nominal growth must land at ≈ 5.03, not 4.3 (indeed 5 − 4.3 = +0.67 ≠ −0.03). Separately, GDPH→2 + JGDP→2 imply nominal growth ≈ 2+2 = 4.0. So the stated post-anchor nominal-growth terminal of 4.3 contradicts both the EFFI/snowball figures (which imply ~5.0) and the real+deflator anchors (which imply ~4.0). At least one number is wrong; most likely 4.3 should be ~5.0 to be consistent with EFFI→5 and i−g = −0.03.
  • [medium] EMPIRICAL_EVALUATION.md — lines 11-12 & 220-221: '56 raw origins ... leaving ~55 once four 2020 origins are dropped' is arithmetically inconsistent (56−4=52, not ~55); §9 provenance implies ~52 per cell. Reconcile the raw window (~60q), post-2020-drop count (~56), and per-cell scored-origin averages (~55/~51 after h-trims and ≥40q rule).
  • [medium] EMPIRICAL_EVALUATION.md — line 312: CRPS formula labeled 'unbiased' but uses the biased plug-in denominator 1/(2m²); unbiased/'fair' estimator uses 1/(2m(m−1)). Make adjective and kernel consistent.
  • [medium] EMPIRICAL_EVALUATION.md — lines 416 & 665: 'delta.US == the pinned scenario only' contradicts §10.1 nonzero frozen US responses (GROWTH −4.370, INFL −2.824) and self-contradicts line 665. Reword to 'delta.US carries only the US's own closed-block response to the pin — no RoW→US feedback'.
  • [medium] PIPELINE.md — lines 346/366: TOL=0.03 vs Monte-Carlo noise floor ≈0.13 — if the floor is really 0.13 the break condition Δ<0.03 can never be met and the loop always runs to MAXIT=12, contradicting TOL as the convergence criterion. Reconcile: likely floor should be ≈0.013 (TOL just above it) OR TOL should be >0.13. Author to confirm; do not auto-change either value.
  • [medium] PIPELINE.md — lines 233 vs 237: same growth-chaining recursion written inconsistently — line 233 level_t = level_{t-1}·(1+g_t) (g_t as fraction) vs line 237 level_t = level_{t-1}·(1 + g_t/100) (g_t as percent, matching FRED PRINTO01CAQ657S). Dimensionally inconsistent; author to confirm the units/convention in build_gvar_2025q4.py.
  • [medium] MODULES.md — gQ vs gNomQ symbol divergence (lines 604/605/651/652 use gQ; 559/574 use gNomQ) — standardize on one symbol or state gQ ≡ gNomQ at first divergence.
  • [medium] MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md — '40-quarter baseline' may conflate history length (historical.json data[~40][n], lines 492-493) with the H=20 forecast horizon (line 172 'Fixed in-script: ... H=20'; modelSig '...20...' line 629; frozen-anchor coupling dim 1380 = 23·3·20 line 640). Verify against the export; if H=20 governs the baseline, change 'the deployed 40-quarter baseline' -> 'the deployed 20-quarter baseline'. Not auto-applied — requires confirming the export horizon (it is a quantitative claim).
  • [medium] MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md — snowball_t is used in the SFA_t definition (line 537) and in prose (lines 854, 931) but never defined in the equation block. Consider inserting into the block: 'snowball_t = d_{t-1}·[(1 + EFFI_t/400)/(1 + gNomQ_t/100) − 1] # the (i−g) interest–growth term'. Not auto-applied — adding an equation is a math/content change requiring maintainer confirmation.
  • [medium] paper_outline.tex — eq:debt, line 174: symbols g^{nom}_t (nominal GDP growth) and pb_t (primary balance) appear in the debt recursion but are never defined; g^{nom} is not among the four named estimated drivers. Add a one-line definition after the equation.
  • [medium] paper_outline.tex — Table tab:spillover (lines 316-327): the 'gap' column is not the row-wise difference of 'endo' minus 'frozen' (e.g. US 1.28-(-4.37)=5.65 not +4.22) because each column is an independently-taken peak (max-abs) at possibly different horizons. Clarify in caption that endo/frozen/gap are each the peak of their respective paths taken independently.
  • [medium] GMAPS_User_Manual.tex — line 7666 CRPS: the 1/(2m^2) double-sum form is the BIASED (energy/NRG, Gneiting-Raftery 2007) plug-in estimator, not the 'unbiased' one. Either relabel 'the unbiased estimator' -> 'the standard (energy-form) estimator', OR change denominator to 1/(2m(m-1)) with sum over k!=l. Author must choose (m^2 form matches cited GneitingRaftery2007).
  • [medium] GMAPS_User_Manual.tex — line 3907 (i-g) debt-dynamics approximation: dimensionally inconsistent with the symbols' defined units (i^eff percent p.a. vs g^n percent per quarter; denominator 1+g^n treats percent as raw ratio; pb_t/sfa_t lose the 1/4 quarterization). Flag as schematic textbook form with decimal annual i,g, or rewrite in consistent quarterized/decimal units; do not present as an exact identity with the percent-unit symbols.
  • [low] scenario-cookbook.md — §5 line ~269: 'the old +3 for 8 q compounded to ~+6 % in 2 yr, ~5–6× the IMF decade path' — vs the ~+5.4–5.6 % / 10 yr US path (line 251), +6 % over 2 yr is ~EQUAL to the decade cumulative, not 5–6×. The 5–6× only holds on an annualized-pace basis. Clarify basis, e.g. 'an annual pace ~5–6× the IMF decade path'.
  • [low] euro-cross-border.md — line 128: 'a two-decimal tooltip can very occasionally show e.g. 2.24 vs 2.25': a ~0.005 pp (≈0.5 bp) residual (line 126) producing a visible 2.24 vs 2.25 (0.01) split is only possible as a rounding-boundary artefact. Optionally append after '2.24 vs 2.25': ' — a two-decimal rounding-boundary artefact of a ~0.005 pp residual'. Author judgment; not auto-applied as it touches a numeric claim's framing.
  • [low] fiscal-block-methodology.md — line 159: summary risk-premium channel 'i_eff += β·(d₋₁−d)' omits the max(0,·) floor present in step-2 (line 109) and code (fiscalAccounting.ts:95). As written it implies a symmetric premium reducing the rate when debt<d. Change to 'i_eff += β·max(0, d₋₁−d*)'.
  • [low] external-block-methodology.md — The valuation sign flips on the sign of the current lagged stock NFA₋₁, not on the t=0 seed nfa0. For t>0 the bloc's NFA₋₁ can differ in sign from nfa0, so conditioning the 'raises NFA' statement on nfa0<0 is imprecise (nfa0 only equals NFA₋₁ at t=0).

Use a distinct symbol (D_band or N_sim) for the band count and adjust the eq:bands summation index, noting these subsample the 500 posterior draws.
