docs.title: Mathematical / quantitative (NEW, pass 2)
docs.text:
• [high] external-block-methodology.md — Step 5, line 92 (NFAₜ = NFA₋₁ + CAₜ/4 + valₜ), plus mapping-table line 47 (NFAₜ = NFA₋₁ + CAₜ + valuationₜ), step 6 line 94, and the "standard BoP stock-flow identity" claim at line 50: The documented recursion contradicts the actual implementation. externalAccounting.ts computes nfaT = nfaPrev/(1+gQ) + caT/4 + valT, where gQ is q/q nominal GDP growth (Δgdp+Δdeflator, or Δgdp alone if gdpIsNominal), and the source header carries an explicit GROWTH DILUTION block stating that omitting the /(1+gQ) term makes a US-sized debtor 'deteriorate ~0.66 pp/quarter too fast'. The doc's step-5 recursion, step-6, and mapping table drop this /(1+gQ) denominator entirely, so the documented BoP identity is not the one the code runs. This ALSO overturns pass-1 flag #15, which adjudicated that the missing growth term is a genuine model asymmetry vs the fiscal block ('the asymmetry with the fiscal block is real') — the code is in fact symmetric (it carries the same /(1+gQ) dilution as computeFiscalBlock's debt roll); the doc is merely stale. -> Rewrite step 5 to NFAₜ = NFA₋₁/(1+gQₜ) + CAₜ/4 + valₜ and correct the mapping-table row (line 47) and step 6 to match; define gQₜ (q/q nominal GDP growth = Δgdp+Δdeflator, or Δgdp alone when gdpIsNominal); note income/val stay on the un-diluted NFA₋₁ (cross-terms second-order). Update the flag-15 adjudication: the growth term is NOT dropped in code — the DOC is out of date and must be corrected to match externalAccounting.ts. Author to confirm exact wording against the source header.
  • [high] DATA_SCHEMA.md — §5 line 305 vs lines 318-323: companion_draws called "flat row-major arrays" in the intro but "column-major" with formula beta[drawkn + j*k + i] below. For shape [k,n,n_draws] that formula has the first axis varying fastest = column-major (MATLAB/Fortran order), so "row-major" is the wrong label and contradicts the correct formula. Suggest changing "flat row-major arrays" to "flat column-major arrays (MATLAB/Fortran flatten — first axis varies fastest, matching the index formula below)"; do NOT touch the formula or line 318. Author to confirm.
  • [medium] scenario-cookbook.md — Corporate levers (FAAA, GLB_USBAA, EACORP, CORP_CN) are yield LEVELS but their pins are described as spreads (+400 bp etc.); in restricted stages that co-pin the safe 10y down (§1 to ~0.75%, ~-115 bp), a +400 bp yield-level move implies a realized corp-to-Treasury spread of ~+515 bp, not +400. Author must state explicitly whether these are yield-level or spread pins, and reconcile the flight-to-safety recipes accordingly (map header line 55; §1 lines 86/90/94; §2 line 137; §4 line 213; §9 lines 414/429).
  • [medium] scenario-cookbook.md — GDP effects quoted as cumulative peak-to-trough LEVEL % (-8.5%) but attributed to the GDPH pin, which per lines 35-36 is a q/q-ANNUALIZED GROWTH deviation. A -8.5% level trough is a multi-quarter sequence of negative growth pins, not a single -8.5 pin; a user could literally enter -8.5 as one (far milder) pin. §2 line 136 distinguishes the two spaces, so §1 line 92 / §4 line 208 / §9 lines 416/429 are inconsistent. Mark level figures as outcomes, separate from the pin.
  • [medium] scenario-cookbook.md — §7 lines 334-339: the tariff price effect is called both a 'one-off pass-through / price-LEVEL step' (permanent) and '~+1.3-1.5% cumulative over six quarters then reverting' (transitory). In growth-pin space a permanent level step leaves the level elevated (growth deviation returns to zero); 'then reverting' reads as the level coming back down, contradicting the one-off-step framing and the cited Amiti-Redding-Weinstein complete pass-through. Clarify that the growth-rate deviation fades while the price level stays elevated.
  • [medium] euro-cross-border.md — Line 42–44: "The transmission uses the deviation of the EA path from the member's own baseline (not the raw EA level) … it never injects the gap between the EA and the member's baseline": The phrase "deviation of the EA path from the member's own baseline" describes EA_path − member_baseline, which is exactly the EA-vs-member level gap the very next clause says is NOT injected — an internal contradiction. It also contradicts the implementation: eaMemberSpillover.ts "THE DELTA RULE" feeds eaDelta = scenLvl − baseLvl, i.e. the EA aggregate's scenario path minus the EA aggregate's OWN baseline, which is then applied as a delta on the member's own path. As written the doc inverts the mechanism and would mislead a reader into thinking the EA-vs-member baseline gap is what gets transmitted. -> Change "the deviation of the EA path from the member's own baseline" → "the deviation of the EA path from the EA aggregate's own baseline (the EA scenario minus the EA baseline), applied as a delta on the member's own path". Keep the rest of the sentence.
  • [medium] euro-cross-border.md — Line 101–102: "Δ YIELD10_EA = w_member · Δ spread_member, which is exactly the mechanical identity for a GDP-weighted area yield (YIELD10_EA ≈ Bund + Σᵢ wᵢ · spreadᵢ)": The decomposition is not exact. The shipped weights in ea_gdp_weights.json sum to 0.99025 over 17 modelled members — the file's own note says HR/CY/MT (~1% of EA20 GDP) are unmodelled. A true GDP-weighted average of member yields, Σᵢ wᵢ(Bund+spreadᵢ) = (Σwᵢ)·Bund + Σwᵢ·spreadᵢ, therefore carries coefficient 0.9902 on Bund (not 1) and omits ~1% of spread mass, so YIELD10_EA ≈ Bund + Σᵢ wᵢ·spreadᵢ is a genuine approximation, not an exact identity. Calling it "exactly the mechanical identity" overstates it. Note this also invalidates the pass-1 flag (2026-07-08 list) which reasoned Σwᵢ=1 and suggested changing ≈ to = — the ≈ should be KEPT and "exactly" dropped. -> Drop "exactly" and keep ≈, e.g. "…which is the mechanical identity for a GDP-weighted area yield (YIELD10_EA ≈ Bund + Σᵢ wᵢ·spreadᵢ), approximate because the 17 modelled members cover ~99% of EA20 GDP (HR/CY/MT are not modelled)." Do NOT change ≈ to =.
  • [medium] external-block-methodology.md — Caveat 3, lines 147-149 ('for a net debtor (nfa0<0, e.g. US), produce a positive valuation gain ... an economically correct J-curve/valuation channel'); channel defined at mapping line 46 / step 4 line 88: The model ties FX-exposure sign to the sign of net NFA (val = −fxShare·NFA₋₁·dFX/100), i.e. it assumes a net debtor holds net FX-denominated LIABILITIES. The US — named explicitly here — is the textbook counterexample: US foreign ASSETS are largely FX-denominated (equity/FDI abroad) while its liabilities are USD-denominated (Treasuries), so a USD appreciation REDUCES US NFA. That is exactly the Gourinchas–Rey 'exorbitant privilege' valuation channel the doc cites in Key references. Calling the model's opposite-signed result 'economically correct' for the US is therefore specifically wrong for the one bloc it names. -> Reframe: state the sign is correct only under the model's assumption that FX exposure sits on the same side as the net position; flag that the US is the known exception (long-FX-asset / short-USD, per Gourinchas–Rey), so the modeled valuation sign is inverted for the US and the twin-deficit read should rely on the flow, not the sign of the modeled US NFA valuation. Author to confirm intended framing.
  • [medium] anchor-review-2026-07.md — Lines 13-17: "autoregressive coefficients are biased downward ... the constant absorbs it, so the implied unconditional mean — the model's long-run terminal — is biased upward.": The stated causal chain (downward finite-sample AR bias + intercept ⇒ upward-biased long-run terminal) is not established and is arguably directionally wrong. For an OLS AR/VAR with intercept the fitted line passes through the sample means, so the implied unconditional mean μ̂ = ĉ/(1−ρ̂) ≈ ȳ (the sample mean) regardless of the downward bias in ρ̂; downward-biased persistence actually makes forecasts revert to that mean FASTER, not overshoot it upward. The empirical fact (US deflator terminal 4.3 vs 2.0 consensus) is therefore more plausibly the historical mean of the estimation window (a sample/regime-composition effect) than a Hurwicz/Kendall small-sample artifact. As written the derivation mislabels the source of the terminal-vs-consensus gap. -> Reconcile/soften the mechanism, e.g.: the persistent VARs with intercepts drive the long-run terminal toward the estimation-sample mean, which for these blocs sits above the current policy consensus; finite-sample (Hurwicz/Kendall) persistence bias compounds forecast instability but does not by itself produce the upward level gap. Do not present the upward terminal bias as a direct consequence of the downward AR bias.
  • [medium] anchor-review-2026-07.md — Line 20-22: δc is a "rigid translation of the whole path" vs "A large terminal gap buys anchor exactness with a front-loaded near-term shift": Internal tension: a rigid translation shifts every quarter of the path by the same amount and therefore cannot be "front-loaded." The two statements are only consistent if δc is a rigid shift in the model's estimation/level space that MANIFESTS as a front-loaded jump in the transformed display space (a uniform level shift shows up as a large near-origin move in growth/%-vs-base space and decays) — exactly the display-vs-anchor-space distinction implied by "displayed US inflation negative for two forecast years." The doc never draws that distinction, so the reader sees a self-contradiction, and the IN example (line 84: near-cast shift ~−2.0 but terminal shift only −1.57) reinforces the non-uniformity. -> State the space distinction once: δc is a rigid translation of the whole path in the model's estimation (level) space; because the display is a transform (growth / %-vs-base), the same uniform shift appears as a front-loaded near-term jump that decays toward the horizon. Then the "rigid translation" and "front-loaded" descriptions are consistent.
  • [medium] EMPIRICAL_EVALUATION.md — §9.1 point 1, line 528: "On relative-RMSE and point CRPS, the DFM wins every growth horizon": The claim that the DFM wins every growth horizon on RELATIVE-RMSE contradicts the doc's own bolded §9.2 table, where AR(p) — not DFM — is the bolded best at growth h=4 (arp 0.968 vs dfm 0.986) and h=8 (arp 0.960 vs dfm 0.962). DFM is bolded-best only at h=1 and h=2. (Separately, 'point CRPS' clashes with line 310 which calls CRPS 'the PRIMARY density score'.) The CRPS-winner claim may be fine, but the relative-RMSE half is falsified by the table. -> Change 'On relative-RMSE and point CRPS, the DFM wins every growth horizon (CRPS/RW = 0.745 / 0.836 / 0.857 / 0.841 at h = 1/2/4/8)' -> 'On CRPS the DFM wins every growth horizon (CRPS/RW = 0.745 / 0.836 / 0.857 / 0.841 at h = 1/2/4/8); on relative-RMSE it leads only at h=1–2, with AR(p) best at h=4 (0.968) and h=8 (0.960)'. Author to confirm the CRPS ranking before finalizing.
  • [medium] EMPIRICAL_EVALUATION.md — §6.2, lines 340-341: Giacomini–White bullet, '(GW assume a finite estimation window / non-vanishing estimation uncertainty — exactly this setup)': Internal methodological contradiction. §4.1 (line 216) states the scheme is 'Expanding window, recursive.' Under an expanding window the in-sample size grows without bound, so parameter-estimation uncertainty vanishes asymptotically — which is precisely the condition Giacomini–White (2006) do NOT cover; their conditional-predictive-ability theory requires a FIXED/rolling finite estimation window so estimation uncertainty stays non-vanishing. The parenthetical therefore asserts the opposite of the actual design, and framing GW as 'recursive/expanding-scheme-correct' is not defensible as written. -> Adjudicate one of: (a) run the GW forecasts on a fixed rolling window so the finite-window assumption holds; (b) drop the 'recursive/expanding-scheme-correct' claim and note GW is used under a finite-sample (non-asymptotic) reading with the expanding scheme as a stated caveat; or (c) substitute a recursive-scheme-valid test (West / Clark–McCracken) for the nested comparisons. Do not auto-edit — this is a substantive method claim.
  • [medium] ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI.md — Lines 266 & 285 (§5·EM pseudocode): TOL=0.03 vs stated MC noise floor ~0.13 — break condition 'max|Δ(stars)|0.03), contradicting 'a few iters suffice'; same defect pass-1 flagged in PIPELINE.md/REESTIMATING_MODELS.md but not here. Author to reconcile the numbers (floor ~0.013 or TOL above true floor) then make annotation consistent.
  • [medium] PIPELINE.md — §5.1 algorithm block lines 336–344 vs prose lines 351–353: EM E-step/M-step labels contradict between pseudo-code and prose. Code (line 339) puts the cgl_bvarV5 GLP posterior re-estimation of β_c,Σ_c under 'E-step / re-estimate', while 'buildstars' (line 336) is labelled 'M-step'; prose (line 352) says the M-step is the Bayesian (GLP) re-estimation plus the trade-weighted star rebuild and (line 351) the E-step is the Durbin–Koopman completion. GLP re-estimation is thus the E-step in code but the M-step in prose. Reconcile: cgl_bvarV5 jointly does the M-step (GLP posterior of β,Σ) and the E-step (DK data-augmentation completion, mean(Xcond,3)); relabel the code block accordingly and label 'buildstars' as the trade-weighting/coupling update. Conceptual/derivation matter — author must confirm intended EM mapping; not auto-applied.
  • [medium] MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md — line 794: "un-gzipped coupling_default.json (~96 MB, over GitHub's 100 MB per-file limit)" (see also line 617 "it would exceed GitHub's 100 MB per-file limit"): The plain file's size is stated as ~96 MB in two places (lines 676, 794) yet described as 'over'/'exceed[ing]' GitHub's 100 MB per-file limit (lines 617, 794). 96 MB does not exceed 100 MB — the two claims are mutually inconsistent within the same sentence at line 794. (A 31 MB gzip of numeric JSON decompresses to ~90-96 MB, so ~96 MB is plausible and the 'over 100 MB' framing is likely the wrong part; but it needs author adjudication.) -> Reconcile: if the plain file is genuinely ~96 MB, change 'over GitHub's 100 MB per-file limit' -> 'approaching GitHub's 100 MB per-file hard limit (well over the 50 MB warning threshold)'; if it is actually >100 MB, correct the '~96 MB' size. Do the same at line 617.
  • [medium] REESTIMATING_MODELS.md — §1.1 line 61 (and env-table line 93): "MAXIT=12, TOL=0.03 (MC noise floor ≈0.13).": Pass-1 flag #36 reads this as an impossible criterion (0.13 floor > 0.03 tolerance ⇒ loop never converges). The script resolves the paradox: the ≈0.13 churn is confined to the COVID-imputed macro-star cells (ROWDEM/ROWINF over 2020Q2–Q4), and those cells are EXCLUDED from the convergence metric (line 140: star_m(covid,1:2)=NaN before computing mc; ROWFIN stays in). So TOL=0.03 is tested only on the retained cells and IS achievable. The doc's bare parenthetical makes the two numbers look like the same quantity. -> Clarify the floor is on excluded cells, e.g.: "TOL=0.03 on max|Δstar| — the ≈0.13 Monte-Carlo imputation churn is confined to the COVID macro-star cells, which are EXCLUDED from the convergence metric, so the tolerance applies to the observed/retained star cells." This also defuses pass-1 flag #36.
  • [medium] paper_outline.tex — eq:coupling, lines 113-117 ("x = M x + d" / "x = (I-M)^{-1} d"), colliding with eq:debt line 174 ("d_t = ..."): The forcing/intercept vector d in the coupling identity x = Mx + d (and x = (I-M)^{-1}d, repeated in the Fig. schematic line 193) is never defined: line 117 defines only x and M. Worse, the same letter d is reused for the debt ratio d_t in the fiscal snowball eq:debt (line 174). A referee reads d as two different objects across two headline equations of the same paper. -> Define d where eq:coupling is introduced (line 117), e.g. append '... and d the stacked baseline/conditioning forcing vector (the pinned bloc deltas)'. To remove the collision, rename either the forcing vector (e.g. b or f) or the debt ratio (the fiscal literature also uses b_t for debt-to-GDP); do not leave both as d.
  • [low] index.md — Line 42 ("across 9 models") and line 63 ("9-model density race"): the model count "9" is restated in two places on the landing page and was flagged as internally disputed in source docs (PIPELINE.md line 664: 9 vs 10 configs; MODULES.md line 966: 9 vs 8 codes). Once the 8/9/10 count is adjudicated, both index.md occurrences must be reconciled in lockstep. Not auto-changed.
  • [low] scenario-cookbook.md — §2 China corp-premium bucket inconsistent: adverse (line 127) says '+50 bp (advanced) / +100 bp (EM ex-China)' explicitly excluding China, yet the adverse restricted pin (line 137) sets CORP_CN = +100 bp (the EM-ex-China number China was carved out of); severe (line 148) regroups China with the advanced bloc '(AE+China)'. Pick one consistent CN treatment (e.g. managed +75 bp in adverse) or explain the AE-vs-EM bucket switch.
  • [low] fiscal-block-methodology.md — Line 38, mapping-table row 'Net interest / debt service', 'This tool' cell: **derived**int = i_eff·d₋₁`: The table writes interest asint = i_eff·d₋₁, dropping the/100that the deployed recursion carries (line 106 and code line 188:int_t = EFFI_t · d₋₁ / 100). With EFFI in % p.a. (~5) and d₋₁ in % of GDP (~100),i_eff·d₋₁evaluates ~100× too large. Same quantity written two inconsistent ways within one file — exactly the class of defect pass-1 flagged for external-block-methodology (flag on line 88/84 /100 drops), but not caught here. The parallel IMF-FPP/DSA cell also writesi_eff · d₋₁; if that column is meant as a decimal-rate schematic, the 'This tool' cell (which uses code identifiers) should still match the code's percent convention. -> Author to reconcile. Option A: change the 'This tool' cell toint = i_eff·d₋₁/100` (i_eff in %, d₋₁ in % of GDP), matching line 106. Option B: annotate the table header that the mapping cells are schematic decimal-rate forms and defer units to §'The debt recursion, precisely'. Do NOT auto-apply — touches a units convention.
  • [low] EMPIRICAL_EVALUATION.md — §7.1, line 424: 'the frozen-anchor 24-bloc production configuration is ≈0.723 at dim = 1380': Possible cross-doc numeric mismatch. This file gives the frozen-anchor coupling as ρ(M)≈0.723 at dim=1380, whereas ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI.md (per the pass-1 flag list, line ~212) quotes the 'pre-endogenous frozen-anchor coupling' as ρ(M)≈0.726 at dim≈1920. A reader may conflate the two. They may be genuinely distinct systems (24-bloc production frozen vs 33-bloc pre-endogenous frozen), but that is not stated here. -> Verify whether the 24-bloc production frozen (0.723 / dim 1380) and the pre-endogenous frozen-anchor in ARCHITECTURE (0.726 / dim 1920) are the same system; if so reconcile the numbers, if not add a half-clause distinguishing them (e.g. 'the 24-bloc production frozen anchor, distinct from the 33-bloc pre-endogenous frozen coupling in ARCHITECTURE'). Numeric claim — do not auto-change.
  • [low] BUILD_AND_CI.md — Line 107: "an artifact-hydrated solve equals the live-built closed-form solve (<=1e-3, the 6-sig-fig rounding bound)" — justifies an ABSOLUTE bound (<=1e-3) via a RELATIVE precision (6 sig figs); these only agree for a specific magnitude. Author should either state the bound as relative (~6 sig figs) or keep <=1e-3 as an empirical tolerance without attributing it to 6-sig-fig rounding. Do not auto-edit the numeric bound.
  • [low] MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md — line 184: "With COVID imputed the optimum is well-behaved (estimated ~0.24–0.56).": The overall observed lambda range's upper bound (0.56) exceeds the maximum of the per-bloc-size sanity table just below it (line 194: small blocs ~0.3–0.5; medium ~0.25–0.4; large ~0.24–0.3 — table max 0.5). Since line 198 calls the table 'a sanity range — a post-run lambda far outside it flags a data problem,' an observed 0.56 would read as outside that very range. -> Reconcile the upper bounds: either widen the small-bloc table entry (e.g. ~0.3–0.55), or restate line 184's range to match the table (~0.24–0.5) and note 0.56 as an occasional outlier. Author to confirm the true observed maximum.
  • [low] REESTIMATING_MODELS.md — §2 line 135: "SFA_t = 4·(d_obs_t − d_{t-1} − snowball_t + pb_t/4)": The residual closes against the OBSERVED debt path (prose lines 126-128), so the lagged debt is the observed value d_obs_{t-1}; but only the current term carries the 'obs' subscript (d_obs_t), while the lag is written as bare d_{t-1}, leaving it ambiguous whether it is observed or reconstructed. -> Write the lag as d_obs_{t-1} to match d_obs_t (author to confirm the one-step residual uses the observed lag, consistent with the |d_obs_t − recon_t|<1e-6 one-step gate in §2.1).
  • [low] paper_outline.tex — eq:bloc (x_{i,t}, lines 84-90) vs eq:coupling (x, lines 111-117): The symbol x is overloaded. In eq:bloc, x_{i,t} is a per-bloc VAR state vector (domestic + star levels for economy i at time t). In eq:coupling, x is a single global vector stacking scenario DELTAS across all blocs and the whole horizon. Same letter, two structurally different objects (per-bloc level state vs global stacked deviations). -> Distinguish the two, e.g. keep x_{i,t} for the per-bloc state and use a different symbol (e.g. \xi or \Delta) for the global stacked scenario-delta vector in eq:coupling, and say one sentence that the coupling runs in deviation space over the stacked blocs/horizon.
  • [low] paper_outline.tex — line 165: "matvec-only, \(O(\dim^2)\)/iteration" vs line 117 "\(M\) the (sparse) ... transmission map": The per-iteration cost of the Neumann fixed point x <- d + Mx is given as O(dim^2), which is the dense matvec cost, yet M is described as '(sparse)' at line 117. For a sparse M the matvec is O(nnz), not O(dim^2); the two statements are in tension. -> Reconcile: either drop '(sparse)' at line 117 if the assembled augmented M is effectively dense, or state the cost as O(nnz) (worst case O(dim^2)) at line 165. Author to confirm the operative sparsity of the augmented-state M.

docs.title: Comprehensiveness gaps (NEW)
docs.text:
• [high] BUILD_AND_CI.md — Lines 44-49, 78, 84-96 — the "seven heavy patterns"/fast-heavy split enumeration is stale: app/package.json's test script has TEN --exclude globs and test:heavy names NINE selectors. Three heavy suites are undocumented here (and in the taxonomy tables): gvar-band-solve-levelunits, gvar-nowcast-completion, gvar-external-spillover. Reconcile counts (lines 78, 94) and enumerations (44-48, 84-92, 96) against live package.json; slot nowcast-completion + external-spillover into taxonomy tables. Not auto-applied: changes counts/enumerations that must match live package.json.
  • [medium] fiscal-block-methodology.md — Line 124 gross financing needsgfn_t = deficit_t + amortization_t` (and mapping-table line 43 'primary deficit + interest + amortization'): gfn is presented as a live derived reporting variable, but in computeFiscalBlockamortizationdefaults tonew Array(H).fill(0)(fiscalAccounting.ts:167) and no production caller supplies it, so the displayedgfnseries currently equals the overalldeficitexactly. §'Where we deliberately simplify' (line 181) does say 'No amortization/maturity profile for GFN', but the recursion section presents gfn as a distinct meaningful chart series without stating it collapses to the deficit in the deployed path. A reader will treat the gfn chart as carrying amortization information it does not. -> Add a clause where gfn is introduced (line 124) or a cross-reference to line 181, e.g. 'In the deployed pathinput.amortizationdefaults to zeros (fiscalAccounting.ts:167), so the displayedgfncurrently equals the overall deficit exactly — the+ amortization` term is a placeholder pending a maturity/amortization profile (see "No amortization/maturity profile", below).' Confirm the zero-default claim before wording.
  • [medium] external-block-methodology.md — idx list at line 159 ('the positional idx ... (exports/imports/gdp/deflator/fx)'); deflator also in CN formula lines 171 & 204: deflator is listed as a positional index and appears in the CN realIndexDeflate GDP reconstruction, but it is never introduced in the element-mapping table or the recursion steps. In fact deflator feeds the growth term gQ (Δgdp+Δdeflator) for EVERY bloc, not just CN — yet neither deflator nor gQ appears anywhere in the documented recursion. A reader cannot tell which BVAR variable deflator is, nor that it is load-bearing in the stock roll. -> Add a mapping-table / recursion definition of deflator (GDP deflator, 100·log) and introduce gQ where the growth-dilution term is added (tie to finding on step 5). Note deflator enters both the CN nominal-USD reconstruction and the all-bloc gQ growth term.
  • [medium] ARCHITECTURE_FOR_AI.md — Line 448 'Debt service (interest, % GDP) = EFFI·d_{t-1}/100' vs line 445 recursion term '(1+EFFI/400)': reported debt service is 4x the per-quarter accrual with no frequency label; unexplained 4x for a doc whose purpose is exact replication. Add an 'annualised' label after author confirms the series is annual.
  • [medium] PIPELINE.md — line 308 'a rate-less partner (CH/NO) still feeds DEM/INF': §5.1 step 2 cites CH and NO as rate-less-partner example, contradicting §3.1 line 96 where build_polrate_hp_group.py adds POLRATE_ (BIS CBPOL) to SE/PL/DK/CZ/HU/NO/IS/CH/IL/TR — i.e. both CH and NO now carry a policy rate and would feed ROWFIN, making the example stale. Confirm which coupled blocs are genuinely rate-less in the ROWFIN build after the polrate additions and either replace 'CH/NO' with truly rate-less blocs or reword generically. Factual claim about which blocs lack rates — author to confirm; not auto-applied.
  • [medium] MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md — line 170: "| GVAR_WEIGHTS_FILE | weights_full.json else weights_24bloc.json | which weights / bloc list |": The estimator's env default prefers weights_full.json, but everywhere else in THIS doc weights_24bloc.json is presented as THE deployed weights/bloc source (line 134 'a new GVAR bloc needs a row in weights_24bloc.json', line 791 commit list, line 1001 file map), and line 1028 describes weights_full.json as the shipped 2021-2023 rolling-weights file that is 'forbidden in the OOS sweep'. A reader cannot tell which file the production estimator actually reads or which is committed. (Pass-1 flagged the same latent conflict only in REESTIMATING_MODELS.md; it is unaddressed here.) -> State plainly which file the deployed production run reads. If production uses weights_24bloc.json, add a note that weights_full.json (if present) is the eval-repo's full/latest-weights artifact and clarify why the env default names it first (or that it is absent from this repo).
  • [medium] REESTIMATING_MODELS.md — §1.1 lines 45 & 48: "COVID + no-partner quarters start NaN" and "the DK ... smoother fills the missing star + COVID quarters → a completed matrix per bloc.": Omits the load-bearing macro-only detail. Per the script (lines 65-140), over 2020Q2–Q4 ONLY the isFinancial==false columns are NaN'd (domestic macro + ROWDEM + ROWINF); the domestic financials AND the ROWFIN financial star are KEPT OBSERVED, so the DK smoother imputes the macro holes CONDITIONED on the observed financials. As written the doc implies all COVID cells (including financial/star) are missing and imputed, which misstates the estimator's active-conditioning-through-COVID design. -> Add a clause, e.g.: "COVID masking is macro-only: over 2020Q2–Q4 only the macro columns (isFinancial==false: domestic macro + ROWDEM + ROWINF) are NaN'd; domestic financials and the ROWFIN star stay observed, so the DK smoother imputes the macro holes conditioned on the observed financials."
  • [low] index.md — Line 43: "the endogenous-US Tier-A spillover analysis" — "Tier-A" appears with no gloss, an outlier since every other acronym on the page (BVAR, GVAR, DSGE, CBO, CRPS, DFM) is expanded on first use. Add a brief inline gloss confirmed against EMPIRICAL_EVALUATION.md's tier definition (e.g. "Tier-A (own-block)") or drop "Tier-A" and let the linked doc carry it. Needs author confirmation of the exact tier meaning, so not a mechanical edit.
  • [low] USER_GUIDE.md — Line 55 "Full does the same with 200 draws.": Quick's draw count is never stated, making the Quick-vs-Full distinction one-sided. Code sets quick=50 / full=200 (app/src/lib/compute/runGvarBandSolve.ts:18). Suggested (NOT applied, per instructions): "Quick uses 50 draws; Full does the same with 200."
  • [low] euro-cross-border.md — Line 106: "real Eurostat data (current-price GDP, 4-quarter-trailing share of the 20-member euro area (EA20) …) — not assumed": The doc presents the weights as EA20 shares but never discloses that the modelled members sum to only 0.9902 (three EA20 members — Croatia, Cyprus, Malta — are not modelled), which is what makes the area-yield decomposition approximate and slightly under-weights the spread pass-through. A reader treating them as a full partition of EA20 GDP would expect Σwᵢ = 1. -> Add a half-sentence noting coverage, e.g. after "…not assumed": "(the 17 modelled members cover ≈99% of EA20 GDP; Croatia, Cyprus and Malta are not modelled as members)."
  • [low] euro-cross-border.md — Line 99–104: "Sovereign Spread (vs Bund). Conditioning a member's spread … feeds the euro-area long yield in proportion to that country's share of euro-area GDP.": The section states only the AREA effect (Δ YIELD10_EA = w_member·Δspread_member) and is silent on the member's OWN long yield, which — since a member long rate is defined as Bund + spread — rises one-for-one (coefficient 1) with its own spread pin. A reader could wrongly infer that pinning Italy's spread moves Italy's own 10Y by only ~14% of the pin. -> Add a clause, e.g. "The pinned member's own long yield (Bund + spread) moves one-for-one with its spread; only the area yield picks it up in proportion w_member."
  • [low] fiscal-block-methodology.md — Line 136 inverse map pb_t = 4·[(d₋₁ + int_t/4)/(1 + gⁿ_t/100) − d_target,t] + sfa_t: The formula's d₋₁ is ambiguous. To pin the whole target trajectory (not just the endpoint) the lag must be taken along the TARGET path, which the code does (fiscalAccounting.ts:237 uses input.targetDebt[t-1]) and its comment states explicitly (line 228: 'd_{t-1} taken along the TARGET path'). The doc's formula and surrounding prose (lines 137-139) never say d₋₁ here is the target-path lag rather than the realized/forecast debt, leaving a reader to assume the realized path. -> Annotate line 136, e.g. append '(with d₋₁ read off the target path — fiscalAccounting.ts:237 — so the whole trajectory is pinned, not just the endpoint)'. Changes meaning of the symbol, so not auto-applied.
  • [low] external-block-methodology.md — Line 65 ('the FX index (idx.fx, log var: US FXTWM, EA NEER_EA, CN REER_CN)') feeding the valuation channel at step 4 / mapping line 46: US FXTWM and EA NEER_EA are NOMINAL effective exchange rates, but CN uses REER_CN, a REAL effective rate. The valuation channel revalues FX-DENOMINATED net assets, which is a nominal-exchange-rate concept; driving CN's valuation off a real effective rate mixes a relative-price move into a pure revaluation term, an inconsistency vs the US/EA nominal indices that the doc does not acknowledge. -> Add a one-line caveat that CN's valuation leg is driven by a real effective rate (REER_CN) whereas US/EA use nominal indices, and that this conflates relative-price and revaluation effects for CN; or confirm a nominal CN FX series is intended. Author judgment.
  • [low] anchor-review-2026-07.md — Lines 51 & 58: EA HICP→2 "terminal 3.36 → 1.53": The EA HICP anchor targets 2, yet the reported post-anchor terminal is 1.53 — an undershoot of ~0.47 pp BELOW the anchor's own target. For per-variable additive-δc anchoring (described as landing each anchored terminal at its target) this is counterintuitive and unexplained, especially since the US inflation anchors (GDPH→2/JGDP→2) apparently land near target. A reader cannot tell whether 1.53 reflects co-anchor cross-drag (EA FPEXP), a horizon effect (tilt moment fixed at a different horizon than the H=20 terminal reported), or an error. This also bears on pass-1 flag #17 (US 4.3 vs 5.0 vs 4.0), which is the same 'anchored terminal ≠ target' phenomenon. -> Add a half-sentence explaining why the anchored EA HICP terminal undershoots its 2.0 target (e.g., residual cross-drag from EA FPEXP within the kept set, or that the tilt fixes a different-horizon moment than the reported H=20 terminal).
  • [low] anchor-review-2026-07.md — Line 76-78: "Fiscal snowball coherence ... CA −1.86 → −2.22": Under a section headed "coherence" whose narrative is that anchoring pulls the too-negative i−g back toward zero (US −3.92→−0.03 etc.), CA moves the wrong way — from −1.86 to −2.22, i.e. MORE negative, making CA's debt-melt channel stronger, not weaker. This regression is presented in the improvement table with no comment, whereas the far smaller UK primary-surplus side effect (line 78-80) is explicitly flagged as "accepted knowingly." The asymmetric treatment leaves the reader to notice the CA worsening unaided. -> Add a short parenthetical acknowledging CA is the one bloc whose i−g moves further from zero (−1.86 → −2.22) and why that is accepted (e.g., no CA growth/rate anchor; move is incidental cross-drag and stays well short of the US-class pathology).
  • [low] anchor-review-2026-07.md — Throughout (e.g. lines 26, 58-59, 78-80, 88): EFFI, FREV, FPEXP, SFA, NSA, SENS, WN used without definition: This standalone review doc leans on project-specific fiscal/estimation acronyms (EFFI, FREV, FPEXP, SFA, NSA, SENS guard, WN prior) that are never expanded here. EFFI is inferable from line 39 ('effective interest rate') and NC is covered by pass-1 flag #65, but FREV/FPEXP/SFA/NSA/WN meanings are not stated anywhere in the file. For the IMF/central-bank reader consuming this note on its own, the fiscal-share and prior-fix references are undecodable. -> Add a one-line glossary or expand on first use (author must supply the intended expansions for FREV = fiscal revenue, FPEXP = fiscal primary expenditure, SFA = stock-flow adjustment, NSA = non-seasonally-adjusted, WN = white-noise prior — confirm before writing).
  • [low] EMPIRICAL_EVALUATION.md — §6.2, line 344: 'instruments g_{t−1} = [1, d_{t−1}]': The GW instrument d_{t−1} is used but never defined; the reader cannot tell it is the lagged loss/score differential. The symbol d is separately used for debt and for GVAR forcing in sibling docs, compounding the ambiguity. -> Add a one-line gloss after the equation, e.g. 'where d_{t−1} is the lagged loss (CRPS or squared-error) differential between the two models.' Confirm the intended instrument (loss differential vs a state variable) before writing.
  • [low] EMPIRICAL_EVALUATION.md — §5 JSON example, lines 272 & 281: '"origin": "2019-Q1"' with '"weightsWindow": "2005-2009"': The example forecast JSON pairs a 2019-Q1 origin with weightsWindow '2005-2009' (the fixed pre-2010 fallback), but §4.2 makes rolling as-of weights the default, under which a 2019 origin should carry the (Y−3)..(Y−1) = 2016-2018 window. The example silently shows the fixed-mode fallback without a WeightsMode field, so it reads as if rolling weights for 2019 = 2005-2009, which is wrong under the default. -> Either set '"weightsWindow": "2016-2018"' to match the default rolling scheme for a 2019 origin, or annotate the example (e.g. add '"weightsMode": "fixed"') so the 2005-2009 fallback is unambiguous. Confirm which the example intends.
  • [low] DATA_SCHEMA.md — §3.1 lines 207 & 230 say "44 non-fiscal blocs" (+6 fiscal ⇒ ~50 total), but the doc's own taxonomy gives 33 GVAR blocs (§10 line 505) + 16 euro FSAP standalones (§6 line 354), and all 6 fiscal blocs sit within the 33, so non-fiscal = (33−6)+16 = 43, not 44. Counts are off by one with no third category to absorb the difference. Author to confirm true bloc census before correcting 44→43 (and ~50→49) or naming a 50th standalone.
  • [low] DATA_SCHEMA.md — §13.2 example lines 758-762: model "emgvar_endo" (US-endogenous variant) carries meta usEndogenous:false, but line 728 defines usEndogenous as whether the US joined the coupled loop with its own ROW*_US block at this origin, so the reader expects true. Reads as self-contradictory. Author to confirm whether to set the value to true or add a clause explaining why an emgvar_endo origin can legitimately record usEndogenous:false.
  • [low] DATA_SCHEMA.md — "FSAP" is load-bearing throughout DATA_SCHEMA.md (first use line 113 "euro FSAP standalones"; recurs 116, 127-129, 184, 258, 354) but is never expanded in this file. Suggest expanding on first use to "euro FSAP (Financial Sector Assessment Program) standalones", consistent with the MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md flag. Author to confirm intended expansion.
  • [low] BUILD_AND_CI.md — Line 89: heavy-table row gvar-closed-form-* lists only gvar-closed-form-routing.test.ts, but the glob also matches gvar-closed-form-convergence-guard.test.ts, which runs heavy. Add it to the cell after verifying current directory contents.
  • [low] BUILD_AND_CI.md — Line 134: PLR (in "the entropic long-run tilt + PLR (longRunTilt.ts)") is used without expansion — project-specific jargon, only occurrence in this file. Expand on first use (e.g. "PLR (prior long-run restriction)"); confirm intended expansion with the author.
  • [low] MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md — line 231: "This is the per-variable Minnesota/GLP prior-mean knob" (GLP also at line 240): GLP is used repeatedly without expansion (also underlies the code path 'GLPreplicationWeb', line 997). For the maintainer/economist audience it is the Giannone–Lenza–Primiceri prior, but the acronym is never spelled out on first use — the same class of gap pass-1 flagged for FSAP/LRP/NC in sibling docs. -> Expand on first use: 'per-variable Minnesota/GLP (Giannone–Lenza–Primiceri) prior-mean knob'. Confirm the intended expansion with the author (consistent with pass-1's non-auto posture on acronym expansions).
  • [low] paper_outline.tex — line 126: "\(0.723\) (24-bloc frozen anchor, \(\dim\approx 1380\))": 24 blocs x 3 vars x 20 horizon = 1440, not 1380. The stated dim 1380 equals 23320 because in the frozen route the US is weakly exogenous and its row is absent from M (as the paper itself states at lines 121-123). A reader who multiplies 24320 gets 1440 and reads dim 1380 as an error. (By contrast the endogenous dim 2060 = 33320 + 4 commons20 checks out cleanly.) -> Add a half-clause reconciling the count, e.g. '(24-bloc frozen anchor; US exogenous so M spans the 23 endogenous blocs, dim = 233*20 = 1380)'. Confirm the horizon/commons treatment against the coupling artifact before wording.
  • [low] paper_outline.tex — Table tab:spillover, line 320 (US growth: endo \(+1.28\), frozen \(-4.37\)): Under the frozen anchor a US +100bp pin gives US growth -4.37 (contractionary, as expected), but under the endogenous solve US OWN growth is +1.28 (expansionary) - i.e. endogenizing the US flips the sign of the US's own-growth response to its own rate hike. This counterintuitive own-response sign flip is stronger than the generic 'sign-flipping across blocs' caveat (line 333) admits and is left unexplained, which undercuts the 'qualitative claim ... is robust' sentence for the very bloc being pinned. -> Either add one sentence explaining why RoW->US feedback plausibly reverses the sign of the US own-growth response (or that this specific reversal is a symptom of the un-validated magnitudes), or foreground it in the honest-caveat paragraph rather than only listing it in the table.
  • [low] paper_outline.tex — Table tab:spillover caption, line 314: "... gap (scored space; ...)": The term 'scored space' is used once, only in the caption, and is never defined anywhere in the paper. A reader cannot tell what transformation/units the responses are reported in (raw deviations, standardized, q/q-annualized, etc.). -> Define 'scored space' at first use or replace it with an explicit description of the units (matching how CRPS is scored). Author must supply the intended meaning; do not guess.

docs.title: Editorial (NEW)
docs.text:
• [high] REESTIMATING_MODELS.md — §1.1 lines 59-60: "COVID window is the argmin of ΔGDP restricted to 2019Q4–2021Q1 (a global argmin misfires, e.g. KR's 2008Q4 GFC drop), then ± quarters around it are NaN'd → DK-imputed.": This describes a DEPRECATED design. We no longer auto-detect a GDP-trough window (which spanned ~7 q and could misfire on other crises)." The doc presents the removed argmin auto-detection (with its KR-2008Q4 misfire rationale) as the current behavior, contradicting the script and the project MEMORY note (COVID = fixed 2020Q2–Q4, 3Q). -> Replace with the current fixed-window description, e.g.: "COVID window is a FIXED 2020Q2–2020Q4 (3 quarters), per spec (B). (The earlier GDP-trough argmin auto-detection — which spanned ~7q and could misfire on other crises such as KR's 2008Q4 GFC drop — was removed.)" docs.text: • [compile] GMAPS_management_slides (PPTX is canonical) — The deck does NOT compile with the instructed command 'cd docs && (lua|pdf)latex GMAPS_management_presentation/GMAPS_management_slides.tex' — it fails with 'Missing $ inserted' at line 211. This is PRE-EXISTING (reproduced on the pristine git-stashed original, both lualatex and pdflatex) and is NOT caused by my edits (which are at lines 394/410/413, far past where the compiler stops). Root cause: \graphicspath and \IfFileExists{figures/...} resolve relative to the CWD; when built from docs/ the figures (which live in docs/GMAPS_management_presentation/figures/) are not found, the \figmask fallback fires, and it typesets underscore-bearing filenames (e.g. s1_macro_triad) in text mode. Building from inside docs/GMAPS_management_presentation/ works: both pdflatex and lualatex produce a clean 13-page PDF (exit=0). Recommend either compiling from the presentation directory or making \IfFileExists path-robust (e.g. use \graphicspath-aware existence check) so the deck builds from the repo's docs/ root.

docs.title: Drivers — model-conditional shock decomposition of a scenario path
docs.text:
Experimental feature, model-conditional claim

The Drivers panel is experimental and is badged as such in the tool. What it reports is conditional on the DSGE model the user selects: the mix of that model's own structural shocks which reproduces the displayed path. It is not a statement about what caused the scenario, and it is not model-free shock labelling. Read Limits of the claim before using any number from it.

The Drivers drawer takes the scenario path the app is currently showing — or an imported external-forecast combination — and asks a chosen model from the Macroeconomic Model Base (MMB) which sequence of that model's structural shocks would have produced it over the first twelve forecast quarters. It draws the answer as a stacked contribution chart in the same units as the main panel, with an explicit grey residual for the part the named shocks cannot reproduce. This is the NAWM-II-style "filter the path through the model" exercise, run on a path object rather than by inverting a state recursion.

It fits the tool's standing division of labour. The fiscal block and the external block take BVAR flow forecasts and derive stocks by accounting identity; Drivers takes the same BVAR path and reads it through a structural lens. In all three cases the reduced form generates the path and a separate, side-effect-free module interprets it. The authoritative implementation is app/src/lib/compute/driversDecomp.ts (the engine) and app/src/components/controls/DriversDrawer.tsx (the drawer); neither writes back into the scenario.

docs.title: The question it answers
docs.text:
A user looking at a scenario in which output falls and inflation stays up wants to know what kind of disturbance that pattern looks like. The variance decomposition answers a population question (how much of the fluctuation in inflation is due to supply shocks?), and the historical decomposition answers a sample question (which shocks moved inflation in 2022?). Drivers answers a third, narrower question: which sequence of this model's shocks, fed into this model, reproduces the path I am looking at?

That question has an honest answer and a dishonest one. The honest answer names the model: through the Smets–Wouters (2007) lens, this scenario is mostly a wage-markup and monetary mix; through the Christiano–Motto–Rostagno (2014) lens it is something else, because CMR14 has a financial block and SW07 does not. The dishonest answer drops the qualifier and claims to have identified what drove the economy. Everything in this page — the budget rule, the collinearity flag, the class-view licence — exists to keep the tool on the first answer.

The exercise is validated by same-model recovery: a path is generated from a model's own known shock sequence, decomposed under that same model, and the recovered contribution paths are compared with the truth. That measures the estimator. It says nothing about whether the model is right.

docs.title: The object, precisely
docs.text:
Let \(H = 12\) be the decomposition horizon in quarters (DRIVERS_H, driversDecomp.ts:46), \(q\) the number of watched observables, and \(K\) the number of named shocks. \(H\) is fixed: the decomposition always covers the first twelve forecast quarters, whatever horizon the main chart grid is displaying. The user supplies a deviation path \(z\) — the scenario's level deviation from baseline, mapped into the model's observable space by the conventions in Unit conventions.

The engine solves the deconvolution

\[ z_o(t) \;=\; \sum_{k=1}^{K}\ \sum_{\tau \le t} R_{k,o}(t-\tau)\, \varepsilon_k(\tau) \;+\; u_o(t), \qquad o = 1,\dots,q, \quad t = 0,\dots,H-1 \]

for the shock sequence \(\{\varepsilon_k(\tau)\}\). Here \(R_{k,o}(h)\) is the model's impulse response of observable \(o\) to shock \(k\) at horizon \(h\), read straight from the shipped MMB impulse-response file, and \(u_o(t)\) is the residual — the part of the path the named shocks cannot reproduce.

docs.title: The stacked response matrix
docs.text:
Stacking observables and quarters turns that convolution into one linear system. Define \(\Theta\) of dimension \((q\!\cdot\!H) \times (K\!\cdot\!H)\) by

\[ \Theta[\,o H + t,\; k H + \tau\,] \;=\; R_{k,o}(t-\tau)\,\mathbf{1}\{t \ge \tau\}. \]

Rows are blocked by observable: row \(oH+t\) is observable \(o\) at forecast quarter \(t\), with the three locked common observables first and any added natives in the order the user toggled them. Columns are blocked by shock: column \(kH+\tau\) is shock \(k\) arriving in quarter \(\tau\). Each \((o,k)\) block is therefore lower-triangular Toeplitz. The system is \(\Theta \varepsilon = z - u\) with \(z\) and \(\varepsilon\) stacked the same way, \(z[oH+t] = z_o(t)\) and \(\varepsilon[kH+\tau] = \varepsilon_k(\tau)\).

The response \(R_{k,o}(h)\) is read as irf[shock_k][irfField_o][h + 1]. Index 0 of every impulse- response array is the pre-impact zero and indices \(1,\dots,H\) carry \(h = 0,\dots,H-1\), which mirrors the MATLAB benchmark's s.obs(2:H+1) exactly (bench_simple_decomp.m:99). The shipped arrays are all of length 21, so horizons \(h = 0,\dots,19\) are available and the engine uses the first twelve.

docs.title: Notation
docs.text: Symbol Meaning \(H = 12\) decomposition horizon, in quarters \(q\) observables watched (three locked common ones, plus added natives) \(K\) shocks — or clusters — named \(o\), \(t\) observable index, forecast quarter (0-based) \(k\), \(\tau\) shock index, arrival quarter (0-based) \(R_{k,o}(h)\) model \(M\)'s response of observable \(o\) to shock \(k\) at horizon \(h\) \(\Theta\) \((qH) \times (KH)\) stacked response matrix \(z\) stacked observable-space deviation path \(\varepsilon\) stacked shock sequence \(D\) \(\mathrm{diag}(\lVert\Theta_{\cdot 1}\rVert,\dots,\lVert\Theta_{\cdot KH}\rVert)\), the column-norm scaling; \(\Theta_N = \Theta D^{-1}\) \(W\) diagonal row weights, \(w = 1/\sqrt{1+\mathrm{me}}\) on added observables, 1 on the locked three \(\lambda\) \(10^{-8}\cdot\mathrm{mean}\,\mathrm{diag}(\Theta_N^{\top}W^2\Theta_N)\) \(u\) residual, \(u = z - \Theta\hat\varepsilon\) \(c_{k,o}(t)\) shock \(k\)'s contribution to observable \(o\) at quarter \(t\)

docs.title: The estimator
docs.text:
The system is square only in the special case \(K = q\); in general it is underdetermined in the shock dimension, so the engine reports the minimum-norm least-squares solution,

\[ \hat\varepsilon \;=\; D^{-1}\cdot \operatorname*{arg\,min}\ \lVert \tilde\varepsilon \rVert \quad\text{subject to minimising}\quad \bigl\lVert W\bigl(\Theta D^{-1}\tilde\varepsilon - z\bigr)\bigr\rVert^2 . \]

That is the pinv solution the MATLAB benches use, computed here without forming a pseudo-inverse (decompose, driversDecomp.ts:227–362). The engine takes the Euclidean norm of every column of the raw, unweighted \(\Theta\), leaving any column with norm below \(10^{-12}\) at a scale of 1 so it stays inert rather than being amplified; divides each column by its norm to get \(\Theta_N\); applies the row weights to both \(\Theta_N\) and \(z\) where an added observable carries measurement error; forms the Gram matrix, adds the ridge \(\lambda = 10^{-8}\cdot\mathrm{mean}\,\mathrm{diag}\) (RIDGE_LAMBDA_SCALE, driversDecomp.ts:49), and LU-factors it once. It then solves the ridge normal equations and runs two iterative-refinement sweeps against that same factorisation (REFINE_STEPS = 2). Every iterate stays in \(\mathrm{range}(\Theta^{\top})\), so the refined solution converges on the min-norm least-squares solution rather than on the ridge-biased one; the source records the worst-case recovery error falling from roughly \(7\times10^{-7}\) under the bare ridge to about \(10^{-15}\) with refinement (driversDecomp.ts:14–16). Finally the recovered shocks are mapped back through the column scaling, \(\hat\varepsilon_j = \hat\varepsilon_{N,j} / \lVert\Theta_{\cdot j}\rVert\).

docs.title: Why the columns are normalised
docs.text:
Scaling every column to unit response norm before the solve imposes an equal-response-energy prior across shocks. Without it the \(\ell^2\) penalty quietly prefers whichever shock moves the observables most per unit of \(\varepsilon\), and prices the others out of their own attribution.

The magnitudes involved are not subtle. Measured from the shipped US_SW07/SW.json, the stacked three-observable \(H = 12\) response norms are 1.28 for the monetary shock interest_, 2.12 for fiscal_, 4.21 for eqs, 4.50 for eb, 4.93 for ea, 11.58 for the wage markup ew and 13.84 for the price markup epinf. Roughly an order of magnitude separates the monetary shock from the markup shocks, and under a raw min-norm solve the monetary shock loses attribution to them for no economic reason.

In identified configurations the normalisation is a pure reparameterisation: the licence fixtures (UK_SM11 at three observables, SW07 at seven observables with seven shocks) still recover to \(10^{-6}\) or better. In underdetermined configurations it removes the small-column bias — for SW07 at three observables, mean off-class leakage falls from 32% to 5% (class_recovery_results.txt). Its signature is visible in a constructed case: with two exactly collinear shocks whose response norms differ 2:1, the shipped solver splits the contribution equally where a raw min-norm solver would split it 4:1.

docs.title: Contributions, fit and residual
docs.text:
Contributions are computed through the raw, unweighted \(\Theta\) and the un-normalised \(\hat\varepsilon\) (contributionsFromEps, driversDecomp.ts:198):

\[ c_{k,o}(t) \;=\; \sum_{\tau \le t} \Theta[\,oH+t,\;kH+\tau\,]\,\hat\varepsilon_k(\tau), \qquad \hat z_o(t) = \sum_k c_{k,o}(t), \qquad u_o(t) = z_o(t) - \hat z_o(t). \]

Because \(\Theta\hat\varepsilon \equiv \Theta_N\hat\varepsilon_N\) exactly, the column normalisation leaves the reported contributions unchanged; and because the row weights enter only the solve, they never touch the reported contributions either. The weights change which shock sequence is chosen, not how a chosen sequence is attributed.

docs.title: Rank and regime
docs.text:
thetaRank (driversDecomp.ts:144) is a pivoted Cholesky on the smaller-side Gram matrix with a relative pivot tolerance of \(10^{-12}\) times the largest diagonal. The engine reports regime = 'exact-fit' when \(\mathrm{rank}(\Theta) \ge qH\) and 'residual-able' otherwise. The threshold is not delicate in practice: the two regimes on the shipped menu are about twenty orders of magnitude apart in conditioning, with full-rank models at \(\mathrm{cond}(\Theta) \lesssim 10^{2}\) and the rank-deficient CA_LS07 at \(\approx 3\times10^{17}\).

Remark 1 (An exact-fit residual is zero by construction). In the exact-fit regime every path is reproducible, so the residual is identically zero and carries no information. It is not evidence that the named shocks explain the path. The residual becomes a genuine test only once the user watches more observables than the named shocks can span — that is, in the residual-able regime, where an unexplained dimension actually exists.

docs.title: The engine's entry point
docs.text:
The whole decomposition runs through one call, displayed here in the form the code uses:

decompose(irf, shocks, observables, H) → DriversDecomposition

irf is a ModelIRFs record mapping each shock name to a record of response arrays keyed by model observable field. shocks is the string array of named shocks, length \(K\), in the order the columns are blocked. observables is an array of length \(q\); each entry carries key (the display key, for instance output or dc), irfField (the field to read from each shock's response record, usually the same string), path (the observable's scenario deviation path, length at least \(H\)), and an optional weight (the measurement-error row weight \(w = 1/\sqrt{1+\mathrm{me}}\), left undefined for the exact common three). H defaults to DRIVERS_H = 12.

What comes back is a DriversDecomposition: eps, a Float64Array of length \(K\!\cdot\!H\) in shock-major order; contributions, a \(K \times q \times H\) nested array; fitted and residual and z, each \(q \times H\); the scalars lambda, rank and rows (\(= qH\)); and regime, either 'exact-fit' or 'residual-able'. The call throws when no shock is named, when a supplied path is shorter than \(H\), and — the budget rule, below — when more shocks are named than observables are watched.

docs.title: Unit conventions
docs.text: Every mapping in this section was measured from the shipped files and is regression-guarded by the test suite. None of it is assumed.

docs.title: From the BVAR panel to the three common observables
docs.text:
The input is the active scenario's level deviation from baseline, indexed [t][j], in the smoother's level space: \(100\cdot\log\) for log variables, native units for linear ones. The long-run drift translates baseline and scenario rigidly, so it cancels in the deviation by construction (useStore.ts:11–16). commonObservablePaths (driversDecomp.ts:392) then builds the three MMB common observables:

Model observable Built from the BVAR panel as US column output GDP level deviation (\(100\cdot\log\)), identity GDPH inflationq \(4\,(p_t - p_{t-1})\) of the price-level deviation, with \(p_{-1} = 0\) JGDP interest policy-rate deviation, annualised, identity — no division by 4 POLRATE

The two factors of four are not conventions chosen here; they are read off the model file, which carries both the MMB common block and SW07's native observables. A regression test checks, on every shock and every horizon with a non-trivial response, that inflationq/pinfobs and interest/robs both equal 4.000 to better than \(10^{-9}\).

docs.title: Native observables (US bloc only)
docs.text:
Two models expose real-side observables beyond the common three, and both maps were measured from the shipped response files rather than taken from the model papers.

For US_SW07 (SW07_NATIVE_MAP) the four addable observables are consumption growth dc, investment growth dinve, real-wage growth dw from \(\Delta\)((LXBC − JGDP) deviation), and hours labobs from the LANAGRA deviation in level. All differences use \(\text{deviation}_{-1} = 0\).

Two of those rows were corrected in August 2026 after an audit against the harmonised observable dictionary of the MMB real-time forecasting platform, which records the exact source construction of every model observable and ships the constructed observables as numbers. That turns a mapping from something argued into something measured: build the candidate from the GMAPS panel, line it up against the platform's own series, and read the fit. The benchmark is the revision floor — the row dy, where both sides are the identical formula on the identical series, and which therefore scores rmse 0.099 pp per quarter from data-vintage differences alone. A row at that floor is exact.

row was measured now measured dc \(\Delta\)(CH) corr 0.837, rmse 0.308 \(\Delta\)(CH + JC − JGDP) corr 0.982, rmse 0.109 dinve \(\Delta\)(FNH) corr 0.881, rmse 0.956 \(0.2384\,\Delta\)FRH \(+\ 0.7616\,\Delta\)FNH corr 0.984, rmse 0.351

CH is chain-weighted real consumption deflated by its own price index, whereas the model observable is nominal consumption deflated by the GDP deflator; swapping the deflator is an identity, and same-vintage it reproduces the platform's series exactly. FNH is the nonresidential component alone, while the model observable is total private fixed investment — roughly a quarter of the series was absent, and it is the quarter that moves in housing and credit scenarios. FNH and FRH share the JGDP deflator, so their level sum is exactly the model's observable; but the log of a sum is non-linear and would break the additivity of §"Contributions", so the shipped row is its first-order share-weighted expansion at the measured residential share 0.2384. Linearising costs rmse 0.048 pp per quarter against the exact sum, 2.7% of the observable's own standard deviation, measured on the shipped US panel. The weights must not be re-tuned to a scenario origin, and a naive 0.5/0.5 average is worse than leaving the row unfixed.

labobs is a proxy, and it is the one row that cannot be built correctly

The model observable is hours per capita. LANAGRA is an establishment-survey employment headcount, and the US bloc carries neither an average-hours series nor population, so the intensive margin — hours per worker — is absent. Measured in the 12-quarter deviation space this panel works in, the proxy scores median correlation 0.906 against the true series with an error at the 12-quarter horizon of roughly 0.6 of the signal. A scenario that moves hours per worker without moving headcount is under-read.

Two numbers circulate for this row and they measure different things. A historical shock decomposition rates it far lower, at 0.699 across seven observables — but that exercise is in levels, where the missing population trend dominates. A scenario deviation carries the same demographics in baseline and scenario, so the trend cancels exactly and only the intensive margin is lost. Quote 0.906 for this panel and 0.699 for a historical decomposition.

A satellite bridge — projecting average hours onto columns the bloc already carries — was tested and rejected. In-sample it looks good (\(R^2\) 0.52, deviation correlation 0.906 → 0.940), but split at the financial crisis three of its five coefficients flip sign, and fitting pre-2008 to predict post-2010 gives \(R^2\) 0.305 against 0.523 in-sample. A within-window fit has no place in a mapping layer whose other rows are identities. The only real fix is adding average hours and population to the bloc, which requires re-estimating it.

For US_CMR14 (CMR14_NATIVE_MAP, driversDecomp.ts:489) the BVAR-side construction is identical, again all factor 1, and the units were pinned by fitting the model's own observation equations. The anchor is gdp_obs \(= \Delta\)output exactly for every non-trend shock, which fixes gdp_obs in percent quarterly log growth, the SW07 dy convention. The three growth observables then fit as consumption_obs \(= 0.6366\,\Delta c + 1.0\,\texttt{log\_muzstar}\), investment_obs \(= 1.2526\,\Delta i + 1.0\,\texttt{log\_muzstar}\) and wage_obs \(= 0.5647\,\Delta\tilde w + 1.0\,\texttt{log\_muzstar}\), each to within \(7\times10^{-14}\). Every one of them carries exactly the same 1.0 trend loading that the percent-anchored gdp_obs does, which is what places them in the same percent-quarterly-growth units; the \(\Delta\)-term factors are internal model-variable scalings and are irrelevant to the data side. wage_obs is the real wage — the two-term fit is exact with no separate inflation loading, and a price-markup shock raises inflation_obs while wage_obs falls. Hours are hours_obs \(= 0.01\,\texttt{lhours}\) exactly, the same 0.01 that links the percent common column to its level counterpart, so hours_obs is a percent level deviation and takes the labobs convention at factor 1.

CMR14's financial observables (credit_obs, networth_obs, premium_obs, Spread1_obs, pinvest_obs, RealRe_obs) are not mapped in this pass. There are no financial observables in the Drivers feature.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text:
The native mode needs the spec columns CH, JC, JGDP, FRH, FNH, LXBC and LANAGRA — seven since the dc and dinve corrections, which draw on JC and FRH respectively. Only the US bloc ships them all. On every other bloc the drawer runs at three observables, the naming budget is three, and the class view is unavailable.

A row assembled from several columns is withheld entirely if any one of them is missing, rather than being built from those present: a partial combination is a different series, not an approximation of the intended one.

docs.title: From observables to the main panel's display space
docs.text:
Contributions are drawn in the units of the panel the user is already reading. Each observable maps into display space through a linear operator, either a gain \(s\,v_t\) or a scaled first difference \(s\,(v_t - v_{t-1})\) with \(v_{-1} = 0\) (obsDisplaySpec and toDisplayDev, driversDecomp.ts:608–643):

Observable Operator Display unit output difference, scale 4 % q/q ann. inflationq gain, scale 1 (already \(4\Delta p\)) % q/q ann. interest gain, scale 1 % native difference-kind (dc, dinve, dw, consumption_obs, investment_obs, wage_obs) gain, scale 4 % q/q ann. native level-kind (labobs, hours_obs) difference, scale 4 % q/q ann.

Because the operator is linear, contributions and residual transform additively, so the stacked bars plus the residual plus the baseline reproduce the scenario line exactly. That identity is pinned to \(10^{-8}\) in the test suite, for per-shock bars and for aggregated class bars alike. Note that dw and wage_obs subtract the deflator column, so the displayed series is compensation growth minus deflator growth.

docs.title: The two licensed rules
docs.text: The validation bench states, in its own verdict block (simple_decomp_results.txt:19–20), the rules it licenses: "name at most as many shocks as observables watched; added observables (with ME) raise the budget; collinear shock pairs are flagged." Both are enforced in the shipped tool.

docs.title: Rule 1 — the naming budget
docs.text:
At \(q\) watched observables the user may name at most \(q\) shocks. The engine throws when \(K > q\) (driversDecomp.ts:236), and the interface disables every un-named chip once the budget is reached (DriversDrawer.tsx:1131). The budget is 3 + addedObs.length where the native mapping is available and 3 otherwise (DriversDrawer.tsx:519).

The rule comes from criterion (e) of the bench: SW07 at its native seven observables with all seven usable shocks is fully identified, rank 84/84, with noiseless recovery at \(3.6\times10^{-15}\) and 100% of contribution paths recovered at 1% noise.

Not every observable raises the budget. SW07's dy, pinfobs and robs, and CMR14's gdp_obs, inflation_obs and Re_obs, are excluded from the addable list because each is an invertible linear transform of an already-watched locked observable: dy is the difference of the output path, pinfobs is inflationq/4, robs is interest/4, and on the CMR14 side Re_obs is a constant \(0.2529\) times interest across all shocks and horizons. Adding one would raise the naming budget by one while buying no new rank, so the identification the budget rule promises would be fictitious. This is pinned against the data rather than against a curated list: a test requires each of the four legitimate SW07 addables to buy exactly \(H = 12\) units of new rank, and each of the three excluded transforms to buy exactly zero, alone and all three together.

docs.title: Rule 2 — the collinearity flag
docs.text:
Two shocks whose stacked response paths point in nearly the same direction cannot be told apart by the data being decomposed, however well-conditioned the system looks. The build step therefore computes \(\lvert\cos\rvert\) between every pair of unit-normalised stacked three-observable \(H = 12\) response paths, exactly as bench_simple_decomp.m:112–125 does, and ships every pair above 0.95 in the index (collinearThreshold). The drawer warns whenever both members of a flagged pair are named, quoting the measured \(\lvert\cos\rvert\) to two decimals.

The one-click "Use all" selection is greedy in the model's fixed shock order and skips any shock that forms a flagged pair with one already picked (useAllShockSelection, driversDecomp.ts:562). Hand-picking a collinear pair remains possible under Customize, with the warning shown.

The rationale is that near-collinear columns break same-model recovery through the validated engine. Concretely, the CMR14 trio e_sigma, e_gamma and e_zetai is mutually flagged (measured \(\lvert\cos\rvert\) of 0.998, 0.983 and 0.975); the shipped greedy seven-shock set, which keeps exactly one of them, recovers the generating sequence far inside the \(10^{-6}\) criterion the test suite pins it against, while freeing a budget slot for a second member can push the worst contribution-path error past that criterion by several orders of magnitude, depending on which member is added.

Remark 2 (Read a flagged pair jointly). Where a pair is flagged, the split of contributions between its two members is not identified — the solver is choosing among observationally equivalent splits by a norm criterion, not by evidence. The sum over the pair is meaningful; the division inside it is not. Keeping only one member of a collinear group is what preserves recovery, which is what the greedy default does.

docs.title: The class-view licence
docs.text: Grouping shocks into Monetary, Demand and Supply is what makes a decomposition readable, and it is also where a model-conditional exercise is easiest to over-sell. The tool therefore treats the class view as licensed at one configuration and greyed everywhere else.

docs.title: What the bench ran
docs.text:
bench_class_recovery.m ran five (model, observable-set) cells under two solvers, against two pre-stated criteria: (f1) the recovered class-total path correlates at least 0.95 with the true class-total path in at least 90% of active-class instances over 20 seeds; (f2) mean off-class leakage is at most 25%. Both must pass. The full results are committed in docs/paper/class_recovery_results.txt:

Model \(q\) Solver (f1) corr ≥ 0.95 (f2) off-class leakage Verdict US_SW07 3 raw 52% fail 32% fail fail US_SW07 3 colnorm 50% fail 5% pass fail US_SW07 7 raw 100% pass 0% pass pass US_SW07 7 colnorm 100% pass 0% pass pass US_CMR14 3 raw 58% fail 34% fail fail US_CMR14 3 colnorm 45% fail 32% fail fail US_CMR14 7 raw 87% fail 8% pass fail US_CMR14 7 colnorm 78% fail 3% pass fail US_FRB22_mcap 3 raw 20% fail 62% fail fail US_FRB22_mcap 3 colnorm 37% fail 47% fail fail

The shipped solver is the column-normalised one. Exactly one cell passes both gates under it: US_SW07 at the full extended seven-observable set, with a perfect diagonal attribution matrix — Monetary, Demand and Supply each recovered at 100% with 0% leakage.

The bench held all three coordinates fixed in that cell. Its observable set is \(\{\)output, inflationq, interest, dc, dinve, dw, labobs\(\}\) (bench_class_recovery.m:35) and its shock set is \(K = 7\), every usable column of SW07's class map.

docs.title: What the shipped code permits
docs.text:
classViewLicensed(model, observableKeys, namedShocks) → boolean

model is the index key of the selected lens, observableKeys the string array of watched observables, and namedShocks the string array of named shocks. The predicate (driversDecomp.ts:694–702) returns true only when the model is US_SW07, the observable keys contain all seven of the bench's set, and the named shocks contain all seven of interest_, eb, fiscal_, eqs, ea, epinf, ew. The drawer additionally requires that a class map exist for the model. The third argument is required, not optional, so a caller who forgets it gets a compile error rather than a silently wider licence.

As shipped, the set of configurations in which the code permits the class view and the set the bench licensed are the same set, on all three coordinates. The predicate is permissive only towards supersets — naming or watching more than the bench's seven still returns true — and neither is reachable through the interface, since SW07 exposes exactly seven usable shocks and exactly four addable observables.

Remark 3 (The licence has three coordinates, and un-naming revokes it). It is tempting to describe the class view as licensed "for SW07 at seven observables". That is wrong, and it was the defect the verification pass closed. If the user drops one shock under Customize, the licensed Monetary/Demand/Supply labels would otherwise survive on a split the bench never ran: the missing shock's energy is redistributed across the classes that remain, which is precisely the quantity the off-class-leakage criterion measures. The licence is a property of (model, watched observables, named shocks) jointly, and the Classes toggle greys out the moment any one of the three moves.

docs.title: Where the class view is and is not available
docs.text:
Model Class map shipped Class view available What the Groups view shows instead US_SW07 yes (7 members) yes, and only at 7 observables with all 7 shocks named textbook shock names US_CMR14 yes (9 members) no its own class map as an organising grouping of families US_FRB22 yes (54 members, via alias) no empirical collinearity clusters US_FRB22_var yes (54 members, via alias) no empirical collinearity clusters US_FRB22_mcap yes (54 members) no menu-hidden; kept for the licence fixtures US_FRB08 no no one series per named shock EA_SW03, EA_SWW14 no no one series per named shock CA_LS07, HK_FP13, BRA_SAMBA08, UK_SM11 no no one series per named shock

Because only the US bloc carries the five spec columns the native observables need, the licensed configuration is reachable on the US bloc only. Everywhere else the drawer runs at three observables and the Classes toggle is greyed, with the tooltip naming the reason and the results file.

The class maps themselves live in pipeline/_shockbench/class_maps.json and are copied verbatim into the shipped index at build time, so they are amended there and not in the app. SW07's map assigns interest_ to Monetary; eb, fiscal_ and eqs to Demand; and ea, epinf and ew to Supply. CMR14's adds a Financial class (e_sigma, e_gamma). The FRB/US map covers all 54 shocks by a rule on the equation each _aerr residual attaches to — 1 Monetary, 16 Demand, 20 Supply, 14 Financial and 3 Other — which is a mechanical assignment, not an economic judgement about the shock.

Remark 4 (CMR14's families are a grouping, not a licensed class split). For US_CMR14 the Groups view renders that model's own class map as "Monetary family", "Demand family", "Supply family" and "Financial family". This is an organising device for nine shocks, not a class decomposition with a licence behind it: the bench recovers those class totals in 78% of test instances against its 90% bar, at 3% off-class leakage. The drawer shows that number verbatim wherever the families appear, and any document describing them should do the same.

docs.title: The model menu
docs.text:
The index ships twelve lenses. K is the number of usable shocks — those with all three common observables present and a stacked \(H = 12\) response norm of at least \(10^{-9}\) — and the rank and regime shown are for the default three-observable configuration.

Index key \(K\) Dropped Flagged pairs (\(\lvert\cos\rvert > 0.95\)) Rank / regime at 3 observables US_SW07 7 em (zero response) none 36/36, exact-fit US_CMR14 9 e_term (zero response) 3: e_sigma~e_gamma 0.998, e_gamma~e_zetai 0.983, e_sigma~e_zetai 0.975 36/36, exact-fit US_FRB08 2 none none 24/36, residual-able US_FRB22 54 none 109 36/36, exact-fit (3 clusters named) US_FRB22_var 54 none 117 36/36, exact-fit (3 clusters named) EA_SW03 6 none 1: fiscal_~inv_ 0.963 36/36, exact-fit EA_SWW14 6 none none 36/36, exact-fit CA_LS07 3 none 1: markup_~flex_ 0.975 24/36, residual-able HK_FP13 5 none 2: interest_~flex_ 1.000, markup_~demand_ 0.960 36/36, exact-fit BRA_SAMBA08 4 none none 36/36, exact-fit UK_SM11 3 none none 36/36, exact-fit US_FRB22_mcap 2 none none menu-hidden

CA_LS07 is residual-able for a substantive reason: two of its three usable shocks are near-duplicates in the three common observables, so its response columns span only 24 of the 36 stacked rows however many of them are named. The greedy default names two, and naming the third would buy no rank. US_FRB08 exposes only a monetary and a fiscal shock, so it is residual-able at any configuration.

The menu is grouped by relevance to the bloc on screen (DriversDrawer.tsx:137–148): "Own country" first (US to the five US lenses, EA to SW03 and SWW14, CA to LS07, HK to FP13, BR to SAMBA08, UK to SM11), then "Reference" (the US SW07/CMR14 pair where they are not already own-country), then "Other". The choice is remembered per bloc in localStorage under gmaps-drivers-model:<bloc>.

docs.title: The FRB/US census lenses
docs.text:
The two 54-shock FRB/US lenses are handled differently from every other model, for two independent reasons. First, the class view is refused for FRB/US by the bench at the only observable set it can run at: at three observables both solvers fail both gates. There is no seven-observable FRB/US configuration, because the native observable mapping exists only for SW07 and CMR14. Second, the individual _aerr equation-residual shocks are not separable in the three common observables in the first place: 109 of the 1,431 shock pairs exceed \(\lvert\cos\rvert = 0.95\) for US_FRB22, and 117 for the VAR-expectations variant. The drawer therefore groups by the structure the response space actually has, rather than by the economics of the equations.

Clusters are connected components of the \(\lvert\cos\rvert > 0.95\) graph, formed by union-find over the shipped pair list (build_drivers_index.mjs:124, mirrored app-side by connectedComponents, driversDecomp.ts:746). Each cluster is labelled by its largest member's equation name — largest stacked three-observable \(H = 12\) response norm, equation being the mnemonic minus the _aerr suffix — and clusters are ordered by size descending, then id ascending. US_FRB22 partitions its 54 shocks into 23 clusters, the largest being hqlfpr with 17 members (the financial/housing blob, which contains fiscal_, so the fiscal shock is not separately nameable in cluster mode), eco_l with 10 (the spending block) and lww_l with 4 (wages, labour force, ECI), followed by three pairs and 17 singletons — among them interest_. US_FRB22_var partitions into 21 clusters, with hqlfpr at 18, eco_l at 10, lww_l at 4, trci at 3, two pairs and 15 singletons.

Remark 5 (Cluster members are chained, not mutually parallel). Collinearity is not transitive. A connected component of the \(\lvert\cos\rvert > 0.95\) graph links its members through a chain of pairwise-collinear edges, so two members of the same cluster can sit well below the threshold against each other. A cluster is therefore not a bundle of near-identical shocks, and the composite column used to represent it is a genuine first principal component of the member set rather than a proxy for an already-parallel bundle. The drawer says this in three places, and it is the wording to mirror.

Naming a cluster names exactly one column. clusterCompositeIRF (driversDecomp.ts:780) builds the first principal component of the members' unit-normalised stacked three-observable \(H = 12\) paths, by 200 power iterations seeded from the largest-norm member, unit-normalised, with the sign fixed by a positive projection on that member. The budget therefore counts clusters, not members: three clusters at three observables, whatever their membership.

Most cluster triples are not usable, and rank does not tell the user which. pickDefaultNamed (build_drivers_index.mjs:363) scans every possible triple through the shipped solver over 20 sparse truth seeds (a deterministic generator, seed 20260806) against the \(10^{-6}\) criterion. Of 1,771 possible triples for US_FRB22, 123 pass; of 1,330 for US_FRB22_var, 122. The builder then picks deterministically among the passers, maximising total member coverage, preferring a triple that contains the interest_ cluster, and breaking ties by shipped cluster order. That yields [hqlfpr, interest_, pcer_l] for US_FRB22, covering 19 of 54 shocks at a measured worst recovery error of \(2.5\times10^{-9}\), and [eco_l, interest_, ki_l] for US_FRB22_var, covering 12 of 54 at \(1.3\times10^{-7}\) — passing, but only an order of magnitude inside the criterion. The drawer warns whenever the user departs from the shipped default naming, because a full-rank \(\Theta\) is not evidence that a triple is usable: the top-three-by-size triple hqlfpr/eco_l/lww_l is full-rank and still fails the recovery criterion by orders of magnitude.

Under Customize there is an "Experimental: raw shocks" fold that decomposes individual _aerr shocks instead of clusters. The chip list is the greedy non-collinear selection: 26 of 54 for US_FRB22 and 25 of 54 for US_FRB22_var. The budget still binds, so at three observables only three of them can be named.

docs.title: Working with the drawer
docs.text:
The Drivers button, carrying an amber exp badge, sits in the scenario-action cluster of the chart grid (ChartGrid.tsx:3868) and appears only once there is something to decompose — that is, when any displayed, isolated or coupled scenario deviation, or an active external-forecast combination, has an entry exceeding \(10^{-9}\) in absolute value. The drawer is a fixed right-side overlay 480 px wide, closed by its × or by Escape, and it does not solve while closed.

Example 1 (Reading a US scenario through the SW07 lens, default settings). We open Drivers on the US bloc with a scenario already displayed and change nothing. The drawer selects US_SW07, watches all seven observables — the three locked common ones plus Consumption (Δ), Investment (Δ), Real wage (Δ) and Hours (level) — and names all seven usable shocks. Because that is exactly the licensed configuration, the [Classes | Groups] toggle sits on Classes and the chart shows three stacked series, Monetary, Demand and Supply, plus a grey Residual, drawn as contribution bars anchored on the baseline path with the scenario line on top. The observable shown is Output, in % q/q ann.; a horizontal 100% shares strip sits underneath.
