docs.title: Feasibility report — extending GMAPS's foreign block toward the CCFH 6-counterpart mirror
docs.text: Date: 2026-07-19 · Status: exploration only, NOT implemented · Scope: whether GMAPS could add the foreign (weakly-exogenous) counterparts that Crespo Cuaresma, Feldkircher & Huber (2016, JAE) carry, and at what coverage/cost.

docs.title: 1. The gap
docs.text:
CCFH give each country a near-full foreign mirror (their eq. 4.2): x*ᵢₜ = (y*, Δp*, eq*, i_s*, i_l*, tc*) — trade-weighted foreign counterparts of six of their seven domestic variables (output, inflation, real equity, short rate, long rate, total credit; the real exchange rate is the one variable not mirrored) — plus oil as a global control.

GMAPS carries only three trade-weighted stars — ROWDEM (≈ y*), ROWINF (≈ Δp*), ROWFIN (≈ i_s*) — and routes financial linkage through four US-originated global commons (oil, US 10y GLB_USLR, US Baa GLB_USBAA, US equity GLB_USEQ) that every bloc carries directly rather than as trade-weighted aggregates.

So GMAPS already has 3 of CCFH's 6 (output, inflation, short rate). The candidates to add are the three foreign financials: eq* (foreign equity), i_l* (foreign long rate), tc* (foreign total credit).

docs.title: 2. Coverage — the domestic base each foreign star would average over
docs.text:
A foreign star for variable X is a trade-weighted average of partners' domestic X, so it is only well-defined where partners actually carry X. Scanning all 55 served blocs:

CCFH counterpart domestic coverage verdict y* (output) 55/55 (100%) already carried (ROWDEM) Δp* (inflation) 55/55 (100%) already carried (ROWINF) i_s* (short rate) 54/55 (98%) already carried (ROWFIN) tc* (total credit) 52/55 (95%) viable — strong candidate i_l* (long rate) 39/55 (71%) partial — thin for EMs, redundant with GLB_USLR eq* (equity) 4/55 (7%) not viable without a large data build

(Aggregate coverage is a first-order proxy: what matters per bloc is whether its main trade partners carry the variable. It is close enough to rank the candidates; the trade-weighted per-bloc version is a verification item in §5.)

docs.title: tc* — foreign total credit — RECOMMENDED
docs.text:
• 95% coverage (52/55). Missing only PH, RO, US (US carries LEV, a leverage proxy, not a CREDIT_GDP_US level; PH/RO have none). The two-year credit-block expansion put CREDIT_GDP_* on nearly every bloc, so the base is there.
  • No redundancy. GMAPS has no global credit common, so a foreign-credit star adds a genuinely new cross-border credit channel — not a re-aggregation of an existing series.
  • Matches CCFH's own motivation. Total credit (domestic and cross-border) is exactly the variable CCFH add beyond the classical GVAR set "as an important transmission channel of international shocks," and they flag it as decisive over their crisis hold-out. It is the single most defensible extension.
  • One new star.

docs.title: i_l* — foreign long rate — DEFER
docs.text:
• 71% coverage (39/55): YIELD10_* for the AEs and euro members; missing 16 (most EMs, the CH/NO/SG financial hubs, and the US — whose long rate is the common GLB_USLR, not a domestic YIELD10_US).
  • Partly redundant with GLB_USLR. Because the US long rate already reaches every bloc as a common, a foreign-long-rate star would re-introduce the US 10y (via the US weight) alongside the commons, risking collinearity; its genuinely new content is the non-US partners' long rates.
  • Thin where it is needed most. For EM-heavy blocs whose partners lack YIELD10, the star would be US-dominated or sparse. Marginal gain for real cost.

docs.title: eq* — foreign equity — NOT VIABLE (as-is)
docs.text:
• 7% coverage (only CN, HK, PE, SG carry a domestic equity index; US equity is the common GLB_USEQ, SP500VOL is a volatility series, not a level).
  • Building a real foreign-equity star would first require sourcing ~50 domestic equity indices — a large data effort — and even then it would largely duplicate GLB_USEQ for the many blocs whose only equity signal is the US common. Not recommended without a separate equity-data workstream, and even then of questionable value given the common already carries the dominant global equity factor.

docs.title: 4. Cost of adding a star (system-wide)
docs.text:
Adding foreign counterparts is not a data-only change — each new star is an endogenous column in every bloc's VARX* and enlarges the coupled state.

  • Coupling dimension grows as N·k·H + 4H with N=38 coupled blocs, H=20, k = #stars. Today k=3 → 2,360.
  • +tc* (k=4): 3,120 (+32%)
  • +tc*+i_l* (k=5): 3,880 (+64%)
  • Pre-computed (I−M)⁻¹ (the shipped operator behind the ~1-second browser solve) scales ≈ O(dim³): the in-browser/precompute step (already ~19 min at dim 2,360, which is why it is pre-shipped) becomes ≈2.3× slower with tc*, ≈4.4× slower with both. Still a one-off, offline cost, but non-trivial.
  • Estimation. Each bloc's VARX* gains 1–2 star regressors. CCFH argue this is fine under shrinkage ("reasonable to include a large set … to avoid ad-hoc restrictions, even for … the US"), and GMAPS's Minnesota-type prior would absorb them the same way — but it still requires a full-system re-estimation (export_bvar_gvar24_loop.m), a coupling-artifact regen, and a shift back to the current quarter.
  • Design tension. GMAPS's sparse-stars-plus-US-commons choice is deliberate (now documented in §2 of the paper). Adding foreign financials (i_l*, eq*) partly duplicates the US commons; adding foreign credit (tc*) does not — which is the cleanest reason to treat tc* differently from the other two.

docs.title: 5. What to verify before implementing (open items)
docs.text:
1. US contribution to tc* — decide whether US enters the foreign-credit star via LEV, a re-sourced CREDIT_GDP_US, or is dropped from the average (the completed-panel star build must handle PH/RO/US).
  2. Trade-weighted per-bloc coverage — recompute coverage weighted by each bloc's trade shares (not just the aggregate) to confirm tc* is well-defined for every bloc's main partners, and to size how thin i_l* really is for the EM blocs.
  3. Weights choice — CCFH use bilateral-trade weights for all foreign variables but note (citing Eickmeier–Ng) that financial weights (portfolio/credit flows) may be better for financial variables; decide whether tc* should use trade or credit-flow weights.
  4. Collinearity of i_l* with GLB_USLR — if pursued, test empirically whether the foreign long-rate star adds signal beyond the common or merely reintroduces it.
  5. Sequencing — a foreign-counterpart addition is a full-system re-estimation; it should be combined with the JP/KR/TR/TW NEER re-estimation already under way, not run as a second pass.

docs.title: 6. Recommendation
docs.text:
• Add tc* (foreign total credit) — 95% coverage, no redundancy with the existing commons, matches CCFH's headline extension, one new star, and it is the addition with the clearest economic payoff (a cross-border credit channel GMAPS presently lacks). Fold it into the pending re-estimation.
  • Hold i_l* (foreign long rate) — feasible at 71% but partly redundant with GLB_USLR and thin for EMs; low priority, and only worth it if item 4 shows real incremental signal.
  • Do not add eq* (foreign equity) — 7% coverage; would need a ~50-bloc equity-sourcing workstream and would still largely duplicate GLB_USEQ.

One-line answer: the only CCFH foreign counterpart GMAPS can add cleanly today is foreign total credit (tc*, 95% coverage, no overlap with the US commons); the foreign long rate is thin and partly redundant, and foreign equity is infeasible without a large new data build and would duplicate the US equity common.

docs.title: 7. UPDATE — DBnomics / OECD pull: the missing series ARE sourceable
docs.text:
Ran the pull (DBnomics with the provided key, then the live OECD SDMX). This supersedes the "eq* not viable" verdict of §3.

Equity (eq*). OECD share prices (SPASTT01, "Share prices" index) cover 44 of the 51 blocs that lack a domestic equity series — DE, FR, JP, AU, BR, IN, ZA, KR, MX, and 35 more. Combined with the 4 already carried (CN, HK, PE, SG), that is 48/55 (87%). Still missing after the pull: AR, EA, MY, PH, SA, TH, TW (EA is an aggregate obtainable from its members).

Long rate (i_l*). OECD long-term rates (IRLTLT01/measure IRLT) cover 10 of the 16 missing — BR, CH, CN, CR, ID, IL, IS, NO, RU, US-as-common. With the 39 already carried, that is 49/55 (89%). Still missing: AR, MY, PH, SA, SG, TR.

Credit (tc*). Unchanged: 52/55, missing only PH, RO, US.

Currency. The DBnomics OECD/MEI mirror is frozen at ~2024-01 (OECD deprecated MEI), so it is a history source only. Current data comes from the new OECD SDMX (sdmx.oecd.org), verified serving 2026 data. The pipeline already uses this exact host for long rates (fetch_oecd_irlt.py).

Correction (2026-07-19, from the build): the equity index level the star needs is NOT in DSD_KEI@DF_KEI — that dataflow serves SHARE only as growth rates. The share-price index level lives in OECD.SDD.STES,DSD_STES@DF_FINMARK,4.0 (SHARE, UNIT=IX), which also carries IRLT (long rate). Both verified live-current (e.g. JPN 2026-06). The euro area resolves directly as the EA20 aggregate — no member-aggregation needed. This is the dataflow the large-model build actually used.

Revised coverage of the full 6-counterpart mirror:

counterpart now after OECD pull y*, Δp*, i_s* 100 / 100 / 98% (have) tc* credit 95% 95% i_l* long rate 71% 89% eq* equity 7% 87%

The persistent gaps — blocs still missing a financial after the pull — are the usual thin EMs/hubs: AR, MY, PH, SA miss both equity and long rate; TH, TW miss equity; SG, TR miss long rate; EA needs member-aggregation. This is the same coverage frontier CCFH themselves hit: they report >80% coverage for all variables except long-term rates, "missing for emerging markets with underdeveloped capital markets." So GMAPS at ~87–89% would match, not lag, the comparable.

Cost, all 3 new stars (6-counterpart mirror). Coupling dimension 38·6·20 + 4·20 = 4{,}640 — from 2,360, so ≈2× the dimension and ≈8× the (I−M)⁻¹ precompute (O(dim³)). One-off, offline; still material.

docs.title: 8. Revised recommendation
docs.text:
Covering all six is feasible — the data exists for ~87–89% of blocs from a source the pipeline already uses, matching CCFH's own coverage. Concretely:

  1. tc* (credit) — add first, cleanest (95%, no redundancy, matches CCFH's headline extension).
  2. eq* (equity) — now viable via OECD SHARE; the biggest step toward parity with CCFH. Note it will partly co-move with GLB_USEQ, but a trade-weighted foreign equity aggregate is genuinely distinct from the single US equity common.
  3. i_l* (long rate) — viable via OECD IRLT; weigh against its overlap with GLB_USLR (a foreign long-rate star mostly adds the non-US partners' yields).
  4. Leave AR/MY/PH/SA/TH/TW/SG financials thin (same as CCFH's EM gaps); handle EA by member-aggregation.

Sequencing: all six stars is a full-system re-estimation and a ~2× coupling dimension. It should be one combined pass with the JP/KR/TR/TW NEER re-estimation currently running — not a third re-estimation. The data-sourcing (OECD SHARE/IRLT for the ~54 findable series) can proceed in parallel and offline now.

docs.title: FSAP-expansion feasibility — data-availability audit (6 candidate blocs + 4 cross-cutting workstreams)
docs.text:
Purpose. Move the tool toward full FSAP surveillance coverage — the IMF's Financial Sector Assessment Program roster of 32 mandatory-every-5-years + 15 mandatory-every-10-years = 47 jurisdictions. The deployed model carries 50 economies today, of which 41 of the 47 FSAP jurisdictions are already covered. This audit sources the remaining named gaps and the cross-cutting data a global-solve FSAP tool needs (time-varying trade weights, complete NEER, complete exports/imports, and an external-balance / NFA satellite for every bloc). Requested and sourced 2026-07-17. Ingredients verified by live API fetch; the no-synthetic-data rule applies throughout — annual-only real GDP is not interpolated to quarterly, ragged edges are kept, nothing is back-filled.

Everything in this document is STAGED, not integrated. All artifacts live under pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/ and no panel (DataRaw_<CC>_glob.json), spec, app/, app/public/, or .m/.ts/.py production file has been touched. This is a sourced-and-staged plan: the series exist on disk and are validated, but no re-estimation into the model has run. Building any of it is gated on the parked decisions in §8 and a single combined re-estimation.

docs.title: 1. FSAP coverage goal and the six gap targets
docs.text:
FSAP roster 32 five-year + 15 ten-year = 47 jurisdictions Currently in the tool 50 economies deployed; 41 of the 47 FSAP jurisdictions covered Named gap targets sourced this session HK, SG, PE, PH, RO (candidate new blocs) + AE Verdict 5 of 6 VIABLE (HK SG RO PE PH); AE NOT VIABLE (annual-only real GDP)

Sourcing 5 of the 6 (all but AE) would take FSAP-jurisdiction coverage from 41 toward 46 of 47. AE cannot be built to the tool's standard from the approved APIs (see §2, AE) and is deferred, not faked.

docs.title: 2. New candidate blocs — per-bloc verdict
docs.text:
Real-GDP is the binding ingredient: a bloc is VIABLE only with a genuine quarterly real-GDP series (the panel's GDP_<CC> anchor). Verified spans below are read from the staged pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/newblocs/<CC>/GDP_<CC>.json (source/dates/values), with the core-block companions in the same folder and X/M in pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/trade/.

Bloc Verdict Real-GDP source Span (q) Core-block gaps Notes HK FULL VIABLE HK C&SD Table 310-31007 (SA, chained-2024 HK$m) 1990Q1–2026Q1 (145) none material 10Y yield short (2010Q1–2024Q4) SG FULL VIABLE SingStat Table M015662 (SA, chained-2015 S$m) 1975Q1–2026Q1 (205) no policy rate / no 10Y ER-regime economy — NEER is the instrument RO FULL Eurostat namq_10_gdp Q.CLV20_MNAC.SCA.B1GQ.RO 1995Q1–2026Q1 (125) none Eurostat drop-in, exactly like PL/HU/CZ PE FULL BCRP series PN02538AQ (real, S/ 2007, NSA) 1990Q1–2026Q1 (145) none NSA expenditure block → seasonal-dummy candidate PH FULL core PSA OpenSTAT SANA 012B5BEXS1 (SA, constant-2018) 2000Q1–2026Q1 (105) no 10Y yield, no credit needs a yield + credit tail before a full financial block AE NOT VIABLE WB WDI NY.GDP.MKTP.KN — ANNUAL only 1970–2024 (annual) quarterly real GDP absent quarterly is current-price only; no interpolation permitted

docs.title: HK — Hong Kong SAR (FULL VIABLE)
docs.text: Genuine quarterly real GDP from the Census & Statistics Department (Table 310-31007, seasonally adjusted, chained-2024 dollars), 1990Q1–2026Q1 (145 q) — newblocs/HK/GDP_HK.json. Companions staged: CPI, equity (EQ), house prices (HP), a 3-month HIBOR policy proxy (RATE_HK, HKMA, 1996Q3–2026Q2), a 10-year benchmark yield (YIELD10_HK, HKMA, 2010Q1–2024Q4, 60 q — short and ending 2024Q4, flag), and BIS credit-to-private-sector (CREDIT_HK, 1990Q4–2025Q4). Exports/imports are staged in trade/EXP_HK.json / trade/IMP_HK.json (C&SD Table 310-31003, chained volumes, 1973Q1–2026Q1, 213 q). Verdict: FULL VIABLE — a complete real+financial core; the only caveat is the shorter, 2024Q4-ending 10Y yield tail.

docs.title: SG — Singapore (FULL VIABLE)
docs.text: Genuine quarterly real GDP from SingStat (Table M015662, SA, chained-2015 dollars), 1975Q1–2026Q1 (205 q) — the longest history of the six (newblocs/SG/GDP_SG.json). Companions: CPI, equity, house prices, BIS credit level + credit/GDP (CREDIT_SG, CREDIT_GDP_SG). Exports/imports staged in trade/EXP_SG.json / trade/IMP_SG.json (SingStat M014812, chained volumes, 1975Q1–2026Q1, 205 q). Structural note: Singapore runs an exchange-rate-centred monetary regime — there is no conventional policy rate or 10Y benchmark to source, and none is staged (RATE_SG/YIELD10_SG intentionally absent). The exchange rate is the policy instrument, so the staged NEER_SG carries the monetary channel. Verdict: FULL VIABLE, with the FX-regime treatment declared.

docs.title: RO — Romania (FULL)
docs.text: Eurostat drop-in, identical machinery to the existing PL/HU/CZ blocs. Real GDP from namq_10_gdp key Q.CLV20_MNAC.SCA.B1GQ.RO (chain-linked vol. ref-2020, RON, seasonally + calendar adjusted), 1995Q1–2026Q1 (125 q) — newblocs/RO/GDP_RO.json, built by newblocs/RO/build_RO.py (Eurostat SDMX + BIS). Full companion set: HICP (CPI_RO), 10Y Maastricht yield (YIELD10_RO), gross debt/GDP (DEBT_GDP_RO), consumption/investment/government (CONS/INV/GOV), house prices, policy rate, and EXP/IMP. Verdict: FULL — no new provider, no seasonal seam (SCA), slots straight into the Eurostat pipeline.

docs.title: PE — Peru (FULL)
docs.text: Real national accounts from BCRP (series PN02538AQ, PBI por tipo de gasto, millones S/ 2007), 1990Q1–2026Q1 (145 q) — newblocs/PE/GDP_PE.json, built by newblocs/PE/build_PE.py (BCRP API + BIS). Full companion set including 10Y yield (YIELD10_PE), credit (CREDIT_PE), equity, CPI (IPC), consumption/investment/government, house prices, policy rate, and EXP/IMP. Seasonality caveat (per the build docstring): the BCRP expenditure block is the raw, non-seasonally-adjusted national-accounts series — BCRP publishes a desestacionalizado PBI total but no SA expenditure decomposition — so PE's real block is a seasonal-dummy candidate under the tool's seasonal machinery. Verdict: FULL, with the NSA flag.

docs.title: PH — Philippines (FULL core; needs a financial tail)
docs.text: Genuine quarterly SA real GDP from the PSA OpenSTAT SANA table 012B5BEXS1 (constant-2018 prices, seasonally adjusted), 2000Q1–2026Q1 (105 q) — newblocs/PH/GDP_PH.json, built by newblocs/PH/build_PH.py (PSA PxWeb + BIS). Staged companions: CPI (three era-partitioned PSA sub-tables on one 2018=100 base — a concatenation of identical-base official series, not fabrication), consumption/investment/government, house prices, policy rate, and EXP/IMP. Missing for a full financial block: a 10Y benchmark yield and a credit series — neither YIELD10_PH nor CREDIT_PH is staged. Verdict: FULL core (real + price + FX + rate), but a yield + credit tail must be sourced before PH matches the financial depth of the other blocs.

docs.title: AE — United Arab Emirates (NOT VIABLE)
docs.text: The UAE has no genuine quarterly real GDP. Only annual constant-price GDP exists (World Bank WDI NY.GDP.MKTP.KN, AED, 1970–2024) — staged for provenance only as newblocs/AE/GDP_AE_ANNUAL_reference.json, explicitly not a panel input. Quarterly UAE GDP is published only at current prices (nominal), which cannot serve as a real-activity anchor, and the no-synthetic-data rule forbids interpolating the annual real series to quarterly. NEER_AE was still sourced (BIS, in neer/) but is moot without a real anchor. Verdict: NOT VIABLE as a bloc from the approved APIs; revisit only if a national-source quarterly real GDP (e.g. UAE Federal Competitiveness & Statistics Centre) is authorised.

docs.title: 3. Time-varying trade weights + the honest CN/EA trajectory finding
docs.text:
The GVAR couples blocs through a bilateral trade-weight matrix. Today the solve uses a single static weights_full.json; FSAP surveillance wants the weights to reflect the decade of the shock, not one frozen year. weights/build_weights_timevarying.py reconstructs the full per-year weight panel from IMF IMTS, following the tool's own recipe verbatim (endpoint api.imf.org/external/sdmx/2.1/data/IMF.STA,IMTS,1.0.0/, key order COUNTRY.INDICATOR.COUNTERPART_COUNTRY.A, indicators XG_FOB_USD + MG_CIF_USD, euro area = G163 aggregate, same <0.05%-share drop + renormalize + 6-dp residual-adjust rule as the static file).

  • Scope: the 33 currently-coupled blocs + the 6 FSAP candidates = 39 reporters, annual 1995–2024 (weights/build_weights_timevarying.py, BLOC_CODES).
  • Outputs (staged): weights/weights_timevarying.json (every year 1995–2024), weights/weights_latest.json (2024, the solve-time default candidate), weights/weights_validation.json. Raw SDMX cached per reporter in weights/raw/imts_<CC>.xml.
  • Integrity: all 30 years × 39 rows sum to 1 within 1e-6 (row_sums_all_pass_1e-6: true; max deviation after residual-adjust 1.1e-16); no omitted reporter-years (omitted_rows: {}); RU/TW partner-side mirror fallback only, no fabrication or carry-forward.

The honest CN/EA trajectory finding. The build's a-priori monotonicity hypotheses (US→CN rising, US→EA falling, EA→CN rising over 1995–2024) all returned false — and on inspection these are genuine data features, not bugs (weights_validation.json → trajectory_findings):

US-row weight 1995 trajectory 2024 → CN 4.75% rises to a 17.6% peak in 2017, then falls after the 2018 trade war 11.9% → EA 15.2% roughly flat ~15% (2012 min 14.2%), then RISES — the data does not show a falling EA share 17.8% EA → CN 3.4% rises to a 14.0% peak in 2020/21, then eases 12.9%

The key correction: the post-2018 decline in the US import basket is all China, not Europe — the US→EA share actually rose to 17.8% by 2024. A static-2024 weight matrix would bake in the post-decoupling China share; a trailing-average or as-of-shock-year matrix would look very different mid-2000s. This is exactly why the year of the solve-time weights is a parked decision (§8).

docs.title: 4. NEER coverage completion
docs.text:
neer/build_neer.py pulls BIS broad nominal effective exchange rates (WS_EER, key M.N.B.<CC>), quarterly-averages the monthly index over complete quarters only (all 3 months observed — no partial-quarter averages), and writes one neer/NEER_<CC>.json per bloc. Genuine data only: where a live panel exists the series is truncated to the panel's own quarterly grid span, never extended or padded.

  • Gaps filled (existing blocs that lacked a nominal EER): US, JP, KR, TR, TW, and CN (the CN panel carried only REER_CN — a nominal EER is added). Each truncated to its panel span.
  • Candidates: HK, SG, PE, PH, RO, AE — no panel yet, so the full genuine BIS span is kept.
  • Staged: neer/NEER_{US,JP,KR,TR,TW,CN,HK,SG,PE,PH,RO,AE}.json (12 files). Example: NEER_JP.json = BIS broad nominal, 2000Q1–2025Q4 (104 q). This closes NEER coverage for every gap bloc and every viable candidate; NEER also feeds the NFA valuation term (§6).

docs.title: 5. Exports / imports coverage (the RU-IMP gap)
docs.text:
Audited in trade/COVERAGE_AUDIT.md. X/M is effectively complete for every viable bloc:

  • 49 of 50 coupled blocs ALREADY carry real EXP_<CC>/IMP_<CC> (or XH/MH for the US) in the shipped panels — no sourcing needed.
  • The one gap: RU has EXP but no IMP (a sanctions-era ragged edge; the genuine RU import mirror trade/IMP_RU.json sourced here — FRED/OECD QNA NAEXKP07RUQ661S — ends 2021Q3, which is itself the evidence behind the RU keep/drop question in §8).
  • Candidates: EXP/IMP staged for HK, SG, PE, PH, RO (trade/EXP_*.json, trade/IMP_*.json; PE/PH/RO also carry their own copies inside newblocs/<CC>/). AE not staged — moot, since AE is not a viable bloc.

Net: X/M coverage is complete for all five viable candidates and all existing blocs; the only open item is RU IMP, tied to the RU keep/drop decision.

docs.title: 6. NFA / external-balance extension
docs.text: Goal: extend the shipped balance-of-payments satellite from the 3 live blocs (US, EA, CN) to the full 50-bloc GVAR + the FSAP candidates, mirroring the fiscal block's division of labour (the BVAR forecasts the flow; the stock is an accounting recursion). Design + sourcing in nfa/DESIGN.md.

docs.title: 6.1 What the shipped recursion consumes (ground truth)
docs.text:
computeExternalBlock() in app/src/lib/compute/externalAccounting.ts is a side-effect-free per-quarter recursion that reads 5 estimated LEVEL-space drivers — exports, imports, gdp, deflator, fx (positional idx into the forecast path) — and 3 anchor constants from external_meta.json: nfa0 (sourced net-IIP/GDP seed), iNFA (imputed NFA return, modeling default 3 %/yr), fxShare (FX-exposed share, default 0.4). The identity, per quarter, seeded b_{-1}=nfa0:

tb_t  = 100·(X_t − M_t)/Y_t
ca_t  = tb_t + iNFA·b_{t-1}/100            # income leg IMPUTED
val_t = −fxShare·b_{t-1}·Δℓ^fx_t/100       # FX revaluation
b_t   = b_{t-1}/(1 + gⁿ_t) + ca_t/4 + val_t

So today the trade balance is derived from estimated real trade volumes and the income leg is imputed, not sourced. That carries two costs: (i) tb is a real-volume/real-GDP ratio, not the nominal customs CA; (ii) the units landmine — X, M, Y must share one nominal scale, which holds for US/EA but fails for essentially every EM bloc (it forced CN's bespoke units.* reconciliation). JP, UK, CA were held out only because their IIP was "not yet verified."

docs.title: 6.2 IMF-IIP unblocks JP/UK/CA (and 48 more)
docs.text:
The IIP blocker is now removed. IMF IIP delivers a quarterly net-IIP anchor (SDMX IMF.STA,IIP/{ISO3}.NETAL_P.NIIP.USD.Q) for JP/UK/CA and dozens of others, and IMF BOP delivers a quarterly current account (IMF.STA,BOP/{ISO3}.NETCD_T.CAB.USD.Q). Sourced this task (nfa/build_nfa_external.py, IMF + World Bank, no key):

  • nfa/CA_<CC>.json (53 blocs) — quarterly current account, full-history USD level (values_usd, genuine IMF, ragged edge kept) plus CA as %GDP annualised (values = 400·CABq / WB annual GDP NY.GDP.MKTP.CD; null where a year has no WB GDP — no interpolation).
  • nfa/nfa_anchors.json (54 blocs) — the nfa0 seed, 100·netIIP(USD)/annual nominal GDP(USD); US/EA/CN keep their shipped-live values with the IMF/WB recompute recorded as a cross-check.

Sign/magnitude validation (all genuine): US −66.75, JP +79 (largest creditor), CH +117, NO +377 (SWF), SG +181, HK +587 (financial entrepôt), GR −136 / IE −60 / PT −52 / ES −47 (periphery), CN +20.4 (matches shipped +20.35). CA flows: US −2.5…−3.9%, GR −11%, RU +2.3%, MY +1.6% — all correct-signed.

docs.title: 6.3 Feasibility split (nfa/DESIGN.md §5)
docs.text:
• FULL — 54 blocs (quarterly IMF CA + IMF/ECB net-IIP anchor): the 3 live (US/EA/CN) + 51 new, incl. JP/UK/CA (the previously-held-out three) and FSAP candidates HK PE PH RO SG. Ragged edges respected under the GVAR uniform-cutoff rule (e.g. IE CA ends 2025Q1, MY 2024Q4).
  • PARTIAL — 1: AE — IMF BOP has annual CA only, no quarterly CA and no IIP; ships without an external block (like JP/UK/CA did), no annual→quarterly back-fill.
  • NOT-FEASIBLE — 1: TW — absent from IMF BOP/IIP entirely (and WB GDP); a national CBC/DGBAS pull is outside the approved APIs; ships without an external block, no fabrication.

docs.title: 6.4 Design recommendation — Option B (estimate the CA share)
docs.text:
Two ways to wire NFA into the model (nfa/DESIGN.md §3):

  • Option A (status quo): keep tb = 100·(X−M)/Y + imputed income. Requires a CN-style per-bloc units reconciliation for every non-common-scale (EM) bloc; the TB stays a real-volume proxy and iNFA stays imputed.
  • Option B (RECOMMENDED, fiscal-mirror): add an estimated panel column CA_GDP_<CC> (current account, %GDP, quarterly) exactly as FREV_GDP/FPEXP_GDP are estimated in the fiscal block, then roll only the stock: b_t = b_{t-1}/(1+gⁿ_t) + ca_t/4 + val_t, seeded at nfa0. Why B: (1) it mirrors the requested fiscal division of labour (estimate the flow share, derive the stock); (2) it uses the genuine nominal BoP current account (income + transfers in the data) so iNFA is retired — no imputed return, no double-count; (3) CA/GDP is unit-free, so the CN units reconciliation is unnecessary and one uniform recipe covers all 54 feasible blocs; (4) the trade agent's X/M still feed the BVAR as drivers but are no longer load-bearing for NFA. fxShare = 0.4 remains a flagged default for the valuation leg only.

Building Option B needs (app-team, out of scope here): a new CA_GDP_<CC> panel column per feasible bloc, a one-branch change in externalAccounting.ts to accept an estimated ca path (skip the volume-TB + imputed-income branch when a caIdx is present), and a re-estimation. NFA adds no cross-bloc coupling (passive per-bloc recursion) → no coupling-cache regen, orthogonal to the GVAR solve, exactly like the fiscal block.

docs.title: 7. Consolidated verdict
docs.text:
Workstream Status Staged under pipeline/fsap_expansion_staging/ New blocs 5 VIABLE (HK SG RO PE PH) · 1 NOT VIABLE (AE) newblocs/<CC>/ Time-varying weights Built + validated (39 blocs × 1995–2024, row-sums pass) weights/ NEER Complete for all gap + candidate blocs (12 files) neer/ Exports/Imports Complete except RU-IMP (ends 2021Q3) trade/ NFA / external 54 FULL · 1 PARTIAL (AE) · 1 NOT-FEASIBLE (TW) nfa/

All sourced-and-staged; none estimated into the model. A build proceeds only after the parked decisions below and a single combined re-estimation (append candidate panels + new columns → full re-estimation with US_ENDOGENOUS=1 → port/metas/manifest/coupling/manual chain → green gate → deploy on explicit go-ahead), combined with any changes from the pending dedup/fiscal-expansion runs so the estimation runs once.

docs.title: 8. Parked decisions (user)
docs.text:
1. RU keep / drop. RU is FSAP-listed, but genuine RU data ends ~2021 (the sourced RU import mirror trade/IMP_RU.json ends 2021Q3; existing RU series already carry tail-possibly-WEO-synthetic flags). Keep for FSAP completeness with a documented ragged edge, or drop for data integrity? (Ties to the RU-IMP gap in §5 and the fiscal audit's RU=NOT-FEASIBLE.)
  2. Solve-time weights year. Use 2024 (weights/weights_latest.json, bakes in the post-decoupling US→CN share) or a trailing average / as-of-shock-year slice from weights/weights_timevarying.json? The honest CN/EA trajectory finding (§3) makes this consequential.
  3. NFA Option A vs B. Recommend B (estimate CA_GDP_<CC>, retire iNFA, unit-free, one uniform recipe) — but it adds a panel column and a re-estimation; A is the fallback for any bloc where an estimated CA share is undesirable.
  4. World Bank GDP-USD denominator sign-off. The NFA anchors and CA/GDP shares use WB annual nominal USD GDP (NY.GDP.MKTP.CD) as the denominator against a quarter-end IIP stock (a ≤1Q vintage seam, negligible for a seed; e.g. US recompute −69.1 vs shipped −66.75 is purely FRED-SAAR-2026Q1 vs WB-annual-2025). Sign off on WB as the denominator source, or switch to a trailing-4-quarter nominal-USD GDP for an exact vintage match?
  5. AE / TW external treatment. AE (annual CA only, no IIP) and TW (absent from IMF BOP/IIP entirely) ship without an external block and without back-fill — confirm, or authorise a national-source pull (UAE FCSC; TW CBC/DGBAS) outside the approved APIs? AE's bloc itself is also NOT VIABLE (§2) pending a national quarterly real-GDP source.

docs.title: Live Smell Test — Deployed BVAR Scenario Tool (51 economies)
docs.text:
Branch: improve-live @ 89c4501 (LIVE deployed) · Model: RW-BVAR, no target-reversion, no Taylor reaction · Horizon: h20 (terminal display) · Read-only diagnostic.

This document grades every deployed economy on the central (terminal) forecast against economic-plausibility bands and confirms whether the UK/CA pathologies flagged by the user are systemic across the model set. All values are terminal-h forecasts. log columns are q/q-ann %, lin columns are levels/rates. Snowball = r − g where r = EFFI if a fiscal block exists, else the policy rate.

Legend: ✅ = within plausibility band · ⚠️ = smell (drift / non-anchoring / no-reaction artifact). Smell thresholds: inflation >3.5% (advanced) / off-target (EM) = not-anchoring · real rate < −0.5 = no-Taylor · snowball < −1.5 = debt-falls-implausibly.

docs.title: 2. Systemic Findings
docs.text: The UK/CA pattern flagged in the brief is not idiosyncratic — it is the dominant failure mode of the deployed model. Counts over the 51 economies:

docs.title: Inflation not anchoring (terminal >3.5% advanced / clearly off-target EM)
docs.text: 25 of 51 (49%) smell on inflation: AU(3.07, above 3% band), CA, CL, CN(deflation −1.21), CO, CZ, EA, EE, HU, IE, IS, IT(too-low 0.69), LT, LU, LV, MX, NZ, PL, RU, SI, SK, TR, UK, US, plus CR/ID/FI on the low side (excluded from the hard count). Of these, the inflation drifts UP and stays high (the RW non-reversion signature) in ~20; a smaller cluster (CN, IT, AT, FI) drifts implausibly low/deflationary — confirming the drift runs in both directions, not just upward.

docs.title: Negative real rate (i − π < −0.5, no Taylor reaction)
docs.text: 21 of 51 (41%): AT(−1.02), CA(−0.93), CH(−1.02), DE(−2.19), DK(−2.00), EA(−1.07), EE(−4.73), IL(−0.66), JP(−1.62), KR(−0.74), LT(−10.09), LU(−4.09), LV(−1.31), NO(−0.60), NZ(−1.87), PT(−0.50), SE(−0.50), SI(−1.90), SK(−2.85), UK(−1.74). (US escapes — its policy rate happens to stay above inflation.) Where a credible nominal-rate path exists it is by luck of the frozen terminal level, not policy logic.

docs.title: Debt snowball << −1.5 (debt falls implausibly)
docs.text: 30 of 51 (59%) — the single most pervasive smell: AU, CA, CH, CL, CN, CZ, DE, DK, EA, EE, FR, ID, IE, IL, IN, JP, KR, LT, LU, LV, MY, NL, NO, NZ, PT, SA, SE, SI, SK, TW, UK, US (32 by the strict −1.5 cut; ~30 are the implausible-direction subset after netting EM growth-driven cases). For high-debt sovereigns where consensus is rising (FR d0~116, JP, EA, UK, US, NL, PT) a sustained r−g << −1.5 is squarely implausible. Three small EA members (EE −8.26, SI −8.69, LT −9.97) show outright debt collapse.

docs.title: Cross-cutting
docs.text:
• 17 economies carry all three core nominal smells (non-anchored inflation and negative real rate and snowball << −1.5) or the EA-common-rate equivalent: CA, CH, DE-adjacent, EA, EE, LT, LU, LV, NZ, SI, SK, UK among them. These are the textbook RW-no-reversion cluster.
  • Real-side drift (no mean reversion in growth/unemployment) is the secondary failure: growth flatlines near 0 (AR, AT, GR −0.94, IT −0.22, HU −0.46) or runs implausibly hot (SA ~8, MY ~6.9, TW ~4.9, US 3.45, IN 7.86); unemployment drifts to absurd levels (SA → 0.1, FI 11.6, GR 12.4 drifting up, CH 6.2 vs true ~2-3).
  • The model is internally honest only where the data's terminal level happens to be sensible (BE, ES, TH, ZA, BR, MX, ID-rates) — i.e. the "clean" blocs pass by coincidence of the frozen RW endpoint, not by any anchoring mechanism.

Verdict: the UK/CA observation is systemic. ~half the set fails inflation-anchoring, ~40% show negative real rates, and ~60% show implausibly favorable debt dynamics — all traceable to the same two missing mechanisms.

docs.title: 3. Worst Offenders
docs.text:
Ranked by number and severity of smells:

  1. EE (Estonia) — worst in set. Inflation 4.68 (volatile −3.81→+4.68, no anchor), real rate −4.73, snowball −8.26 → debt collapses from d0~24. Every band fails except unemployment.
  2. SI (Slovenia) — inflation drifts back UP to 5.71 (no glide to 2%), growth 5.2 >> potential, real rate −1.9, snowball −8.69 → debt collapse.
  3. LT (Lithuania) — inflation 10.27 oscillating (−13 to +14), real rate −10.09, snowball −9.97, nominal growth 12.4 absurd. Pure RW artifact contaminating everything.
  4. SK (Slovakia) — worst-anchored EA inflation 7.32, real rate −2.85, snowball −6.87.
  5. CA (Canada) — the brief's textbook case. Inflation 3.69 sticks, policy 2.77 < π → real rate −0.93, snowball −1.97 → debt falls vs CA consensus.
  6. UK (United Kingdom) — canonical pathology. Inflation 4.35 never glides to 2% BoE target, real rate −1.74, EFFI 3.32 << nominal growth 6.39 → snowball −3.07, debt falls vs consensus-rising.
  7. US (United States) — inflation 4.13 drifts up, growth 3.45 above potential, nominal growth 7.58 >> EFFI 4.16 → snowball −3.41; debt-fall masked by SFA drift to +14pp.
  8. EA (Euro Area aggregate) — inflation 3.32 RISES through horizon, real rate −1.07, snowball −3.12.
  9. NZ (New Zealand) — inflation RISES monotonically 2.83→5.45, real rate −1.87, snowball −3.87.
  10. CH / DK / DE — the negative-rate cluster: frozen near historical negative-rate regimes (CH −0.43, DK −0.51, DE 0.71 vs 2.9 π), real rates −1.0 to −2.2, snowballs −2.8 to −4.0.

Opposite-direction offenders (drift to a bad equilibrium): GR (growth −0.94, unemployment drifts 8.4→12.4, snowball +1.29 = debt RISING vs consensus-falling), IT (inflation 0.69, growth −0.22, nominal growth ~0), SA (unemployment → 0.1). These prove the drift is not a one-sided upward-inflation bias but a generic absence of any attractor.

docs.title: Root cause
docs.text:
The deployed model is a random-walk-in-levels BVAR with a Minnesota/RW prior whose constant row acts as a drift, not a steady-state intercept. Two specific absences produce every smell above:

  1. No target-reversion for inflation. With a unit-root companion and no long-run mean, the terminal forecast is whatever the recent sample drifted to. Nothing pulls π toward 2% (advanced) or the EM target → inflation sticks high (UK, CA, NZ, EA…) or drifts low (CN deflation, IT) with equal ease.
  2. No monetary reaction function. The policy rate is a free RW series, not a function of the inflation/output gap. When π drifts up, the rate does not follow → systematically negative real rates (21 economies).

These compound in the debt block: high un-anchored nominal growth − a frozen-low EFFI/policy rate → snowball << −1.5 → debt falls implausibly (30 economies). The real-side analog (no reversion in growth/unemployment) gives the flatline/hot-growth/unemployment-drift smells.

docs.title: Lightweight LIVE-version fix options
docs.text:
(Not the full trend-cycle rebuild — that is parked on feature/trend-cycle-longrun-targets.) These are bolt-ons to the deployed RW-BVAR, ordered by effort:

  • (A) Per-country long-run prior tilt (cheapest, post-estimation). Entropic/PLR tilt of the existing posterior draws toward a per-country terminal target vector (π = target, i = π + neutral real rate, g = potential, u = NAIRU). Lives entirely in the projection layer; no re-estimation. Risk per MEMORY/PLR-vs-tilt: joint multi-constraint tilt degenerates (ESS→1) at 500 draws — apply per-constraint* (inflation-only, then rate) rather than a joint 13-moment tilt.
  • (B) Taylor-rule overlay on the rate path (targeted). Replace the free RW rate forecast with a reaction rule i_t = r* + π_t + φ_π(π_t − π*) + φ_y·ỹ_t evaluated on the model's own π/output draws. Fixes the 21 negative-real-rate blocs and feeds a sane r into the snowball, without touching the macro block. Cheapest fix for the debt-falls-implausibly smell on rate-proxy economies.
  • (C) Target-reverting inflation prior (medium, in-prior). Add a soft long-run mean (a "sum-of-coefficients"-style or explicit mean-reversion dummy) so π glides to π* over the horizon. This is the most economically honest of the bolt-ons but requires a (cheap) re-estimation per country.
  • (D) Combination A+B (tilt the macro terminal targets + Taylor-overlay the rate) addresses inflation-anchoring, negative-real-rate, and debt-snowball simultaneously with no macro-block re-estimation — the recommended interim while the trend-cycle rebuild matures.

Recommendation (original, superseded — see the status update below): ship (B) Taylor overlay first (mechanical, no re-estimation, kills the negative-real-rate + a large share of the snowball smells), then layer (A) per-constraint inflation tilt for anchoring. Reserve (C) for the next re-estimation cycle. Defer to the parked trend-cycle VAR for the structural cure.

Status update (implemented). Option (A) shipped as a deterministic δc drift overlay, not the entropic tilt — per-variable "Long-run targets" sliders that shift the companion drift so a variable's terminal forecast hits a user target (instant, exact, band-coherent; no re-estimation, no draw reweighting). It replaces the tilt (which degenerated, ESS→1) and sidesteps the per-constraint workaround entirely. The policy rate carries its own long-run-target slider like every other variable — set its terminal value directly through the drift setter. Option (B) Taylor overlay was not retained: an early taylorOverlay policy-rate-row toggle was shipped briefly and then removed (commit 9142265) — it was confusing and inert next to the rate's own slider; no taylorOverlay/setTaylorOverlay symbol remains. The perverse/near-singular policy-rate sliders (BE, CA, CZ) are instead disabled + labelled (the |sens| < 0.3 guard), not routed through any overlay. See MAINTAINER_OPERATIONS.md §G4 and USER_GUIDE.md §14. Option (C) (in-prior reversion) and the structural trend-cycle rebuild remain the next-cycle work.

docs.title: MP Committee — Live Demo Script (15 min, laptop only, no slides)
docs.text: A timed, click-by-click runbook for the live tool demo. Each segment gives the exact clicks, the one-line econometric point to say out loud, and the expected on-screen result. Language rule: every conditional path is "the most likely projection given the conditioning assumptions" (a Waggoner–Zha / DK conditional forecast). Never say "entropic tilting."

docs.title: Pre-flight checklist (do this before the room)
docs.text:
• [ ] Tool open in the browser, live build loaded (production bvarscenario/main).
  • [ ] Country = United States (top-right Country dropdown, GVAR optgroup; US is the default on load).
  • [ ] Units toggle = "q/q ann." — NOT "% vs baseline" (that view is read-only and disables dragging).
  • [ ] Anchors confirmed ON: left ControlPanel → "Long-run targets" header reads "(7 set)". If the debt path looks flat, anchors haven't seeded yet (async fetch of default_anchors.json) — refresh and wait a beat.
  • [ ] Clean scenario: ControlPanel header → "Reset all" → "Yes, reset all" once, so no stray pins and spillover switches are OFF.
  • [ ] Know where the financial charts live: 10Y (GLB_USLR), Baa (GLB_USBAA), oil (GLB_OIL), equity (GLB_USEQ) are in the "Global commons" section near the bottom. Aaa corporate (FAAA) and domestic WTI (PZTEXP) are in the "Country-specific variables" section. Scroll down once now so you can find them fast.
  • [ ] Between cases use "Reset" (clears this scenario's pins, keeps anchors). Only use "Reset all" when you want spillover switches OFF too.

docs.title: (0:00–0:30) — What it is
docs.text: "This is a multi-country Bayesian VAR forecasting tool with a fiscal satellite and a GVAR cross-country layer. Everything you'll see is live: I open the central projection, then build scenarios by conditioning, and export the whole thing to Excel."

docs.title: Monetary block (0:30–2:00)
docs.text:
Clicks: The grid is already on US. Row 1 (macro triad) holds Inflation (source JGDP, "GDP Chain Price Index"), Policy Rate (POLRATE, "Effective Federal Funds Rate"), and GDP Growth (GDPH).

Say (one-liner — rates vs levels): "Price indices like JGDP are modeled as 100·log price levels with a Minnesota / Litterman random-walk prior; what you see on the Inflation chart is a display transform — 4·Δ of that log level, i.e. q/q annualized. The policy rate and yields, by contrast, are modeled directly as levels in percent. So inflation is a transform of a modeled price level; the policy rate is a modeled level itself."

Also say (prior + COVID, one line each): "Estimation is GLP — Giannone–Lenza–Primiceri — Minnesota prior shrinking toward a random walk. And the 2020 COVID quarters are treated as missing data, imputed inside the Gibbs sampler, so the pandemic outliers don't contaminate the dynamics."

Expected on screen: Inflation glides to ~2%, policy rate toward neutral. Frame it: "the central projection with long-run targets anchored to consensus" — the consensus long-run anchors (the δc forward-pass: inflation→2%, policy→neutral, fiscal→OBR/IMF/CBO) are ON by default and are a deterministic drift, separate from any scenario conditioning. (If asked to show the raw BVAR: in a panel click "reset all to estimate" — inflation/debt revert to the drifting RW path; re-apply with "Apply consensus anchors.")

docs.title: Fiscal satellite (2:00–3:15)
docs.text:
Clicks: Scroll to Row 2 — the 4 estimated BVAR fiscal variables, each its own chart: Revenue (FREV_GDP), Primary Expenditure (FPEXP_GDP), Effective Interest Rate (EFFI), Stock-Flow Adjustment (SFA). Directly under them: the header "Fiscal block — derived by accounting identity" with 3 derived charts: Primary Balance, Δ Debt-to-GDP, Debt-to-GDP.

Say (one-liner — the satellite): "Government debt is not a BVAR variable. The BVAR estimates only these four — revenue, primary spending, the effective interest rate on the stock, and the stock-flow-adjustment residual. Debt is derived by rolling them through the budget identity: dₜ = dₜ₋₁·(1+i)/(1+g) − pb/4 + sfa/4, seeded at d₀ = 122.6% of GDP."

Say (the snowball, one line): "(1+i)/(1+g) is the snowball — when the effective rate exceeds nominal growth, debt rises even with a balanced primary budget; pb = revenue − primary spending is the discretionary effort; SFA is the deficit-debt residual — below-the-line and valuation items the headline deficit misses."

Expected on screen: Debt-to-GDP rises realistically (not a flat degenerate path) — because the consensus anchors hold inflation at ~2%, the effective rate near neutral (EFFI 5.0), and revenue/spending at CBO ratios. The four WN-prior fiscal ratios mean-revert (revenue ~17.5%) rather than drift, which is what keeps the path defensible.

docs.title: Excel export (3:15–4:00)
docs.text:
Clicks: First set Uncertainty = Quick (TopBar) and press Compute so the bands populate. Then on the bottom ScenarioBar click the Excel button.

Say: "It downloads forecast_US_<name>_<timestamp>.xlsx — one sheet per variable, columns Quarter | Date | Uncond. Q16 | Baseline (median) | Uncond. Q84 | scenario Q16 | scenario median | scenario Q84 | Deviation, plus a Summary sheet and a Notes sheet documenting each source variable and unit."

Expected on screen: File downloads; every monetary and fiscal variable (including derived Debt-to-GDP) has its own tab. (Scenario columns are blank until a scenario is computed — that comes next.)

docs.title: (4:00–8:00) — CASE 1: GFC corporate-yield shock (Waggoner–Zha)
docs.text: Story: pull the corporate yield up. First without pinning the govt 10Y (flight-to-quality), then with it pinned unchanged (clean credit-spread shock).

docs.title: Step 1 — corporate up, 10Y FREE (4:00–6:00)
docs.text:
Clicks: Scroll to "Country-specific variables" → Moody's Seasoned Aaa Corporate Bond Yield (FAAA). Click the panel's "condition" button (turns blue → "CONDITIONED"). Drag the line UP ~+150–200 bp in the early quarters (t+1..t+4), or right-click a quarter to plant the bullet exactly at the cursor value. Do not touch the 10Y. Press Compute (Quick).

Say (one-liner): "Only the corporate yield is pinned, so the Treasury 10Y is free. This is the most likely projection given that one conditioning assumption — and the model pulls the risk-free 10Y down: flight-to-quality, with output and inflation softening. A recession read."

Expected on screen: Corporate yield up where you pinned it; the 10Y (GLB_USLR, Global commons) drifts down; growth/inflation soften.

docs.title: Step 2 — ADD 10Y held UNCHANGED (6:00–8:00)
docs.text:
Clicks: Scroll to "Global commons" → 10-Year Treasury Note Yield (GLB_USLR; conditionable because Country==US). Click its "condition" button but do not move the line — a fresh condition starts at the baseline (zero-deviation), which is "held unchanged." Press Compute again.

Say (one-liner): "Now both yields are pinned — corporate up, risk-free curve held flat. That isolates a pure credit-spread / financial-conditions shock with no flight-to-quality offset. The clean scenario."

Expected on screen: Corporate up, 10Y flat at baseline; the spread blowout is now the whole story. (Tip: per-quarter sliders in the left ControlPanel "Conditioning" section let you pin only the early impact window and leave the tail free; "All" toggles all 20 quarters.)

docs.title: (8:00–11:30) — CASE 2: EA-yield shock → US & global spillovers (GVAR)
docs.text:
"Reset, switch to the Euro Area, shock the same yield there, and watch it reach the US through the cross-country coupling."

Clicks: 1. ControlPanel header → "Reset all" → "Yes, reset all" (clean, not stacked on the GFC; also returns spillover switches to OFF — we turn them back on deliberately). 2. Top-bar Country dropdown → Euro Area (GVAR-linked section). 3. Shock the same yield you used for the US: EA 10Y Gov Bond Yield (YIELD10_EA) for the govt version, or EA IG Corporate Bond Yield (EACORP) for the corporate version. Right-click the chart at the target quarter/level (right-click conditions AND plants the bullet in one step), then drag up ~+100–150 bp across the first few quarters. 4. Left ControlPanel → "Cross-border spillovers" → set "Scenario spillovers (GVAR solve)" to On. 5. Click "▶ Solve full GVAR" for the complete coupled fixed point (all feedback loops, RoW→US).

Say (one-liner): "The GVAR links blocs through three trade-weighted RoW star variables per country — foreign demand, foreign inflation, foreign short rate. The EA shock raises EA's contribution to every partner's stars, and the solver iterates the coupled fixed point x = Mx + d. A single-country EA BVAR would hold the US fixed; the GVAR lets EA tightening pull on US financial conditions and global activity. This is where the cross-country coupling shines."

Expected on screen (two read-outs): - Stay on EA and watch the in-model Global commons charts move: US 10Y (GLB_USLR), US BAA (GLB_USBAA), US equity / S&P 500 (GLB_USEQ), WTI oil (GLB_OIL). - Switch Country → United States — the EA pins persist across the switch (separate store slice), so the full US bloc (growth, inflation, policy rate, yields) shows the EA→US spillover even though the US has no own pins.

Gotcha to remember: without turning the spillover switch On (or pressing Solve full GVAR), EA moves alone and the US/global charts won't budge — this is the #1 thing to not forget. A full 50-bloc solve is ~4.5s warm; press once and let it land.

docs.title: (11:30–14:30) — CASE 3: US oil/energy — demand vs supply
docs.text:
"Reset first — this is NOT on top of the GFC. Condition only on higher oil → demand dominates. Then add short-term Cholesky-type sign restrictions to flip it to an adverse supply shock."

Setup clicks: Country back to United States. ControlPanel header → "Reset" (clears this scenario's pins; keeps the consensus anchors — exactly what we want). Confirm all "condition" buttons are grey.

docs.title: Step 1 — oil UP alone → DEMAND-dominant (11:30–13:00)
docs.text:
Clicks: Use the US-domestic oil series Spot Oil Price: West Texas Intermediate (PZTEXP, "Country-specific variables"). Click "condition", then drag the line UP to a higher level (e.g. ~\(70 → ~\)100). It's a level-display var, so you're setting a $/bbl level, not a growth rate — drag to the actual target price. Press Compute (Quick).

Say (one-liner): "With only oil pinned, the conditional solve reads the historical oil–output covariance as demand-driven — so US output rises with the oil price. The demand-dominant response."

Expected on screen: Oil at the pinned level; US output up.

docs.title: Step 2 — add sign restrictions → ADVERSE SUPPLY (13:00–14:30)
docs.text:
Clicks: Keep oil conditioned up. Now also condition GDP Growth (GDPH) and drag it DOWN at t+1..t+2; condition Inflation (JGDP) and drag it UP at t+1..t+2. Use the per-quarter sliders / "All"-off-then-enable-early so only t+1..t+2 are active and the tail stays free. Press Compute.

Say (one-liner): "The 'Cholesky-type' move here is multi-variable Waggoner–Zha conditioning that pins the early signs: output down, inflation up in the impact window. That forces the supply-shock identification — a stagflationary response — instead of the demand read. The later quarters stay free, so the model fills in the dynamics."

Expected on screen: Same oil rise, but now output down and inflation up early — stagflation. The contrast with Step 1 is the whole point.

docs.title: (14:30–15:00) — Close + Excel
docs.text:
Clicks: After the final Compute, hit the ScenarioBar Excel button once more.

Say: "Every case exports the same way — one sheet per variable, organized by date, with the unconditional baseline and ±1-s.d. band sitting next to the conditional path, band and deviation — including the satellite's derived Debt-to-GDP. The Summary tab lines all variables up. That's the full forecasting system: a central projection anchored to consensus, scenario conditioning on top, cross-country spillovers via the GVAR, and a one-click Excel hand-off."

docs.title: "If asked" — FAQ
docs.text:
• The prior? "Minnesota / Litterman, GLP (Giannone–Lenza–Primiceri) implementation, shrinking toward a random walk on the macro and financial variables. The three fiscal ratios — revenue, primary spending, SFA — instead carry a white-noise prior so they revert to a long-run mean rather than drift; that's what keeps revenue at ~17.5% and stops the debt path running away."
  • Weak exogeneity of the RoW stars? "Each bloc's three trade-weighted foreign aggregates (ROWDEM/ROWINF/ROWFIN) enter as weakly exogenous regressors in the country VAR — standard Pesaran-type GVAR identification. At solve time the blocs are coupled and the foreign aggregates become endogenous to the system; we solve the fixed point x = Mx + d (closed form (I−M)⁻¹d), so consistency holds across the coupled solution. The US is endogenous in the live system with its own RoW stars."
  • COVID treatment? "2020 quarters are treated as missing data, imputed inside the Gibbs sampler — data augmentation in cgl_bvarV5, not Lenza–Primiceri volatility scaling. The outliers never enter the likelihood for the dynamics or the prior."
  • Anchors on vs raw? "The consensus long-run anchors are a deterministic δc forward-pass drift to publicly-defensible targets (inflation→2%, policy→neutral, fiscal→OBR/IMF/CBO). They're on by default, separate from the Waggoner–Zha conditioning, and toggle off via the 'Long-run targets' panel ('reset all to estimate') to show the raw drifting RW-BVAR."
  • Does the BVAR forecast debt? "No — it forecasts the four fiscal drivers; the satellite accumulates debt by the budget identity. The debt/PB bands come from running the recursion per-draw."

docs.title: Refined boss-reply (4 sentences)
docs.text: The 15-minute script is written to docs/mp-presentation-prep.md and follows your exact flow: (0:30–4:00) the unconditional US central projection — monetary block (inflation as a 4·Δ display transform of a 100·log price level vs the policy rate modeled directly as a level, Minnesota/GLP prior, COVID-as-missing) and the fiscal satellite (4 BVAR drivers → snowball/primary-balance/SFA debt recursion, now rising realistically with consensus anchors on by default), plus the per-variable Excel export. Case 1 is the GFC corporate-yield Waggoner–Zha scenario — FAAA up with the 10Y free (flight-to-quality), then GLB_USLR pinned unchanged (clean credit-spread shock); Case 2 is the EA-yield shock (YIELD10_EA/EACORP) with the GVAR spillover switch and "Solve full GVAR" showing the US/global response via the trade-weighted RoW stars; Case 3 resets and runs US oil (PZTEXP) demand-dominant alone, then early-quarter output↓/inflation↑ sign restrictions to flip it to an adverse supply shock. Throughout it's framed as "the most likely projection given the conditioning assumptions" — never entropic tilting — with the anchors kept separate from the scenario layer, and it ends on the per-variable/per-date Excel hand-off. A pre-flight checklist (tool open, anchors-on confirmed, clean reset between cases) and an "if asked" FAQ (prior, weak exogeneity, COVID, anchors-on vs raw) are appended.

docs.title: Pre-ship smoke test — default δc long-run anchors (CONSOLIDATED, all economies)
docs.text:
What this is. The earlier docs/live-smell-test.md found the LIVE GMAPS (BVAR Scenario Tool, branch improve-live) is systemically implausible out of the box: the RW-prior baselines have a constant row that is a pure drift term, so the model has no steady state — the H=20 (5-year) terminal forecast is just "wherever the drift carried the level path." That produced inflation not anchoring (~49% of cases), negative terminal real rates (~41%), and a falling debt-snowball (~59%).

This file does the per-country × per-variable version and asks the operational question: does a single, simple, publicly-known, common-sense long-run anchor (one δc per variable) make the forecast sensible? If yes, that anchor is a recommended ship-with default the tool can present as a one-click preset. Method is the verbatim app/src/lib/compute/driftSetter.ts algebra (companion T from betahat, S_h=Σ_{k<h}Tᵏ, sens_j=4·(S_H−S_{H-1})[j,j] for log / S_H[j,j] for lin, δc_j=(anchor−terminal)/sens_j; glided terminal = anchor by construction). Replicated and the identity holds. READ-ONLY — no app/src or data files were modified.

The consolidated synthesis below covers all 46 graded blocs; the per-alphabet-band sections that follow (D–G, H–K, L–N, S–Z, A–C, plus PL/PT/RU folded in) are the full supporting detail.

docs.title: 1. Coverage scorecard (all 46 blocs, 227 graded variables)
docs.text:
metric value Blocs graded 46 (every bvar/<C> bloc except gvar; EA/EE/IE/IT not separately graded) Key variables graded 227 Resolved by one simple, public δc 219 / 227 = 96.5% Not resolved by a δc (structural / regime) 8 Additional ill-conditioned-but-finite sliders to flag (resolve, do not auto-ship) US POLRATE, JP POLRATE, SK EFFI, PT LENDR

A simple common-sense δc resolves essentially the entire smell test. Every flagged inflation-non-anchoring, every negative terminal real rate that lives on a well-behaved rate slider, every above/below-potential growth drift, and every snowball-from-π/g-drift is fixed by a single publicly-defensible long-run shift. The exceptions below are not drift — they are accounting identities or regimes a long-run intercept cannot move.

docs.title: The 8 that do NOT resolve via a δc — and why
docs.text:
# bloc:var category reason a long-run δc cannot fix it 1 UK debt direction primary-balance identity Debt falls because the terminal primary balance is a +3.1% surplus (rev 43.1 > pexp 40.0). The snowball does resolve via the π δc; the direction is an accounting fact the rev/pexp sliders are no-ops against. 2 SK primary deficit primary-balance identity Structural −6.0% primary deficit (pexp 50.4 ≫ rev 44.3) drives debt regardless of the (drift-fixable) snowball. The pexp slider is a no-op. 3 CN inflation structural reflation Terminal −1.21% (deflation); the δc (+1.18) is a +3.2pp regime reflation a deflationary RW will not deliver credibly — flag, don't slider-nudge. 4 AR inflation hyperinflation regime No in-sample point target; active disinflation/hyperinflation. No anchor defined → skip the nominal slider. 5 AR policy rate hyperinflation regime Non-stationary regime rate; no neutral defined → skip. 6 BE policy rate perverse/near-singular slider sens −0.36 (inverted, barely above the 0.3 guard). Default 2.61 is coincidentally near neutral, but the slider moves the path the wrong way → disable + label the near-singular policy slider, don't ship the thumb. 7 CA policy rate perverse slider sens −6.92 (inverted). Default 2.77 ≈ neutral by coincidence; raising the target lowers the path → disable + label the near-singular policy slider. 8 CZ policy rate perverse slider + bad default sens −3.62 (inverted) and default 5.61 ≫ ~3% neutral → neither trustworthy → disable + label the near-singular policy slider.

Pattern: 4 of the 8 are the three EM/euro perverse policy-rate sliders (BE, CA, CZ) plus the AR regime — exactly the subset the smell test's negative-real-rate finding flagged. Their fix is to disable + label the near-singular policy slider, not the drift thumb. The other 4 are 2 debt primary-balance identities (UK, SK — the brief's canonical "debt = primary balance, not snowball" case), 1 deflation reflation (CN), 1 hyperinflation regime (AR nominal block). None is a defect in the δc machinery; each is a known category that needs a different lever.

docs.title: Largest (but still finite, resolving) δc — context, not failures
docs.text: These are pure RW runaway, fixed by one coherent shift, never a structural break: TR inflation −3.44 (RW carries 32% hyperinflation forever; CBRT 5% goal is aspirational), LT inflation −3.34 (tool-wide-worst 10.27% → ECB 2%), HU growth +2.74 / inflation −2.29 (broken central path), SI growth −2.62, MY growth −2.23 (small-sens catch-up drift), CO inflation −1.84 (largest clean A–C correction on a healthy slider), SA unemployment +1.68 (RW collapse to 0.1%).

Public-knowledge long-run values (central-bank inflation target / band-midpoint; IMF-WEO or OECD potential growth; neutral policy = r* + π*; structural/NAIRU unemployment). Parenthesised policy rates are the defensible anchor but the slider is perverse — disable + label the near-singular policy slider. — = no such series in the bloc's spec.

docs.text: Bloc Out-of-the-box smell One-click default fixes it to US g 3.45 (>potential), deflator π 4.13, snowball falling, policy 5.46 g→1.9, π→2.0 (CPI 2.3), unemp→4.2; 10Y/EFFI carry the real rate. Don't auto-ship the raw policy δc (sens 0.51, ill-conditioned). EA core (DE/FR/ES) DE π 2.9 over + real rate −2.2%; FR g 2.4 hot; ES already clean All → ECB 2.0% infl, 2.25% neutral, potential g, NAIRU. ES is the healthiest bloc in the tool. docs.title: 4. Ship verdict
docs.text:
YES — presentable, with the default anchors shipped as one-click presets and four labels.

  • 96.5% (219/227) of every smell across 46 blocs is resolved by a single, publicly-defensible δc. With the default-anchor preset applied, the out-of-the-box forecasts anchor at each central bank's inflation target, a positive neutral real rate, IMF-WEO potential growth, and the country NAIRU — i.e. sensible by inspection. The δc overlay is a band-invariant rigid translation, so shipped uncertainty is unchanged.
  • The 8 non-resolving cases are not bugs — they are known categories that need a different lever and a UI label, not a fix: UK & SK debt direction (primary-balance identities), the BE/CA/CZ perverse policy-rate sliders (→ disable + label the near-singular slider), CN deflation (structural reflation), AR nominal block (hyperinflation regime). All five economies still have sensible defaults for their other variables.
  • Four ill-conditioned-but-finite sliders to flag, not auto-ship the raw δc: US POLRATE (sens 0.51 → anchor π/g, let 10Y/EFFI carry the real rate), JP POLRATE (sens 0.53), SK EFFI (sens 0.56), PT LENDR (sens 0.52). PL POLRATE (sens −9.94) works but has a counter-intuitive sign → tooltip.

Recommendation: ship the §2 preset as the default slider positions (replacing the degenerate RW drift), with UI labels on the 8 structural/regime exceptions and the 4–5 sensitive sliders. The tool is presentable out of the box. The remaining structural items (UK/SK debt direction, AR/CN regimes) are the trend-cycle / fiscal-rebuild track, not a blocker for the anchored-default ship.

docs.title: APPENDIX — full per-economy supporting detail (by alphabet band)
Pre-ship smoke test — default δc long-run anchors (economies D–G)
docs.text:
Scope. The LIVE GMAPS (BVAR Scenario Tool, branch improve-live) ships RW-prior BVAR baselines whose constant row is a pure drift term, so the model has no steady state — the H=20 (5y) terminal forecast is just "wherever the drift has carried the level path." The earlier docs/live-smell-test.md found this is systemically implausible (inflation not anchoring, negative terminal real rates, debt-snowball falling). This file does the per-country × per-variable version for the D–G economies and asks the operational question: does a single, simple, publicly-known, common-sense long-run anchor (one δc per variable) make the forecast sensible? If yes, that anchor is a recommended default the tool can ship with.

Economies graded: DE, DK, ES, FI, FR, GR. (All European; DK is non-euro but pegs the krone to the euro under ERM-II, so it imports the ECB's de-facto 2% objective and runs its own policy rate a hair above the ECB to defend the peg.)

Method (verbatim app/src/lib/compute/driftSetter.ts). Companion T is built from companion_mean.json betahat (row 0 = constant dropped; T[i,j]=betahat[j+1][i]; identity shift in the lower block). S_h = Σ_{k<h} Tᵏ. Terminal display forecast is read off baseline.json mean[H-1]. Sensitivity of variable j's terminal display to a unit δc on its own equation: - log vars (GDP, HICP → chart shows 4·Δlevel = q/q annualised %): sens_j = 4·(S_H−S_{H-1})[j,j] - lin vars (rates, ratios → chart shows the level): sens_j = S_H[j,j]

Required anchor shift: δc_j = (anchor − terminal) / sens_j. The glided terminal is, by construction, exactly the anchor. (Replicated in /tmp against the TS; identity holds.)

Anchor basis (all PUBLIC reference values — not tuned to the model): - Inflation → the central bank's stated target. ECB 2.0% (DE, ES, FI, FR, GR). Denmark: ERM-II krone peg ⇒ imports the ECB's 2.0% objective. - Real growth → IMF WEO / OECD potential-growth consensus: DE ~0.8, DK ~1.5, ES ~1.5, FI ~1.2, FR ~1.3, GR ~1.0. - Policy rate → neutral = r* + π*. Euro area ECB neutral ≈ 2.0–2.5% (we use 2.25). DK ≈ ECB neutral (peg). - Unemployment → structural / NAIRU (OECD/EC estimates): DE ~3.5, DK ~4.5, ES ~11.5 (persistently high), FI ~7.0, FR ~7.0, GR ~11.0.

resolves = true ⇔ the anchor is defensible AND the required δc is a modest constant-shift (the model is merely drifting, not structurally broken). It would be false only if a long-run shift cannot fix it (e.g. UK debt = a primary-deficit identity, not a snowball drift — not present here).

docs.title: Cross-cutting smell-test (terminal, H=20)
docs.text:

docs.title: Verdict
docs.text:
Every flagged variable across D–G is a drift/anchoring failure of the RW prior, and in every case a single, publicly-defensible δc resolves it (resolves = true for all flagged vars). The required δc are modest constant-shifts (|δc| ≲ 0.5 almost everywhere; the lone outlier is FI GDP at −1.88, driven by a small sens=0.83, still a finite single-target correction — not a structural break). No D–G variable is in the UK-debt category (a primary-deficit identity that a long-run shift cannot repair).

Recommended ship-with defaults (the anchors above):

Shipping these as the default slider positions (instead of the degenerate RW drift) makes the out-of-the-box forecasts anchor at the central bank's inflation target, a positive neutral real rate, potential growth, and the NAIRU — i.e. sensible by inspection. The cross-variable S_h[:,j] response then drags the rest of each bloc along the estimated dynamics, as designed.

Read-only smoke test; no app/src or data files were modified.

docs.title: Pre-ship smoke test — default δc long-run anchors (economies H–K)
docs.text:
Scope. Same exercise, same improve-live LIVE GMAPS, for the economies whose code starts with a letter in [H..K]: HU, ID, IL, IN, IS, JP, KR (gvar skipped). Per country × per variable: terminal forecast, plausible?, common-sense PUBLIC anchor (+basis), the δc to glide there, the glided terminal (= anchor), and whether a simple δc resolves it (model merely drifting, not structurally broken).

Method (verbatim app/src/lib/compute/driftSetter.ts, replicated in Python, identity holds). Companion T from companion_mean.json betahat (T[i,j]=betahat[j+1][i], identity shift in the lag block); S_h=Σ_{k<h}Tᵏ to H=20; sens_j = 4·(S_H−S_{H-1})[j,j] (log: display = 4·Δlevel = q/q annualised %) or S_H[j,j] (lin: display = level); δc_j=(anchor−terminal)/sens_j; glided = anchor by construction. Anchor basis (PUBLIC reference values, not tuned): inflation → the central-bank target; real growth → IMF WEO / OECD potential; policy rate → neutral = r* + π*; unemployment → structural / NAIRU; 10Y / short rate → neutral policy (+ a small term premium for 10Y).

docs.title: Pre-ship smoke test — default δc long-run anchors (economies L–N)
docs.text:
Scope. Same LIVE GMAPS, same driftSetter.ts method as the sections above. This section grades the economies whose code begins with L, M, or N: LT, LU, LV, MX, MY, NL, NO, NZ. For each, the key forecastable own-bloc variables (real growth, inflation, policy/short rate, unemployment, and the 10Y yield where it is an own-bloc state) are reported with: the terminal display forecast, plausible y/n, the common-sense public anchor (+basis), the required δc, the glided terminal (= anchor by construction), and whether a simple δc resolves it.

Method/values verified by replicating driftSetter.ts exactly in Python against companion_mean.json (companion T, S_h = Σ_{k<h}Tᵏ, sens_j = 4·(S_H−S_{H-1})[j,j] for log and S_H[j,j] for lin), terminal from baseline.json mean[H-1] (H=20). Every sensitivity passes SENS_GUARD = 0.3 — no slider disabled — and each glided terminal equals its anchor to machine precision. So the only live questions are raw-terminal plausibility and δc size.

Anchor basis (all PUBLIC reference values — not tuned): - Inflation → the official central-bank target: ECB 2.0% (LT, LU, LV, NL); Banxico 3.0% (MX); BNM implicit ~2.5% midpoint of its 2–3% comfort band (MY); Norges Bank 2.0% (lowered from 2.5% in March 2018) (NO); RBNZ 2.0% midpoint of the 1–3% PTA band (NZ). - Real growth → IMF WEO / OECD / national potential: LT ~2.5, LV ~2.5 (EU catch-up), LU ~2.0, NL ~1.3 (CPB), NO ~1.7, NZ ~2.2, MX ~2.0, MY ~4.5. - Policy / short rate → neutral = r* + π*: EA short rate ~2.0 (LT/LU/LV/NL 3M, in the shared external block); MX 6.0 (r*~3 + π*3, ~Banxico neutral); MY 3.0 (BNM neutral OPR); NO 2.5 (Norges neutral); NZ 3.0 (RBNZ neutral OCR, 2.75–3.25 range). - Unemployment → structural/NAIRU: LT/LV ~6.5, LU ~5.5, NL ~4.0, NO ~3.8, MX ~3.5, MY ~3.3, NZ ~4.3. - 10Y yield → neutral policy rate + a positive term premium: MX 7.0, NZ 3.75.

docs.title: Pre-ship smoke test — default δc long-run anchors (economies S–Z)
docs.text:
Scope. Same exercise, same method, for the S–Z blocs in app/public/data/bvar/: SA, SE, SI, SK, TH, TR, TW, UK, US, ZA. No edits — the matrices below are recomputed from companion_mean.json / baseline.json / transformations.json with the verbatim driftSetter.ts algebra; the terminal forecasts reproduce docs/live-smell-test.md exactly (e.g. UK π 4.35, US g 3.45, TR π 32.3), confirming the pipeline.

Method (verbatim app/src/lib/compute/driftSetter.ts). Companion T from betahat (T[i,j]=betahat[j+1][i], identity shift below); S_h = Σ_{k<h} Tᵏ; terminal = baseline.mean[H-1] (H=20, lags=3 for all S–Z blocs). sens_j = 4·(S_H−S_{H-1})[j,j] for log vars (GDP, CPI/HICP → q/q-annualised %), S_H[j,j] for lin vars (rates, ratios). δc_j = (anchor − terminal)/sens_j; glided terminal = anchor by construction. SENS_GUARD = 0.3 ⇒ |sens|<0.3 disables the slider (no S–Z key slider hits the guard, but two are near-singular — US POLRATE sens 0.51 and SK EFFI sens 0.56 — so their δc are large/ill-conditioned though finite).

Anchor basis (all PUBLIC reference values — not tuned): - Inflation → official target/band midpoint: ECB 2.0 (SI, SK euro members); Riksbank 2.0 (SE); BoE 2.0 (UK); Fed 2.0 GDP-deflator-equiv / 2.3 CPI (US); BoT band 1–3 → 2.0 (TH); CBC implicit 2.0 (TW); SARB band 3–6 → 4.5 (SA, ZA); CBRT long-run goal 5.0 (TR). - Real growth → IMF WEO / OECD potential: SA ~2.5, SE ~1.8, SI ~1.5, SK ~2.0, TH ~3.0, TR ~3.5, TW ~2.5, UK ~1.3 (OECD/OBR), US ~1.9 (CBO/FOMC), ZA ~1.5. - Policy rate → neutral = r* + π*: SE 2.5, SI/SK 2.0 (ECB depo neutral), TH 2.5, TR 9.0 (≈π*5 + r*4 EM premium), TW 2.0, UK 2.75 (BoE r*0.75+2.0), US 2.9 (FOMC SEP longer-run dot), SA 7.0, ZA 7.0; 10Y/lending = neutral + term/credit premium. - Unemployment → structural/NAIRU: SA ~27, SE ~7, SI ~4.5, SK ~6, TH ~1, TR ~9, TW ~3.7, UK ~4.5, US ~4.2 (FOMC longer-run), ZA ~28.

A flagged var resolves=yes when the anchor is publicly defensible AND the δc is a reasonable single-target shift (the model is merely drifting). resolves=no when the smell is a structural accounting identity a long-run δc cannot repair (the UK/SK debt direction, a primary-balance fact, not the snowball that the inflation/growth δc fixes).

docs.title: Verdict (S–Z)
docs.text:
Across the 10 S–Z blocs, every flagged nominal/real variable is a drift/anchoring failure that a single publicly-defensible δc resolves. The required shifts are modest constant-shifts almost everywhere (|δc| < 1 in companion-constant units), with three understandable larger ones — SA unemployment +1.68 (RW collapse to 0.1%), SI growth −2.62, TR inflation −3.44 (RW carries 32% hyperinflation forever). The two genuine non-resolvable cases are exactly the brief's primary-balance category: - UK debt direction — falls because of a structural +3.1% primary surplus, not the snowball (which the inflation δc fixes). resolves=no. - SK primary deficit (−6.0%) — drives debt regardless of the (drift-fixable) snowball. resolves=no for the deficit.

Two ill-conditioned sliders (above the 0.3 guard but near-singular): US POLRATE sens 0.51 (δc −5.0 to reach the 2.9% dot — ship inflation/growth anchors instead) and SK EFFI sens 0.56. SK POLRATE has a negative sens (−6.88, the ECB common-rate cross-loading) so its δc sign is counter-intuitive though finite.

Recommended ship-with defaults (S–Z):

C GDP Infl Pol Unemp Notes SA 2.5 4.5 7.0 27.0 SARB band-mid; unemp RW-collapse fix (+1.68) SE 1.8 2.0 2.5 7.0 clean bloc; lift real rate only SI 1.5 2.0 2.0 4.5 snowball is the π/g drift SK 2.0 2.0 2.0 6.0 snowball drift-fix; primary deficit structural TH 3.0 2.0 2.5 1.0 too-cold equilibrium → lift TR 3.5 5.0 9.0 9.0 CBRT goal; π δc −3.44 aspirational TW 2.5 2.0 2.0 3.7 only GDP runs hot UK 1.3 2.0 2.75 4.5 snowball drift-fix; debt direction = primary surplus (no-fix) US 1.9 2.0 2.9 4.2 POLRATE δc ill-conditioned (sens 0.51) — anchor π/g instead ZA 1.5 4.5 7.0 28.0 cleanest EM bloc

Shipping these as the default slider thumbs anchors each bloc at its central bank's inflation target/band-midpoint, a positive neutral real rate, IMF-WEO potential growth, and the country NAIRU — sensible out of the box. The two structural exceptions (UK/SK debt) should be labelled in the UI, not "fixed" by a long-run slider.

Read-only smoke test; recomputed from shipped data with the verbatim driftSetter.ts algebra; no app/src or data files were modified.

docs.title: Pre-ship smoke test — default δc long-run anchors (economies A–C)
docs.text:
Scope. Same exercise, same improve-live LIVE GMAPS, for the economies whose code starts with a letter in [A..C]: AR, AT, AU, BE, BR, CA, CH, CL, CN, CO, CR, CZ (gvar skipped). The LIVE RW-prior BVAR baselines have a constant row that is a pure drift, so the model has no steady state — the H=20 (5y) terminal forecast is just "wherever the drift carried the level path." The earlier docs/live-smell-test.md found this systemically implausible. Per country × per variable: terminal forecast, plausible?, common-sense PUBLIC anchor (+basis), the δc to glide there, the glided terminal (= anchor), and whether a simple δc resolves it (model merely drifting, not structurally broken).

Method (verbatim app/src/lib/compute/driftSetter.ts, replicated in Python, identity holds). Companion T from companion_mean.json betahat (row 0 = constant dropped; T[i,j]=betahat[j+1][i]; identity shift in the lag block); S_h = Σ_{k<h} Tᵏ to H=20; terminal display read off baseline.json mean[H-1]. Sensitivity of variable j's terminal display to a unit δc on its own equation: log vars (GDP, CPI/HICP → chart shows 4·Δlevel = q/q annualised %) sens_j = 4·(S_H−S_{H-1})[j,j]; lin vars (rates, ratios → chart shows the level) sens_j = S_H[j,j]. Required shift δc_j = (anchor − terminal)/sens_j; glided terminal = anchor by construction. SENS_GUARD = 0.3: a slider whose |sens| is below it is near-singular and disabled by the UI.

Anchor basis (all PUBLIC reference values — not tuned to the model): - Inflation → the central bank's stated target: ECB 2.0 (AT, BE); RBA 2.5 midpoint (AU); BoC 2.0 (CA); SNB de-facto ~1.0 (CH); CNB 2.0 (CZ); EM official targets BCB 3.0 (BR), BCCh 3.0 (CL), BanRep 3.0 (CO), BCCR 3.0 (CR), PBoC de-facto ~2.0 (CN). AR has no in-sample point target (an active-disinflation/hyperinflation regime) → skipped. - Real growth → IMF WEO / OECD potential: AR ~2.0, AT ~1.0, AU ~2.2, BE ~1.2, BR ~2.0, CA ~1.7, CH ~1.3, CL ~2.0, CN ~4.0, CO ~3.0, CR ~3.5, CZ ~2.3. - Policy rate → neutral = r* + π*: euro-area ECB ~2.0 (AT, BE); advanced AU ~3.1, CA ~2.75 (BoC nominal-neutral midpoint), CH ~1.0, CZ ~3.0; EM higher per its target + a positive real neutral: BR ~7.5, CL ~4.0, CN ~3.0, CO ~5.5, CR ~4.0. AR rate skipped (non-stationary regime). - Unemployment → structural / NAIRU: AR ~7.0, AT ~4.8, AU ~4.25, BE ~5.5, BR ~8.5, CA ~6.0, CH ~2.5, CL ~7.5, CO ~10.0, CR ~9.0, CZ ~2.6. CN has no unemployment series in its spec.

resolves = true ⇔ the anchor is defensible AND the δc is a reasonable single long-run shift on a well-behaved slider (positive sens comfortably above the 0.3 guard — model merely drifting). resolves = false where a long-run intercept move cannot fix it: a perverse / near-singular policy-rate slider (negative or near-guard sens, so the thumb moves the path the wrong way), a structural reflation (CN deflation), or a regime case (AR hyperinflation).

docs.title: Verdict (A–C)
docs.text:
40 of the 45 graded key variables resolve with a single, publicly-defensible δc — modest, well-behaved constant shifts on positive sliders comfortably above the 0.3 guard (|δc| ≲ 0.55 almost everywhere; the largest clean correction is CO inflation at −1.84 on a healthy sens). Inflation glides to the central-bank target, growth to potential, unemployment to NAIRU, most policy rates to a positive neutral real rate — exactly the anchoring the smell test called for.

Five exceptions do NOT resolve via a simple δc (carry as known limitations): 1. BE policy rate — sens −0.36 (near-singular, inverted); default coincidentally OK, slider unsafe. 2. CA policy rate — sens −6.92 (inverted); default ≈ neutral, slider moves the wrong way. 3. CZ policy rate — sens −3.62 (inverted) and default 5.61 too high; neither trustworthy. 4. CN inflation — terminal −1.21 (deflation); δc +1.18 is a structural reflation, not a drift nudge. 5. AR nominal block (CPI, policy rate) — a hyperinflation/disinflation regime, not a drift; skip.

The three perverse policy-rate sliders (BE, CA, CZ) are precisely the subset the smell test's negative-real-rate finding flags — the fix there is to disable + label the near-singular policy slider, not the drift slider. Debt-direction is out of scope for a single macro δc (per the driftSetter.ts caveat the real-growth slider owns the debt direction but the snowball with a frozen-low EFFI is a fiscal-block issue) — it stays parked on the trend-cycle / fiscal rebuild, as in live-smell-test.md for UK.

Recommended ship-with defaults (the anchors above):

C GDP Infl Pol Unemp note AR 2.0 — — 7.0 nominal block (CPI/policy) skipped — regime AT 1.0 2.0 2.0 4.8 AU 2.2 2.5 3.1 4.25 healthiest out of the box BE 1.2 2.0 (2.0) 5.5 policy slider perverse → disable + label near-singular slider BR 2.0 3.0 7.5 8.5 CA 1.7 2.0 (2.75) 6.0 policy slider perverse → disable + label near-singular slider CH 1.3 1.0 1.0 2.5 CL 2.0 3.0 4.0 7.5 CN 4.0 (2.0) 3.0 — inflation structural (deflation); GDP real since 2026-06 CN-only re-est CO 3.0 3.0 5.5 10.0 inflation needs the largest clean δc (−1.84) CR 3.5 3.0 4.0 9.0 CZ 2.3 2.0 (3.0) 2.6 policy slider perverse → disable + label near-singular slider

Parenthesised policy rates are the defensible anchor but the slider is perverse — disable + label the near-singular policy slider rather than shipping the drift thumb.
