• Faulty parallelism after either/or — gmaps:362-363: "a realistic response is either persistent rather than one-off, or it accepts part of the loss." Mixes an adjective phrase with a clause. Fix: "either is persistent rather than one-off, or accepts part of the loss."
  • Dangling modifier — gmaps:309-310: "Treated as a US-only event, world growth dips 0.54 percentage points…" It is the scenario, not world growth, that is treated as US-only.
  • Awkward stacking — gmaps:595-596: "with its seasonal treatment and with and without the shipped long-run anchors." Read: "with its seasonal treatment, both with and without the shipped anchors."
  • Garden-path word order — sec2:363-365: "which makes the global amplification the solve produces powerful…" The predicate adjective lands too far from "makes." Rewrite: "which makes the amplification produced by the solve powerful."
  • Missing comma — sec2:198-200: "and of the foreign variables ROWDEM and ROWINF are masked…" Needs a comma: "and, of the foreign variables, ROWDEM and ROWINF are masked…"
  • Sentence fragment — sec2:451: "A last word on the fiscal side, because it works differently from the rest of the bloc and users notice." No main verb.
  • Awkward "and hold" — sec2:181-182: "no rank and restriction decisions have to be made, and hold, for 38 blocs." Reads as "decisions … hold." Rewrite ("made — and kept").
  • \emph inside math mode — sec2:277: $\emph{affine}$ will not italicize as intended inside $…$; move the emphasis outside the math.
  • Visible TODO in the manuscript — gmaps:591-592: \todo{GIRF figure pending the toolbox estimation run.} plus "will appear … in the next revision." A referee will read this as an incomplete submission.
  • Unhyphenated numeric modifier — "a 100 basis point rise" (gmaps:74, gmaps:158, fig_naive_true.tex:39) should be "a 100-basis-point rise" when attributive (contrast the correctly hyphenated "ten-year", "five-year").
  • Loose count — sec2:348: "a fifty-economy system" understates the 55 served models and does not match the 38 coupled blocs; use one of the exact macros or "fifty-odd."
  • Terminology drift for the stock-flow variable — "stock-flow term" (sec2:179), "stock-flow residual" (sec2:465), "stock-flow adjustment" (sec2:466, eq. 20). Standardize (SFA = "stock-flow adjustment").
  • Same series, two names — "ten-year government yield" (gmaps:227) vs "ten-year Treasury yield" (gmaps:212, 222).
  • Gendered generic pronoun — gmaps:419: "when the user changes her mind." The only gendered pronoun in the paper; prefer "their" for consistency.
  • Informal abbreviation — "applied macro" (gmaps:370) and "macro forecasts" (App. B, gmaps:601); spell out "macroeconomics"/"macroeconomic."
  • Inconsistent capitalization — "the model data base" (gmaps:515) vs the proper name "Macroeconomic Model Data Base" (gmaps:331, 459).
  • Near-verbatim duplication — the "algorithm fine print" footnote (sec2:245-249) and Appendix A paragraph (gmaps:553-556) repeat almost the same sentences; consolidate or cross-reference.
  • Possible latent contradiction — global_constants.tex:9 sets \GlobalSweeps = 1 ("sweeps to converge"), while sec2:296 states "hundreds of sweeps are needed." The macro is currently unused, so nothing renders wrong, but if it is ever cited the two will clash. (Also unused and worth pruning or wiring in: \RhoM, \WorldAmp, \NaiveLrPeakBp, \CFResidualPct, \ExtUsCaAnchor, \ExtUsNfaH, \ExtScenCaDevH, \WUSEA/\WUSMX/\WUSCA/\WUSCN, \LastObsQ, \NowcastQ.)

docs.title: Style Patterns to Fix Throughout
docs.text:
• Oxford comma is inconsistent. Present: gmaps:91 ("growth, inflation, and interest rates"), gmaps:318, gmaps:465, sec2:427. Absent: gmaps:135 ("interest rates and financial prices"), gmaps:253 ("exports, imports and exchange rate"), sec2:121 ("credit, housing and, for…"). Pick one (the paper leans serial-comma in most lists) and apply it everywhere.
  • Em-dash spacing is inconsistent. The dominant style is spaced --- (e.g., gmaps:92, gmaps:132, gmaps:107), but the external-accounts paragraph uses unspaced ---: "value---for" and "output---and" (gmaps:253-254) and "stock---the external" (gmaps:261). Normalize.
  • "pre-computed" vs "precomputed." gmaps:277 ("pre-computed operator") against sec2:293, sec2:297 ("precomputed"). Choose one.
  • Intensifier/filler overuse. "exactly" recurs ~8× (gmaps:275, gmaps:406, sec2:433, sec2:438, sec2:462, sec2:399, sec2:447, and more), "simply" ~4× (gmaps:228, gmaps:310, sec2:128, sec2:215), "actually" 3× (gmaps:378, sec2:276, sec2:445). Thin these out; most sentences are stronger without them.
  • Authorial self-flagging / "worth noting" family. "One consequence deserves emphasis" (sec2:139), "All three deserve to be on the table" (sec2:331), "The costs deserve equal daylight" (sec2:359), "a division of labor that deserves to be stated precisely" (gmaps:452), "One choice is worth flagging" (gmaps:262), "we want to state it plainly" (gmaps:366). This is the essayistic register's version of "it is worth noting"; keep one or two, cut the rest.
  • Person/register drift. Second-person "you" ("the model surprises you", gmaps:159; "what you hold still as by what you move", gmaps:161, gmaps:242) sits alongside "we," "a user," "the user," and "a desk economist." A field journal will want the second person removed in favor of the consistent "we"/"the user."
  • Repeated signature phrase. "from a first click to a policy conclusion" appears near-verbatim three times (abstract gmaps:74; gmaps:158; gmaps:185). Vary two of them.
  • Comma-spliced enumerations of independent clauses recur as a stylistic tic: sec2:58-60 ("Each country model is cast…, the number… is determined…, estimation is by…"), sec2:434, sec2:445-447, gmaps:346. Where the items are full clauses, prefer semicolons.
  • Numeric compound modifiers are hyphenated unevenly — "ten-year," "two-year," "five-year," "one-off," "one-click" are hyphenated, but "100 basis point rise" is not. Standardize attributive numeric compounds.

One structural note beyond prose, flagged for the authors: the coverage table (coverage_table.tex) still lists RU among the 38 coupled blocs, which the constants (\NBlocs=38) and the eigenvalue/\dim x=2,360 arithmetic all assume — internally consistent as written, but confirm RU is intended in this vintage before submission.

docs.title: 2. Internal Consistency & Cross-Reference Verification
docs.text: I have completed a full cross-check of every number against its source, all cross-references, citations, and terminology. Findings below.

docs.title: Critical Inconsistencies
docs.text:
C1. The naive policy-rate peak (44 bp) contradicts its own script-generated figure data (≈42 bp). - figs/data/us_constants.tex:3 defines \newcommand{\NaivePolPeakBp}{44} and the body quotes it: "the policy rate climbs \NaivePolPeakBp{} basis points at its peak" (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:213). - But figs/data/us_spread.csv (same script, us_spread_cf.mjs, identical timestamp) has the naive policy path pol_n peaking at 0.4192 (q4) → 41.9 ≈ 42 bp, not 44. The maximum over the whole column is 0.4192; no value reaches 0.435+. - This is a text-vs-exhibit mismatch: Figure~\ref{fig:naivetrue}'s policy-rate panel plots pol_n (peaks just above 0.4), so a reader comparing the text ("44 bp") to the figure sees a disagreement. Either the constant is stale relative to the CSV or the peak extraction in the script has a bug. The 10-year impact (\NaiveLrImpactBp{}=69, csv lr_n q1=0.6871→69) checks out; only the policy peak is off. Verify/regenerate.

C2. The body asserts a classical-GVAR confrontation that the appendix admits does not yet exist (plus a live \todo in the PDF). - sec2_methodology.tex:366 states, present tense: "Appendix~B confronts the resulting responses with the impulse responses of a classical GVAR estimated on the same data." - But app:cred (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:590-592) says the exhibit "is being produced with the restarted evaluation (below) and will appear in this appendix in the next revision," followed by a rendered \todo{GIRF figure pending the toolbox estimation run.} (:592). The \todo macro (:52) prints a red bracketed note into the compiled PDF. - For a top-field submission this is both an internal overstatement (a claimed comparison that isn't there) and a submission-readiness defect (visible TODO). The forward-reference at gmaps_platform_paper.tex:371 ("Appendix B returns to this distinction in more detail") is fine, since the interpretation distinction is in app:cred; only the confrontation claim overstates the current content.

docs.title: Cross-Reference Errors
docs.text:
X1. "The full roster appears in Appendix C" — Appendix C does not contain the roster. - sec2_methodology.tex:429: "The full roster appears in Appendix~C." - Appendix C (app:repro, gmaps_platform_paper.tex:608-611) contains only the bloc-level coverage table (n, sample, seasonal, fiscal) and explicitly redirects the per-variable roster elsewhere: "the per-variable rosters, sources, and transformations for all \NModels{} economies are in the online manual, and for the United States in \citet{CrumpEusepiGiannoneQianSbordone2025}." The claim should say the roster is in the online manual, not Appendix C.

X2. Hardcoded appendix letters instead of \ref{} (currently correct but fragile). - "Appendix~B" (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:371, sec2_methodology.tex:366) and "Appendix~C" (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:188, sec2_methodology.tex:429) are typed literally rather than \ref{app:cred} / \ref{app:repro}. They resolve correctly given the current A/B/C ordering (app:model/app:cred/app:repro), but any reordering silently breaks them. Not an error today; a hazard worth converting to \ref.

All other cross-references verified correct: every \ref/\eqref (Figures ui-cond, naivetrue, external, ui-ea, global, cf, ui-cf, pesaran, gbvar; Tables coverage, gvar-vs; eqs varx, starsclassical, stack, mffmbloc, partition, rowdem–rowfin, wtilde, ss, fixedpoint, debt, softpin, anchor, delta; Sections intro/method/example/solve/estimation/classical/counterfactual/conclusion) points to an existing target that shows what is claimed. The two TikZ schematics (figs/tikz/fig_pesaran.pdf, fig_gbvar.pdf) both exist.

docs.title: Terminology Drift
docs.text:
T1. \RhoM (0.989) is defined but never used; \rho(M)=0.98917 is hand-typed three times — a direct violation of the paper's own binding style contract. - constants.tex:20 defines \newcommand{\RhoM}{0.989} "updated ONLY by regeneration," and gmaps_platform_paper.tex:8 states the contract: "Every quoted number is a macro from constants.tex (script-generated; never hand-typed)." - Yet 0.98917 is hardcoded at sec2_methodology.tex:291, :363, and :412 (the comparison table), and \RhoM appears 0 times. The value is not a contradiction (0.98917 rounds to 0.989), but three hand-typed copies of a number that is supposed to live in a macro is exactly the maintenance hazard the contract forbids, and the two representations (0.989 vs 0.98917) can drift apart on the next regeneration. Route all three through a macro (a precise \RhoMexact or widen \RhoM).

T2. "\NModels economies" (55) mildly double-counts the euro area. Abstract (:69) and intro (:134) call \NModels{}=55 a count of "economies," but constants.tex:10 defines it as 55 country models = \NBlocs(38) + \NMembers(17). Since the euro-area aggregate is one of the 38 blocs and its 17 members are counted separately, "55 economies" counts the euro area both as an aggregate and via its members (distinct economies ≈ 54). "55 models" is precise; "55 economies" is loose. Minor.

No drift found in the terms the brief flagged: the prose uses GMAPS consistently (the "G-BVAR" string survives only as the internal label sec:gbvar, never in text); net IIP / net international investment position is used uniformly in prose (the "NFA/Nfa" spelling lives only in invisible macro names and CSV headers); and "anchor" means the long-run anchor throughout the prose (the external nowcast "anchor" appears only in macro identifiers). These are clean.

docs.title: Minor Inconsistencies
docs.text:
• Sign/wording double-negatives from signed macros. gmaps_platform_paper.tex:236 renders "growth dipping −1.86 percentage points below baseline" (\TrueGdpGrowthMinPp{}=-1.86 already carries the minus), and :260-261 renders "the net-IIP ratio still slips −0.35 points below baseline" (\ExtScenNfaDevH{}=-0.35). "Dipping/slips −X below baseline" is a double negative. The same \TrueGdpGrowthMinPp macro is used correctly at :300 ("from −1.86 … to −2.37"), which is what exposes the inconsistency: either drop the sign in the macro or drop "below baseline" at :236/:260.

  • Forecast origin/nowcast date is never stated, and its macros are unused. \LastObsQ(2026Q1) and \NowcastQ(2026Q2) are defined (constants.tex:16-17) but used 0 times; the example leans heavily on "the nowcast quarter" (:194, :349, all figure captions) without ever dating it, while the coverage table and \USSampleEnd report the estimation sample ending 2025Q4. The 2025Q4-estimation-vs-2026Q1-origin shift is coherent in the tool but invisible and unexplained in the paper; a reader cannot tell whether pins land in 2026Q1 or 2026Q2. Consider stating the origin once.

  • \GlobalSweeps{}=1 conflicts with the "hundreds of sweeps" footnote. global_constants.tex:9 labels it "Gauss-Seidel sweeps to converge = 1," while sec2_methodology.tex:296-297 says Gauss–Seidel at ρ=0.989 needs "hundreds of sweeps." Harmless today (the macro is unused), but the data file is internally contradictory with the text.

  • LenzaPrimiceri2022 is cited for a treat-as-missing choice that is not their method. sec2_methodology.tex:196-198 cites them for masking 2020Q2–Q4, but Lenza–Primiceri's method is volatility rescaling, not treat-as-missing. Citing them for the general "estimate a VAR after March 2020" problem is defensible, but as written it can read as attributing the missing-data method to them. Consider "in the spirit of the post-2020 estimation problem raised by …" or citing the data-augmentation lineage already present (DurbinKoopman2002, TannerWong1987).

  • Housekeeping — defined-but-unused macros: \WorldAmp, \WUSEA/\WUSMX/\WUSCA/\WUSCN, \NaiveLrPeakBp, \CFResidualPct, \ExtUsCaAnchor, \ExtUsNfaH, \ExtScenCaDevH are all defined but cited 0 times in prose. Not errors, but note \WorldAmp(23.1×, cumulative) measures a different quantity than the "roughly four times"/"quadruples" trough ratio the text actually uses (2.35/0.54≈4.35×) — keep them from being conflated if either is later surfaced.

docs.title: Numbers that verify clean (spot-checked against CSVs)
docs.text: All of the following match their script-generated sources exactly: \NaiveLrImpactBp=69 (lr_n q1=0.6871); two-pin GDP trough \TrueGdpTroughPct=1.01 at q4 (gdp_scen_lvl=−1.0103), \TrueGdpGrowthMinPp=−1.86 (gdp_t q1); \DebtGapHPp=1.9 (debt 124.29−122.35 at q20); \CFEasingBp=281 (pol_cf−pol_scen at q1=−2.815); \CFResidualPct=0.00 (gdp_cf_lvl q4=−0.0000); \USGdpTroughGlobPp=2.37, \EAGdpTroughPp=2.11, \JPGdpTroughPp=2.38, \WorldTroughUsoPp=0.54, \WorldTroughGlobPp=2.35, \WorldTroughJointPp=2.62 (all match global_spread.csv/world.csv troughs); external anchors -3.66/3.61/3.99, seed -66.8, \ExtScenCaPeakPp=0.25, \ExtScenNfaDevH=−0.35. \dim x = 38·3·20+4·20 = 2360 is correct. Bloc/count consistency all holds: coverage table has exactly 38 rows (=\NBlocs), 25 "yes" fiscal (=\NFiscal), 18 seasonal (=\NSeasonal); 38+17=55 (=\NModels); US 1998Q3–2025Q4 = 110 quarters (=\USSampleT), n=40 (=\NUSVars, and "the other thirty-eight variables" = 40−2 pins). The abstract's "roughly quadruples" matches the body's "roughly four times" (4.35×). Every citation key used resolves to a references.bib entry — no missing bibliography items, including the two easily-confused AdolfsonLaseenLindeVillani2007 and AdolfsonLindeVillani2007.

docs.title: 3. Unsupported Claims & Identification Integrity
docs.text: The paper is, on the whole, unusually disciplined about the boundary this review polices: it repeatedly and correctly distinguishes the reduced-form conditional forecast ("a statement about likelihood, not about cause," sec2_methodology.tex:578; gmaps_platform_paper.tex:325-332, 366-371, 450-479) from the structural DSGE overlay, draws the counterfactual as a separately-labeled line, and defers both the out-of-sample horse-race and the classical-GVAR confrontation to a companion paper rather than claiming them as done. It does not claim "first." That restraint is real and should be credited. The findings below are where specific claims still outrun the exhibits, plus one load-bearing math inconsistency a referee will catch immediately.

docs.title: Internal consistency & math (blocking)
docs.text:
• The debt identity has an inconsistent unit conversion (sec2_methodology.tex:456-462). Equation \eqref{eq:debt} is d_t = d_{t-1}(1+i_t/400)/(1+g_t/100) − pb_t/4 + s_t/4, with the definitions (line 461-462) stating i_t is "percent per annum" and g_t is "nominal GDP growth (percent, quarter-on-quarter annualized)." Both i_t and g_t are therefore in the same units (annualized percent), yet the interest term divides by 400 (correct: annual %→quarterly fraction) while the growth term divides by 100. For a one-quarter recursion the annualized growth must also be /400 (quarterly log-change ≈ g_t/400). As printed, the denominator grows ~4× too fast, biasing the level of the debt ratio downward every quarter. This is exactly the "4·diff = q/q annualized" scaling trap; the interest term (EFFI = 400×quarterly-interest/debt) confirms the /400 convention is the intended one. Either g_t/100 should be g_t/400, or g_t is mislabeled as annualized. Because the fiscal block's rhetorical force is that "the debt line moved because accounting moved it" (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:248, 466-467), the printed identity has to be exactly right. (The headline \DebtGapHPp{}=1.9pp is a scenario-minus-baseline difference, in which a common multiplicative denominator bias largely cancels, so the reported number is probably robust even though the level path is not — but the equation as displayed is wrong.)

  • The "nothing typed by hand" reproducibility claim is not yet true (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:615-617, gmaps_platform_paper.tex:8). The style contract and Appendix C both assert "every number quoted in the text is generated by scripts … nothing is typed by hand." But constants.tex:2-4 states it is "HAND-SEEDED for the skeleton … Step 3 of the plan replaces this file with a SCRIPT-GENERATED version." So \NBlocs, \NMembers, \RhoM, \NFiscal, etc. are currently hand-seeded. Relatedly, \rho(M)=0.98917 is hard-typed three times in prose (sec2_methodology.tex:291, 366, 412) instead of using the defined macro \RhoM (=0.989, constants.tex:20), which is left unused. A referee who opens the repo will find the reproducibility claim only partially honored; either regenerate constants.tex before submission or soften the claim.

docs.title: Causal / claim overreach
docs.text:
• "A US credit event is a world credit event in this model, by design rather than by accident" (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:305), with EA/JP GDP troughs "magnitudes comparable to the US's own" (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:306-307, global_constants.tex: EA −2.11, JP −2.38, US −2.37). This is transparently attributed to design (the pinned variables are the global prices carried by every bloc), which is honest. But the near-symmetry — Japan's GDP falling slightly more than the US's from a US-originated shock — is a mechanical consequence of broadcasting the four US financial prices onto every bloc with no attenuation, amplified by ρ(M)=0.98917. The text never cautions the reader that these cross-country magnitudes are therefore not an empirical estimate of international transmission; they are what the global-price-broadcast assumption plus a near-unit multiplier mechanically produce. State this where the magnitudes are reported, not only obliquely in the costs section.

  • "everything it shows comes from one estimated model" (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:69). The abstract's own later sentences contradict this: the priced policy response is a Smets–Wouters overlay (a different, structural model), and the fiscal/external paths are accounting identities, not BVAR output. Qualify to "everything in the baseline and scenarios," since the counterfactual and the satellites are explicitly not from the estimated BVAR.

  • The counterfactual's causal reach is narrower than "adjust coherently around the structural core" implies (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:471-476). After the SW07 deltas for r/π/y are imposed as pins, the other thirty-odd variables move via the reduced-form smoother — i.e., by conditional correlation, not by the DSGE's structural propagation. The causal interpretation strictly attaches only to the three imposed core deltas; the derived responses of everything else are still likelihood statements. The paper elsewhere is scrupulous about this distinction and should extend it here. (Also worth a line: SW07 is a closed-economy model, so the priced easing omits the exchange-rate channel the rest of the tool carries.)

docs.title: Generalization issues
docs.text:
• The entire quantitative case is one example and, for the global claims, three displayed blocs. "Every economy in the dropdown now shows its own response" (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:279) but only US/EA/JP + a world aggregate are shown (fig_global.tex). The leap to "the world" (:305) and "roughly four times as much" (:312-313) is asserted for the aggregate while individual behavior of the other 35 blocs is neither shown nor summarized. For a top-field methods paper, a distribution of trough responses across all coupled blocs (even a single summary panel) would convert an illustration into evidence.

  • "reproduces the published external position … each inside its published range" (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:254-257) is asserted, not shown, and overstated. No published figure is cited alongside \ExtUsTbAnchor{}=−3.66, \ExtEaTbAnchor{}=3.61, \ExtCnTbAnchor{}=3.99. And "external position" overclaims: the very next sentences concede the current account "runs more negative than the published figure" (:265-266; \ExtUsCaAnchor=−5.66 vs a published US CA nearer −3.5%). Only the trade balance matches; say that.

  • The external/NFA block is a pilot presented as a settled feature. The constants come from nfa_pilot.mjs (nfa_constants.tex:1) and the main text (:250-268) presents the satellite without the word "pilot." Only one calibration default — the flat imputed primary-income return — is disclosed (:262-268). The currency-composition/valuation default (fxShare), quantitatively first-order for the US "exorbitant privilege," is nowhere mentioned, even though NFA is "rolled forward quarter by quarter" (:254). Disclose that the satellite is preliminary and that valuation effects are not modeled.

docs.title: Missing caveats
docs.text:
• The \CFEasingBp{}=281 bp headline is order-of-magnitude sensitive to the DSGE/rule choice, and this is not quantified (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:351, 355-364). The paper says "different DSGE models give different deltas" and calls switching "a one-click sensitivity check" (:478-479), but the reader is given one number, framed as "itself the finding" (:355), with no indication that a different admissible policy rule can move it by roughly an order of magnitude. Put a sensitivity range (or at least an explicit "this magnitude is specific to SW07's rule") next to the 281 bp.

  • The "4× world amplification" and the comparable EA/JP troughs ride on ρ(M)=0.98917, a near-unit quantity, with no sensitivity shown. The costs section admits ρ "close to one … makes the global amplification powerful" (sec2_methodology.tex:363-366), but the headline payoff (\WorldTroughUsoPp=0.54 → \WorldTroughGlobPp=2.35) is never stress-tested against ρ. Since ρ is a fragile, vintage-dependent object, a reader cannot tell how much of the "quadrupling" is robust versus an artifact of near-unit amplification. A one-line sensitivity ("at ρ=0.95 the amplification is X") would settle it.

  • MATLAB cross-validation and the internal-consistency checks are asserted, not demonstrated (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:567-576). "cross-validated against the MATLAB reference implementation," "verified against the iterative fixed point," "agree to numerical precision" — no tolerances, no exhibit, no number. Compounding this, the paper's one committed quantitative credibility exhibit — the classical-GVAR GIRF confrontation — is a \todo{} absent from the paper (:585-592). So at submission every behavioral claim rests on the tool's own output with no external cross-check shown. State a tolerance or point to a reproducible artifact for the MATLAB check, and do not submit with the credibility exhibit as a TODO.

  • The frozen-companion within-year update is presented purely as a benefit (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:356-357, 502-504). "the model untouched" / "the model stays fixed" is framed as a gain, but it is an approximation: within-year forecasts use a companion estimated on older data, and its accuracy cost is never acknowledged. Note that the worked example itself is run on such a vintage — estimation ends 2025Q4 (us_constants/coverage table) while the tool's last historical quarter is \LastObsQ=2026Q1 and the pinned nowcast is \NowcastQ=2026Q2 (constants.tex:16-17), i.e., the companion is frozen relative to the data the example conditions on.

  • SFA as a catch-all residual is disclosed as white-noise-priored but not flagged as hard-to-forecast (sec2_methodology.tex:178-181, :457-466). Since s_t enters the debt identity directly and absorbs everything the other three drivers miss, a line noting that debt projections inherit its residual uncertainty would be honest.

docs.title: Minor language issues
docs.text:
• "shock" terminology vs. the paper's own claim that conditioning is not causal. Section titles "Two pins make a risk shock" (:226) and pervasive "credit shock"/"spread shock" invite exactly the structural-innovation reading the paper disclaims at :578-579. Consider "credit-spread scenario" in the headings.
  • w_j(1)=1/S_H[j,j] is not "essentially zero" and the near-term path is not strictly un-jumped (:436-437). For a persistent variable the first-quarter weight is small but finite; "starts small" is accurate, "essentially zero"/"no jump" is loose. Relatedly, calling the h=H=20 value "its new steady state" (:436) sits awkwardly with the correct admission two lines later that the true infinite-horizon steady state "is not available here" (:438).
  • Sign-carrying macros produce double negatives in prose: "growth dipping \TrueGdpGrowthMinPp{}(=−1.86) percentage points below baseline" (:237-238) and "the net-IIP ratio still slips \ExtScenNfaDevH{}(=−0.35) points below baseline" (:261) read as "−1.86 below" / "−0.35 below." Store magnitudes in these macros or reword.
  • \WorldAmp=23.1 (cumulative) vs. "four times" (trough) (global_constants.tex:8 vs :312-313). The unused cumulative-amplification macro is a much larger number under a different metric; specify explicitly that the "four times" claim is the trough ratio so a referee recomputing does not find "23×."
  • \GlobalSweeps=1 (global_constants.tex:9) latently contradicts "hundreds of sweeps are needed" (sec2_methodology.tex:296-297). Unused in the compiled text, but reconcile before anyone wires it in.
  • "about five hundred tests" (:567) — verify against the actual suite size before submission (the current count appears to be materially under 500); "about five hundred" rounds up generously.

docs.title: 4. Mathematics, Equations & Notation
docs.text: Scope: sec2_methodology.tex (§2 equation blocks) plus the three toolkit equations in gmaps_platform_paper.tex (soft-pin, Villani anchor, DSGE convolution), cross-checked against constants.tex, the figs/data/*_constants.tex, and the TikZ/figure captions. The core derivations are sound — the VARX*→stack algebra (Eq. varx→stack), the affine coupled solve \((I-M)^{-1}d\), the dimension count, the seasonally-averaged projection intercept, and the Toeplitz back-solve all check out. The issues below are a mix of one substantive documentation error, several genuine symbol clashes, and formatting/process defects.

docs.title: Mathematical Errors
docs.text:
1. Debt identity — the growth term is mislabeled as "annualized" (substantive; replication hazard). sec2_methodology.tex:456-462, Eq. eq:debt: $\(d_t = d_{t-1} rac{1+i_t/400}{1+g_t/100} - rac{pb_t}{4} + rac{s_t}{4}\)$ with prose "\(g_t\) nominal GDP growth (percent, quarter-on-quarter annualized)" (line 462). The interest term divides by 400 (annualized percent → quarterly fraction), so for internal consistency the growth term's /100 requires \(g_t\) to be the non-annualized quarterly growth in percent. I confirmed against the code: app/src/lib/compute/fiscalAccounting.ts:12 documents gNomQ : % per QUARTER … (e.g. 1 = 1% q/q), line 105 sets gQ = gNomQ/100, and line 104 sets iQ = effAdj/400. So the formula is correct but the verbal label "annualized" is wrong — it should read "quarter-on-quarter, in percent (not annualized)." This matters: the model's displayed GDP growth uses the annualized \(4\Delta(100\ln)\) convention (line 126), so a reader taking \(g_t\) off the chart and plugging into \(1+g_t/100\) would overstate the growth adjustment ~4×. Fix the word, not the equation.

  2. "unique solution if and only if \( ho(M)<1\)" is imprecise (Eq. eq:fixedpoint). sec2_methodology.tex:290: "with a unique solution if and only if \( ho(M)<1\)." The linear system \(x=(I-M)^{-1}d\) has a unique solution iff \(1 otin\mathrm{spec}(M)\) (i.e. \(\det(I-M) eq0\)). \( ho(M)<1\) is sufficient for uniqueness — and it is the correct condition for the Neumann series / the Gauss–Seidel iteration to converge and for the multiplier to be stable — but it is not necessary for uniqueness, so the "only if" is false as stated. Given \( ho(M)=0.989\) sits just under one, the distinction is worth stating correctly: recommend "…has the unique solution \((I-M)^{-1}d\) whenever \(1 otin\mathrm{spec}(M)\); \( ho(M)<1\) additionally guarantees the iterative (Gauss–Seidel) path converges to it."

docs.title: Notation Inconsistencies
docs.text:
• \(d\) / \(d_t\) carries three meanings. Global-variable vector \(d_t\) in the classical GVAR (sec2:34,51,404, and \(d_{t-s}\) inside Eq. varx line 31); the pin-impact vector \(d\) in Eq. eq:fixedpoint ("let \(d\) collect the direct impact of the user's pins", line 286); and debt-to-GDP \(d_t\) in Eq. eq:debt (line 457). Three distinct objects share the symbol.
  • \(g_t\) carries two meanings. The four global financial prices (vector) in the partition Eq. eq:partition (sec2:119,122) versus nominal GDP growth (scalar) in Eq. eq:debt (sec2:458,462).
  • \(i\) vs \(i_t\). \(i\) is the bloc/country index throughout, but \(i_t\) is the effective interest rate in Eq. eq:debt (sec2:461). Eq. debt drops the bloc subscript, so \(i_t\) reads as "index \(i\) at time \(t\)."
  • \(j\) is both a partner-country index and a within-bloc variable index. Country index in the star sums \(\sum_{j\neq i}\) (Eqs. eq:rowdem–rowfin, eq:wtilde); variable index in the soft-pin \(y^{\mathrm{pin}}_{j,t+h}\) (paper:394-397) and the anchor \(S_h[j,j]\), \(w_j(h)\), \(\Delta^*_j\) (paper:426-432).
  • \(\Delta\) is overloaded. First-difference operator in "\(4\Delta\)" (sec2:126) and the star growth diffs; but a deviation / terminal displacement in \(\Delta y_{j,t+h}\) and \(\Delta^{*}_{j}\) (paper:427,432) and in \(\Delta r_{t+h}\) (paper:465). Consider a distinct symbol (e.g. \(\delta\)) for the anchor/counterfactual displacement.
  • \(H\) is overloaded. The classical lag-stack coefficient matrix in Eq. eq:stack (\(Gy_t=a_0+Hy_{t-1}+u_t\), sec2:75) versus the forecast-horizon scalar \(H=20\) in \(\dim x\) (sec2:280) and \(S_H\) (paper:428).
  • Minor: \(\mathbf T_i\) (Eq. ss, sec2:209) loses its subscript as \(\mathbf T\) in the anchor (paper:429-431); \(\ell\) is both the lag index (\(B_{i\ell}\), \(\lambda_i^2/(\ell^2\psi_j)\)) and the log-level symbol \(\ell^g,\ell^\pi\); \(w\) is both the trade weight \(w_{ij}\) and the anchor weight \(w_j(h)\).

docs.title: Undefined Notation
docs.text:
• \(c_\alpha\) in Eq. eq:ss (sec2:209) is never defined — the companion-form intercept is left implicit. More importantly it is written as constant, but see Spec/Identity below (it must be time-varying for the 18 seasonal blocs).
  • \(\eta_t\) in Eq. eq:ss (sec2:209) — the state innovation appears with no distribution or selection given (it should map \(\Sigma_i\) into the top companion block only).
  • \(\gamma_{i,Q2},\gamma_{i,Q3},\gamma_{i,Q4}\) (sec2:186) are used in \(\bar c_i\) without being introduced as the columns of \(\Gamma_i\) (inferable, but undefined at first use).
  • \(\Delta^{*}_{j}\) (paper:427,432) is described verbally ("terminal shift that lands the variable on its stated value") but its construction (stated target minus model terminal forecast) is only implied.
  • Star dimension \(k_i^{*}\) of \(y^{*}_{it}\) is never given (only \(k_i\) for the domestic block, sec2:33).
  • Lower summation limit in Eq. eq:delta (paper:465): "\(\sum_{k\le h}\)" leaves the start (presumably \(k=0\) at the nowcast) unstated; the Toeplitz system's invertibility also silently requires \(\phi^r_0\neq0\).

docs.title: Spec / Identity Issues
docs.text:
• Eq. eq:ss transition intercept drops the seasonal term. \(\alpha_t=\mathbf T_i\alpha_{t-1}+c_\alpha+\eta_t\) (sec2:209) uses a constant \(c_\alpha\), but for the \(\NSeasonal{}=18\) seasonal blocs the deterministic term \(c_i+\Gamma_i D_t\) is time-varying; strictly \(c_\alpha\) should be \(c_{\alpha,t}\). Given the paper emphasizes seasonal blocs, worth a half-sentence.
  • Debt identity annualization (cross-referenced with Mathematical Errors #1) — the identity itself is a correct spec; only the units gloss on \(g_t\) is wrong.
  • Eq. eq:starsclassical (sec2:37-38) writes \(y^{*}_{it}=\sum_j w_{ij}y_{jt}\) as a weighted sum of full country vectors of possibly different dimension \(k_j\). This is the standard GVAR shorthand (the weighting is really variable-by-variable), but a conformability footnote would prevent a literal-minded dimension objection at a top-field venue.
  • Anchor weight \(w_j(h)=S_h[j,j]/S_H[j,j]\) (paper:428) implicitly assumes the diagonal partial sums are non-negative and monotone so that \(w_j\in[0,1]\). For variables with oscillatory near-Nyquist roots (the seasonal/EFFI roots your own notes flag) \(\mathbf T^k[j,j]\) can be negative and \(w_j(h)\) non-monotone or outside \([0,1]\). The "\(S_h/S_H\) stands in for \((I-\mathbf T)^{-1}\)" motivation is well argued (paper:436-439); one caveat sentence about monotonicity would close the gap.
  • GlobalSweeps=1 macro comment contradicts the text. global_constants.tex:9 labels it "Gauss-Seidel sweeps to converge = 1", but footnote sec2:296 correctly says "hundreds of sweeps are needed" at \(\rho=0.989\). The macro is unused in the tex so no visible contradiction ships, but the data-file comment is misleading (it is really counting the one closed-form application).

docs.title: LaTeX Math Formatting
docs.text:
• \emph inside math mode. sec2_methodology.tex:277: $\emph{affine}$. \emph in math mode does not emphasize and typesets in math italic; change to \emph{affine} (outside $…$).
  • \(\rho(M)=0.98917\) is hand-typed, violating the paper's binding style contract. Literal 0.98917 appears at sec2_methodology.tex:291,363,412 and figs/tikz/fig_gbvar.tex:81, while the macro \RhoM (=0.989) defined at constants.tex:20 is never used (verified by grep). This breaks the header rule "Every quoted number is a macro from constants.tex (script-generated; never hand-typed)" (paper:8), and the two values disagree at the fourth digit (0.98917 vs 0.989), so a future regeneration of constants.tex will silently desync the body. Route all four through one macro at full precision.
  • Sign-carrying macros produce double negatives. \TrueGdpGrowthMinPp = -1.86 (us_constants.tex:7) is used at paper:235-236 as "growth dipping \TrueGdpGrowthMinPp percentage points below baseline" → renders "dipping −1.86 pp below baseline." Same pattern: \ExtScenNfaDevH = -0.35 at paper:259 "slips −0.35 points below baseline." Either strip the sign from the macro or drop "below." (At paper:300 the signed macro reads fine because it pairs with an explicit $-\USGdpTroughGlobPp$.)
  • Minor: appendix cross-references mix hard-typed "Appendix~B/C" (paper:365,371) with \ref{app:cred} (paper:448); the letters happen to be correct given appendix order, but the hard-typed ones will break if an appendix is inserted.

Net assessment: no error invalidates a result — the headline algebra (stack/solve, dimension \(38\cdot3\cdot20+80=2360\), the naive/true/global magnitudes, the SW07 counterfactual arithmetic) is internally consistent and matches the constants. The one item that a careful replicator would genuinely trip on is the mislabeled \(g_t\) in the debt identity (Mathematical Errors #1); the "iff \(\rho(M)<1\)" imprecision and the \emph-in-math / unused-\RhoM process defects are the next priorities for a top-field submission.

docs.title: 5. Tables, Figures & Documentation
docs.text:
I've read all the TeX sources, verified every quoted constant against the generating CSVs, and confirmed all referenced assets exist. Here is the production-editor review.

Files reviewed (absolute root /home/farkas/github/BVAR Policy Calibration Tool/): docs/paper/gmaps_platform_paper.tex, docs/paper/sec2_methodology.tex, docs/paper/constants.tex, docs/paper/figs/data/{us,global,nfa}_constants.tex, docs/paper/figs/{fig_naive_true,fig_external,fig_global,fig_cf}.tex, docs/paper/figs/data/coverage_table.tex. All CSVs, TikZ PDFs (fig_pesaran.pdf, fig_gbvar.pdf), and the three screenshots exist; every CSV column referenced by a TikZ plot is present (no broken plot references).

docs.title: Tables with Missing Notes
docs.text:
• coverage_table.tex (Table tab:coverage) has no notes at all. Caption (line 3) is only "The coupled blocs: size, sample, and blocks." Missing: (a) definition of the n column (number of endogenous variables); (b) meaning of the -- cells in "Seasonal dummies" and "Fiscal block" (no "-- = none" legend); (c) statement that "Estimation sample" is the estimation window that ends before the 2026Q1 data shift/nowcast (the text elsewhere uses \LastObsQ{}=2026Q1, \NowcastQ{}=2026Q2, so a reader sees "2025Q4" in the table and "2026Q1/Q2" in the prose with no reconciliation); (d) data source; (e) note that the 17 euro-area members are excluded here (they are only mentioned in the surrounding prose, line 609). Also IL is the only bloc ending 2024Q4 (coverage_table.tex line 37) while every other bloc ends 2025Q4 — this warrants a footnote or it reads as a typo.
  • Coverage-table generating script is unnamed / circular. coverage_table.tex line 1 says "GENERATED by the Appendix-C coverage script"; the reproducibility text (gmaps_platform_paper.tex line 624–625) says the table "is generated ... by the script recorded in its header comment." Each points at the other; the actual script filename appears nowhere, so the table is not reproducible as documented.
  • Table tab:gvar-vs (sec2_methodology.tex line 372) needs no data notes, but it hard-codes $\rho(M)=0.98917$ (line 412) — see the constants issue below.

docs.title: Figures with Missing Notes
docs.text:
• No figure shows uncertainty bands, and no caption says so. All four TikZ figures (fig_naive_true, fig_external, fig_global, fig_cf) plot posterior-mean/central lines only. Yet the paper repeatedly promises bands: abstract "uncertainty bands throughout" is implied, intro line 136 "uncertainty bands throughout," and the fig:ui-cond caption (line 202) explicitly says "and the uncertainty band." Not one response-figure caption states that the plotted lines are posterior means or that bands are omitted for legibility. This is the single largest note gap — add "lines are posterior means; bands omitted for legibility" (or plot the band on the headline fig:naivetrue).
  • fig:global puts units only in the caption, unlike the other three figures. Panel titles are bare country names ("United States", "Euro area", "Japan", "World"; fig_global.tex lines 10, 17, 21, 25); the unit "pp, q/q annualized" lives only in the caption (line 32). fig_naive_true, fig_external, and fig_cf all carry units in each panel title. Add the y-unit to the fig:global panels (or a shared y-label).
  • Two of four TikZ captions omit the x-axis note. fig_naive_true.tex line 44 and fig_external.tex line 30 end with "Horizontal axis: quarters from the nowcast."; fig_global.tex and fig_cf.tex captions have no such sentence, though all four share xlabel={quarters} and start at the nowcast.
  • Screenshot captions: provenance wording is inconsistent and slightly at odds with the appendix. fig:ui-cond (line 205) and fig:ui-ea (line 290) end "Interface view from an earlier release; the layout is unchanged." fig:ui-cf (line 344) says only "Interface view from an earlier release." — dropping "the layout is unchanged." Separately, the captions say "from an earlier release" whereas the reproducibility text (line 624) says the views are "screen captures of the deployed tool." Standardize the boilerplate and reconcile "earlier release" vs "deployed tool."
  • fig:external: fine on self-containedness (states derived-not-estimated, % of GDP, seed), but note it plots levels while the other three plot deviations — worth one clause so a reader does not expect a zero baseline.

docs.title: Cross-Reference Issues
docs.text:
• Numeric text/figure mismatch: naive policy-rate peak. Text (gmaps_platform_paper.tex line 213) says "the policy rate climbs \NaivePolPeakBp{} basis points at its peak" with \NaivePolPeakBp{}=44 (us_constants.tex line 3). But the plotted naive policy line pol_n in us_spread.csv peaks at 0.4192 → 41.9 bp (≈42), not 44, at quarter 4. Both files are stamped as generated by the same script (us_spread_cf.mjs) at the same time, so this is an internal inconsistency to reconcile (re-run to sync, or the constant is measured on a different series). All other quoted constants verify exactly against the CSVs (checked: 10y impact 69 bp = lr_n 0.6871; GDP growth trough −1.86 = min gdp_t; level trough 1.01% at q4; CF easing 281 bp = pol_cf−pol_scen at q1 = −2.815; US/EA/JP troughs 2.37/2.11/2.38; world 0.54/2.35/2.62).
  • Reproducibility block has stale figure numbers and a missing script. gmaps_platform_paper.tex lines 620–621 comment us_spread_cf.mjs # Figs 1, 3 and global_spread.mjs # Fig 2. In the current document those scripts produce Figs 4 & 8 (fig:naivetrue, fig:cf) and Fig 7 (fig:global) respectively — the "1, 3 / 2" numbering is from an earlier draft. More seriously, nfa_pilot.mjs is not listed at all, even though it generates fig:external (Fig 5) and nfa_constants.tex (per those files' own headers). A replicator cannot regenerate the external-balance figure/constants from the printed commands.
  • Figures cited out of order in §3.4. fig:cf is \input at line 335 (so it gets the lower float number) but is referenced after fig:ui-cf in the prose: line 350 cites Figure~\ref{fig:ui-cf} then line 351 cites Figure~\ref{fig:cf}. Readers hit "Figure N+1" before "Figure N." Swap the two float placements (put fig:ui-cf before the \input{figs/fig_cf}).
  • Referencing is otherwise complete: every TikZ figure, screenshot, and both tables are referenced exactly once in the text; no dangling or unreferenced float. us_debt.csv is generated but not consumed by any figure (the debt result is text-only via \DebtGapHPp); harmless, but note it.

docs.title: Formatting Inconsistencies
docs.text:
• The same line style encodes different meanings across figures — the worst offender. In the shared preamble (gmaps_platform_paper.tex lines 38–43), jointline and cfline are byte-identical (jointgreen, thick, dashed), and trueline/globline are identical (scenblue, thick). Consequences: green-thick-dashed = "spreads in US+EA+JP" in fig:global (fig_global.tex line 16) but = "with policy response / counterfactual" in fig:cf (fig_cf.tex line 15). Red-dashed (naiveline) = "one pin (naive)" in fig:naivetrue (line 15) but = "baseline" in fig:external (line 14). A reader who learns "red-dashed = the wrong/naive line" in Fig 4 will misread Fig 5 where red-dashed is the baseline. Give each distinct series its own consistent encoding, or at minimum keep "baseline" a single style everywhere.
  • "Baseline" has three different visual encodings. Dotted (per the fig:ui-cond screenshot caption, line 202: "the baseline (dotted)"), the flat gray zeroline in the deviation plots (fig_naive_true, fig_global, fig_cf), and red-dashed naiveline in the level plot fig_external. Pick one convention for baseline across screenshots and TikZ.
  • Sign convention of the trough constants is inconsistent and produces double-negatives in prose. \TrueGdpGrowthMinPp{}=-1.86 (carries its own minus) but \USGdpTroughGlobPp{}=2.37 (magnitude). So line 300–301 reads "from -1.86 percentage points alone to $-2.37$" — one intrinsic sign, one hand-added $-$. Worse, line 235–236 prints "growth dipping -1.86 percentage points below baseline" and line 262 prints "the net-IIP ratio still slips -0.35 points below baseline" (\ExtScenNfaDevH{}=-0.35) — both literal double negatives. Make the trough constants magnitudes and let the prose supply "below baseline," or standardize all as signed and drop "below."
  • \RhoM is defined but never used; ρ(M) is hand-typed instead. constants.tex line 20 defines \RhoM{}=0.989, but the actual value shown is the literal 0.98917, hard-typed three times (sec2_methodology.tex lines 291, 364, 412). This violates the paper's own binding style contract (line 8: "Every quoted number is a macro from constants.tex ... never hand-typed"). Relatedly, constants.tex still self-identifies as "HAND-SEEDED" (lines 2–4), not script-generated — so the whole constants.tex tier is currently outside the "no hand-typed numbers" guarantee.
  • Numerous dead constants (defined, never referenced) indicate constants↔prose drift: \LastObsQ, \NowcastQ, \WUSEA/\WUSMX/\WUSCA/\WUSCN (constants.tex); \NaiveLrPeakBp, \CFResidualPct (us_constants); \WorldAmp, \GlobalSweeps (global_constants); \ExtUsCaAnchor, \ExtUsNfaH, \ExtScenCaDevH (nfa_constants). Not reader-facing, but they undercut the "single source of truth" discipline and should be pruned or wired in.
  • Minor: mixed decimal precision among quoted numbers (e.g., \DebtGapHPp{}=1.9 one decimal vs \TrueGdpTroughPct{}=1.01 two decimals vs bp values as integers) — acceptable but worth a house-style pass.

Verified-clean items: 38 coverage-table rows = \NBlocs{}=38; \NModels{}=55 = 38 + \NMembers{}17; fiscal-"yes" count = 25 = \NFiscal{}; seasonal-"yes" count = 18 = \NSeasonal{}; the 8 even-EFFI blocs (\NEvenEffi) are all fiscal; US 1998Q3–2025Q4 = 110 quarters = \USSampleT; \dim x = 38·3·20 + 4·20 = 2{,}360 (sec2 line 281) is arithmetically correct; all non-\NaivePolPeakBp response constants match their CSVs to the rounding.

docs.title: 6. Contribution & Referee Assessment
docs.text: (Tool/platform-documentation paper, adapted framework. All files read in full: gmaps_platform_paper.tex, sec2_methodology.tex, constants.tex, the four figs/data/*_constants.tex, the four fig_*.tex, and coverage_table.tex.)

docs.title: Part 1 — Central Contribution
docs.text:
One-sentence claim. The GMAPS is a browser-based, second-fast platform that produces internally consistent baseline forecasts and conditional scenarios for 55 economies from a single estimated global Bayesian VAR — 38 coupled blocs linked by three trade-weighted foreign variables and four global financial prices, estimated jointly across ragged/pandemic-missing data by an EM/data-augmentation loop, and solved for any scenario as one precomputed linear fixed point x=(I−M)⁻¹d — with fiscal and external accounting satellites, soft outside-forecast conditioning, a reactive Villani-style long-run anchor, and a DSGE policy overlay layered on top.

Is it genuinely new vs. the closest priors? Mixed, and the paper's own framing ("the contribution is the integration", gmaps_platform_paper.tex:169) is the honest one. - Not new: a Bayesian GVAR with Minnesota shrinkage in levels instead of cointegration already exists — Crespo Cuaresma–Feldkircher–Huber and the BGVAR package. The paper positions only against the classical cointegrated GVAR (Pesaran/Dees, sec2_methodology.tex:17–102) and never cites the Bayesian GVAR line. The claim of novelty on the econometric core (sec2:174–176, "we discipline it with shrinkage") is undercut by this omission and cannot stand until it is confronted head-on. - Genuinely new / valuable: (i) the conditional-forecast global operator — the observation that each bloc's smoother mean is affine in the pins, so cross-country conditional consistency is a single linear fixed point (I−M)⁻¹d (sec2:264–297). GVAR practice ships GIRFs from G⁻¹, not a coupled conditional solve; this is the paper's sharpest methodological idea. (ii) The joint EM completion of a 38-bloc unbalanced panel with pandemic-as-missing and a Jacobi star fixed point (sec2:236–262) is a real, non-trivial estimation contribution. (iii) The engineering integration (precomputed inverse → interactive world scenarios in ~1s) is genuinely useful and, for a policy institution, non-obvious.

Closest prior: the ECB multi-country/ECB-BASE model documentation (AngeliniBokanCiccarelliLalikZimic2025, cited and explicitly held up as the genre standard, gmaps_platform_paper.tex:119–124) for the institutional-tool comparison; and Bayesian GVAR (Feldkircher–Huber, uncited) for the econometric comparison.

Rating: Significant as a platform + conditional-solve operator; Incremental on the pure econometrics. But this rating is conditional — as written the paper does not yet demonstrate the contribution quantitatively (see Part 2), so on delivered evidence it currently sits at the Incremental/Significant boundary.

docs.title: Part 2 — Credibility
docs.text:
Does the paper convince that the tool does what it claims? The mechanics are described carefully and honestly; the behavioral claims are largely unvalidated and, in two places, internally inconsistent with the shipped constants.

Threat 1 — No quantitative validation is actually in the paper. The single credibility exhibit the paper "commit[s] to" — the classical-GVAR GIRF confrontation on the same data — is a placeholder: "The exhibit is being produced … and will appear in this appendix in the next revision. \todo{GIRF figure pending the toolbox estimation run}" (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:590–592). The out-of-sample evaluation is likewise deferred: "Results go to a companion paper; this one documents the platform" (:604; also :510–513). So a tool paper whose headline is a novel global solve contains zero external benchmarking of that solve. A skeptical seminar's first question — "how do I know these numbers are right and not an artifact?" — has no answer in the current draft.

Threat 2 — ρ(M)=0.98917 is close to unity, and the amplification it produces is enormous. sec2:291,366,412 report ρ(M)=0.98917; the paper concedes this "makes the global amplification the solve produces powerful and places weight on the star equations that generate it" (sec2:363–366). The generated constants make the stakes concrete: the cumulative world amplification is \WorldAmp = 23.1× (global_constants.tex:8) — a 23-fold blow-up of a US credit shock. No sensitivity to ρ is shown, and a re-estimation that nudged ρ above 1 would make (I−M)⁻¹ non-existent. This near-unit multiplier is the single biggest credibility risk and is essentially unaddressed.

Threat 3 — the "4× world spillover" is partly definitional, not discovered. The two pinned variables (US 10y, US Baa) are two of the four global commons carried as regressors in every bloc (sec2:124–129). So EA and Japan trough at −2.11 and −2.38 pp — comparable to the US's own −2.37 (global_constants.tex:2–4) — largely because the shock is mechanically imposed on their own equations, not because it propagates through trade. The paper is admirably explicit ("A US credit event is a world credit event in this model, by design", gmaps_platform_paper.tex:304), but the abstract's framing — "the global solve carries it to every economy and roughly quadruples the world output loss" (:78) — reads as a spillover finding when it is substantially a consequence of the common-commons construction. A US→EA GDP spillover as large as the US domestic effect is far outside standard empirical GVAR estimates, and a referee will say so.

Threat 4 — the NFA baseline is internally inconsistent with its own current account. The US seed is \ExtUsNfaSeed = −66.8% of GDP and the baseline net-IIP endpoint is \ExtUsNfaH = −55.4% at 5y (nfa_constants.tex:4–5) — an 11-point improvement — while the model runs a current account of \ExtUsCaAnchor = −5.66% (:3). A persistent −5.7% CA cannot coexist with an improving NFA/GDP unless the flow is not being accumulated: −66.8 rescaled by ~22% nominal growth over 5y is −54.9%, i.e. the endpoint is almost exactly the pure denominator effect with zero net flow contribution. Either the roll-forward drops the CA flow or the reported −5.66% CA is not the flow used. Compounding this, the balance-of-payments/NFA identity is never written down — the paper writes the debt identity \eqref{eq:debt} (sec2:456–462) but only refers to the external identity (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:250–268, fig_external.tex:26–30). For a paper that stakes the "external satellite" as a headline exhibit, the identity must be on the page and the baseline reconciled. The authors flag the CA-level return issue (:262–268) but not this stock-flow tension.

Threat 5 — the frozen-companion approximation is the shipped default, unquantified. "the smoother's companion is held at the previous pass's posterior mean … An exact data-augmentation pass … is available behind a flag as a final polish" (sec2:245–249, gmaps_platform_paper.tex:553–556). The shipped model is therefore the approximate one; the paper never quantifies how far the exact-DA solution differs. For an estimator paper this gap must be closed with a number.

Threat 6 — smaller internal inconsistencies that a careful referee will catch. - Style-contract violation + precision mismatch on ρ. The build contract says "Every quoted number is a macro from constants.tex … never hand-typed" (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:8), yet ρ(M)=0.98917 is hand-typed three times in sec2 while constants.tex:20 defines \RhoM = 0.989. The macro is defined but not used, and at a different precision. - "spread barely changed" contradicts the numbers. The naive case pins Baa +100 and returns 10y \NaiveLrImpactBp = 69 bp (us_constants.tex:2), so the spread widens by 31 bp — a third of the shock — yet the text says "the spread between corporate and government yields barely changed" (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:223). - Debt identity vs. its variable definition. In \eqref{eq:debt} the interest term is i_t/400 (annual %→quarterly) but the growth term is (1+g_t/100), while g_t is defined as "nominal GDP growth (percent, quarter-on-quarter annualized)" (sec2:462). An annualized g should enter as /400, not /100; as written the two conversions are inconsistent (the label or the formula is wrong). This is exactly the "conventions that matter and are easy to get wrong" the paper warns about (gmaps_platform_paper.tex:471). - \GlobalSweeps = 1 (global_constants.tex:9, labeled "Gauss-Seidel sweeps to converge") directly contradicts the paper's own footnote that "hundreds of sweeps are needed" at this ρ (sec2:296–297). Unused in the text, but a generated constant that is simply wrong. - IL sample ends 2024Q4 (coverage_table.tex:37), the only bloc not reaching 2025Q4; unexplained.

What a skeptical seminar would say: "You've built an elegant and honest instrument, but you've shown me its plumbing, not that its water is clean. Your world multiplier rests on a spectral radius of 0.989 and a 23× cumulative amplification; your cross-country 'spillovers' are as large as domestic effects because you impose the same financial prices everywhere; your external satellite's baseline improves while running a 5.7% deficit; and every validation you promise is in a different paper."

docs.title: Part 3 — Required analyses (blockers)
docs.text:
1. Put the classical-GVAR GIRF confrontation in the paper. It is the one exhibit the paper commits to (:585–592) and it is a TODO. Without it there is no external check on the global solve. This is the top blocker.
  2. Ship a minimal out-of-sample slice, not a forward reference. At least one horizon/one target set: GMAPS (with and without anchors) vs. random walk, AR(1), closed-economy BVAR, and the classical GVAR (the benchmark set the paper itself names, :594–604). A tool paper can defer the full horse-race, but "trust us, it's in the companion paper" is not sendable to a leading journal.
  3. ρ(M) robustness. Report how ρ(M), the world trough, and \WorldAmp (23.1×) move under perturbations of the star equations / weights, and confirm the operator stays invertible across estimation vintages. The near-unit multiplier is the paper's load-bearing wall and is currently untested.
  4. Write the external/NFA identity and reconcile the baseline. Put the balance-of-payments recursion on the page next to \eqref{eq:debt}, and explain how a −5.66% CA is consistent with a baseline NFA that improves from −66.8% to −55.4% (nfa_constants.tex:3–5). If the CA flow is not accumulated, that is a bug to fix, not a caption to hedge.
  5. Quantify the frozen-companion approximation. One table: shipped (frozen) vs. exact-DA on the canonical conditional forecast and on ρ(M)/the world trough. If the gap is negligible, say so with a number; if not, it changes the headline exhibits.

Suggested analyses (strengtheners)

  • Position explicitly against Bayesian GVAR (Feldkircher–Huber BGVAR): what does the EM completion + conditional-solve operator add beyond an existing Bayesian GVAR? This is the difference between "Significant" and "Incremental."
  • Decompose the world response into the trade channel vs. the global-commons channel, so the reader can see how much of the "4×" is genuine spillover vs. imposed common shock (the paper gestures at this in prose, :296–307, but numbers would settle it).
  • A coverage/calibration check on the shipped uncertainty bands (do the posterior bands attain nominal coverage on held-out data?), since bands are advertised throughout.
  • Show the reactive anchor's cost: because it "moves the mean and nothing else" (:444), it is not a Villani steady-state prior (which would tighten long-run bands). One figure contrasting the reactive re-centering with an actual steady-state-prior re-estimation would make the honesty precise.
  • A one-figure sanity check that the DSGE-delta overlay + re-run smoother produces a coherent object — the SW07 general-equilibrium co-movements differ from the BVAR's, and "laying the delta on top then re-running the smoother" (:472–477) mixes two covariance structures.

docs.title: Part 4 — Literature positioning
docs.text:
Right citations, well used. The scenario/GaR frame (Adrian et al. 2019/2020/2025), the classical GVAR lineage (Pesaran–Schuermann–Weiner, Dees et al., Chudik–Pesaran, di Mauro–Pesaran, Smith–Galesi toolbox, Pesaran–Shin GIRF), the Bayesian-VAR machinery (Giannone 2015, Doan–Litterman–Sims, Litterman, Sims–Zha, Waggoner–Zha, Banbura–Giannone–Lenza, Durbin–Koopman, Tanner–Wong, Dempster–Laird–Rubin, Lenza–Primiceri), Villani 2009 for the anchor, Antolín-Díaz et al. for the causal/conditional distinction, MMB (Wieland et al.) and Smets–Wouters for the overlay, and the institutional comparators (Vitek IMF-GMM, Adrian et al. IPF, ECB multi-country, Darracq-Paries, Adolfson et al., Lindé–Smets–Wouters) are all appropriate and largely deployed correctly.

Missing majors. - Bayesian GVAR — the closest econometric prior — is absent. Crespo Cuaresma–Feldkircher–Huber; Huber (2016) density forecasting with Bayesian GVARs + SV; the BGVAR package. This is the omission: the paper claims shrinkage-in-levels as its distinguishing move against cointegration (sec2:172–190) without acknowledging that Bayesian GVARs already do exactly that. Non-negotiable to add and confront. - Pesaran–Schuermann–Smith (2009), "Forecasting … with Global VARs" (IJF) — the canonical GVAR forecast-evaluation paper and the natural benchmark design for the promised OOS. - Bańbura–Giannone–Reichlin (2010), "Large Bayesian VARs" — the cornerstone for the large-BVAR + conditional-forecast approach; only the 2015 conditional-forecast piece is cited. - Minor: for the conditional-forecast-as-tilting interpretation, Robertson–Tallman–Whiteman (relative entropy) and Cogley–Morozov–Sargent would round out the "outside forecast as data" framing (:387–411); for the DSGE-VAR hybrid, Del Negro–Schorfheide.

Best framing. Lead with the two-comparator structure the paper already has (classical GVAR on one side, ECB institutional-tool documentation on the other) but insert Bayesian GVAR as the third leg and state precisely what the conditional-solve operator + EM completion + interactivity add on top of it. The "we keep the GVAR skeleton, replace weak exogeneity twice and cointegration with shrinkage" story (sec2:299–313, Table tab:gvar-vs) is genuinely good and should survive the revision intact.

docs.title: Part 5 — Journal fit + recommendation
docs.text:
Realistic targets, in order. 1. International Journal of Central Banking (IJCB) — best fit. It publishes exactly this genre (policy-model documentation, BVAR/DSGE tools, institutional forecasting infrastructure), tolerates "documentation" papers, and the IMF-authorship + policy framing land well. Highest probability of acceptance after the Part-3 blockers. 2. International Journal of Forecasting (IJF) — strong fit iff the OOS evaluation is brought into the paper; IJF is the home of GVAR forecasting (Pesaran–Schuermann–Smith) and of tool/method papers with real forecast validation. Without the horse-race, it will bounce. 3. Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control / Economic Modelling — plausible secondary homes for the computational-platform angle. 4. JAE / JBES — the most demanding econometrics targets. In current form these are desk-rejects: they require methodological novelty plus validation, and the novelty is partly pre-empted by Bayesian GVAR while the validation is deferred to another paper.

Recommendation: Revise before sending. The writing is unusually clear, the mechanics are documented to a high standard, and the conditional-solve operator + EM completion are real contributions. But the paper cannot go to referees at a leading journal while its one committed quantitative exhibit is a \todo, all OOS validation lives in a "companion paper," the load-bearing ρ(M)=0.989/23× amplification is untested, and the NFA baseline contradicts its own current account.

Concrete path to sendable. (a) Land the classical-GVAR GIRF confrontation and a minimal OOS slice in Appendix B. (b) Add a ρ(M) robustness table and confirm invertibility across vintages. (c) Write the external/NFA identity and reconcile the −66.8→−55.4 baseline against the −5.66% CA. (d) Cite and confront Bayesian GVAR (Feldkircher–Huber) explicitly. (e) Fix the internal-consistency defects: route ρ through \RhoM, correct the debt-identity g_t/100 vs. "annualized" mismatch, fix "spread barely changed", and drop/repair \GlobalSweeps=1. With (a)–(e), send to IJCB (or IJF if the horse-race is complete).

docs.title: Part 6 — Referee questions (targeting the weakest points)
docs.text:
1. ρ(M)=0.98917 and a 23.1× cumulative world multiplier: how stable is the spectral radius across re-estimation vintages and across perturbations of the star weights, and how do the headline world troughs move as ρ→1? At what ρ does the shipped (I−M)⁻¹ cease to exist, and how close are you to it?
  2. Is the "4×" a spillover or a construction? Since the two pinned variables are global commons carried in every bloc, decompose the euro-area/Japan −2.1/−2.4 pp troughs into the trade channel vs. the direct common-price channel. What fraction survives if the pinned prices are not broadcast to the other blocs' own equations?
  3. External satellite: please write the balance-of-payments/NFA identity explicitly and reconcile it — how does the baseline net-IIP improve from −66.8% to −55.4% of GDP over five years while the model runs a −5.66% current account? Is the CA flow being accumulated into the stock?
  4. Frozen-companion approximation: the shipped model holds the companion at the previous pass's posterior mean. Quantify the difference between the shipped solution and the exact data-augmentation solution on the canonical conditional forecast and on ρ(M) — is the approximation innocuous for the headline exhibits?
  5. Reactive anchor: because it re-centers the mean and leaves the bands unchanged (:444), in what sense is this "the reactive counterpart" of Villani's steady-state prior rather than a cosmetic level shift? What is lost relative to a prior that actually informs the estimated long-run?
  6. DSGE overlay coherence: you lay a Smets–Wouters IRF delta on the reduced-form scenario and re-run the smoother. Why is the combined path internally coherent given that the DSGE's general-equilibrium co-movements differ from the BVAR's covariance? Show that the re-smoothed bloc is not double-counting or fighting the imposed delta.
  7. Positioning: what does the GMAPS add over an existing Bayesian GVAR (Feldkircher–Huber BGVAR) — is the novelty the conditional-solve operator and EM completion specifically, and can you demonstrate that with a like-for-like comparison rather than only against the classical cointegrated GVAR?

docs.title: Priority Action Items
docs.text:
CRITICAL (could cause desk rejection / major objections): 1. No in-paper quantitative validation. The one committed credibility exhibit — the classical-GVAR GIRF confrontation on the same data — is a visible \todo{} (gmaps:585–592), and the entire out-of-sample horse-race is deferred to a companion paper. Land the GIRF confrontation and a minimal OOS slice (GMAPS ± anchors vs. RW / AR(1) / closed-BVAR / classical GVAR) in Appendix B; "trust us, it's in the companion paper" is not sendable. [Agent 3; Agent 6 Threat 1 / Part 3-1,2; Agent 2 C2] 2. ρ(M)=0.98917 near-unity, untested. It drives a 23.1× cumulative / ~4× trough world amplification that is never stress-tested, and a re-estimation nudging ρ above 1 makes (I−M)⁻¹ non-existent. Report ρ / world-trough / \WorldAmp sensitivity to star-equation and weight perturbations and confirm invertibility across estimation vintages. [Agent 3; Agent 6 Threat 2 / Part 3-3] 3. The "4× world spillover" is substantially definitional, not estimated. The two US pins (10y, Baa) are two of the four global commons broadcast into every bloc's own equations, so the EA/JP troughs (−2.11/−2.38) ≈ the US's own (−2.37) mechanically. Decompose the trade channel vs. the common-price channel and state, where the magnitudes are reported, that these are not an empirical estimate of international transmission. [Agent 3; Agent 6 Threat 3] 4. The external/NFA baseline contradicts its own current account. Net-IIP improves −66.8%→−55.4% over 5y while the model runs a −5.66% CA (the endpoint is almost exactly the pure denominator effect with zero net-flow contribution — likely the CA flow is not being accumulated, i.e. a bug), and the balance-of-payments/NFA identity is never written down. Put the identity on the page and reconcile the baseline; also disclose that the satellite is a pilot and that valuation/fx-share effects are unmodeled. [Agent 6 Threat 4 / Part 3-4; Agent 3] 5. Debt-identity unit inconsistency (Eq. eq:debt). The interest term divides by 400 but the growth term by 100 while g_t is labeled "quarter-on-quarter annualized"; the formula matches the code (g is quarterly, non-annualized) so the verbal label is wrong. As printed, a replicator taking g off the annualized-growth chart overstates the growth adjustment ~4×. This is load-bearing for the "accounting moved the debt line" claim — fix the word. [Agent 3; Agent 4 Math Error 1; Agent 6 Threat 6] 6. Closest econometric prior (Bayesian GVAR) is uncited. Crespo Cuaresma–Feldkircher–Huber, Huber (2016), the BGVAR package — a Bayesian GVAR with Minnesota shrinkage in levels instead of cointegration already exists, yet the paper claims shrinkage-in-levels as its distinguishing move without confronting it. Cite it and state precisely what the conditional-solve operator + EM completion add; this is the difference between "Significant" and "Incremental," and at JAE/JBES its absence is a desk-reject risk. [Agent 6 Part 1 / Part 4] 7. Frozen-companion approximation (the shipped default) is unquantified. One table: shipped (frozen) vs. exact-DA on the canonical conditional forecast and on ρ(M) / the world trough. If negligible, say so with a number; if not, it changes the headline exhibits. [Agent 3; Agent 6 Threat 5 / Part 3-5] 8. The "nothing is typed by hand" reproducibility claim is currently false, and a \todo ships in the PDF. constants.tex still self-identifies as HAND-SEEDED; ρ(M)=0.98917 is hand-typed three times (sec2:291,363,412) while \RhoM(=0.989) is defined but unused (also a fourth-digit precision mismatch that will desync on regeneration). Regenerate constants.tex / route ρ through one full-precision macro before submission, or soften the claim — and remove the visible TODO. [Agent 1 Crit 6; Agent 2 T1/C2; Agent 3; Agent 4]

MAJOR (referees will likely raise): 1. Claim overreach on "everything from one estimated model" and on the counterfactual. The abstract's "everything it shows comes from one estimated model" is contradicted by the SW07 overlay and the accounting satellites (qualify to "baseline and scenarios"); and the counterfactual's causal reach is only the three imposed core deltas — the other ~30 variables move by conditional correlation, and SW07 is closed-economy so the priced easing omits the exchange-rate channel. [Agent 3] 2. "Reproduces the published external position … inside its published range" is asserted, not shown, and overstated — only the trade balance matches; the CA runs more negative than published. Cite the published figures and restrict the claim to the trade balance. [Agent 3] 3. The 281 bp counterfactual easing (\CFEasingBp) is order-of-magnitude sensitive to the DSGE/rule choice, unquantified. Give a sensitivity range or state explicitly that the magnitude is specific to SW07's rule. [Agent 3] 4. Text-vs-figure mismatch: naive policy-rate peak. Text quotes 44 bp (\NaivePolPeakBp) but the plotted pol_n peaks at ≈42 bp (0.4192) in us_spread.csv; regenerate or reconcile. [Agent 2 C1; Agent 5] 5. "The spread barely changed" contradicts the numbers. Baa +100 bp with 10y +69 bp means the spread widens 31 bp — a third of the shock; fix the sentence. [Agent 6 Threat 6] 6. Wrong cross-reference: "The full roster appears in Appendix C." Appendix C does not contain it — the roster is in the online manual; correct the pointer. [Agent 2 X1] 7. "unique solution iff ρ(M)<1" is imprecise. Uniqueness holds iff 1∉spec(M); ρ(M)<1 is sufficient and is the correct condition for Gauss–Seidel/Neumann convergence. Restate. [Agent 4 Math Error 2] 8. Add "lines are posterior means; bands omitted for legibility," or plot the band on the headline figure. [Agent 5] 9. Reproducibility block is not executable as printed. Line-style semantics collide across figures. jointline/cfline are byte-identical and trueline/globline are identical, so green-thick-dashed and red-dashed each mean two different series across figures, and "baseline" has three encodings. Notation clashes and undefined symbols in §2. d/d_t (three meanings), g_t (two), H (two), Δ overloaded, i vs i_t, j (two index roles); and c_α, η_t, γ_{i,Q·}, Δ*_j, k_i*, the eq:delta lower limit are undefined at first use. Disambiguate. [Agent 4] 13. Spec gaps. The eq:ss transition intercept drops the time-varying seasonal term (should be c_{α,t} for the 18 seasonal blocs), and the anchor weight w_j(h)=S_h/S_H needs a monotonicity/[0,1] caveat for oscillatory near-Nyquist roots. [Agent 4] 14. Lenza–Primiceri is miscited for a treat-as-missing choice that is not their method (their method is volatility rescaling); recite to the data-augmentation lineage already present. [Agent 2] 15. Coverage table (tab:coverage) has no notes (n-column definition, "--" legend, estimation-window-vs-nowcast reconciliation, data source, euro-members-excluded), and IL ending 2024Q4 — the only bloc not reaching 2025Q4 — is unexplained. docs.title: Writing checklist — McCloskey, Economical Writing
docs.text:
Applied to every non-technical passage of gmaps_platform_paper.tex. A paragraph that fails a rule gets rewritten, not patched. The polish pass (step 5) re-runs the whole list.

  1. One point per paragraph. The first sentence states it; everything after supports it. If a paragraph makes two points, split it; if it makes none, cut it.
  2. Connect. Begin sentences with what the reader already has; end on the new thing. The stress falls on the last word. Each section's last sentence hands off to the next section.
  3. No boilerplate. No roadmap paragraphs, no "this section describes", no "it is worth noting", no "we now turn to". If a signpost is needed, one sentence, doing real work.
  4. Verbs, not nouns. "We estimate", not "estimation is performed". Hunt nominalizations (-tion, -ment, -ity) and convert them back into verbs.
  5. Active voice, unless the actor is genuinely unknown or genuinely irrelevant.
  6. Concrete beats abstract. A number, a name, a variable the reader can touch. "The euro area carries a weight of 0.17" beats "trade weights are calibrated appropriately".
  7. Short words. Use, not utilize; so, not consequently; about, not approximately.
  8. Cut intensifiers and hedges. Very, quite, rather, genuinely, importantly, arguably — delete and see if anything is lost. (It almost never is.)
  9. No elegant variation. The same object keeps the same name. The stars are the stars.
  10. No naked "this". "This" takes a noun: this restriction, this loop, this number.
  11. "However" never leads a sentence. Prefer "but"; put "however" inside if kept at all.
  12. Read it aloud. Break any sentence that needs two breaths. Vary sentence length; a short sentence after two long ones lands the point.
  13. Prose argues; tables enumerate. Lists of properties belong in a table or a figure, not welded into a sentence with semicolons.
  14. Spare the acronyms. "The tool" and "the model" carry most sentences; GMAPS appears where identity matters, not as a drumbeat.
  15. The so-what test. For every paragraph: if it were deleted, what would the reader lose? If the answer is "nothing", believe the answer.
  16. Rewrite. The first draft is never economical. This checklist is re-applied at every checkpoint, not once.
